notes: FAMILY-FRIENDLY naturist resort!  AANR affiliated.  Hot springs, hiking.  Cabins + camping.  Mountain paradise!

name: Olympic Training Center Colorado Springs
notes: OLYMPIC athlete training!  FREE guided tours.  See athletes practicing.  Olympic museum.  INSPIRATIONAL!

name: Paint Mines Interpretive Park
notes: PAINTED clay formations!  Hoodoos + Spires.  Rainbow colors.  4-mile loop trail.  FREE hidden gem!

name: Red Rock Amphitheater + Red Rock Canyon
notes: ICONIC concert venue!  Natural rock amphitheater.  Hiking trails around.  Workout stairs.  LEGENDARY shows!

name: Rocky Mountain National Park
notes: ICONIC Colorado park!  Trail Ridge Road (12,183ft).  Elk, bighorn sheep.  300 miles of trails.  RESERVATIONS needed summer!

name: Sasquatch Outpost
notes: BIGFOOT museum!  Casts, sightings, evidence.  Gift shop full believers.  Mountain highway stop.  HILARIOUS + earnest!

name: Scarlet Ranch
notes: UPSCALE swingers club Denver!  22,000 sq ft facility.  Themed rooms, dance floor.  Couple + single female nights.  DRESS CODE enforced!

name: St. Elmo Ghost Town
address: St Elmo, CO 81236 (west of Buena Vista)
notes: BEST preserved ghost town Colorado!  1880s mining town.  40+ buildings intact.  General store still operates!  FREE wandering!

name: Stanley Hotel
address: 333 E Wonderview Ave, Estes Park, CO 80517
notes: THE SHINING inspiration!  Stephen King stayed room 217. Ghost tours daily.  Historic 1909 hotel.  ESTES PARK icon!

name: Steamboat Ski Resort ⛷️ Ikon
address: 2305 Mt Werner Circle, Steamboat Springs, CO 80487
notes: Ikon Pass: UNLIMITED. Perfect home base for several weeks! Top-tier adult ski school for Els. Lower half of the mountain = exceptionally soft and forgiving. Enough repeat days for real progress. Town Steamboat Springs = cozy après-ski, hot springs. DISADVANTAGE: long isolated drive from I-70. Plan 5-7+ days! Break day: Hot Sulphur Springs on the way to Winter Park ♨️

name: Strawberry Park Hot Springs
notes: RUSTIC hot springs!  Multiple pools.  Clothing optional after dark.  4WD winter required.  NATURAL setting. PEACEFUL!

name: Telluride Mountain Village Gondola
address: Mountain Village Blvd, Mountain Village CO 81435
notes: FREE gondola!  Connects town + ski resort.  13 minute ride.  10,540ft views.  SCENIC transportation!

name: The Airplane Restaurant
notes: EAT in Boeing KC-97 tanker!  Cockpit dining.  Burgers, wings.  Kids LOVE it.  AVIATION theme park!

name: The Broadmoor
notes: 5-STAR luxury resort!  Since 1918. Lake, golf, spa, zip line.  Multiple restaurants.  SPLURGE destination!

name: The Fort Restaurant
notes: ADOBE fortress replica!  Mountain man cuisine.  Buffalo steaks, Rocky Mountain oysters.  Red Rocks views.  ATMOSPHERIC dining!

name: The International Church of Cannabis
notes: CANNABIS Church!  Psychedelic interior art.  Elevationists religion.  Wednesday services.  DENVER only!

name: The John Denver Sanctuary
notes: MEMORIAL garden!  Rocky Mountain High lyrics carved.  Boulders + native plants.  Aspen tribute.  FREE peaceful stop!

name: UFO Watchtower
notes: UFO spotting platform!  San Luis Valley hot spot.  "Healing garden" with offerings.  Alien merchandise.  QUIRKY roadside stop!

name: United States Air Force Academy
notes: CADET chapel iconic!  17 spears.  Visitor centre.  Self-guided campus tour.  FREE. IMPRESSIVE!

name: United States Mint – Denver
notes: COIN production facility!  FREE guided tours.  Reservations required months ahead.  See money being made!  EDUCATIONAL!

name: Valley View Hot Springs
address: Orient Land Trust, Villa Grove, CO 81155
notes: CLOTHING OPTIONAL resort!  Multiple hot spring pools.  Mountain views.  RESERVATIONS required.  AANR peaceful retreat!

name: Winter Park Resort ⛷️ Ikon
notes: Ikon Pass: UNLIMITED. Discovery Park = fantastic self-guided beginner zone with great instructors for Els. BUT: the rest of the mountain is dominated by HUGE moguel fields - Serge liked it, Els less so. 2-3 day stopover. Easy via US-40/I-70, close to Denver. Connected to Mary Jane (expert terrain). Go through Hot Sulphur Springs on the way there or back!

name: Abbott's Lobster in the Rough
notes: Classic waterfront lobster stand since 1947. BYOB (bring your own drinks!). Seasonal (May-October). Lobster, shrimp, and mussels enjoyed at picnic tables by the sea. ~$30-50 pp. Niantuc CT. Perfect summer lunch pairing with Mystic.

name: Beinecke Rare Book & Manuscript Library
notes: One of the largest libraries in the world for rare books and manuscripts, on the Yale campus. The building itself is spectacular: the marble exterior walls are so thin that light shines through them. Gutenberg Bible on permanent display. FREE admission. Architecturally and historically stunning. Must-stop in New Haven.

name: Center Church Crypt
notes: Church built in 1813 above a cemetery. 137 gravestones from 1687–1812 visible beneath the floor, including Rev. James Pierpont (founder of Yale) and Margaret Mansfield (first wife of Benedict Arnold). Free tours available. New Haven center.

name: Frank Pepe Pizzeria Napoletana
notes: Original pizza (pronounced 'ah-beetz') since 1925. White clam pizza is the specialty — unique in the US. Reagan's favorite pizza. Lines of 2+ hours on weekends, come early or on the weekdays. New Haven pizza is in a category of its own — no tomato sauce, charcoal oven, thin crust. MUST EAT.

name: Frog Bridge
notes: Bridge with giant frogs on it commemorating the Battle of the Frogs in 1754, when residents of Williamant believed croaking frogs were war invaders. Free, always visible. Typical New England absurdism. Quick photo stop.

name: Gillette Castle
notes: Medieval fieldstone castle built by Sherlock Holmes actor William Gillette. 47 unique doors with various wooden locks. Mirrors to spy on guests from above. Beautiful view of the Connecticut River. Harriet Beecher Stowe Museum nearby. Free parking, ~$10 pp.

name: Hampton Inn & Suites Mystic
notes: Reliable $100-150/night. Breakfast included. Pool. Close to Mystic Seaport, Mystic Aquarium, and Abbott's Lobster. Good base for a day at Mystic.

name: Holy Land USA
notes: Abandoned religious theme park, replica of Bethlehem built by John Baptist Greco. Closed in 1984 after his death. Vandalized, but the 56-foot steel cross is still visible from the highway. CLOSED to the public but visible from the road. Surreal and melancholic.

name: House of 1833
notes: UNIQUE! Historic mansion from 1833 as a B&B. Antiques, fireplaces, ~$200-350/night. Stunning but above budget. Special occasion option. Mystic area.

name: Kent Falls State Park
notes: Beautiful 76-meter cascade waterfall, short hike to the top. Best in spring or after rain. Autumn colors excellent in September/October. Day visit, no camping. Free (CT State Parks). Combine with a drive along Route 7 through the Litchfield Hills.

name: Lake Compounce
notes: Oldest continuously operating amusement park in the US (opened 1846!). Boulder Dash wooden coaster won Best Wooden Coaster in the World 5 times. Wildcat is the 14th oldest wooden coaster in the world. Crocodile Cove water park included in the admission price. Historic 1898 carousel. ~$45 pp. Six Flags Prestige Pass NOT valid (separate chain).

name: Lime Rock Park
notes: Historic race track in the Litchfield Hills — active since 1957. Paul Newman raced here for many years. Various race events from May to October (~$20-50 pp for spectators). Beautifully situated in rolling countryside. Even without a race, the track is beautiful to drive. Combine it with a drive along Route 44 through the Litchfield Hills.

name: Louis' Lunch
notes: Inventor of the hamburger (1900)! NO KETCHUP ALLOWED (house rule). Toast bread, no bun. Tiny historic building in New Haven. Cash only. ~$10 pp. Hamburger at its most original. Combine with Yale and the pizza route on the same day.

name: Mark Twain House
notes: Victorian Gothic mansion in Hartford where Mark Twain wrote Huckleberry Finn and Tom Sawyer. 25 rooms. Magnificent architecture. No photos allowed inside. Harriet Beecher Stowe Museum on the adjacent grounds — two legends in one day.

name: Modern Apizza
notes: No lines! Claims Casino Pie — locals prefer this over Frank Pepe. Quieter, more relaxed. Good option if the lines at Frank Pepe are too long. Third pillar of the New Haven pizza triangle.

name: Mohegan Sun
notes: One of the largest casinos in the US, run by the Mohegan tribe. 300,000 m² casino, hotels, 40+ restaurants, large concert venue (Arena at Mohegan Sun). Not just for gamblers — the architecture is impressive (Wolf Den free performances every night). Compare with Foxwoods nearby for a 'casino day'.

name: Mystic KOA
notes: Camping, RV/tent, cabins. Budget option for the F-150. Close to Mystic Center and Seaport. Campsites with electricity available. Good for one or two nights as a base for the Mystic area.

name: Mystic Seaport Museum
notes: Historic maritime village on the water. Authentic 19th-century sailing ship (Charles W. Morgan). Beautiful coastal atmosphere. Combine with Mystic Aquarium, Abbott's Lobster, and a night at Mystic for a perfect day at the coast. ~$30 pp. Mystic Pizza restaurant nearby (yes, the one from the movie).

name: Old Mystic Village
notes: Colonial-style shopping center with independent shops, galleries, and restaurants in a picturesque village. Free admission. Close to Mystic Seaport and Mystic Aquarium. A nice addition to a Mystic day for a leisurely stroll and souvenir shopping.

name: PEZ Visitor Center
notes: The only PEZ factory and visitor center in North America. Museum featuring the history of PEZ (Austrian invention, 1927), 5,000+ dispensers on display, and you can see the factory running through the windows. ~$5 pp for the museum. PEZ shop with exclusive variants. Unique and absolutely fun for a vlog.

name: Route 146 Scenic Drive
notes: Scenic coastal route along Long Island Sound via Guilford and Branford to Stony Creek (Thimble Islands). Historic colonial towns, saltwater marshes, marinas. Free driving. Combine with a Thimble Islands boat tour for a perfect day at the coast. Best in autumn or early summer.

name: Sally's Apizza
notes: Frank Sinatra's favorite in New Haven. Charred, crispy crust, iconic pepperoni pizza. Family business. Same style as Frank Pepe but with a more loyal local following. Literally two streets away from Frank Pepe — do both in one day ('Pizza Tour New Haven').

name: Sheffield Island Lighthouse
address: Ferry vanuit Hope Dock, Norwalk CT 06850
notes: Victorian lighthouse on a small island in Long Island Sound, accessible by ferry from Norwalk (~$30-40 pp, season May-October). Picnics on the island are possible. Quiet and photogenic. Birdwatching and views over Long Island Sound. Combine with lunch in historic center of Norwalk.

name: Skydive Danielson
notes: Tandem skydiving ~$200-300 pp. Specializes in first-time jumpers. Danielson Airport. Serge Y. Combine with a day in Connecticut's Quiet Corner for a rural getaway.

name: Sleeping Giant State Park
notes: Hiking trails. The mountain ridge resembles a sleeping giant when viewed from afar. Tower Trail leads to a stone observation tower with a view. Beautiful autumn colors. Free (CT State Parks). Combine with the Yale Peabody Museum in nearby New Haven.

name: Snickerdoodle Cookie – State Food
address: Diverse bakkerijen in CT (o.a. Lyman Orchards, Middlefield CT)
notes: The snickerdoodle is the unofficial state cookie of Connecticut — a cinnamon-sugar cookie with a soft interior and a slightly crispy exterior. Modest but typically New England. Best spot: Lyman Orchards in Middlefield (also apple picking in the fall). Not a major attraction, but a nice local food note.

name: Solair Recreation League
notes: 360-acre family nudist resort since 1934. Pond, pool, hot tub, cabins, campground. AANR affiliated. Intro day pass ~$35 (first 4 visits). Nudity MANDATORY at the pool/pond. Best naturist resort in the Northeast! Golf cart required for first-visitor tour. Friendly atmosphere. RV sites available for the F-150.

name: Sticks and Stones Farm
notes: Cabin in the woods. Quiet and rural. Budget-friendly. A good alternative if other hotels are fully booked or if a quiet evening in the woods is desired.

name: Sun Ridge Resort
notes: Adults only, no clothing. Day pass $60-70 (9:30-5:30). RV sites $30-40/night. More limited than Solair. More geared towards couples. Serge Y. Combine with Solair if there are multiple CT nights — Solair is the better choice for a first visit.

name: Taber Inn & Suites
notes: Budget $100-150/night. 9.6 rating on Booking. Family-friendly. Mystic. Good value for the area.

name: Ted's Restaurant
notes: Steamed cheeseburgers — A UNIQUE Connecticut invention since 1959. The steam cooks the meat and melts the cheese from the top. Cash only. Small and fast. One of the strangest but tastiest burgers in the US. ~$10 pp. Meriden CT.

name: The Adventure Park at Storrs
notes: Ziplines and aerial routes through 5 wooded hectares. Climbing ladders, rope bridges. Create your own course. ~$30-50 pp depending on skill level. Combine with a day at the University of Connecticut campus in Storrs.

name: The Dinosaur Place
notes: Outdoor park with 40+ life-sized dinosaur statues spread across a 1.5 km walking path through the forest. Mini golf, climbing structures, water park in the summer. ~$20 pp. Fun and photogenic — ideal for a quick stop. Close to Mystic and Foxwoods casino.

name: The Glass House – New Canaan
notes: Iconic modernist glass palace by architect Philip Johnson (1949) — a fully transparent house in the middle of the woods, he lived there himself. National Historic Landmark. Tours ~$35-55 pp, book weeks in advance. Architecture enthusiasts: world class. Combine with a visit to Greenwich or Stamford.

name: The River Rats Resort
notes: UNIQUE! Spend the night on a houseboat on the river. Airbnb/VRBO formula. Serge Y. Unusual sleeping experience. Ideal for vlog content: 'night on the water in Connecticut'. Check availability well in advance.

name: Thimble Islands
notes: Archipelago of 365 small islands in Long Island Sound, accessible by tour boat from Stony Creek. Victorian summer houses, boathouses, seals. ~$25 pp for the tour (~45 min). Season May-October. Charming and photogenic — a unique stretch of the Connecticut coast. Combine with lunch in Branford.

name: Yale Peabody Museum
notes: Giant blue whale hangs from the ceiling. Dinosaur fossils. Famous for the 16-foot tapeworms extracted from a Yale student's body in 1896! Fun activity on a rainy day. New Haven also has the best pizza in the US — pair it with Frank Pepe.

name: Yale University
notes: One of the most prestigious universities in the world (1701). The campus is beautifully Gothic and collegiate to visit — free tours. The Sterling Memorial Library resembles a cathedral. Combine with Frank Pepe pizza, Louis' Lunch, and the Peabody Museum for a full day in New Haven.

name: 20-voet Amish Man Statue
notes: Quick photo stop. 20-foot fiberglass Amish man outside a drawing shop. Was mascot of Dutch Pantry House.

name: Air Mobility Command Museum (GRATIS)
notes: FREE. Only museum in the world for airlift & refueling. 30+ historic aircraft outside + WWII hangar. C-141 and C-130 open for self-guided tours. Top 10% on TripAdvisor worldwide.

name: Bethany Beach
notes: Quieter family beaches south of Rehoboth. Big Chill Beach Club nearby for sunset + drinks over the water. Less crowded than Rehoboth.

name: Big Chill Beach Club
notes: Rooftop bar and restaurant above the Indian River Inlet. Watch the sunset from the terrace with views of the Atlantic Ocean and the bay. Tropical cocktails, seafood. Excellent for golden hour content.

name: Blair's Ballooning Delaware
notes: Local balloon operator. Sunrise/sunset flights over the countryside. ~$200-250 pp. Great content for the vlog.

name: Bombay Hook National Wildlife Refuge
notes: 20,000+ acres of tidal wetlands. Spectacular bird migration (autumn = best time). Cranes, geese, grey herons. America the Beautiful Pass valid.

name: Cape Henlopen State Park
notes: 5,000 acres where Delaware Bay and the Atlantic Ocean meet. WWII Fort Miles towers, free bike rental, fantastic campground. Bortle 4 dark skies for stargazing.

name: Cape May–Lewes Ferry
notes: 1.5-hour ferry Delaware → New Jersey. Brought the Ford F-150 on board. Smart route: Delaware coastal stops → ferry → Cape May, NJ. Two states in one day.

name: Corporation Trust Center - Wilmington
notes: America's most famous address: 300,000+ companies registered in this single office building (Amazon, Apple, Google...). Delaware's quirky tax trick. Photo-op from the outside — bizarre roadside curiosity.

name: Crooked Hammock Brewery – Lewes
notes: Backyard party atmosphere: hammocks, lawn games, live music, craft beer. Close to Cape Henlopen. Perfect for a relaxed afternoon.

name: Delaware Seashore State Park Camping
notes: Camping between the Atlantic Ocean and Indian River Bay. Spacious F-150 RV sites. Starry sky over the water. No campfires allowed. ~$40-55/night.

name: Dogfish Head Brewings & Eats
notes: Delaware's most famous craft brewery (1995). Off-center ales. Chesapeake & Maine seafood restaurant on the side. Combine with a visit to the Steampunk Treehouse in Milton.

name: Dogfish Inn – Lewes (hotel)
notes: Boutique hotel from Dogfish Head Brewery. Bicycles included. Craft beer in the room. ~$120-180/night. Perfect pairing with a brewery visit.

name: Fort Delaware State Park (eiland-gevangenis)
notes: Civil War prison on Pea Patch Island, by ferry only. Paranormal tours available. Spooky atmosphere, unique experience.

name: Futuro House – UFO-huis Milton
notes: Prefab UFO house by Finnish architect Matti Suuronen, 1968. Only ~20 pieces in all of the US. Just stands in a field. Perfect vlog content.

name: Giant Doctor's Bag & Stethoscope
notes: Quick photo stop. 20-foot doctor's bag + stethoscope at a medical center. Random roadside weirdness.

name: Golden Fleece Tavern - Dover
notes: The place where Delaware ratified the US Constitution in 1787. New café a few streets from the historic location. English pub vibe, local Fordham beer. Good story for the vlog: 'The First State'.

name: Hagley Museum - Wilmington
notes: 235-acre site of the original DuPont gunpowder factory (1802). Working 19th-century engine room. And: the Rothschild Patent Model Collection is located here — 5,000+ miniature inventions including a mechanical dog and a whip/cane combo.

name: Henlopen City Oyster House
notes: Fresh oysters, lobster rolls, steamed prawns. Always a line – go early! No reservations. Local hit.

name: Lewes Beach (Savannah Beach)
notes: Quiet beach on the Delaware Bay side (no waves). Ideal starting point for the Cape May-Lewes Ferry. Close to Dogfish Inn and Cape Henlopen.

name: Miles the Monster – Dover Speedway
notes: 46-foot concrete monster with a NASCAR car in his hand. Free photo opportunity off the track. Delaware's most iconic roadside attraction.

name: Nemours Estate (Mansion and Gardens)
notes: Louis XVI-style DuPont country house with 77 rooms + formal French gardens. Largest French-style garden in North America. Tours. Impressive, but more for Els than Serge.

name: Noah's Ark Church – Seaford
notes: Quick photo stop. Church as a replica of Noah's Ark with animal silhouettes in the windows. Biblical roadside kitsch.

name: Oddporium – Gallery of the Peculiar
notes: Shop + museum: working Tesla coil, cyclops pig, skulls, medical curiosities. Building from 1911 – the owner family died there multiple times.

name: Peach Pie - State Food of Delaware
notes: Peach pie is the official state dessert of Delaware. Fresh peaches grow in Kent County. Best place: local bakeries near Dover or the farmers' market in Milford/Harrington. Not to be missed when the season is right (summer).

name: Rail Haus Beer Garden – Dover
notes: Beer garden next to the old railway line. Picnic tables in the sand, fire pits, railway carriages as bars. Pretzel bites + bratwurst. Ideal pit stop next to the AMC Museum.

name: Rehoboth Beach + Funland
notes: Funland: retro family attraction on the boardwalk since 1962. Classic rides, Haunted Mansion, arcade. Rehoboth Beach itself = Delaware's busiest coastal city with unique restaurants and bars.

name: Rothschild Patent Model Collection (Hagley)
address: 298 Buck Road East (Hagley Library), Wilmington DE 19807
notes: 5,000+ miniature inventions from 1790-1880 — combination whip/walking stick, sofa that turns into a boat, mechanical dog. FREE to view via the Library entrance. Second largest private collection in the world.

name: Sambo's Tavern – Steamed Crabs
notes: Quiet cafe along the Leipsic River. Fresh steamed crab at sunset. Paper on the table, dirty hands, beer in hand. Far from tourists, a local favorite.

name: Smith's Bridge (covered bridge)
notes: Historic covered wooden bridge over Brandywine Creek. Photogenic and peaceful. Close to Brandywine Creek State Park. Quick stop for beautiful photos.

name: Steampunk Treehouse - Milton (Dogfish Head)
notes: 40-foot sculpture of rusting metal + recycled wood at Dogfish Head Milton Brewery. Brewery tours, beers on tap, live music. Combine with a visit to the Futuro UFO House (also in Milton).

name: Thrasher's Fries
notes: Delaware's holiest boardwalk ritual since 1929. Only fries, nothing else. Vinegar + salt — NO ketchup (that is sacrilege here). Simple but unforgettable. A MUST EAT on the boardwalk.

name: Tiki Murph – Roadside Tiki Kingdom
notes: Quick photo stop. Hundreds of tiki statues along the road, artists at work. Tropical madness in Delaware.

name: Trap Pond State Park
notes: Kayaking through the northernmost bald cypress forest in the US. Rare habitat. RV camping available for the F-150.

name: Winterthur Museum, Garden and Library
notes: DuPont mansion + largest collection of American decorative heritage. Enchanted Woods: 3-acre fairy garden with a bird's nest to sit in, fairy houses, and a mystical mushroom ring.

name: World's Largest Frying Pan – Seaford
notes: Quick photo stop. 10-foot cast iron skillet outside the historical museum. On the way to the coast.

name: Zwaanendael Museum + Fiji Merman
notes: Replica of a Dutch city hall for the 300th anniversary of the Dutch colony. Inside: a fake merman made of animal parts. Belgian touch: Dutch architecture!

name: Ben's Chili Bowl
notes: DC icon since 1958 on the famous U Street. Half-smoke (local spiced sausage) + chili is THE specialty. Obama ate here. Cheap + authentic. No visit to DC without this.

name: Congressional Cemetery
notes: Bizarre 19th-century cemetery with enormous cubic cenotaphs for Congressmen – John Philip Sousa + J. Edgar Hoover lie here. Gothic atmosphere. FREE. Perfect content.

name: Dupont Underground
notes: Abandoned underground tram station converted into an art gallery with rotating exhibitions. Bizarre and photogenic. Check opening hours - not always open. ~$10-15pp.

name: Eastern Market
notes: Historic covered market from 1873 on Capitol Hill. Fresh fruit + meat + flowers + artisanal products. Expanded with an outdoor market on weekends. FREE admission. Good for breakfast.

name: Ethiopic Restaurant
notes: DC has the largest Ethiopian community in the Americas - Ethiopian on H Street is one of the best. Injera + doro wat + kitfo. Eat with your hands the proper way. ~$20-30pp.

name: Ford's Theatre & Petersen House
notes: Where Lincoln was shot on April 14, 1865. The museum, the chair, and John Wilkes Booth's pistol are on display. Diagonally across: Petersen House, where Lincoln died. FREE museum.

name: Georgetown Neighborhood
address: M St NW & Wisconsin Ave NW Georgetown DC 20007
notes: Historic neighborhood with cobblestone streets + Federalist architecture + canal walk + good food + shops. E-bike recommended - Georgetown is quite large. Ideal for a full day.

name: Ghosts of Lafayette Park Tour
notes: Guided ghost tour of the White House by lantern light - Victorian-clad guides. Murder, murder, and betrayal in DC's darkest corners. ~$20pp. Great for evening entertainment.

name: Graduate Washington DC (Georgetown)
address: 1075 Thomas Jefferson St NW Georgetown DC 20007
notes: Trendy boutique hotel in Georgetown with an academic theme and good design. Close to the Exorcist Steps and the canal walk. ~$150-200/night. Good location for exploring Georgetown.

name: Great Falls Park (Virginia)
notes: Spectacular waterfall about 30 minutes from DC - the Potomac rushes over giant boulders. America the Beautiful Pass valid! One of the most impressive waterfalls on the East Coast.

name: Hillwood Estate Museum & Gardens
notes: Hidden gem: beautiful mansion with the largest collection of Russian imperial art outside Russia (Fabergé eggs!) + stunning gardens. Hardly any visitors. ~$18pp.

name: Hotel Zena
notes: Striking female-empowerment themed hotel with statement art throughout the building. Unique concept - funny for Belgians. ~$150-220/night. Good location in the 14th Street Corridor.

name: House of the Temple (Vrijmetselaars)
notes: Impressive neoclassical Masonic building - free tours. 33rd Degree Scottish Rite temple. Mysterious and fascinating. Serge: this is pure Da Vinci Code content.

name: International Spy Museum
notes: One of the coolest museums in all of America. Interactive spy museum with gadgets + secret operations of real CIA/KGB agents. Admission ~$27pp. MANDATORY!

name: Jaleo (José Andrés)
notes: Tapas restaurant by Spanish-American star chef José Andrés – the man who fed DC after Hurricane Maria. Lively + flavorful. ~$50-80pp. Reserve in advance.

name: Kenilworth Aquatic Gardens
notes: Hidden gem: national park with giant water lilies and lotus plants. In July, everything is in bloom – magical atmosphere. FREE + America the Beautiful Pass. Few tourists.

name: Kimpton Hotel Monaco DC
notes: Boutique hotel in a beautiful neoclassical old post office building. Amazing interior + central location near museums. ~$200-280/night. Free wine hour every evening for guests.

name: Library of Congress (Jefferson Building)
notes: Most magnificent interior in DC - stunning rotunda with a golden dome. FREE but reserve, timed entry. The Gutenberg Bible and the very first photo of a human are on display here.

name: Lincoln Memorial
address: 2 Lincoln Memorial Cir NW Washington DC 20037
notes: Iconic monument - FREE and open 24/7. Best time to visit: sunrise or sunset for perfect photos. Martin Luther King gave his I Have a Dream speech here.

name: National Air and Space Museum
notes: THE aviation museum of America. Wright Brothers plane + Apollo 11 capsule + spacesuits. FREE. An absolute must for Serge - reserve timed entry online in advance.

name: National Arboretum & Bonsai Museum
address: 3501 New York Ave NE Washington DC 20002
notes: Large botanical garden with 400-year-old bonsai trees (received from Japan after WWII) + original Capitol pillars in the middle of a meadow. FREE. Bizarre + beautiful at the same time.

name: National Archives
notes: The original Declaration of Independence + Constitution + Bill of Rights behind glass. FREE, but reserve for timed entry. Historical goosebumps guaranteed for Belgians.

name: National Building Museum
notes: Spectacular interior – 15m high Corinthian columns in an impressive grand hall. Temporary exhibitions are often experimental and surprisingly creative. Free basic admission.

name: National Museum of African American History
notes: Powerful and unforgettable museum. FREE but timed passes REQUIRED - book months in advance! Emotionally + historically impressive. Do not miss.

name: National Museum of Health and Medicine
notes: Military medical museum with hairballs in intestines + skull fragments of Lincoln after his assassination. Not for the faint of heart. FREE. Serge will love this.

name: National Museum of Natural History
address: 10th St & Constitution Ave NW Washington DC 20560
notes: Hope Diamond + dinosaurs + living coral tank. FREE. One of the most visited museums in the world – come early or reserve timed entry.

name: National Portrait Gallery / American Art Museum
address: 8th and F Streets NW Washington DC 20001
notes: Two museums in one beautiful neoclassical building - Yayoi Kusama installations + presidential portraits. The inner courtyard (Kogod Courtyard) is architecturally spectacular. FREE.

name: National Zoo (Smithsonian)
notes: Free zoo in Rock Creek Park. Big cats + rhinos + elephants. Anoas (rare buffaloes from Indonesia) are also at home here. FREE. Good for half a day.

name: Old Ebbitt Grill
notes: Oldest bar/restaurant in DC (1856) - a few steps from the White House. Victorian decor + oysters + classic American grill. Busy but historic atmosphere. Reservations on weekends.

name: Planet Word Museum
notes: Immersive language museum in the restored Franklin School building (1869). Unique and playful concept centered on language and communication. ~$20pp. A 10/10 for Els.

name: Rock Creek Park
notes: Large, wooded city park in the middle of DC. Walking and cycling paths through a real forest. America the Beautiful Pass valid for admission. Good for an e-bike ride along the creek.

name: The Barbie Pond on Q Street
notes: Anonymous street art installation featuring Barbie dolls in political and social scenarios. Regularly updated for holidays. Free. Perfect quirky content stop.

name: The Exorcist Steps (Georgetown)
notes: 97 steep stairs from the horror film The Exorcist (1973) - free and 24/7. Serge: let yourself roll from top to bottom for the content. Iconic for film fanatics.

name: The Watergate Hotel
notes: THE scandal hotel of America - fully renovated and luxurious again. Room has a 'Do Not Disturb' sign with 'No Need to Break In'. Above budget (~$350/night) but GOLD for contentment.

name: The Wharf (voedselwijk)
notes: New waterfront district with a dozen restaurants + food halls + live music + kayak rentals along the Potomac. Great place for an evening. Fresh fish + seafood recommended.

name: Theodore Roosevelt Island
address: George Washington Memorial Pkwy McLean VA 22101
notes: Peaceful forest island in the Potomac with walking paths and a large statue. Accessible via a small footbridge. FREE + America the Beautiful Pass valid. Perfect escape from the hustle and bustle.

name: Tidal Basin & Cherry Blossoms
notes: Famous Japanese cherry blossoms in late March/April. If the timing coincides with your DC visit (Spring 2028?), this is a SPECTACLE. Go early to beat the crowds.

name: Topless George Washington (NMAH)
address: 14th St & Constitution Ave NW Washington DC 20001
notes: The Smithsonian American History Museum houses a half-naked Zeus-like Washington sculpture (1840) – a huge scandal at the time. Free. Combine with the rest of the museum.

name: U Street Corridor
notes: Historic Black Broadway neighborhood – Duke Ellington was born here. Murals + live music venues + Ethiopian restaurants + Ben's Chili Bowl. Evening atmosphere is great. Free walking neighborhood.

name: Udvar-Hazy Center (NASM Dulles)
address: 14390 Air and Space Museum Pkwy Chantilly VA 20151
notes: HUGE aircraft hangar at Dulles Airport with Space Shuttle Discovery + SR-71 Blackbird + hundreds of aircraft. FREE (parking $20). Serge is going to wander around here for hours. Absolute must!

name: United States Holocaust Memorial Museum
address: 100 Raoul Wallenberg Pl SW Washington DC 20024
notes: Poignant and necessary museum. FREE, but timed entry recommended. Emotionally heavy but of great importance. As Belgians with a history of war, this is a special visit.

name: US Capitol & Rotunda Tour
notes: Free tours of the Capitol via online reservation. Impressive Rotunda + National Statuary Hall. Historical weight palpable like never before in recent years. FREE.

name: Washington Monument
notes: 169m tall obelisk with elevator to the top and panorama over all of DC. FREE but tickets REQUIRED via recreation.gov - book in advance. Lines can be long.

name: White House Visitors Center
notes: An interior visit to the White House requires an invitation via a Congressman – not realistic. The Visitors Center (FREE) provides a good impression nonetheless. You can always photograph the exterior from the street.

name: 🏨 Everglades International Hostel
notes: Quirky bohemian hostel near the Everglades NP gate - bursting with character! Tropical garden, hammocks, canoe rentals, alligator spotting nearby. Perfect base for the Everglades + Florida Keys. Dorms or private rooms. Approx. $50-80/night. Bohemian atmosphere.

name: 🏨 Hawk's Cay Resort - Duck Key
address: 61 Hawks Cay Blvd, Duck Key, FL 33050
notes: Resort on a private island in the middle of the Florida Keys! MM 61. Private lagoon, dolphin program, water sports, 5 restaurants. PERFECT end to the road trip before Malta. Duck Key = between Marathon and Key West. Slightly over budget but worth it for the grand finale. Approx. $200-300/night.

name: Aardwolf Brewing Company
notes: Jacksonville's hippest brewery in a historic railway ice house with a large outdoor beer garden. Specializing in IPAs, barrel-aged stouts, and sours; one of the most acclaimed taprooms in North FL. Combine with a visit to Ripley's in St. Augustine, a 45-minute drive away.

name: African Queen boottour
address: Key Largo Harbor, Key Largo, FL 33037
notes: Cruise on the original steamship from the film 'The African Queen' (1951, Humphrey Bogart and Katharine Hepburn). The ship traveled the world before ending up in Key Largo. Cruises through the canals of Port Largo. Film history and Florida Keys atmosphere in one bizarre combination. Book online in advance.

name: African Queen boottour Key Largo
address: Key Largo Holiday Inn Marina, Key Largo, FL 33037
notes: A trip on the REAL African Queen from the famous 1951 film starring Humphrey Bogart and Katharine Hepburn. The steamboat has been restored and still sails through the Key Largo canals. ~$65 p.p. for a 1-hour tour. Perfect vlog content: 'We are sailing on Bogart's movie boat.' Combine with Pennekamp snorkeling.

name: Airboat in de Everglades (Black Hammock)
address: 2356 Black Hammock Fish Camp Rd, Oviedo, FL 32765
notes: Wilder and cheaper than the Everglades tours near Miami: small private boats sailing deep into Lake Jesup, one of the most densely populated alligator areas in the US. Hundreds of alligators guaranteed. Also known as the starting point for bioluminescent kayaking in summer. Combine with Gatorland, 30 minutes away, for a complete gator day. Airboat entrance ~$30 p.p.

name: American Victory Ship Museum
notes: One of only four fully operational WWII ships in the US — 9 decks to explore without restriction. Crawl through engine rooms, sleeping quarters, radio rooms, and captain's quarters of a ship that saw three wars. Admission ~$15 p.p. Combine with Ybor City and Cigar City Brewing for a complete Tampa waterfront day.

name: Ancient City Brewing
address: 10 E Bay St, St. Augustine, FL 32084
notes: Authentic craft brewery in the heart of the oldest town in the US, also featuring a taproom at 16 State Road. Castillo Coconut Porter and Orange Amber Ale are local classics; found in 200+ restaurants in North FL. Logically, combine this with Ripley's and Potter's Wax Museum on the same St. Augustine Day.

name: Apalachicola Oesterdorp
notes: The most charming coastal village in the Florida Panhandle, responsible for 90% of all oysters in Florida. Every restaurant serves the freshest oysters straight from the bay; Tamara's Café and Boss Oyster are legendary. Combine with Florida Caverns, 45 minutes away, and the John Gorrie air conditioning museum in the middle of the village.

name: Aquatica Orlando (waterpark)
notes: SeaWorld's water park with 40+ slides, a lazy river, and a unique slide through a dolphin tank. Covered by the SeaWorld Fun Card (~$150 with FL ID) — pay once, unlimited access for the entire year. Combine with SeaWorld Orlando on the same site. Ideal for warm Florida weather (Feb-Nov).

name: Bahia Honda State Park
address: 36850 Overseas Hwy, Big Pine Key, FL 33043
notes: Consistently voted the most beautiful beach in Florida and one of the most beautiful in the US. Snorkeling, kayaking, remnants of the original Overseas Railway bridge, and stunning sunsets. Park entrance ~$8 p.p. (America the Beautiful pass). Camping available, but waiting lists of months. Midway to the Keys, an ideal rest stop.

name: Barrel of Monks Brewing
address: 1141 N Federal Hwy, Boca Raton, FL 33432
notes: For two Belgians, it is almost a religious obligation: Barrel of Monks brews authentic Belgian beer styles in Florida. Wheat beer, dubbel, tripel, and experimental Belgian creations — taken impressively seriously. Open Tue-Sun; a tasting flight is recommended. Combine with Sunsport Gardens for an absurd but delightful day.

name: Big Betsy the Lobster
notes: A 9-meter-high lobster sculpture marks the Rain Barrel Artisan Village in the Upper Keys. Stroll past local artists, galleries, and souvenirs — free admission. Perfect photo stop on the way to Key West; combine with Islamorada Brewery nearby.

name: Bioluminescent Kayak Tour (Space Coast)
notes: Kayaking on a dark evening in the shallow waters of Merritt Island: every paddle movement illuminates the water in neon blue due to bioluminescent plankton. One of Florida's most magical experiences — it looks like swimming in a Milky Way. Best season: May through October. Tour ~$55 p.p. Combine with Kennedy Space Center the following morning.

name: Blue Heaven
notes: An absolute Key West legend: an open-air café with chickens roaming free and a hippie vibe that works flawlessly. Ernest Hemingway once boxed in the courtyard. Breakfast and brunch are must-dos; guaranteed to wait a long time. Combine Big Betsy the lobster at Islamorada and Coral Castle on the way back.

name: Bob's Balloons (heteluchtballon)
notes: Magical sunrise flight over Central Florida up to 300 m high — spectacular vlog content guaranteed. Approximately 1 hour in the air, followed by a champagne toast. ~$175-200 p.p. Early rise required. Combine with a day at Cypress Cove nudist resort or Gatorland on the same day.

name: Bok Tower Gardens Singing Tower
notes: A Neo-Gothic carillon tower on Florida's highest hill — daily concert at 3 pm with bells weighing up to 3 tons. Beautiful botanical gardens with Mediterranean plants you wouldn't expect in Florida. Picturesque and totally different. Combine with Spook Hill, a 10-minute drive away, for a full 'Lake Wales weirdness' afternoon.

name: Busch Gardens Adventure Island Tampa
notes: Busch Gardens' Tampa water park with 30-meter-high slides, a lazy river, and a large wave pool. Covered by the Busch Gardens Fun Card (~$90 with FL ID), which also covers Busch Gardens itself. Season April through September; next to Busch Gardens Tampa for an easy day combination.

name: Busch Gardens Tampa
notes: African-themed park with wild roller coasters (Cheetah Hunt, Tigris, Iron Gwazi), safari animal experiences, and live shows. Included in the same SeaWorld Fun Card as SeaWorld Orlando — duo deal with Florida ID. Combine with Cigar City Brewing 10 min away and Lake Como naturist resort 30 min away.

name: Caliente Club & Resorts
notes: Florida's largest and most impressive lifestyle/swingers resort on 125 acres near Tampa. Caribbean feel: lagoon pools, waterfalls, 3 poolside bars, 2 restaurants, and day passes available. Be warned: more swinger-oriented than naturist-oriented. Lake Como is the better naturist alternative nearby.

name: Chihuly Collection - Morean Arts Center
notes: The permanent Chihuly Collection in St. Pete displays gigantic glass artworks by Dale Chihuly in a specially designed space. Combine it with the Salvador Dalí Museum on the same day, a 1 km walk away — a perfect double art day that is hallucinatory in a good way. Admission ~$16 p.p. St. Pete also has a great brewery scene for the evening.

name: Cigar City Brewing
notes: Tampa's flagship brewery — the Jai Alai IPA and Maduro Brown Ale are internationally famous. Taproom with tours Wed-Sun; flights available. The surrounding Ybor City area is also worth a visit. Perfect stop after Busch Gardens or as the start of a Tampa brewery crawl towards Lake Como.

name: Citrus Tower Clermont
notes: A 69-meter-high observation tower from 1956, built to show visitors Florida's endless orange groves. Ironically, the orange plantations have long since disappeared — now you look out over new buildings and Disney hotels on the horizon. Great kitsch value for $5 admission. Combine with Spook Hill and Gatorland for a Central Florida road kitsch day.

name: Clearwater Marine Aquarium
notes: Most famous for Winter, the dolphin with a prosthetic tail who inspired the movie 'Dolphin Tale'. A real rehabilitation center that rehabilitates injured marine animals — no shows, but authentic repair work. Admission ~$28 p.p. Clearwater Beach is right next door for Florida's most beautiful city beach.

name: Coral Castle
notes: Mysterious stone castle, built single-handedly by the 45 kg Edward Leedskalnin over 28 years. Coral stone blocks up to 30 tons — how he did that without machines continues to amaze engineers to this day. Admission ~$18 p.p., open daily. Combine with the Florida Keys route or El Carajo in Miami.

name: Cypress Cove Nudist Resort
notes: Florida's most famous AANR-certified naturist resort on 300 acres near Kissimmee, 20 minutes from Disney World. Two heated pools, restaurant, bar, kayaks on a private lake, tennis, pickleball, and camping sites. Discount for AANR members. Ideal base combining theme parks and a naturist experience.

name: De Leon Springs State Park (Old Sugar Mill Pancakes)
address: 601 Ponce de Leon Blvd, De Leon Springs, FL 32130
notes: Crystal-clear spring water (22°C all year round) for swimming and snorkeling, surrounded by ancient cypress trees. The famous Old Sugar Mill Pancake House is located *inside* the State Park — bake your own pancakes at the table for breakfast. Free park entry with the America the Beautiful pass. Combine with Ocala NF and Sunny Sands naturist resort.

name: Dinosaur World
address: 5145 Harvey Tew Rd, Plant City, FL 33565
notes: 150+ life-sized dinosaurs hidden among moss-covered Florida forest — T-Rexes peeking through the treetops. Fossil excavation site where visitors can dig themselves. Admission ~$16 p.p. Ideal stop on I-4 between Tampa and Orlando; combine with Spook Hill and Cigar City Brewing.

name: Discovery Cove
notes: All-inclusive day ticket (including all meals and snacks) for swimming with dolphins, snorkeling on a coral reef, and roaming freely with exotic birds and monkeys. Maximum of 1,300 visitors per day — never crowded. FL residents get up to a 20% discount. A little apart from the big parks and spectacular vlog content. One day is enough, but don't forget to book.

name: Don Garlits Museum of Drag Racing
notes: The most complete collection of drag racing vehicles in the world, built by 'Big Daddy' Don Garlits — the father of drag racing. From early street cars from the 1950s to modern Top Fuel dragsters that go faster than 500 km/h in 3 seconds. Admission ~$15 p.p. Serge will want to stay here for hours. Close to Ocala NF for camping afterwards.

name: Dry Tortugas National Park
notes: A remote island 110 km from Key West accessible by high-speed ferry or seaplane — no car traffic, dark starry skies. Fort Jefferson: an impressive hexagonal brick fort in the middle of the sea, plus exceptionally clear snorkeling water. Ferry service ~$185-200 p.p. return; seaplane ~$350+. America the Beautiful pass for park entry. Book early.

name: Dry Tortugas NP (seaplane)
address: 3471 S Roosevelt Blvd, Key West, FL 33040
notes: 70 miles off the coast of Key West: a lonely hexagonal Civil War fort in the middle of turquoise waters — accessible only by seaplane or ferry. The National Park Service protects pristine coral reefs and one of the largest colonies of seabirds in the world. Seaplane return ~$350 pp; ferry ~$180 pp (3.5h). Seaplane is, however, the most epic option for the vlog.

name: Dunedin (Schotse whisky & bierstadtje)
notes: Florida's most Scottish town descends from Scottish pioneers and celebrated that with a handful of craft breweries. Dunedin Brewery is the oldest in Hillsborough/Pinellas County; 7venth Sun Brewery nearby is known for innovative beers. Combine the 'Dunedin Brewery Crawl': 5+ taprooms within walking distance. Close to Clearwater Beach for a perfect combination day.

name: Edison & Ford Winter Estates Fort Myers
notes: The adjacent winter villas of Thomas Edison and Henry Ford in Fort Myers, including Edison's workshop and a huge botanical garden. Edison's laboratory has been preserved exactly as he left it — a perfect time capsule spot. Admission ~$25 p.p. Combine with The Bubble Room restaurant on Captiva Island, a 45-minute drive away.

name: El Carajo (tapas in benzinestation)
notes: Authentic Spanish tapas restaurant and wine bar tucked away in the back of an ordinary Shell garage in Miami. Jamón ibérico, queso manchego, and wine bottles to choose from straight off the shelves — run by a Spanish family. Absolutely one of the most quirky yet delicious dining spots in the US. Combine with Haulover Beach and Coral Castle.

name: Everglades Airboat Tour
notes: Zipping through the shallow Everglades swamps on an airboat while alligators move aside. Wildlife spotting: herons, turtles, manatees — and Florida Panthers if you're lucky. Combine with the Skunk Ape Research HQ on the Tamiami Trail and Coral Castle on the way back.

name: Florida Caverns State Park
notes: The only Florida State Park with accessible, dry caves filled with stalactites, stalagmites, and dripstone formations. Guided cave tours ~$5 p.p. (in addition to park entrance ~$5). America the Beautiful pass valid. Combine with Possum Monument in Wausau and Torreya State Park for a full Panhandle day out.

name: Florida Keys Wild Bird Rehabilitation Center
notes: A free bird rehabilitation center in the Upper Keys where pelicans, herons, and birds of prey can be admired on a beautiful boardwalk. Temporary home for injured birds — some have become permanent residents. Moving and photogenic. Free (donations appreciated). Combine with Pennekamp and the African Queen in Key Largo.

name: Fort Zachary Taylor Historic State Park
address: 601 Howard England Way, Key West, FL 33040
notes: National Historic Landmark: an imposing Civil War-era fort with the largest known collection of Civil War cannons. The fort is located on Key West's most beautiful beach — snorkeling, picnicking, and history all in one. Admission ~$6 p.p. (America the Beautiful pass). Guided tours daily at 12 p.m. and 2 p.m.

name: Fun Spot America Orlando
notes: Old-fashioned American amusement park with go-karts on 4 multi-level tracks, roller coasters, and an arcade — no reservation needed. Wristband for unlimited riding ~$35-45. FL residents get a discount via the Fun Spot app. Perfect as an alternative to the mega-parks — more relaxed, cheaper, and spontaneous to visit.

name: Funky Buddha Brewery
notes: Renowned brewery near Fort Lauderdale, famous for culinary beer creations. Maple Bacon Coffee Porter and Peanut Butter & Jelly Brown Ale are literally legendary in the craft beer world. Huge taproom, tours on weekdays. Combine with Mai-Kai and Funky Buddha for a full FL evening.

name: Gatorland
address: 14501 S Orange Blossom Trail, Orlando, FL 32837
notes: Florida's original crocodile park from 1949 with hundreds of alligators, a signature alligator mouth entrance, and a 7-story high zipline right over a crocodile pit. Much more original and affordable than the big theme parks. Admission ~$30 p.p. Combine with Cypress Cove naturist resort, 20 minutes away, for a complete Orlando day out.

name: Gibsonton Showmen's Museum
notes: For decades, Gibsonton was the winter quarters for circus artists and freak show performers. This unique museum preserves that strange history with vintage carnival rides and sideshow banners. Absolutely unknown to the average tourist. Close to Tampa; combine with Busch Gardens or Cigar City.

name: Haulover Beach Park (naturistenstrand)
notes: The most famous public nudist beach in the US — officially clothing-optional, completely legal, and well-guarded. Free beach, only parking costs ~$5. Popular with locals and tourists from all over the world. Combine with Coral Castle, El Carajo, or the Wreck Bar for an unforgettable Miami day.

name: Hemingway Home & Museum
notes: The Spanish Colonial house where Ernest Hemingway lived and worked from 1931–1940 — including the descendants of his famous six-toed cats. ~60 six-toed cats roam freely as guardians of the house; the property is recognized as an official museum. Admission ~$16 p.p. Combine with the Key West Lighthouse Museum, a 2-minute walk away.

name: History Miami Museum
notes: 10,000 years of South Florida history in downtown Miami, from prehistoric Tequesta cultures to the Cuban Exodus and the Art Deco explosion. 37,000 3D artifacts and rotating exhibitions; one of the best regional history museums in the US. Admission ~$10 p.p. Combine with Wynwood Walls and El Carajo for a full cultural day in Miami.

name: History of Diving Museum
notes: The largest collection of diving helmets, armored suits, and underwater equipment in the world — collected over 40 years by Doctor Joe and Sally Bauer. From medieval diving bells to modern rebreathers: the complete evolution of diving in one fantastic museum. Combine with feeding Robbie's tarpons nearby for a complete Islamorada afternoon.

name: Homosassa Springs Wildlife State Park
notes: The only park in Florida where you can view manatees year-round through an underwater observation window — no neoprene wetsuit needed. Also home to Louisiana Lu, a hippopotamus who was once made an 'honorary citizen of Florida'. Admission ~$15 p.p. (America the Beautiful pass). Combine with Weeki Wachee mermaids, 30 min away.

name: Islamorada Brewery & Distillery
notes: The leading Keys brewery with Florida Keys-inspired beers: Iguana Bait IPA, Islander Lager, and seasonal beers. Relaxed waterfront taproom with a mangrove view; also their own rum and whiskey. Combine with feeding Robbie's tarpons and Big Betsy the lobster for a complete Islamorada afternoon.

name: John Gorrie Museum (airco-uitvinder)
notes: A museum dedicated to the inventor of air conditioning and artificial ice, a Florida native who literally made the world more pleasant. Irony: the museum is located in one of Florida's most remote coastal towns, Apalachicola. Admission is only ~$2. Perfect as a bizarre cultural stop on the way to St. George Island. 'Without this man, Florida would not be habitable.'

name: John Pennekamp Coral Reef State Park
notes: America's first underwater park featuring the famous 'Christ of the Abyss' underwater statue at a depth of 8 meters. Snorkel boat tours (~$30 p.p.) and glass-bottom boat tours over the US continental coral reef. Combine with the History of Diving Museum, a 5-minute drive away. Best visibility Nov-April.

name: Jules' Undersea Lodge
notes: The world's only underwater hotel: scuba dive to your room 6 meters below the water surface in a Key Largo Lagoon. Overnight stay ~$700-900 pp — includes unlimited diving in the lagoon. Day visits (3 hours) also possible for ~$125. An absolute once-in-a-lifetime experience and unforgettable vlog content. Book well in advance — always fully booked.

name: Jungle Adventures & Swampy the Giant Alligator
notes: Swampy is a 60-meter-long cartoon alligator that serves as both a building and a roadside icon in the village of Christmas (FL). Jungle Adventures Wildlife Park also features live gators, Florida animals, and shows. The village of Christmas sends letters with a Christmas postmark for the holidays. Combine with Black Hammock Adventures and a visit to the village of Christmas on December 25.

name: Kennedy Space Center
address: Space Commerce Way, Merritt Island, FL 32953
notes: Space Shuttle Atlantis, Saturn V rocket, astronaut lunch, and the chance to attend live rocket launches. A full day is actually not enough. Admission ~$75 p.p. Space enthusiast's heaven on earth. Combine with the Valiant Air Command Warbird Museum in Titusville and a tandem jump over the Space Coast.

name: Kermit's Key West Key Lime Shoppe
notes: The best Key lime pie in Key West: frozen on a stick, dipped in Belgian chocolate — a combination Serge and Els want to make you feel at home. Dozens of Key lime variations: pie, candy, butter, perfume. Free tasting at the bar. A must-see in Key West. Combine with a Duval Street walk and Mallory Square.

name: Key West Butterfly & Nature Conservatory
notes: Beautiful glass greenhouse filled with 60+ species of butterflies and 20 species of exotic birds from around the world. Butterflies literally land on your shoulder — a soothing oasis in the bustling center of Key West. Admission ~$15 p.p. Perfect stopover between the historic center and Mallory Square.

name: Key West Conch Train Tour
notes: An absurd tourist train shaped like a conch shell that takes you through the entire Key West in 1.5 hours. Kitsch but efficient: all the sights, funny commentary, and the ideal way to decide where you want to return. Admission ~$35 p.p. Perfect first stop upon arrival in Key West to understand the lay of the land.

name: Key West Lighthouse Museum
notes: Climb 88 steps for a 360° panorama of Key West and the surrounding turquoise water. The lighthouse keeper's cottage has been converted into a museum featuring an authentic 19th-century living environment. Admission ~$12 p.p. A 2-minute walk from Hemingway House — a logical combination for a half-afternoon.

name: Kissimmee Prairie Preserve (dark sky park)
notes: Florida's only certified International Dark Sky Park — special telescope pads with a red-light-only policy. Milky Way visible to the naked eye; water and electrical hookups at campgrounds (~$18-25/night). Book at reserve.floridastateparks.org. Ideal Oct-March for clear stargazing.

name: Lake Como Family Nudist Resort
notes: One of the most popular naturist resorts in North America on 200 acres near Tampa, AANR certified. Golf course, petanque courts (!!), tennis, café, and campgrounds with electricity on a 35-acre lake. The 'Bare Buns Café' and 'Butt Hutt' bar are iconic. Combine with Cigar City Brewing or Busch Gardens.

name: LEGOLAND Florida
address: One Legoland Way, Winter Haven, FL 33884
notes: 50+ attractions, shows, and the LEGO Ferrari Build & Race Experience — including a water park on the same grounds. FL resident discounts available; the atmosphere is cozier and more relaxed than the large Orlando parks. Not the trendiest park, but the LEGO Ferrari circuit and the miniature city of the USA are really worth a visit.

name: Lightner Museum St. Augustine
notes: The former Alcazar Hotel (1888, Flagler) now houses a bizarre collection of Victorian curiosities: stained glass, antique musical instruments, taxidermied animals, and Gilded Age showpieces. The building itself is almost more interesting than the collection — Spanish Renaissance Revival at its most extravagant. Combine with Ripley's and Potter's Wax Museum for a full day of strange St. Augustine.

name: Mai-Kai Restaurant & Polynesian Show
address: 3599 N Federal Hwy, Fort Lauderdale, FL 33308
notes: Reopened in 2024 after restoration: 60+ year old Polynesian dinner show restaurant, voted best tiki bar in the US. Spectacular show, exotic tiki cocktails, and tropical decor that teleports you to Polynesia. Dinner + show ~$80-100 p.p. Combine with Funky Buddha Brewery and the Wreck Bar for a full FTL evening.

name: Mallory Square Sunset Celebration
notes: Every evening, 2 hours before sunset, Mallory Square erupts like a street carnival: fire-eaters, acrobats, magicians, and musicians. A Key West ritual for over 50 years — collective applause at sunset is mandatory. Free admission; combine with a cocktail on the waterfront at Sloppy Joe's Bar, a 5-minute walk away.

name: Medieval Times Dinner & Tournament
address: 4510 W Irlo Bronson Memorial Hwy, Kissimmee, FL 34746
notes: Knight tournament with real horses, lances, and swords while you eat a medieval feast with your hands. Admission including dinner ~$65 p.p.; Florida resident discount available. 2-hour show, for all audiences. Sounds like a tourist trap but works surprisingly well for an evening. Combine with Cypress Cove, 20 min away.

name: Mel Fisher Maritime Museum
notes: The story of Mel Fisher, the tenacious treasure hunter who searched for 16 years for the Spanish galleon treasures of the Atocha (found 1985: $400 million). Original gold bars, emeralds, and 8-dollar silver pieces are tangibly present — not behind glass, but held in your hands on certain tours. One of Key West's most fascinating museums. Combine with Hemingway House and Mallory Square.

name: Morse Museum (Tiffany-glas)
address: 445 N Park Ave, Winter Park, FL 32789
notes: The LARGEST collection of Louis Comfort Tiffany glasswork in the world — lamps, jewelry, chapels, and breathtaking stained glass. Highlight: the fully restored Tiffany Chapel from the 1893 World's Fair in Chicago. Admission only ~$6 p.p. — incredible value for money. Winter Park is also simply a charming town to stroll through.

name: Museum of Science & History Jacksonville
notes: Jacksonville's most visited museum featuring the Bryan-Gooding Planetarium and rotating science exhibits. Interactive body and energy exhibits, local and regional history, and special temporary exhibitions. Admission ~$18 p.p. Combine with Aardwolf Brewing for a Jacksonville culture day.

name: National Comedy Hall of Fame
address: 4500 US Hwy 19, New Port Richey, FL 34652
notes: The only museum in the world dedicated to the art of comedy: from Charlie Chaplin to Jerry Seinfeld, and from stand-up legends to slapstick masters. Interactive funny installations, memorabilia, and a theater for live performances. Combine with a visit to Weeki Wachee Springs, a 30-minute drive away.

name: National Naval Aviation Museum
notes: Third-largest aviation museum in the world and completely FREE — 150+ historic aircraft. On Tuesdays and Wednesdays (March through November), the Blue Angels train here just 50 cm apart. Highly recommended for Serge. Combine with the Air Force Armament Museum at Eglin AFB, 1 hour away.

name: No Name Pub
address: 30813 Watson Blvd, Big Pine Key, FL 33043
notes: Legendary bar in the middle of nowhere on Big Pine Key, covered from floor to ceiling with banknotes from 160+ countries. Best pizza in the Keys and the most authentic locals-only atmosphere you can find in the tourist area. Combine this with spotting the cute miniature Key deer that roam free on Big Pine Key.

name: Ocala National Forest (dispersed camping)
address: Hopkins Prairie, Ocala National Forest, FL 32702
notes: Florida's largest national forest allows primitive camping outside official zones — pitch your tent next to the F-150 along quiet forest trails. Recognized dark sky site with astronomy observation platforms at Hopkins Prairie. No reservation needed for dispersed camping. Combine with Silver Glen Springs for crystal-blue spring water.

name: Ochlockonee River State Park (camping)
notes: Remote campground in the Panhandle, buffered by Apalachicola National Forest — minimal light pollution for stargazing. 30 campsites with 50-amp hook-ups, perfect for the F-150 tent setup. Camping ~$18-25/night. Combine with the World's Smallest Police Station in Carrabelle, 40 min away.

name: Orlando Slingshot & Starflyer (I-Drive)
notes: The HIGHEST slingshot ride in the world (91 m) catapults you vertically upwards in an open cage. Right next to the 137 m high Starflyer swing chair — together the most extreme combination on I-Drive. Each ~$35 p.p. Evening line with a view of illuminated Orlando is the premium option. Short line, fast experience.

name: Overseas Highway (Florida Keys Scenic Drive)
address: US-1, Key Largo to Key West, FL
notes: 113 miles across 42 islands via 42 bridges over turquoise water — one of the most photogenic routes in the US. Highlight: the 7 Mile Bridge with panoramic views in all directions. Combine with Big Betsy, Blue Heaven, and Coral Castle. Free driving; America the Beautiful pass valid for State Parks along the way.

name: Pirate's Dinner Adventure Orlando
notes: Dinner and show on a replica of an 18th-century pirate schooner in a covered lagoon — with real sword fights, pyrotechnics, and cannonballs. Admission ~$70 p.p. including meal. More grown-up and crazier than Medieval Times. On International Drive, easily combined with WonderWorks and the Orlando Slingshot.

name: Ponce de León Inlet Lighthouse
address: 4931 S Peninsula Dr, Ponce Inlet, FL 32127
notes: Florida's tallest lighthouse (52m) and one of the most beautiful in the US — fully restored with the original Fresnel lens still present. The climb (203 steps) rewards with spectacular views of the Atlantic coast and Daytona Beach. Admission ~$7 p.p. Combine with a visit to Daytona Beach and the nearby Daytona International Speedway.

name: Possum Monument Wausau
notes: Florida's most absurd monument: a memorial to the opossum as a 'beautiful relic of the marsupial family.' Every year in August, the Possum Festival takes place in this remote Panhandle village. Completely free — an absolute must for road trippers with a sense of absurd humor.

name: Potter's Wax Museum St. Augustine
notes: America's very first wax museum (1948!), featuring over 160 lifelike figures in a historic building. From Napoleon to modern celebrities — the quality of the figures is remarkably good. Combine with Ripley's on the same day for a complete 'bizarre St. Augustine' program.

name: Ripley's Believe It or Not! St. Augustine
address: 19 San Marco Ave, St. Augustine, FL 32084
notes: The original Ripley's Museum in a Moorish-Renaissance mansion in the oldest town in the US. Over 800 bizarre artifacts: real severed heads, a matchstick Tower of London, vampire hunting kits. Combine with Ancient City Brewing and the photogenic historic center of St. Augustine.

name: Robbie's of Islamorada (tarpons voeren)
notes: Buy a bucket of fish and throw them at the jetty for a school of 100+ hungry tarpons — an absolutely unique Florida ritual. Tarpons are big, wild, and leap out of the water for the fish — spectacular vlog content! Free entry to the jetty; fish ~$5. Close to Big Betsy in Islamorada, ideal Keys combination.

name: Salvador Dali Museum
notes: The largest collection of Dali works outside Spain in a spectacular building with a double spiral ramp and glass geodesic dome. From early oil paintings to monumental surrealist masterpieces — including the gigantic 'Hallucinogenic Toreador'. Admission ~$24 p.p. Combine with the Chihuly Collection and the 3 Daughters Brewing taproom within walking distance in St. Pete.

name: Salvador Dalí Museum
notes: The largest Dalí collection outside Spain, housed in an architectural masterpiece featuring a spiral glass 'enigma' staircase. Original oil paintings of 'The Hallucinogenic Toreador' and 'Dalí's Dream of Venus'. Admission ~$25 p.p. A must-do in St. Pete. Combine with Cycle Brewing and 3 Daughters Brewing for a full day.

name: Satchel's Pizza
notes: Gainesville legend: pizzeria filled with recycled objects as art, live music, and a vintage 1960s Ford bus as a dining area. Homemade soft drinks, artisanal pizzas, and one of the most eccentric atmospheres in Florida. Combine with First Magnitude Brewing nearby and Silver Glen Springs in Ocala National Forest.

name: Seaside Seabird Sanctuary
notes: The largest wildlife bird rehabilitation center in the US with hundreds of seabirds recovering on the beach. Pelicans, cormorants, herons, and owls that you can view up close — completely free. Unique and moving; combine with the Dunedin Brewery route and a Clearwater Beach sunset.

name: SeaWorld Orlando
notes: Spectacular combination of animal park and theme park with roller coasters, dolphin and orca rides. SeaWorld Fun Card (~$150, requires FL ID) gives unlimited admission and covers Aquatica water park next door. The same pass also covers Busch Gardens Tampa. Plan both on separate days, using Cypress Cove as a base.

name: Secrets Hideaway Resort
notes: Florida's premier lifestyle/swingers resort near Orlando: clothing-optional pools, 4,000 sq ft play areas, Club Secret nightclub. Three bars and kitchen service until 2:00 AM. Rooms ~$125-200/night. Themed weekend parties year-round. Combine with Cypress Cove 15 mins away for an AANR naturist experience.

name: Seven Mile Bridge (wandelen)
notes: The historic Seven Mile Bridge (1912, Flaglers Railway) is now a walking and cycling path with spectacular 360° ocean views. It runs parallel to the new bridge — strange and majestic to stand on a bridge in the middle of the sea with water on all sides. Free admission; start at the Monroe County Sheriff's Department. Sunrise or sunset is magical.

name: Silver Glen Springs (neon-blauw bronwater)
notes: Crystal-blue spring water that looks so surreal you think you are in the Caribbean — right in Ocala National Forest. Swim and snorkel in fish-infested water at a constant 20°C. Limited visitors per day — book early. America the Beautiful pass grants access; use in addition to dispersed camping in Ocala NF.

name: Silver Glen Springs (Ocala)
notes: Crystal-clear spring water at a constant 22°C in Ocala National Forest, perfect for snorkeling with freshwater fish. One of the most photogenic spots in Florida: turquoise blue water surrounded by palm trees and white sand. Entrance ~$5 p.p. (America the Beautiful pass). Ideal day camper combo with dispersed camping in the forest.

name: Skunk Ape Research HQ
notes: Florida's stinking Bigfoot has its unofficial HQ deep in the Everglades. Plaster casts of footprints, blurry photos, live alligators, and passionate eyewitness accounts. A perfect mix of roadside kitsch and real Everglades wildlife. Combine with an airboat tour on the Tamiami Trail.

name: Skydive Space Center
notes: Skydiving over the Space Coast with a view of Kennedy Space Center during freefall — nowhere else in the world. Tandem jump from an altitude of ~4,200 m, ~$180-220 p.p. Book early; weekends fill up fast. Combine with Valiant Air Command Museum on the same grounds for an epic aviation day.

name: Sloppy Joe's Bar
notes: Hemingway's favorite bar opened in 1933 on the day Prohibition was lifted — live music 365 days a year from 9 a.m. The original Sloppy Joe sandwich (ground beef, onions, peppers) is a Key West classic you simply *must* try. Open all day and evening; combine with Mallory Square Sunset Celebration and Mel Fisher Museum.

name: Solomon's Castle
notes: A complete castle constructed from discarded newspaper aluminium printing plates by artist Howard Solomon. Inside: eccentric recycled objects as artwork, gallery space, and a 'boat in the canal' restaurant. Open Thu-Sun; make reservations for lunch. Absolutely original — Gaudí would have approved.

name: Spongeorama Sponge Museum
notes: Tarpon Springs is the 'sponge capital of the US' thanks to Greek divers who have been harvesting sponges here for over 100 years. Spongeorama tells this absurd story with diving demonstrations, the largest sponge collection in the world, and a film about the industry. Free or a small donation; the entire surrounding Greektown quarter is also great, with authentic Greek restaurants.

name: Spook Hill (optische illusie)
address: N Wales Dr & 5th St, Lake Wales, FL 33853
notes: Put your car in neutral and it seems to roll uphill — a classic optical illusion in Lake Wales. Free, accessible 24/7, and an absolute must for road trippers with a sense of absurdist humor. Combine with Bok Tower Gardens (5 min away) and Dinosaur World in Plant City (30 min away).

name: St. Augustine Lighthouse
notes: Climb the 219 steps of the black-and-white striped lighthouse for the best view of St. Augustine and the coast. The lighthouse keeper's cottage has been converted into a maritime museum featuring ship's logs and local history. Admission ~$15 p.p. St. Augustine is a must-stop anyway — do all the 'bizarre' in one day.

name: St. Augustine Old City Walls & Castillo
address: 1 S Castillo Dr, St. Augustine, FL 32084
notes: The oldest masonry fort in the US (1672) with walls of coquina stone that absorbed cannonballs instead of breaking. Live living history demonstrations with cannon shots at set times. America the Beautiful pass valid (free). Combine with Ripley's, Potter's, and Ancient City Brewing for a complete bizarre St. Augustine day.

name: St. Augustine Pirate Museum
address: 12 S Castillo Dr, St. Augustine, FL 32084
notes: 48 exhibition rooms about the Golden Age of Piracy with real artifacts — Blackbeard's blunderbuss, an authentic Jolly Roger flag, and the ONLY known authentic pirate treasure chest in the world. Admission ~$14 p.p. In the historic heart of St. Augustine, within walking distance of Ripley's and Potter's Wax Museum. Combine all three in one 'bizarre St. Augustine' day.

name: St. George Island SP (dark sky camping)
address: 1900 E Gulf Beach Dr, St. George Island, FL 32328
notes: Pristine barrier island in the Panhandle with 60 campsites with water and 50-amp electricity. Minimal light pollution = ideal for stargazing; beautiful white beach nearby. Camping costs ~$24/night + $7 utility costs. Combine with World's Smallest Police Station in Carrabelle, 30 min away.

name: Sun 'n Fun Aerospace Expo
notes: Second-largest aviation event in the world, every year in APRIL in Lakeland — 14-30 shows per day. Fireworks, parachute jumps, Blue Angels, and vintage aircraft over 6 days. Admission ~$50/day. April 2028 fits PERFECTLY into the road trip! Plan this carefully in your calendar.

name: Sunken Gardens St. Petersburg
notes: Florida's oldest roadside attraction from the 1930s: a sunken botanical garden filled with tropical plants, flamingos, and fan palms. Like a kind of private jungle in the middle of the city. Admission ~$15 p.p. Combine with the Dalí Museum, a 10-minute drive away, for a complete St. Petersburg culture day.

name: Sunny Sands Nudist Resort
notes: Small-scale, quiet AANR naturist resort on 42 acres in rural North Florida. Petanque courts and a 9-hole naked golf course — Serge will never want to play normal golf again. Less commercial than Cypress Cove, more of a community feel. Combine with Ocala NF for stargazing.

name: Sunsport Gardens Naturist Resort
notes: The most ethical naturist resort in South Florida, AANR certified, with jungle trails and ponds. Swimming pool, sauna, pétanque, tennis, and restaurant in an atmosphere preferred by serious naturists. Near Palm Beach. Combine with Haulover Beach and Barrel of Monks Brewing in Boca Raton.

name: Swamp Thing Airboat Everglades
notes: Lightning-fast airboat tours through the shallow Everglades swamps near Miami, with alligators within arm's reach. Shorter (30 min) and longer (1 h) tours; guide points out wildlife and talks about the ecosystem. ~$30-50 p.p. Ideal if you are in Miami anyway — 40 min from South Beach. Combine with Coral Castle.

name: Tarpon Springs (Griekse spons-duikers)
notes: The 'Greek capital of America': Greek sponge-diver families settled here in 1905, and the town has remained authentically Greek ever since. Boat tours depart for the sponge plantations; the Spongeorama museum tells the full story. Boat tour ~$10 p.p. Authentic Greek restaurants (Hellas, Costas) complete the day. Unique in the US.

name: The Bubble Room Restaurant
notes: On picturesque Captiva Island: every room has a different theme — vintage toys, Christmas lights, and oversized desserts. One of Florida's most iconic eccentric restaurants. Book well in advance. Island location via toll bridge (~$6). Combine with Fort Myers and the Sanibel Naturist Club.

name: The Ringling Museum (circus + kunst)
notes: The impressive complex of circus king John Ringling: a European art museum, two circus museums, his extravagant Ca' d'Zan villa, and beautiful Italian bay gardens. The circus museums showcase the full scale of the greatest touring show on earth — Belgian cardboard theater included as an atmosphere correction. Admission ~$25 p.p. Allow at least half a day. Combines perfectly with Sarasota's St. Armands Circle.

name: The Wreck Bar (zeemeerminnenshow)
notes: Drink while mermaids glide past large glass windows in the pool — a unique underwater bar experience. Family-friendly during the day, adults-only burlesque mermaid version on Friday and Saturday nights. Book window seats in advance. Combine with Mai-Kai for a bizarre but unforgettable Fort Lauderdale night.

name: Three Sisters Springs & Manatee Tour
address: 601 Three Sisters Springs Trail, Crystal River, FL 34428
notes: Swim alongside wild manatees in 22°C spring water — a unique wildlife experience only possible in Florida. Snorkeling tours depart from Kings Bay (Nov through March best season). Park entrance ~$5 (America the Beautiful pass). Combine with Weeki Wachee Springs, 30 min away.

name: Titanic Museum Orlando
notes: Immersive museum recreating parts of the ship: the Grand Staircase, a first-class cabin, and a 2-ton piece of the original hull. Every visitor receives a boarding pass from a real passenger and discovers at the end whether they survived. Option: 2-hour gala dinner in character. Surprisingly moving for a tourist strip attraction.

name: Torreya State Park (dark sky + steile ravijnen)
address: 2576 NW Torreya Park Rd, Bristol, FL 32321
notes: Florida's most unexpected landscape: steep canyons, hilly forest, and the rare Torreya tree — an Ice Age relic. One of the best stargazing locations in the Panhandle with 29 campgrounds with full hookups. Camping ~$16/night + $7 utility costs. Close to civilization (Bristol 14 km) but dark as night.

name: Truman Little White House
notes: Florida's only presidential museum: Harry Truman's winter residence from 1946–1952 — also used by Eisenhower, Kennedy, and Carter. Guided tours of the authentically furnished rooms showcase original furniture and personal memorabilia. Admission ~$22 p.p. Combine with Hemingway House, Mel Fisher Museum, and Mallory Square for a full Key West day.

name: Turtle Hospital Marathon
notes: The world's first certified sea turtle hospital — tours show the recovery process of injured turtles. Opportunity to guide released turtles back into the ocean. Hugely popular, book in advance! Combine with a walk across the historic Seven Mile Bridge, a 5-minute drive away.

name: Universal Epic Universe
notes: BRAND NEW park opens May 2025 — Universal's most ambitious creation ever with 5 fully immersive worlds. Super Nintendo World, Harry Potter Ministry of Magic, How to Train Your Dragon, Dark Universe (classic monsters), and Celestial Park. 50+ attractions including racing dueling coaster Stardust Racers. By 2028, the hype will have subsided slightly, but the park will be operating at full speed.

name: Universal Orlando Resort (FL Resident pass)
notes: Florida residents save ~$50 on multi-day tickets for Studios Florida + Islands of Adventure + Volcano Bay. Annual Power Pass (FL resident): cheaper and includes Epic Universe access in 2028. Combine with Epic Universe at the new South Campus — free bus connection between all parks.

name: Universal Studios Florida
notes: Harry Potter Diagon Alley, Simpsons Springfield, Fast & Furious, and Hollywood studio atmosphere. Florida Resident Annual Pass ~$17-30/month (no Epic Universe). 2-Park Annual Pass also covers Islands of Adventure. The most mature Universal park — fewer kids, more movie references. Butterbeer at The Leaky Cauldron is mandatory.

name: Valiant Air Command Warbird Museum
notes: Impressive collection of airworthy WWII aircraft at Space Coast Regional Airport. Annual airshow (Titusville Thunder, March) with real WWII flying demonstrations. Admission ~$20 p.p. Combine with Kennedy Space Center (30 min away) and Skydive Space Center at the same airport.

name: Wakulla Springs State Park
address: 550 Wakulla Park Dr, Wakulla Springs, FL 32327
notes: One of the world's largest and deepest freshwater springs — boat tours showcase alligators, giant mammoth bones on the bottom, and hundreds of songbirds. The historic Wakulla Lodge (1937) is a National Historic Landmark and a budget accommodation option on-site. Combine with Florida Caverns SP and Apalachicola NF for a complete Panhandle day.

name: Walt Disney World – Animal Kingdom
notes: Adventurous Disney park with Pandora (Avatar), real safari animals, and the insane Tron roller coaster. Florida resident ticket ~$65/day. Arrive early for Pandora: Flight of Passage — the line moves up quickly. Less crowded than Magic Kingdom but more impressive in terms of nature and animal park atmosphere.

name: Walt Disney World – EPCOT
notes: The most 'adult' Disney park: World Showcase with 11 country pavilions, including a Belgium-style European village and the Guardians of the Galaxy roller coaster. Florida resident ticket ~$65/day. The food and drink tour around the world is the highlight. Combine with Magic Kingdom at the same resort with a multi-day Florida resident ticket.

name: Walt Disney World – Hollywood Studios
notes: Star Wars: Galaxy's Edge (including Millennium Falcon controls), Toy Story Land, and a Twilight Zone Tower of Terror. Florida resident ticket ~$65/day. Rise of the Resistance is Disney's best park attraction. Combine all 4 Disney parks in one week with a multi-day Florida resident ticket (~$55-70/day).

name: Walt Disney World – Magic Kingdom
notes: The classic Disney park with Cinderella Castle, Pirates of the Caribbean, and Space Mountain. Florida resident ticket ~$65/day (Summer Magic Ticket, proof of FL address required). Jan, Feb, and Sep are the quietest months — short lines and pleasant weather. Combine with EPCOT on a separate day.

name: Walt Disney World (FL Resident tickets)
address: Walt Disney World Resort, Orlando, FL 32830
notes: As a Florida resident, you get substantial discounts: 2-day tickets starting at ~$99 pp, 4-day summer passes at ~$59/day. Magic Kingdom, EPCOT, Hollywood Studios, and Animal Kingdom — each park deserves a separate day. Not the cheapest option, but truly worth it as a Florida resident. Book well in advance for reservations.

name: Weeki Wachee Springs (zeemeerminnen)
notes: Live mermaid show in an underwater theater since 1947 — a Florida icon you won't see anywhere else. Actresses in mermaid costumes swim and perform shows in front of large glass windows in crystal-clear spring water. Combine with the on-site Buccaneer Bay water park and Lake Como nudist resort 30 min away.

name: Wizard of Oz Museum Cape Canaveral
address: 7099 N Atlantic Ave, Cape Canaveral, FL 32920
notes: 46 display cases filled with chronologically sorted Wizard of Oz memorabilia from 1939 to the present — dolls, games, masks, and props. Weird but fascinating; combined with a Van Gogh immersive experience in the same building. Admission ~$12 p.p. Perfect bad-weather stop if you have Kennedy Space Center on your agenda.

name: WonderWorks Orlando (omgekeerd gebouw)
notes: A building that literally stands upside down — and inside 100+ interactive science exhibits, an indoor ropes course, and an earthquake simulator. Admission ~$30 p.p.; Florida resident discount available. Less crowded than large parks, a half-day is ideal. On International Drive, easy to combine with ICON Park and WonderWorks on the same evening.

name: World Erotic Art Museum Miami Beach
notes: The largest erotic art museum in the world: 4,000 years of human sexuality in art, from Pre-Columbian to contemporary.
