A 1-ton bed engraved with the Kama Sutra, dominatrix Barbie dolls, and art ranging from ancient Greek vases to modern photography. 18+ (ID required), admission ~$16 p.p. Surprisingly respectful and historically curated. Combine with Haulover Beach.

name: World's Smallest Police Station
notes: An ordinary phone booth on a street corner in Carrabelle that officially serves as a police station. Free roadside curiosity, perfect photo stop on the Gulf Coast route to St. George Island. Combine with the St. George Island State Park campground, 30 minutes away.

name: Wynwood Walls
notes: The world's most famous street art museum: a fully open-air gallery in Miami's hip Wynwood neighborhood featuring murals by the world's best street artists. Admission tickets provide access to the courtyard; the outer streets are free and equally impressive. Courtyard entrance ~$12 p.p. Combine with the Museum of Graffiti and El Carajo for a complete Wynwood afternoon.

name: Ybor City Historic District
notes: Tampa's Cuban cigar district, once the cigar production capital of the US — now a vibrant entertainment district with brick architecture. Artisanal cigar rollers in historic shops, live music, tapas bars, and craft beer on 7th Avenue. Free to explore; combine with Cigar City Brewing and the Gibsonton Showmen's Museum near Tampa.

name: Amicalola Falls State Park
address: 240 Amicalola Falls State Park Rd, Dawsonville, GA 30534
notes: HIGHEST waterfall east of the Mississippi – 729 feet! Start of the Appalachian Trail (8 km from Springer Mountain). Choice: stairs up (600 steps!) or drive up. Zipline, archery, GPS scavenger hunts in the park. Recommended to stay overnight at the Lodge for misty mountain mornings.

name: Andersonville National Historic Site
notes: Infamous Civil War POW camp where 13,000 Union soldiers died. The only monument IN America to a WAR CRIMINAL (Commander Wirz). Next up the National POW Museum – oppressive and impressive at the same time. Combine with Pasaquan (1-hour drive) for a surreal day combo.

name: Atlanta Ghost Tour – Fox Theatre
notes: Fox Theatre from 1929 – Moorish fantasy architecture + officially maintained! Oakland Cemetery: Margaret Mitchell and Civil War generals. Nighttime walking tour through Midtown past hundreds of years of dark history. Ghosts of Atlanta tours available daily, rain or shine.

name: BabyLand General Hospital
notes: Birthplace of the Cabbage Patch Kids! 70,000 m² fake hospital where nurses 'give birth' to dolls. Magic Crystal Tree produces live babies for a cheering crowd. Daddy Serge: finally a birth where they don't kick you out ;) FREE admission. Original hand-sewn dolls for sale for hundreds of dollars.

name: Balloons Over Georgia
notes: Hot air balloon over North Georgia – see Lake Lanier, Stone Mountain AND the Atlanta skyline! Blue Ridge mountains also visible in clear weather. Sunrise flights – the most magical moment of the day. ~1 hour flight time. Perfect anniversary or birthday gift.

name: Bell Acres – Naturist Resort
notes: 113-acre naturist park 30 miles N of Athens. Nature trails, cabins, RV and tent sites along a stream. 52 electrical hook-ups. Saltwater pool. Managed by William & Gloria: 'We do this out of love.'

name: Blue Ridge Scenic Railway
notes: 26-mile vintage train ride through the Blue Ridge Mountains along the Toccoa River! Autumn color tours Sept-Nov: spectacular red-orange mountain colors. Open-air carriage or enclosed climate-controlled – choose your adventure. Perfectly combined with downtown Blue Ridge shopping afterwards.

name: Bonaventure Cemetery – Savannah
notes: One of the most beautiful and most photographed cemeteries in the world! Spanish moss hangs from centuries-old oaks above Victorian gravestones. Famous from John Berendt's 'Midnight in the Garden of Good and Evil'. Magical morning twilight photo opportunity.

name: Charlemagne's Kingdom – Helen
notes: Detailed miniature model railway theme park in a Bavarian-German fairytale village. Helen is already a bizarre fake German Alpine village in the middle of Georgia. Scenery recreates European train stations, mountain villages, and tunnels. Combine with the rest of Helen – it is a European bubble in the Peach State.

name: Chateau Elan Winery & Resort
notes: French château with 3,500 acres of vineyards 40 min N of Atlanta! 30+ award-winning wines – including local Muscadine grapes. European spa, 8 restaurants, 45-hole golf, tennis center. Wine tasting in a private bungalow above the vineyard is the ultimate Els date. Serge can view the motor car collection on the grounds. Win-win.

name: Chattooga River Rafting – Wildwater
notes: Class IV whitewater on the Chattooga – Mississippi’s only Wild & Scenic river with commercial rafting! The infamous 'Five Falls' section is pure adrenaline. Zipline, kayaking, and high ropes course available as well. The filming location of 'Deliverance' (1972) – squeal piggy squeal ;)

name: Cloudland Canyon State Park
address: 122 Cloudland Canyon Park Rd, Rising Fawn, GA 30738
notes: 300-meter-deep canyon with sandstone cliffs, caves, and waterfalls! Cherokee Falls and Hemlock Falls along the Waterfalls Trail. Mountain biking, camping, spectacular views. This is Georgia's best-kept secret for canyon lovers. Located close to Tennessee – combine with Chattanooga.

name: College Football Hall of Fame
notes: Even if you aren't an American Football fan – the technology is impressive! Personalize your visit to your favorite college team at the entrance. Interactive: try scoring a point or throwing a pass yourself. Georgia Bulldogs = home team. Enthusiasm is expected.

name: Cotton & Rye – Savannah
notes: Upscale Southern cuisine IN a renovated bank vault! Seasonal menu with a modern twist on Lowcountry classics. Booking a table in the vault is the most unique experience. Fried chicken with artisanal sauces, fresh seafood.

name: Creature Comforts Brewing – Athens
notes: Georgia's BEST brewery in a former car dealership!  Tropicalia IPA – Thor's choice of beer in Avengers: Endgame. Real.  Athens Beer Trail: multiple breweries, collect stamps, let someone else drive.  Program includes: Athens Beer Trail Trolley Tour on Thu and Fri.

name: Cumberland Island National Seashore
notes: Pristine island accessible only by ferry! Wild horses roam freely among Gilded Age ruins. Isolated beaches among the most beautiful on the Atlantic coast. Greyfield Inn for a glamping experience. Wild camping also possible. The Carnegie couple built mansions here – which are now in decay. Magnificent.

name: Delta Flight Museum – Atlanta
notes: VAN Delta Airlines Aviation History Museum, at the airport. Climb into a real Boeing 767 cockpit and 'fly' it. A fully restored Constellation propeller aircraft from the 1950s is on display. Combines well with departures or arrivals in Atlanta.

name: Doll's Head Trail
address: Constitution Lakes Park, 1305 McAuliffe Dr, Atlanta, GA 30316
notes: Local carpenter Joel Slaton created this creepy art trail. Visitors find trash along the path and contribute it. Doll heads dominate the installations. Every shape imaginable. 1.5 miles through a swamp forest in East Atlanta. FREE. Perfect photo location when life is running out.

name: Drive a Tank – Georgia
notes: DRIVE A REAL TANK over fake cars! Pay a fee, climb in, and turn metal into pancakes. Ox Ranch Texas is the big name, but Georgia has similar providers. Serge's dream. Els' nightmare. So go for it.

name: Elvis Wart Museum (Loudermilk)
notes: 30,000+ Elvis items including the highlight: a WRAT from Elvis Presley's wrist! Owner Joni Mabe bought it at an auction. Yes. Seriously. His severed toenail is also on display. Biggest shrine to The King outside Graceland. Belgian parallel: relic worship, but kitschier.

name: Expedition Bigfoot Museum
address: 4551 E Ellijay Rd, Cherry Log, GA 30522
notes: MOST LEGIT Bigfoot museum in the US! Nationally largest collection of Bigfoot artifacts. Includes the world's only Bigfoot buttock print. 4,000 m² full of evidence, dioramas, theater space. And no, Serge – they don't sell it as 'proof' but as 'evidence'. Big difference ;) Kids under 5 free, military personnel too.

name: Fernbank Museum of Natural History
notes: LARGEST dinosaur ever found: 37-meter Argentinosaurus in the Great Hall! 65 acres of ancient jungle with walking paths right next to the building. 4-story IMAX theater showing science films. 'Fernbank After Dark' – adult cocktail night every 2nd Friday of the month.

name: Finster Fest – Paradise Garden
notes: Annual festival in October at Howard Finster's Paradise Garden. 60+ folk art and craft stalls, 3 live music stages. Highlight of the outsider art world in Georgia. October matches the autumn colors in North Georgia.

name: GBI Crime Lab Museum
notes: Official Georgia Bureau of Investigation museum. Main attraction: a PEPPED-SERVed monkey from Mars (actually a missing toy monkey). Also a voodoo murder axe, a meth lab display, and an electric chair! FREE and realistically macabre. Serge is going to take 10 photos here.

name: Georgia Aquarium – Atlanta
notes: LARGEST aquarium in the world – whale sharks and beluga whales! Snorkeling with whale sharks bookable (extra cost). For Els: belugas. For Serge: diving experience with sharks. Combine with World of Coca-Cola next door. 15+ specialized exhibitions.

name: Ghost Tour Savannah
notes: MOST HANDLED CITY IN AMERICA – every stone has a story! Choose from a walking tour, pub crawl, trolley, or paranormal investigation. Hamilton-Turner Inn, Marshall House, and 17Hundred90 are highlights. Hoodoo Joe and Madam Redrum are the best guides – google them!

name: Goats on the Roof – Tiger
notes: Goats on a ROOF. This is Georgia's most literal name for an attraction. Petting zoo, ice cream, and cheesy souvenirs all in one. Norm Georgians: this is special. Norm Belgians: why is there a goat on the roof? Kids love it. Adults do too, but they won't admit it.

name: Hampton Inn Savannah Historic District
notes: Most budget-friendly option IN the historic district. Rooftop terrace and pool with river views. Walking distance from City Market, Riverboat cruises, and squares. Free breakfast every morning.

name: Helen Alpine Village
notes: A fake German village in the Blue Ridge Mountains of Georgia. Indeed. Transformed in 1969 from a dying little town into a Bavarian fairytale. Wooden clogs, bratwurst, Oktoberfest, and a real Bavarian brewery atmosphere. Funny: Serge and Els are from Belgium and are driving to a fake Germany in Georgia.

name: Hidden River Resort – St. George
notes: On the St. Marys River – right on the Florida-Georgia border! The 'most state park-like' naturist resort in the region. Campsites, jacuzzi, pool, rare river nature. Annual Nudie Blues music festival in April! Perfect stop if you are driving from Georgia to Florida as a Floridan.

name: Jekyll Island Club Resort
notes: Gilded Age resort frequented by Rockefellers, Vanderbilts, and Morgans! Victorian country house with separate 'cottages' belonging to the original millionaire families. Jekyll Island is 100% state-owned – so well preserved. Historic tours, crocodiles, turtles, and breathtaking beaches included.

name: Jimmy Carter Peanut Statue
notes: 13-foot-tall fiberglass grinning peanut based on Carter's smile. Made for his 1976 presidential campaign. Carter himself didn't think much of it. Combine with Jimmy Carter National Historic Site. Plains is a small town of 600 people with the most photographed peanut in the world.

name: Krog Street Tunnel – Street Art
notes: Legal graffiti tunnel that is constantly changing – never the same thing twice. Beloved wedding venue AND political manifesto at the same time. The entire Inman Park neighborhood is worth a walk.

name: Leopold's Ice Cream – Savannah
notes: Handmade ice cream since 1919 – truly LEGENDARY. Special flavors: Rum Bisque, Savannah Socialite (pecans + bourbon caramel). Jennifer Lopez and Tom Cruise have been here. Queue outside, but it is worth the wait. Sandwiches and pimento cheese are also available.

name: Lookout Mountain Flight Park
notes: The only location in Georgia for tandem gliding and paragliding! 20-mile long mountain ridge with thermal upwellings – ideal for soaring. Beginner training also available – learn it in a day! Combine with Cloudland Canyon 5 minutes away.

name: Martin Luther King Jr. National Historic Site
notes: MLK's birthplace, church, and grave – FREE by NPS. Ebenezer Baptist Church, where he preached, still stands here. Most important civil rights site in the US. Atlanta's Auburn Ave is historically America's wealthiest Black street.

name: Moon River Brewing – Savannah
notes: Oldest building in Savannah (1821!) – was first a hotel and post office. HANDLED! Appeared in Ghost Adventures and other shows. Beers with names like Yoga Pants and Swamp Fox. Add a comfort food menu – the grilled chicken sandwich is too good. Book a ghost tour after the beer? Perfect Savannah evening.

name: Mrs. Wilkes Dining Room
notes: Family-style Southern soul food at a long table with strangers! Rice, fried chicken, ham, biscuits, collard greens – all included. Since 1943. ALWAYS full. The line is part of the experience. Lunch only from 11am to 2pm. Closed Tuesdays. Like a Belgian peasant wedding, but with fried chicken.

name: Museum of Aviation
notes: Second largest Air Force museum in the entire US! Acres of outdoor exhibits + 4 gigantic hangars full of military aircraft. FREE MONEY. Open since 1984. Bombers, fighters, transport planes from WWII to the present.

name: National Infantry Museum – Columbus
notes: Second-largest Air Force museum in the US – AND it’s FREE! Acres of outdoor exhibits with real tanks, helicopters, and planes. 4 gigantic hangars full of military history. Combines well with Pasaquan in Buena Vista (40-minute drive).

name: Native Woods Naturist Park – Darien
notes: Small adults-only naturist park near I-95 between Savannah and Jacksonville. 8 RV sites, 1 cabin, tent sites, 28-foot saltwater pool. Convenient as a stopover between Savannah and Florida. Near Sapelo Island Research Reserve and Fort King George Historic Site.

name: Oakland Cemetery – Atlanta
notes: Victorian garden cemetery from 1850 in the heart of Atlanta. Margaret Mitchell, Maynard Jackson, and Bobby Jones are buried here. The Great Locomotive Chase saboteurs are reburied outside the walls. Guided tours year-round, Halloween 'Capturing the Spirit' tours SOLD OUT. FREE admission.

name: Okefenokee Swamp
notes: Largest blackwater swamp in North America – 700 km² of dark water. Boat trips past alligators, warblers, black bears, and carpets of water lilies. Paddington Beer isn't brewed here, but the bears look like this. Night camping on wooden platforms above the water is unrealistically magical. Els: beautiful nature. Serge: alligators close-up. Win-win.

name: Old Car City USA
notes: 34 ACROSS classic wrecks overgrown with kudzu and moss. 4,000+ vintage cars blending in with nature. Post-apocalyptic photo paradise – Instagram gold! Large-format printer art by the owner in the gift shop. Open Wed-Sat. Bring a serious camera!

name: Olde Pink House – Savannah
notes: 18th-century Pink Mansie – oldest restaurant in Savannah. Concise Lowcountry menu: fried green tomatoes, she-crab soup, crispy sole. Food & Wine's most romantic restaurants in America. Cellar tavern for a more casual atmosphere. Spirits included. Reservations highly recommended.

name: Original Crab Shack – Tybee Island
address: 40 Estill Hammock Rd, Tybee Island, GA 31328
notes: Historic fishing camp right on the water with wild crabs and shrimp. Lowcountry boil, deviled crab, and peel-and-eat shrimp under gnarled oaks. Crocodiles in a separate pond on the grounds. Really. Every few years, you spot a pirate for the annual Buccaneer Ball. Also appeared in TV series. Iconic Georgia address.

name: Paradise Garden (Howard Finster)
notes: Baptist minister Howard Finster created 47,000 works here. Mosaic walls, mirrored trees, bicycle tower art, and Bible verses everywhere. National top folk art attraction – just imagine: Belgian monuments, but made of plywood. Finster once created album covers for R.E.M. and Talking Heads! Airbnb on the premises available for true fans.

name: Paradise Valley Resort – Naturist
notes: Clothing-optional resort 1 hour northeast of Atlanta. 3 pools, indoor/outdoor jacuzzi, volleyball, walking trails, bar, restaurant. DJ every Friday and Saturday – party atmosphere! Condoms, motels, and RV spots available. Youngest membership of all Georgia naturist resorts. Chilled party vibe.

name: Pasaquan (St. EOM's Compound)
address: 238 Eddie Martin Rd, Buena Vista, GA 31803
notes: Eddie Martin (St. EOM) was visited by future beings and built this. 7-acre psychedelic temple complex with neon totem poles & Aztec murals. If Dr. Seuss had an LSD trip in a Mayan temple – this is the result. Funded his art with fortune-telling. Hats off. Managed by the Columbus Museum of Art.

name: Providence Canyon State Park
notes: Georgia's 'Little Grand Canyon' – 43 canyons in colored clay soil. Pink, orange, lilac, and cream-white colors – photogenic, insane colors! Entirely CAUSED by poor drainage practices in the 1800s. Hiking along colorful canyon walls.

name: Richard Russell Scenic Highway
notes: Most SPECTACULAR mountain drive in Georgia – seriously impressive! GA Hwy 348 winds through the Chattahoochee National Forest. Access to Anna Ruby Falls, Dukes Creek Falls, and other hidden waterfalls. Best autumn color driving route in North Georgia – late October is the sweet spot.

name: Rock City – Lookout Mountain
notes: Historic park on Lookout Mountain on the GA-TN border. 7 states visible in clear weather from one point! Fairyland Caverns: gnomes and fairies in the darkness illuminated by blacklight. Red barns with 'SEE ROCK CITY' are America's quintessential road trip marketing.

name: Rock City & Fairyland Caverns
notes: Historic park on Lookout Mountain on the GA-TN border. 7 states visible in clear weather from one point! Fairyland Caverns: gnomes and fairies in the darkness illuminated by blacklight. Red barns with 'SEE ROCK CITY' are America's quintessential road trip marketing. 1930s tourist trap that is still worth it.

name: Rock Garden – Calhoun
notes: 50 miniature buildings made of stone, shells, and porcelain fragments. Cinderella's castle, Notre-Dame, monasteries – all thumb-sized! Built by volunteers on the church grounds. FREE and open every day. Els: think Bruges in miniature. Serge: think Bruges, but funnier.

name: Savannah Historic District
notes: 22 historic squares covered in Spanish moss and oaks – ENCHANTING. First planned city of the New World (1733). Bonaventure Cemetery: one of the most beautiful cemeteries in the world. Open container legislation – stroll through the city with a beer in hand. Film sets of Forrest Gump, Midnight in the Garden, and more.

name: School Bus Graveyard
notes: Field full of colorful graffiti buses along Highway 365. More of a road trip art gallery than an ordinary junkyard. Each bus features its own murals, pop art, and strange commentary on life. Free and unguarded – take your best photos. Striking along the road towards the North Georgia mountains.

name: Screaming Eagle Zipline – Banning Mills
notes: GUINNESS WORLD RECORD: longest zipline course in the world! Historic Banning Mills – 35+ ziplines and rope courses over canyons and waterfalls. Screening Eagle is the grand finale – heart palpitations guaranteed. Treehouse stays are also available for the true adventurer.

name: Serendipity Park – Naturist
notes: Georgia's BEST naturist park – 8x AANR Koch Award for friendliness! 90 minutes NE of Atlanta in the North Georgia mountains. Pool, cafe, cabins, RV sites, camping sites, and a stream. Family-friendly and 'clothing comfortable' policy. Els & Serge: 'The Dip' as locals call it. Welcome home.

name: Service Brewing – Savannah
notes: Veteran-owned microbrewery near the famous River Street. Beers with military names: Ground Pounder, Rally Point, Battlewagon, Gun Bunny. A portion of the profits goes to veterans' organizations. New season beer every 3 months. Harvest Host available for RVers!

name: Six Flags Over Georgia
notes: Six Flags Prestige Pass – FREE admission for Florida residents! Elite roller coasters including Goliath, The Riddler Mindbender, and Batman. Full day of fun – ensure early arrival during the summer months. 20 minutes from downtown Atlanta.

name: Skydive Georgia – Cedartown
notes: LARGEST tandem skydiving facility in the South! Jump from 14,000 feet above the Georgia hills. AFF training available for those who really want to learn. Cedartown Airport – small and relaxed atmosphere, no big crowds.

name: StillFire Brewing – Suwanee
notes: 20-barrel brewery in a renovated fire station in the heart of Suwanee! Dog and family-friendly with an outdoor patio next to a playground. College Dropout Lager – Silver Medal Great American Beer Festival 2024! Food trucks present 6 days a week.

name: Stone Mountain Park
address: 1000 Robert E Lee Blvd, Stone Mountain, GA 30083
notes: LARGEST bas-relief sculpture in the world – three Southern Civil War generals carved in granite. Controversial (Confederate symbolism) but absolutely spectacular in terms of scale. Cable car to the top, laser show in the evening, walking paths around the granite mountain. A half-day tip from Atlanta. Els: historic complex. Serge: the sculpture is bigger than the Statue of Liberty. Impressive.

name: Subdivision Stonehenge – Athens
notes: Mysterious Stonehenge replica in the median strip along the road. Built in the '90s for a subdivision named 'Stonehenge' that was never built. Origin unconfirmed even by Roadside America. COMPLETELY FREE absurdist roadside moment.

name: Tallulah Gorge State Park
address: 338 Jane Hurt Yarn Rd, Tallulah Falls, GA 30573
notes: MOST IMPRESSIVE canyon in the eastern US! 1,000 feet deep, 2 miles long with 6 waterfalls in the canyon. Suspension bridge 80 feet above the churning river – spectacular! Karl Wallenda once walked across here on a slackline. Permit required for the canyon floor (limited number per day – book EARLY!)

name: Tellus Science Museum – Cartersville
notes: Incredible minerals and rocks museum – 10,000+ specimens! Paleontology section with real fossil dinosaur finds. Planetarium and a vintage car collection. Gold panning in the outdoor sluice – a real Georgian gold experience!

name: The Big Chicken (KFC Marietta)
notes: 56-FOOT tall steel chicken that actually moves! Built in 1963 by a Georgia Tech student. Now just a KFC. Pilots use it as a navigation point when landing. Seriously. Marietta lets you know: 'Turn right at the Big Chicken'. This is the kind of bizarre that makes Belgians a cult people. STOP HERE.

name: The Grey – Savannah
address: 109 Martin Luther King Jr Blvd, Savannah, GA 31401
notes: JAMES BEARD awarded in an Art Deco Greyhound bus station from 1938! Fixed price menu focused on Lowcountry seafood and seasonal produce. Formerly a segregated bus station – now the best spot in Savannah. Also a casual Diner Bar available for à la carte. Reservations book MONTHS in advance – serious.

name: The Loft – Swinging Atlanta
notes: Midtown Atlanta's newer lifestyle club. Various party formats every weekend – check swingingatlanta.com. Membership required but cheaper than Trapeze. 21+ only events for couples and single ladies. Recently renovated. Younger crowd than Trapeze.

name: The Tree That Owns Itself – Athens
address: Corner Dearing & Finley St, Athens, GA 30606
notes: Owner William Jackson gifted the oak to himself in the 1800s. Official title deed. The tree is the legal owner of the land beneath it. The original tree fell in 1942 – this one is a descendant of the same seed. FREE, 5 minutes, and 100% Georgia absurdist.

name: Thunderbird Inn – Savannah
notes: Retro 1964 motor inn fully renovated in iconic Savannah style. Every room decorated differently – Instagram gold! Virtually the ONLY quirky budget hotel in Savannah's historic district. Walking distance from River Street, squares, and restaurants.

name: Tiny Doors ATL
notes: 8 5 cm miniatures hidden throughout Atlanta! Artistic project by Karen Anderson building 'portals to other worlds'. FREE neighborhood scavenger hunt with interactive map on website. Miniatures at Krog Street Tunnel, BeltLine locations, and more. Perfect for Instagram – find them on the website.

name: Titan I Missile – Cordele
notes: Real 30-meter ICBM rocket on the highway at a gas station! Here since 1969 – albeit with safe aluminum panels instead of radioactive ones. Accessible 24/7 and FREE. If Serge stops to pose next to it: at least 3 likes guaranteed. Perfect I-75 rack spot between Florida and Atlanta.

name: Trapeze Club – Atlanta
notes: Atlanta's oldest and most highly regarded lifestyle club. Danceable DJ music, dining areas, private rooms, group spaces. Open Wed-Sun 8-3 AM. Couples and singles welcome (Sat: couples only). Strict dress code – you'll be able to take it off anyway, but dressing up is mandatory. Reputation as the best East Coast lifestyle club north of Florida.

name: Tree Spirits of St. Simons Island
notes: Artist Keith Jennings carves faces into oak tree wounds – for over 40 years. 20+ hidden faces scattered across the island. Each face is unique and represents a drowned sailor. FREE walking and scavenger hunt through beautiful island forest. St. Simons Island Map available at tourist info.

name: Two Tides Brewing – Savannah
notes: Brewery in a renovated house in the Starland District! Each room has a different atmosphere – balcony overlooks Starland Yard with live music. Specialties: Sours, Hazy's, and fruit beer slushies for the heat. Mini-arcade in the building. Dogs and children welcome until 9 p.m.

name: Tybee Island Beach & Lighthouse
notes: Savannah's Beach Island – 20 minutes from the city! Climb the 178-foot historic lighthouse (1773!) for a coastal panorama. Relaxed beach village with good seafood restaurants and a hippie vibe. Go for the sea, stay for the atmosphere. Els: beach day. Serge: climbing the lighthouse. Combine with the Original Crab Shack for the perfect day out.

name: Whitewater Columbus
notes: LONGEST urban whitewater course in the world – 2.5 miles of Chattahoochee rapids! TOP 12 Man-Made Adventures in the World by international media. AS A BONUS: the only zipline in the US connecting two states (GO to AL and back). Family-friendly and professionally equipped.

name: World of Coca-Cola – Atlanta
notes: America's most iconic corporate museum – and you can taste EVERYTHING! Tasting room with 100+ Coca-Cola products from around the world. The Secret Recipe and the Vault Room are highlights. Next to the Georgia Aquarium – perfect day trip to Atlanta.

name: World's Largest Peanut – Ashburn
notes: 16.5-foot peanut on a 20-foot pedestal along I-75! LED crown lighting at night. A ROYAL peanut. Hurricane Michael wrecked the original in 2018 – Ashburn rebuilt it bigger in 2023. Free parking at the gas station. Perfect rack stop.

name: Yonah Mountain Vineyards – Cleveland
notes: The only WINE CELLAR (cave tour) in the state of Georgia! Spectacular view of Yonah Mountain from the tasting room. Chardonnay, Merlot, Malbec, and Pinot Noir from their own vineyard. Top 25 winery in the USA. Combined with BabyLand General (5 minutes) = a perfect day.

name: Akaka Falls State Park
notes: 442-foot-high (134m!) waterfall in the middle of the rainforest — Hawaii's most photogenic waterfall. Short 1.5km loop through bamboo and heliconia jungles. $5 entrance fee. Tomorrow morning = fewer people. Perfect content shot for @roamingbonbons.

name: Bishop Museum – lava pit replica
notes: Hawaii's largest museum with a REAL planetarium and a life-size fire-spitting lava demo. World-class Hawaiian collection — not the standard 'souvenir shop' experience. America the Beautiful Pass valid for some exhibitions — check in advance.

name: Blue Hawaiian Helicopter Tour – Kauai
address: Blue Hawaiian Helicopters, 3501 Rice St, Lihue, HI 96766
notes: Doors-off helicopter flight over Waimea Canyon, Na Pali Coast, and Waialeale crater lake. Best way to truly see Kauai — 65% is inaccessible by land. ~$300-400 p.p. depending on route. Premium is a one-time purchase. @roamingbonbons: cinematic gold.

name: Byodo-In Temple – Valley of Temples
notes: Exact replica of a 900-year-old Japanese Buddhist temple — right in the middle of Hawaii! Built in 1968 for the 100th anniversary of Japanese immigration. $5 p.p. Peacock, black swans, and giant koi in the pond. Peacocks included. Surreal.

name: Da Poke Shack – Kona
notes: BEST poke bowls on the Big Island — fresh ahi tuna, limu seaweed, masago. Different fresh options every day, sometimes sold out before noon. ~$15-20 p.p. Serge: *this* is poke, not the fake poke from Whole Foods.

name: Dole Plantation – ananas-doolhof
notes: Officially GUINNESS World Records largest labyrinth in the world — made of pineapple bushes! Dole Whip ice cream is legendary and nowhere in the world is it as good as here. The train ($12) is kitschy but fun. Serge: this is silly enough to do.

name: Enchanted Forest Neon Zoo
address: Ward Village, 1240 Ala Moana Blvd, Honolulu, HI 96814
notes: Neon-lit wild animals in an immersive blacklight forest in the middle of Honolulu. Mouthwatering photo opportunities — perfect for the @roamingbonbons feed. Book tickets online. Evening = best atmosphere.

name: Green Sand Beach – Papakolea
notes: GREEN sand beach due to olivine crystals — one of only 4 green sand beaches in the world! ~5 km trek round trip OR shuttle for ~$20 p.p. from locals. No facilities. Bring: water, sunscreen, and a Belgian sense of adventure.

name: Haleakalā Sunrise – Boven de wolken
notes: Sunrise above the clouds at an altitude of 3,055m — the most magical moment in Hawaii. America the Beautiful Pass valid. REQUIRED reservation for sunrise ($1 p.p.). Bring: warm clothes (it is COLD), a thermos of coffee, and a camera. Serge: this is better than any mountain.

name: Halona Blowhole Lookout
notes: Lava blowhole spraying water high into the air — spectacular! FREE, on the side of the highway on Oahu's east coast. From Here to Eternity beach nearby (this rolling wave scene). Els: this wave. Serge: this coast.

name: Hana-Maui Resort – Travaasa
notes: Legendary remote resort at the end of the Road to Hana — total detachment. Cottages with open fires, horseback riding on the beach, farm-to-table dining. ~$300-400/night (luxury). But Hana is so remote that you will want to stay for the atmosphere.

name: Hedonism-style: Secret Beach Kauai
notes: Kauai's secluded naturist beach — a 900m jungle hike to get there. No facilities, no guards. Popularity fluctuates, but locals know it. FREE. Swimming DANGEROUS in rough weather. Bring lunch. Serge and Els: this is the real deal.

name: Helena's Hawaiian Food – Kalihi
notes: James Beard Award winner — family recipe taro leaf laulau and pipikaula ribs. Open only a few days a week, always a line. Founded in 1946, still family-run. ~$15-25 p.p. Check opening hours. This is HONEST local Hawaiian food.

name: Ho'okipa Beach – Windsurfer Heaven
notes: Windsurfing World Championship venue with daily professional shows to watch for FREE! Turtles sleep on the beach in the afternoon — protected by NPS rangers. FREE. Paia nearby = hippest village on Maui with good eateries.

name: Honolulu Museum of Art
notes: Surprisingly strong art museum with Asian, Pacific, and European collections in a beautiful building. Film room, sculpture courtyard, and rotating exhibitions. ~$20 p.p. FREE every first Wednesday of the month. Serge: You wouldn't expect this in Honolulu.

name: Iolani Palace – enige koninklijk paleis USA
notes: THE ONLY royal palace on American soil — last Hawaiian monarchy. Queen Lili'uokalani was imprisoned here in 1895 following the American annexation. ~$22 p.p. audio tour. Amazing that this isn't in every history book.

name: Ka Lae – Zuidelijkste punt USA
notes: THE SOUTHERNST POINT of the USA — more South than Key West! People jump from the cliffs ~15m into the sea — an extreme local tradition. FREE, wind-battered, and surreal. Serge: feel like you are standing at the end of the world for a moment.

name: Kaena Point – Meest afgelegen strand Oahu
notes: 8km off-road hike to Oahu's most remote corner — albatross colony and seals! Laysan albatross breeding colony (November-July) — ONLY here in Hawaii can be seen on land. FREE. 4x4 recommended for the off-road route. Serge: the F-150 couldn't have been more perfect.

name: Kauai ATV Adventure Tours
notes: ATV tours through sugarcane plantation grounds and off-road to hidden waterfalls. Film locations from Pirates of the Caribbean, Jurassic Park, and Indiana Jones. ~$130 p.p. Minimum age 16. Serge and Els: this is definitely your thing.

name: Kauai Beer Company
notes: Kauai's first and only in-house brewery — Pacific IPAs and coconut porters. Food menu with local Hawaiian influences. Welcoming, modern taproom in Lihue. ~$7-10 per pint. Combine with Wailua Falls, 20 min away. Els: coconut porter = surprisingly good.

name: Kealakekua Bay – Captain Cook Monument
notes: Place where Captain Cook died in 1779 — now a snorkeling paradise! Snorkel boat trip (~$70-90 p.p.) to the monument AND the best coral reef in Hawaii. Alternatively: kayak from the bay (5km). Dolphins are almost guaranteed here.

name: Kilauea Lighthouse – Wildlife Refuge
notes: Active lighthouse on Kauai's northernmost point with spectacular seabird colonies. Red-billed auklets, frigatebirds, boobies, and rare Laysan albatrosses. $10 p.p. America the Beautiful valid. Serge: this is better than the Zwin in Knokke.

name: Koa Kea Hotel – Poipu Kauai
notes: Boutique hotel right on Poipu Beach — one of the most beautiful beaches on Kauai. Small and personal — not a mega-hotel, genuine service. Restaurant with local fish. ~$200-250/night (premium). Special occasion material. Serge: this is justified for once.

name: Kohala Distillery – Big Island rum
notes: Artisanal rum made from real Hawaiian sugarcane — unique to the USA. Sugarcane rum aging in small barrels with tropical influences. Tastings ~$20-25. Hawi is also a cute little town on the Kohala coast.

name: Koke'e State Park – Kauai Highlands
notes: Highland forest at 1,100m with hiking trails, mist, and a 180-degree view of Waimea Canyon. Wild chickens roam free — everywhere on Kauai, but here it is particularly absurd. FREE + America the Beautiful valid. Cold temperatures — bring a coat!

name: Kona Coffee Living History Farm
notes: America's only working historic coffee plantation from the 1920s — full demo. Guide in period costume explains EVERYTHING about Kona coffee cultivation. ~$20 p.p., book online. Combine with a real Kona coffee tasting nearby.

name: Kono's – North Shore Breakfast
notes: North Shore's favorite breakfast spot — kalua pork breakfast burritos are legendary. A resort next to the famous surf beaches of the North Shore. ~$12-18. Haleiwa is highly recommended in general — one of Oahu's smallest, hippest coastal towns.

name: Kualoa Ranch – Jurassic Park
notes: THE filming location of Jurassic Park, Lost, Hawaii Five-O, and dozens of other movies! Horseback riding, ATV tours, and ziplines through the valley you KNOW from the movies. ~$45-60 per activity. Serge: This is the dino valley. Els: Where is Jeff Goldblum?

name: Lava Ocean Entry – Kalapana (als actief)
notes: See REAL lava flowing into the ocean — volcanic rock that magnifies the Earth in real time! Not always active — check the Hawaii Volcanoes Observatory website before visiting. Boat trips available (~$200 p.p.) for a closer view. One of the most bizarre nature events in the world.

name: Liliha Bakery – Coco Puffs
notes: The one and only Coco Puff from Hawaii — chocolate cream puff with haupia filling. Open 24/7. Honolulu's most beloved bakery with a locally legendary reputation. ~$3-5 per Coco Puff. Also ask for the chantilly cake. Serge: test as a Belgian chocolate expert.

name: Little Beach – Maui (naturisten+zondagsfeest)
notes: Hawaii's best-known informal nudist beach — be patient past Big Beach towards the rocks. Every SUNDAY: spontaneous drum circle and dance party at sunset. LEGENDARY. FREE. Officially not allowed but legally tolerated. America the Beautiful for parking.

name: Little Beach Sunday Drum Circle
address: Little Beach, Makena State Park, Kihei, HI 96753
notes: EVERY SUNDAY EVENING: semi-naked drum circle on the nudist beach at sunset! Guitarists, fire-eaters, dancers, and tourists mingling in freedom. FREE. Arrive early for parking. Starts ±16:00, highlight at sunset. Viral content guaranteed.

name: Loco Moco bij Cafe 100 – Hilo
notes: Inventor of the Loco Moco — rice + hamburger + fried egg + brown gravy. Opened in 1946. More than 30 variations of Loco Moco on the menu. ~$8-15. Hilo's rainy weather makes this comfort food absolutely justified.

name: Lumahai Beach – South Pacific film
notes: THE beach from the movie South Pacific (1958) — completely pristine and remote. DANGEROUS swimming due to strong currents — DO NOT enter the sea. Just admire. FREE. Serge: this is Hollywood, but for real.

name: Makapuu Lighthouse Trail
notes: Easy 2.5km coastal path to spectacular cliff lighthouse. January-March: chance to spot whales from the cliffs! FREE. Go early for the best light conditions. Perfect content for @roamingbonbons.

name: Mama's Fish House – Maui
notes: Hawaii's undisputed number 1 restaurant — fresh fish on the menu caught within hours. The menu lists the name of the fisherman and the vessel. Hawaii regional at its best. Book weeks in advance. ~$70-100 p.p. Romantic and unforgettable.

name: Manoa Falls Trail – Honolulu
notes: Rainforest trail with 45m waterfall right behind Honolulu — totally unexpected! Parking app required: ~$5. 2.5km loop, muddy after rain — shoes you don't mind wearing. Jurassic Park scenes were filmed here. Els: you might see a dinosaur.

name: Maui Brewing Co. – Kihei
notes: Hawaii's most famous craft brewery — Big Swell IPA, Bikini Blonde, and Pineapple Mana Wheat. Brewery tours available on weekends. Spacious terrace with a view of the brewing process. ~$7-12 per pint. Serge: This is what Duvel would be if Duvel were Hawaiian.

name: Maui Ocean Center – zeeschildpadtunnel
notes: Best marine life aquarium in Hawaii with a walk-through underwater dome for sea turtles. On-site humpback whale research center — chance to ask real biologists questions. ~$40 p.p., good for a half-day. Both children and adults are impressed.

name: Mauna Kea Summit Observatories
address: Mauna Kea Summit Rd, Hilo, HI 96720
notes: 14 international observatories at 4,205m — the BEST place on Earth for stargazing! FREE visit to the summit. Visitor Center at 2,800m with telescopes, free in the evening. NECESSARY: acclimatize at the visitor center for at least 30 min. 4x4 required — F-150 go!

name: Merrie Monarch Festival
address: Afook-Chinen Civic Auditorium, 50 E Puainako St, Hilo, HI 96720
notes: Hilo's world-famous hula festival — the Olympics of the hula world. Every year in April. HARD to get tickets — waiting list years in advance. FREE street party surrounding the festival: parade, crafts market. Hilo itself is charming and cheaper than Maui.

name: Musubi Mama's – Spam Musubi
notes: Hawaii's most iconic street food: Spam Musubi — a sushi roll with spam and rice. Sounds terrible, tastes surprisingly good. This IS the fast food of Hawaii. ~$3-5 each. Serge: give it a chance. Els: momentarily forgot it's spam.

name: Na Pali Coast Zodiac Boat Tour
notes: Hawaii's most spectacular coastline from a rubber speedboat! Na Pali cliffs, 1,200m high, are inaccessible by land — boat or helicopter. ~$140-175 p.p. Summer only (May-September). Serge: this is the best $150 you will spend.

name: Pearl Harbor Aviation Museum
notes: WWII aircraft, including a bullet-riddled hangar still exactly as it was on December 7, 1941. F-15, Zero, and Dauntless dive bombers in an operational museum on Ford Island. ~$25 p.p. Combine with USS Arizona Memorial — perfect same-day Pearl Harbor experience.

name: Plate Lunch bij Rainbow Drive-In
notes: Iconic Hawaii 'plate lunch' spot — open since 1961, still lines stretching onto the sidewalk. Macaroni salad + two scoops of rice + meat: THIS is what locals eat, not poke. ~$10-14. Cash recommended. Barack Obama ate here as a child. Enough said.

name: Poipu Beach – Sea Turtle Basking
notes: Popular beach on Kauai where Hawaiian monk seals (ENDANGERED!) just lie sleeping. FREE beach. Turtles are also regularly present at sunset. NPS volunteers keep the public at a distance — respect the animals.

name: Pololu Valley Lookout + Trail
notes: Spectacular view of sea cliffs and a secluded black sand beach. Steep descent to the beach (~500m). Muddy after rain — sturdy shoes required. FREE and almost no tourists. The 'real' Hawaii that the majority never sees.

name: Polynesian Cultural Center
notes: Six Polynesian 'villages' (Fiji, Samoa, Tonga, Tahiti, Marquesas, Hawaii) on one site. Live shows, canoe demos, fire dancing, and an evening buffet package available. ~$60 p.p. base, more for all-inclusive. Completely re-ridicted by BYU Utah — original.

name: Puka Dog – Hot Dog Hawaii-style
notes: HOT DOG in a toasted bun seared with a hot iron — with tropical relish and lilikoi mustard. Bizarre concept, incredibly tasty. The only original Puka Dog in Poipu, Kauai. ~$10-12. Vegetarian options too. Serge: this is the sausage he deserves after Waimea Canyon.

name: Punalu'u Bake Shop – Big Island
notes: Southernmost bakery in the US — Hawaiian sweet rolls, macadamia nut treats. Naalehu is also the southernmost town in the US. Two records for one stop. ~$5-10. Free parking and outdoor seating. Perfecto na Punalu'u black sand beach.

name: Punalu'u Black Sand Beach
notes: BLACK volcanic sand beach — one of the few in the world! Hawksbill and green sea turtles simply sunbathe on the beach here. FREE. Not a tourist trap, just bizarre nature at its best. America the Beautiful valid for parking zone.

name: Road to Hana – Sacred Pools
notes: Famous Maui route with 600 curves, 50+ waterfalls, and bamboo forests. Ohe'o Gulch (Seven Sacred Pools) = NPS site, America the Beautiful Pass valid! Start EARLY: it gets crowded very quickly. Bring bread and lunch — few restaurants along the way.

name: Road to Hana – Waianapanapa Black Sand
notes: Hawaii's SECOND black sand beach — but this is the most dramatically situated! Lava arches, blowholes, green cliffs, and a blue-tinted cave with legends. $10 p.p. Reservations required via Hawaii DLNR! Popular — book weeks in advance.

name: Sea Life Park Hawaii
notes: Dolphin swimming, shark diving, and sea lion shows — all in one place. ALSO: 'wolphin' present (hybrid between dolphin and orca) — the only one on Earth! ~$45 p.p. base. Dolphin experiences separate ~$150+. Serge: the wolphin is really a selling point.

name: Shave Ice – Matsumoto's North Shore
notes: Hawaii's MOST ORIGINAL shave ice — open since 1951, world-famous among locals. Not to be confused with 'snow cones' — this is real crushed ice with real syrups. ~$4-6. Go for it. Els: sweeter than a Liège waffle but just as addictive.

name: Skydive Hawaii – North Shore Oahu
notes: Tandem skydiving over the North Shore with a view of the breakwater world surf spots. Drop over turquoise ocean, green mountain ridges, and sugarcane fields. ~$200-280 p.p. One of the most beautiful skydiving locations in the world. @roamingbonbons gold.

name: Snorkelen – Molokini Crater
notes: Partially submerged volcanic crater = perfect sheltered snorkeling lagoon. Water visibility up to 45m deep, 250+ species of fish and shark sightings possible. Boat trips from Ma'alaea Harbor ~$80-120 p.p. Book early — Maui's most popular excursion.

name: Surfen bij Waikiki Beach
notes: Learn to surf on the most iconic wave in the world — beginner-friendly and warm water. Surf lessons: ~$40-50 p.p. for 1.5 hours with an instructor. Believe it or not: almost everyone stands up after 30 min. Els and Serge on a surfboard = guaranteed viral. But: Waikiki is overtourist.

name: Taro Ko Chips – Hana Highway snack
notes: Handmade taro chips sold from a small farm stand along the Road to Hana. Truly artisanal — cut and fried in batches. A unique find on Maui. ~$6-8 per bag. Always sold out by noon. Stop early!

name: Thurston Lava Tube – Hawaii Volcanoes NP
notes: Walk through a real lava tunnel — 500 years old and illuminated for tourists. Hawaii Volcanoes NP: America the Beautiful Pass valid! Otherwise, entrance fee is $35 per vehicle. Active lava flows possible — check NPS website for current access. ABSOLUTELY A MUST DO.

name: Upcountry Maui Lavender Farm
notes: Lavender farm on the slopes of the Haleakalā — with English gardens AND hula. Lavender shortbread, lavender lemonade, and lavender honey. Elvis deserved this. Free to visit, products are affordable. Serge: this isn't Provence, but it's close.

name: USS Arizona Memorial – Pearl Harbor
notes: Holy site: 1,177 sailors still lie in the sunken ship. FREE boat trip to the memorial (America the Beautiful). Museum $10 recommended but not mandatory. Serge: this is the Normandystrand of the Pacific. Quiet, emotional experience.

name: Waikiki Banyan – Centrale ligging
notes: Centrally located condo-style apartments in the heart of Waikiki — affordable option. Full kitchen, rooftop playground. No hotel service, but good for a long stay. ~$100-140/night via Airbnb. Serge: this is the smartest budget choice for Oahu.

name: Waikiki Trolley Hop-On Hop-Off
address: Royal Hawaiian Center, 2201 Kalakaua Ave, Honolulu, HI 96815
notes: Convenient day pass for tourist transport on Oahu — 4 lines through Honolulu and the surrounding area. No car needed for a day in Honolulu. ~$25-35 day pass. Not necessary if you have the F-150 with you, but handy if you don't want a car for a change.

name: Wailua Falls – Fantasy Island waterval
notes: THE waterfall from the Fantasy Island TV series opening — recognizable to everyone of our generation! FREE to see from the road. Short walk to the base (unofficial path, sometimes closed). Els: 'The planes! The planes!' — Serge gets the reference.

name: Waimea Canyon – 'Grand Canyon of Pacific'
notes: FREE FREE FREE — the 'Grand Canyon of the Pacific' on Kauai. 1,100m deep, 16km long, and filled with red and green layers. Mark Twain was impressed. America the Beautiful pass: free parking. Combine with Kokee State Park above.

name: Waipio Valley Lookout
notes: The most dramatic valley in Hawaii — 600m high green cliffs with a black sand beach. FREE lookout. The road down is 4x4 ONLY and extremely steep — the F-150 is perfect! Optional: muleback tour ($100+) to the valley floor. Serge: The F-150 does better here than any car.

name: Balanced Rock Park
notes: A 48-ton rock balances on a narrow 3x17 inch pedestal! Completely unbelievable natural phenomenon. FREE. Small but MIND-BLOWING. Near Castleford, 25 min from Twin Falls. Seriously: how is this thing still standing?

name: Bardenay Distillery + Restaurant - Boise
notes: America's FIRST restaurant-distillery! Makes gin, rum, and whiskey on-site. Tours available. Boise's Basque Block neighborhood. Locally developed concept. Cocktails with their own spirits are their pride. Grove Street = Boise's lively bar/restaurant strip.

name: Bare Mountain Resort - Boise
address: Hidden location, 30 min from Boise, ID
notes: AANR-affiliated naturist resort on 130 acres! 30 MINUTES from Boise! ​​In the middle of nowhere, Ponderosa Pines. Pool, hiking trails, campfire events. Open late April to mid-October. Since 1981. Couples ONLY for overnight stays. Reservation required!

name: Basque Block - Boise
notes: BOISE has the largest Basque community outside of Spain! Basque Block: museum, bars, restaurant Leku Ona, parties. Completely unexpected for an Idaho prairie town. Bar-Gernika: best veal stews outside of Bilbao. St. Ignatius's feast day in July = Basque dancing in the street!

name: Big Don - Janitor Muffler Man Pocatello
notes: Giant Muffler Man dressed as a cleaner! Pocatello's craziest roadside attraction for a year. Located at a business along the main road. FREE photo stop. Almost 6 meters tall. Combine with Museum of Clean - themed day!

name: Big Idaho Potato Hotel
notes: SLEEPING IN A POTATO. No, really. 6-ton promo potato from the Idaho Potato Commission. Queen bed, vinyl records, mini fridge, silo bathroom with a starry sky. 400-acre farm with Dolly the Jersey cow. 30 min from Boise. Airbnb - book months in advance! For 2 people. Instagram gold.

name: Birch Creek Petroglyphs
notes: Ancient petroglyphs in a remote valley. BLM managed. FREE but remote. Leadero region - beautiful in combination with the Salmon River route. Summer access most reliable (unpaved road). Little-known gem for prehistory enthusiasts.

name: Boat Box Hot Springs
notes: Literally a BOAT converted into a hot spring tub! Fits only 2 people - romantic and intimate. Right along the road next to the Salmon River. FREE. Clothing optional, customary here. Stanley region. Go early or wait - but worth it!

name: Bogus Basin Mountain Recreation Area - Boise
notes: Boise's own ski resort! 45 min from the center. Summer: mountain biking, scenic tram, hiking. Winter: day skiing for locals. Not on Ikon, but good for a day trip. Known as 'Bogus' by locals. Charming.

name: Bruneau Dunes State Park
notes: Largest freestanding sand dunes in North America! 470 feet high. Desert campground. Star observatory on site. Lake for swimming and fishing. Near Bruneau, South Idaho. At night: the best night skies in Idaho. America the Beautiful Pass.

name: Burke Ghost Town
notes: Mining town built in a canyon SO NARROW that the train ran through the hotel! The railway line literally ran through the lobby of the Tiger Hotel. Boomed as a silver/lead mine in the late 1800s. 10 min drive from Wallace. Abandoned buildings are still standing. Time range: summer best access.

name: Center of the Universe - Wallace
notes: City Council OFFICIALLY DECLARED: Wallace = Center of the Universe. A manhole cover marks the exact spot on Bank Street. Someone tried to route I-90 through the city – they fought back! Wallace is also the 'Silver Capital of the World'. FREE. And meant absolutely seriously. Or not.

name: Cleo's Ferry Museum & Nature Trail
notes: Birdhouse-covered path, peacocks, animal sculptures AND a graveyard! A private owner spent years building this absurdist art park. Classic American folk art at its best. 30 min from Boise. Small but special. Call for opening hours - family-run.

name: Cowboy Muffler Man - Wendell
address: Intermountain Motor Homes, 1894 N Frontage Rd, Wendell, ID 83355
notes: 22-foot-tall cowboy in a yellow shirt and gray hat! Standing at an RV dealer along I-84. Classic American roadside kitsch at its best. FREE. Quick stop along the highway. Wendell: otherwise nothing to do, but this is enough.

name: Craters of the Moon
address: 1266 Craters of the Moon Loop, Arco, ID 83213
notes: Astronauts trained here for the moon – and you can see it! Lava tubes, cinder cones, volcanic landscape. Looks like something straight out of a sci-fi movie. National Monument + Preserve. America the Beautiful pass! Best time: May-Sept. Summers are HOT on the black lava.

name: Custer Ghost Town
notes: Gold rush mining town from 1879. Abandoned in 1910. One street, half a mile long. Empire Saloon still standing! 600 residents at its peak. Now: zero. Near Stanley. Sawtooth NRA manages it. Perfect combination with a visit to Redfish Lake.

name: Dog Bark Park Inn (Sweet Willy)
notes: 30-foot-tall beagle! Formerly a B&B, now free to view. Dennis & Frances Conklin built this wooden marvel. Gift shop with hand-carved dog sculptures. No overnight stays since 2024 - but STOP PHOTOS! Cottonwood = small Idaho County sleep town. Worth it!

name: Elevated Ballooning - Driggs (Teton Valley)
notes: HOTAIR BALLOON over the Teton Mountains from the IDAHO side! Sunrise over the Tetons - literally breathtaking. Max 4 people per balloon - an intimate experience. Driggs is quieter than the Jackson Hole side. May-October. Champagne toast after landing. DO IT!

name: Elevation 486 - Twin Falls
address: 195 River Vista Place, Twin Falls, ID 83301
notes: Fine dining on the rim of the Snake River Canyon! The name refers to the difference in elevation of the canyon. Globally inspired cuisine, indoor + outdoor. 486 meters above the canyon floor = spectacular! Sunset dining here is unforgettable.

name: Emma's Cafe - Bosnian - Twin Falls
notes: Bosnian restaurant in Twin Falls - completely unexpected! Cevapi, stuffed cabbage rolls, pljeskavica (cheese-filled!) Vegetables from their own garden. Local meat. Twin Falls has a large Bosnian diaspora since the war in the 1990s. Baklava for dessert. Real, authentic, delicious.

name: Ernest Hemingway's Grave - Ketchum
address: Ketchum Cemetery, 100 Cemetery Rd, Ketchum, ID 83340
notes: Papa Hemingway chose Ketchum to die (1961). Simple, unadorned grave. A stark contrast to his life. Ketchum was his beloved Idaho retreat. Sun Valley is 2 km away – a nice combination. FREE. Contemplative. Serge: bring The Sun Also Rises.

name: Evel Knievel Snake River Jump Site
notes: On September 8, 1974, Evel Knievel attempted to jump across the Snake River Canyon. Rocket-powered Skycycle X-2. Parachute opened too early. Epic fail! He survived. The legend did not. Monument + commemorative plaque at the visitor service. FREE. Absolute MUST for road trip folklore.

name: Falls Inn - Priest River area
notes: Former US Forest Service ranger station as a restaurant! The water of Torrelle Waterfall runs UNDER the building. Sandwiches and pizzas with waterfall sounds. Near Priest Lake - Northern Idaho. One of Idaho's most unique restaurant locations.

name: Goldbug Hot Springs
notes: YOUR FAVORITE STYLE hot springs! Already done but deserves a spot. 6 waterfall-fed clothing-optional pools on BLM grounds. 3.6 mile round-trip hike, 270m elevation gain - well deserved! Mostly clothing-free crowd, everyone friendly. FREE. South of Salmon on US-93. Arrive early for parking.

name: Grand Teton Brewing - Victor
notes: Idaho's Teton Valley craft beer - with 90% Idaho barley! Teton Range IPA uses Idaho 7 hops: unique aroma profile. Victor = quiet side of the Tetons (versus busy Jackson). Brewpub with food. Local atmosphere. Combine with Elevated Ballooning in Driggs!

name: Hells Canyon
notes: DEEPEST canyon in North America! Deeper than the Grand Canyon. 8,043 feet deep at the deepest point. Whitewater rafting, jet boat tours, hiking. Riggins is the Idaho gateway town. Cannot be seen by car - boat or helicopter required.

name: Home
notes: Our Starting Point

name: Idaho Balloon Adventures - Eagle
notes: Sunrise balloon ride over Treasure Valley! Municipal: Boise area, Snake River plain. Private and shared flights. Champagne landing. 1-hour flight, morning departure. Book in advance - weather permitting. Kids from 5 years old.

name: Idaho Potato Museum
notes: Temple for the potato! World's largest potato chip. Build your own Mr. Potato Head. Potato signed by a VP! Free baked potato upon entry. Seriously. Blackfoot is 30 min from Idaho Falls. A MUST-VISIT! 'We take our potatoes seriously' - and how!

name: Idaho White Rose - Post Falls (lifestyle club)
notes: Inland Northwest's premier lifestyle club! Post Falls = 30 min from Coeur d'Alene. Safe, clean, sexy, and judgment-free. Couples and select single females. Events schedule online. Find us via Kasidie. Reserve via website.

name: Johnny Sack Cabin
address: 4598 S Big Springs Loop Rd, Island Park, ID 83429, USA

name: Kirkham Hot Springs
notes: FREE wild hot springs in a river gorge! Springs flow directly into the South Fork Payette River. Some sections are also accessible in winter. Garden Valley, 1.5 hours from Boise. Idaho's most popular hot springs. Come early!

name: Koenig Distillery & Winery - Caldwell
notes: Idaho's leading potato vodka and wine! The farm-to-glass potato processing is fascinating. Wineries in the Treasure Valley – unexpectedly good. Caldwell, 30 min from Boise. Free tasting with a small entrance fee.

name: Last Stoplight on I-90 - Wallace
notes: The LAST traffic light on Interstate 90 was in Wallace! Removed in 1991 to build a tunnel. The city CELEBRATED this as a cultural monument. Now a replica as a tourist attraction. Wallace: the city that held the government back. RESPECT.

name: Lava Hot Springs
address: 430 E Main St, Lava Hot Springs, ID 83246
notes: Natural geothermal springs of 38-46°C! City pools, private springs, Olympic pool. Little resort town with vintage charm. Warm all year round. Combo with Downtown Hot Springs. Idaho's ultimate relaxation after the skiing phases. Highly recommended!

name: Leku Ona Basque Restaurant - Boise
notes: AUTHENTIC Basque cuisine in the heart of Boise! An unexpected culinary adventure: txistorra, kokotxas, porrusalda. At the famous Basque Block. Boise = the largest Basque expat community outside of Spain. Els: here you feel like you're in Bilbao for a moment. Almost.

name: Lionhead Natural Water Slides
notes: FREE natural rock slides in the forests of North Idaho! Hidden gem – accessible only via a hiking trail. Cold stream water. Mountain setting. No crowds of tourists. Priest Lake region. Summer only. Bring: swimwear, water sandals, and a sense of adventure.

name: Map Rock Petroglyph Site
notes: 12,000 years old! Prehistoric map of the Upper Snake River. Hunter-gatherers carved into the river, landscapes, and routes. Nationally Significant petroglyph site. Managed by the BLM. FREE. Outside Melba, 30 min from Boise. Visit early in the morning – best light.

name: Mesa Falls Visitor Center
address: Upper Mesa Falls Rd, Ashton, ID 83420, USA

name: MickDuff's Brewing - Sandpoint
notes: Sandpoint microbrewery on Main Street! Huckleberry Wheat beer: typical Idaho flavor. Fresh pub food + beer menu with 10+ taps. Sandpoint = beautiful city on Lake Pend Oreille. Combine with Schweitzer Mountain and the lake.

name: Milner's Gate - Twin Falls
address: 205 Shoshone St N, Twin Falls, ID 83301
notes: Industrial-chic tri-level pub in Twin Falls center. Reinvented American pub food: good quality. Craft beer, cocktails, extensive menu. Modern look in a historic building. Local favorite. Casual atmosphere.

name: Museum of Clean
notes: A MUSEUM about cleaning. No, we aren't crazy. 70,000 objects: vacuum cleaners, laundry detergent commercials, brooms through the ages. Founded by Don Aslett, America's 'Mr. Clean'. A completely absurd concept, brilliantly executed. Pocatello. Unique. Funny. Go!

name: Niagara Springs - Wendell
notes: IMPRESSIVE waterfall in the cliffs of Snake River Canyon! Crystal-clear spring erupts from the lava rock face. FREE. Small state park. Beautiful in combination with Balanced Rock. Near Wendell along I-84. Little visited. Unexpectedly beautiful.

name: Northwest Passage Scenic Byway (US-12)
address: US-12 tussen Lewiston en Lolo Pass, ID
notes: Lewis & Clark route! Follows the Clearwater + Lochsa Rivers. Drive through the Clearwater National Forest. 202 miles from Lewiston to the Montana border. Ravers and fishing waters along the way. Autumn colors are extraordinary. Sometimes narrow and winding.

name: Oasis Bordello Museum - Wallace
notes: Last brothel in Idaho closed in 1988 - by the FBI! Still completely intact: rooms, 'work clothes', diaries. Interviewed sex workers described the atmosphere in detail. Wallace had 5 officially tolerated brothels until the 1980s! Run by the grandson of an owner. HISTORICAL AND SHAMELESS.

name: Old Idaho State Penitentiary
notes: Prison built by the prisoners themselves (1870-1973). Riots, fire, real criminals. Closed after major riots in 1973. Self-guided tours of cells and punishment chambers. Boise's most haunted attraction. Locals just call it 'The Pen'. Highly recommended.

name: PATRIOT Motorsport Adventures - St.Anthony Sand Dune Rentals
address: 867 Red Rd, St Anthony, ID 83445, USA

name: Payette Brewing - Boise
notes: Boise's most famous craft brewery! Award-winning IPAs. Nat 20 Session IPA: local favorite. Large taproom with terrace. On-site food trucks. Garden City/Boise border – popular neighborhood. Great American Beer Festival medal winners.

name: Pilgrim's Market - Coeur d'Alene
notes: Gourmet deli + restaurant with organic, local food. Yak burger is the local legend. Organic and vegan options. Juice bar, handmade ice cream, hot soup bar. Coeur d'Alene alternative foodie spot. Good value for money. Healthy and tasty.

name: Ponderosa Pine Scenic Byway (SH-21)
address: SH-21 tussen Boise en Stanley, ID
notes: 130 miles from Boise through gold-dumping history to Sawtooth. Idaho City en route: gold rush town with panning for gold. Boise National Forest canopies of Ponderosa pines. Lowman: hot springs access and rest. Autumn: MAGNIFICENT spectacle of colors.

name: Redfish Lake
notes: One of Idaho's most beautiful lakes. Seriously special. Sawtooth Mountains reflected in turquoise water. Fjord-like canyon lake. Campsites, kayak rentals. Salmon swim upstream here (heroic - 900 km!). Stanley: 1,000 inhabitants at 1,900 m. COLD at night!

name: Riverside Hot Springs Inn & Spa - Lava Hot Springs
address: 280 E Main St, Lava Hot Springs, ID 83246
notes: Hotel with private geothermal hot spring pools! Right on the Portneuf River. Adults Only resort. Romantic and quiet. Lava Hot Springs walk-bare-feet-town atmosphere. Book well in advance of the season. Sometimes only $100/night!

name: Robert Limbert Visitor Center
address: 1266 Craters Loop Road, Arco, ID 83213, USA

name: Sawtooth National Recreation Area
notes: 756,000 acres of wild mountain landscape. 40 peaks above 3,000m. Redfish Lake - turquoise water, sawtooth backdrop. ICONIC. Hiking, fishing, kayaking, campgrounds. Sun Valley + Ketchum are the gateway. The America the Beautiful pass works here. An absolute must in summer.

name: Sawtooth Scenic Byway (SH-75)
address: SH-75 tussen Shoshone en Stanley, ID
notes: 116 miles through the heart of the Sawtooth NRA. Galena Summit: a view that makes you forget to breathe. Ketchum, Sun Valley, and Stanley along the route. Following the Salmon River at the end: epic. Best time to drive: June–Oct. Winter weather is unpredictable.

name: Schweitzer Mountain Resort - Sandpoint
notes: Northern Idaho's largest ski resort. On Ikon Pass! 2,900 acres. View over Lake Pend Oreille = WOW. Sandpoint: one of Idaho's most beautiful towns. Summer: gondola open for hikers and mountain bikers. Perfect after a visit to Coeur d'Alene.

name: Shaddow Domain - Idaho Falls
notes: Shop + museum full of curiosities and artifacts! Horror theme, vintage kitsch, strange collections. Idaho Falls' most mysterious establishment. Small, dark, fascinating. Think Weird Museum light. Combines well with the Potato Museum route.

name: Shoshone Bird Museum of Natural History
address: 323 S Rail St W, Shoshone, ID 83352
notes: Private museum with 4,000+ stuffed birds! Three generations of the Young family built this. Next to the Mammoth Cave, which they discovered themselves. 100% family-built and managed. Shoshone = small town, big taxidermy adventure.

name: Shoshone Falls
address: 4155 Shoshone Falls Grade, Twin Falls, ID 83301
notes: NIAGARA OF THE WEST - and actually 45 feet HIGHER than Niagara! 212 feet high, 900 feet wide at Snake River. Best visited: spring (snowmelt) - spectacular volume. Summer: less water but always beautiful. Twin Falls day trip essential. State park entrance.

name: Shoshone Ice Caves
notes: 1,000-foot lava tube with ice - all year round! Temperature: -8 to 0°C. In the summer! Bring a coat. Known as 'spooky' - footsteps and voices heard. Indian princess Edahow buried here? No one knows. Most visited: May-Sept. Next to Craters of the Moon!

name: Skydive Sun Valley
address: Hailey Airport, 803 Airport Rd, Hailey, ID 83333
notes: Tandem skydive over the Sawtooth Mountains! Hailey Airport next to Sun Valley resort. Drops from 15,000 feet. 60-second free fall. Sawtooth panorama from the air = surreal. Summer only. Book early in the season.

name: Soda Springs Geyser (Controlled)
notes: THE ONLY controlled geyser in the world! Timered. Goes off every hour. Warm spring water gushes upwards. Accidentally drilled in 1937 during swimming pool construction. FREE to see from the parking lot. Soda Springs = charming little carbonate water town.

name: Spirit of Boise Balloon Classic
address: Ann Morrison Park, 1000 Americana Blvd, Boise, ID 83702
notes: Annual balloon festival in Ann Morrison Park, Boise! Last weekend in August. Morning launches + Nite Glow Spectacular. Dozens of balloons. Free to watch. Since 1991. One of Boise's most beloved events. If the timing is right (Aug): ABSOLUTELY catch it!

name: SpringHill Suites by Marriott Idaho Falls
address: 665 River Walk Dr, Idaho Falls, ID 83402, USA

name: SpringHill Suites by Marriott Island Park Yellowstone
SpringHill Suites by Marriott Rexburg
address: 1177 S Yellowstone Hwy, Rexburg, ID 83440, USA

name: Sun Meadow Resort - Worley
notes: AANR naturist resort in North Idaho forest pines! 75 acres. Two pools (indoor + outdoor) + large spa. Western Naturist Gathering location. Family-friendly. Completely cloth-free: everyone join in! Near Coeur d'Alene. Camping + lodge rooms.

name: Sun Valley Resort ⛷️ Ikon
address: 1 Sun Valley Rd, Sun Valley, ID 83353
notes: Ikon Pass: 7 DAYS. Ski trip starting point! Dollar Mountain = BEST place for beginners in the Northwest. Treeless, wide, quiet, and separated from the main mountain. Serge: Bald Mountain = beautiful bowls + groomed runs. Town Ketchum = more affordable than Sun Valley Village itself. Book lessons for Els immediately upon arrival!

name: Sun Valley Ski Resort
address: Sun Valley Rd, Sun Valley, ID 83353
notes: IKON PASS! America's first chairlift (1936). Bald Mountain. 7 lifted days included on Ikon. Dollar Mountain for beginners. Warren Miller filmed here for decades. Sun Valley: glamour + authentic mountain town mix. Ketchum next door. Hemingway's favorite hangout.

name: Sunbeam Hot Springs
notes: Geothermal springs flowing directly into the Salmon River! Natural stone pools on the riverbank. FREE. Clothing-optional atmosphere (remote location). Near Stanley – combine with Redfish Lake and Sawtooth drives. Accessible in winter too – contrast of warm water and snow!

name: The Cedars Floating Restaurant - Coeur d'Alene
notes: The region's only FLOATING restaurant! 1.2 million pound artificial island on the Spokane River head. Prime rib and fresh fish are the stars. Surrounding Coeur d'Alene lake views. Reserve. Unique concept, solid food.

name: The Limelight Hotel - Ketchum/Sun Valley
notes: Boutique hotel in the heart of Ketchum/Sun Valley. Skiers' favorite with a modern mountain aesthetic. Walking distance from the Hemingway bar (Sun Valley Lodge). Winter: premium prices. Off-season: more affordable. Mountain modern design, good service.

name: The Warehouse - Boise (lifestyle club)
notes: Treasure Valley's only private lifestyle social club! Kink and swingers. BYOB facility. Themed nights: Rainbow Rave, Pineapple Nights, etc. Members-only: vetting required via website. 18+. Dress code. Consent-first policy. Pre-registration required.

name: Turf Club Twin Falls
address: 195 River Vista Place, Twin Falls, ID 83301
notes: Fine dining WITH a hidden speakeasy bar! Snake River Canyon view. Reimagined steakhouse classics. Seasonal local produce. Speakeasy: behind a secret door in the lounge! Book in advance. The Canyon side is the most beautiful. One of Idaho's best restaurant concepts.

name: Wallace Brewing Company - Wallace
notes: Microbrewery in the heart of the historic silver city of Wallace! RedLight Irish Red Ale + 1910 Black Lager are top choices. No in-house kitchen – but The 1313 Club is next door. 1313 Club: poutine is legendary. Combine with the Center of Universe and Bordello Museum!

name: Warfield Distillery & Brewery - Ketchum
notes: Brewery + distillery combination in the Sun Valley region. Ketchum's hippest spot. Local crowd and skiers. House spirits + craft beer. No choice needed! Combo with Hemingway's grave for a themed day. Open year-round. Mountain town charm.

name: Weir Creek Hot Springs
notes: Hidden hot springs ALONG the Lochsa River! Short and easy trail (< 1 mile). Clothing-optional atmosphere. Near the Northwest Passage Scenic Byway (US-12). Lochsa River = famous whitewater + wild nature. FREE. Good alternative to Goldbug style.

name: Yellowstone Zone of Death (ID kant)
address: Zone of Death Trailhead, Island Park, ID 83429
notes: Legal TRAP: 50 km² Idaho side of Yellowstone. Due to federal jury requirements, murder can go unpunished here! Constitutional vacuum discovered by law professors. Never tested. Fortunately. FREE entry. Feeling a bit anxious is normal.

name: Al's #1 Italian Beef - Chicago
notes: Inventor of the CHICAGO ITALIAN BEEF sandwich (1938)! Dip your bun in the cooking liquid. 'Wet' or 'dry' is the choice. Taylor Street, Little Italy. Legendary address. Guaranteed queue. Cash register on the outside. The Bear TV series made this dish cool again. But Al's was there first.

name: Alinea - Chicago
notes: 3 Michelin stars. Molecular gastronomy theater. Grant Achatz: food as art-performance. 16-22 courses. Wednesday-Sunday. Reservations required months in advance. WORLD'S best restaurant in various rankings. For a special occasion: birthdays in 1969 perhaps?

name: American Oddities Museum - Alton
notes: Stuffed 'mermaid', vampire coffin, hundreds of bizarre objects! Private museum of pure roadside curiosities. Alton = Illinois' most bizarre town (also the most 'haunted'). Serious competition for Ripley's, but local and authentic. Combine with Wadlow Statue for Alton Day.

name: Anderson Japanese Gardens - Rockford
notes: Best Japanese garden outside Japan – according to the experts! Designed by Hoichi Kurisu. Waterfalls, teahouse, rock formations. Rockford, 90 min from Chicago. Spring: cherry blossoms. Summer: lush greenery. Japanese culture workshops all year round.

name: Bishop Hill Swedish Colony
notes: Utopian Swedish religious community founded in 1846! The entire village is now a historic landmark. Swedish shops, artisans, P.L. Johnson's restaurant. Bishop Hill: 125 inhabitants. Completely out of this world. Christmas here = magical Scandinavian idyll.

name: Blue Lake Resort - Erie
notes: Illinois' ONLY AANR-affiliated naturist resort! 20 acres in Rock River Valley, NW Illinois, 2 hours from Chicago. Swimming lake, jacuzzi, volleyball, camping + rooms. NOT clothing-optional - full nudity mandatory! (Practically Belgian.) May through October. Book in advance. +1-309-507-6897.

name: Cahokia Mounds UNESCO
notes: Prehistoric city larger than medieval London! 20,000+ inhabitants between 700-1400 AD. UNESCO World Heritage Site. 80 earthen mounds surrounding a large square. Woodhenge. FREE! Visitor center with explanations. Collinsville, just outside St. Louis. Most underrated site in the US.

name: Casey World's Largest Things
notes: One small town - TWELVE world's largest records! Giant rocking chair (56ft), barber pole, golf ball, key, corn fork... All invented by one man: Jim Bolin. Casey's Casey Welcome Center provides a map of all locations. FREE. Route I-70 Exit 129. Allow 2 hours. ABSOLUTELY DO IT!

name: Chicago Architecture Helicopter Tour
notes: Helicopter over Chicago's iconic skyline! Lake Michigan, Millennium Park, Navy Pier from above. Departure from Midway or Meigs Field area. Various operators available. Sunset flight = absolute top photos for @roamingbonbons.

name: Chicago Riverwalk
address: Wacker Dr & Michigan Ave, Chicago, IL 60601
notes: 1.25-mile promenade along the Chicago River in the city center! Kayak rentals, restaurants, art, fountains. FREE walking. Architecture tours depart from here. Best view of the Chicago skyline: Riverwalk sunset. Combine with the Architecture Boat Tour for a complete river experience.

name: Chicago Skydeck - Willis Tower
notes: 412 meters high on protruding glass balconies! Skydeck Chicago on the 103rd floor. View of 4 states. Glass floor-balconies: literally AIR under your feet. Sears Tower = Willis Tower. Formerly the tallest building in the world. Book online. Avoid rush hour.

name: Cross at the Crossroads - Effingham
notes: 198-foot-tall METAL CROSS - just barely no FAA permit required! 'Cross at the Crossroads': exactly 1 foot below the aviation limit. Visible from the I-57 and I-70 intersection. FREE. Effingham, central Illinois. Whether you are religious or not - it is impressive.

name: Fermilab - Batavia
notes: Particle accelerator where the Higgs boson was almost discovered! Freely accessible grounds with a herd of buffalo on the lawn. Wilson Hall observation deck: free. Visitor center with explanations. Batavia, 45 min from Chicago. Where quantum physics and bison become friends.

name: Friends Night Out (FNO) - Aurora/Chicago
notes: Private members-only lifestyle club in the Chicago area! On-premise and off-premise events. BYOB facility. Aurora location. Theme nights, mixers. Vetting via website required. More of an 'adult social club' style than a hard swinger club.

name: Garden of the Gods - Shawnee
address: Garden of the Gods Rd, Herod, IL 62947
notes: Spectacular sandstone rock formations in Southern Illinois! Millions of years of erosion. Hiking trails between the rocks. Shawnee National Forest. FREE. America the Beautiful pass. Herod, the southernmost tip of Illinois – another world. Spring and autumn: perfect weather conditions.

name: Gemini Giant Muffler Man - Wilmington
notes: Astronaut Muffler Man with rocket - along Route 66! Gemini Giant (1965) at the Launching Pad Drive-In. Classic fiberglass Muffler Man converted into an astronaut. Wilmington, Route 66, I-55. FREE photo stop. Iconic image of the Space Race era Americana.

name: Girl & the Goat - Chicago
notes: Stephanie Izard's James Beard Award restaurant! Serves small plates full of creative flavors. Everything wood-fired. West Loop restaurant row. Warm, busy, delicious. Book far in advance—months sometimes. Top Chef winner. Goat dishes are the star. Amazing.

name: Goose Island Salt Shed BrewPub - Chicago
notes: Chicago's most famous craft brewery! Bourbon County Stout. Clybourn Ave taproom: original location since 1988. Brewery tours available. Barrel aging program. Bourbon County Stout = annual event (Black Friday release). Now part of AB InBev, but has remained top quality.

name: Green Mill Jazz Club - Chicago
notes: Al Capone's FAVORITE speakeasy - now a legendary jazz club! Opened in 1907. Capone had his own table with a view of both doors. Still live jazz every night. Uptown neighborhood. Sundays: Poetry Slam (for over 35 years!). One of the best-preserved authentic jazz venues in the US.

name: Haymarket Pub & Brewery - Chicago
notes: Haymarket Pub & Brewery in the Pilsen Corridor! Beers brewed after Chicago labor history. Haymarket Riot (1886) = theme. Historic and tasty. Large taproom. Pub food. Politically conscious beer. Pilsen neighborhood: Chicago's Mexican-American cultural heart.

name: Hippie Memorial - Arcola
notes: Bob Moomaw's conceptual anti-Reagan monument full of 60s memorabilia! Scooters, murals, hippie paraphernalia, Volkswagen vans. Private property, but visible from the road. Arcola: also known as the 'Broomcorn Capital of the World'. FREE. Early in the morning for the best light.

name: Kaskaskia Dragon - Vandalia
notes: 11-meter metal dragon that REALLY breathes FIRE! Coins in the slot = dragon blows flames. Spectacular! Vandalia, central Illinois. FREE to see, pay for fire. Under a bridge along the road. Don't underestimate it. Kids go completely wild. So do we.

name: Koval Distillery - Chicago
notes: Chicago's FIRST micro-distillery after Prohibition (2008)! Organic grains, single barrel. Whiskey, gin, liqueurs. Ravenswood, Chicago North. Tours + tastings. Winner of international awards. Owners are former ethics professors! Pure story.

name: Leaning Tower of Niles
notes: 94-foot-tall REPLICA of the Leaning Tower of Pisa - in Illinois! Built in 1934 as decoration for a swimming pool. Seriously. Niles, northern Chicago suburb. FREE to view. No line (this isn't Italy). Even more crooked than the original in some photo angles.

name: Lifestyle Playtime - Chicago
notes: Chicago's premium swingers event organizer! Private venue in the Chicago area. Couples and select singles. Theme events, couples' nights, parties. Register via website + vetting. The Chicago lifestyle scene is active and well-organized.

name: Lou Mitchell's - Chicago
notes: Breakfast legend since 1923 - Route 66 starting point! Free Milk Duds upon entry. Free donut for ladies. Marble rye toast + egg dish + coffee = Chicago morning. Jackson Blvd, close to the Route 66 start. Wait in line. Cash recommended. Pure nostalgia.

name: Luna Café - Granite City
address: 201 E Chain of Rocks Rd, Granite City, IL 62040
notes: Al Capone's Route 66 hangout – now a restaurant! Opened in 1924. Capone had a secret meeting room there. Dishes named after gangsters. Themed menu. Route 66 museum atmosphere while you eat. Granite City, just across the St. Louis Bridge.

name: Metropolis Superman Museum
notes: Superman's OFFICIAL hometown - Illinois declared it law! 15-foot-tall Superman bronze statue in the town square. Super Museum: 70,000+ Superman items in one place. Local newspaper is called the 'Metropolis Planet'. Really. Right next to the Mississippi. Stop on the way to Kentucky.

name: Moonshine, Illinois
notes: Town with 2 inhabitants and 1 building - but WORLD-FAMOUS citizens! Moonshine Store: open Friday + weekend. A place of pilgrimage for decades. In the middle of the absolute middle of nowhere in Illinois. 'Best burger in the state' - say visitors who drive there specifically. Call for opening hours. Cash. Small. Unforgettable.

name: Nine Mile Prairie - Springfield area
notes: Rim Rock + Pounds Hollow in Shawnee National Forest! Hiking trails through hills, forests, and waterfalls. Southern Illinois has a completely different character from the rest. FREE. Unpaved roads to the most beautiful spots. Autumn: beautiful foliage. Spring: wildflowers.

name: Oz Park - Chicago
notes: City park COMPLETELY dedicated to the Wizard of Oz! Life-size bronze Dorothy, Tin Man, Cowardly Lion, Scarecrow. Lincoln Park neighborhood, Chicago. FREE. Charming and completely unexpected. Who expects an Oz temple in Chicago?

name: Pequod's Pizza - Chicago
notes: Yelp's #1 pizza in the US 2024! Deep dish with a caramelized crust. The cheese melts on the edges = crispy + soft in one bite. Lincoln Park location + Morton Grove original. Wait in line. It is worth the wait. Seriously. Italian beef on the pizza: Chicago combination that changes your life.

name: Pink Elephant Antique Mall - Livingston
notes: Giant pink elephant + ice cream stand + bizarre kitsch statues outside! Route 66 roadside classic at its absolute best. Inside: endless rooms full of vintage Americana. I-55, halfway between Springfield and St. Louis. FREE to view from the outside. Shopping costs whatever it takes.

name: Pizzeria Uno - Chicago
notes: Where deep dish pizza was INVENTED in 1943! Rudy Malnati Sr. came up with the recipe here. Historic. River North. Tourists come, locals sniff – but it is authentic. Order takes 45 min – pizza needs to bake. Patience! A historic must-do for every Chicago visitor.

name: Revolution Brewing - Chicago
