notes: Chicago's largest independent craft brewery! Anti-Hero IPA = their icon. Various seasonal releases. Logan Square. Large taproom + full restaurant. Produce 100,000 kegs per year - truly huge. Milwaukee Avenue taproom = best atmosphere.

name: Robert Wadlow Statue - Alton
notes: Life-size statue of the TALLEST man ever! Robert Wadlow (1918-1940): 2.72 m and still growing when he died. Bronze statue to his exact scale - shockingly large. Alton, Mississippi River. Free. Combine with the nearby American Oddities Museum.

name: Route 66 Corridor - Chicago to Springfield
address: Adams St, Chicago tot Springfield, IL
notes: Starting point of the MOTHER ROAD: Chicago to Springfield! Adam Street in Chicago = official starting point of Route 66. Dwight, Pontiac, Bloomington, Lincoln, Springfield. Pontiac: free Route 66 Museum + Walldog murals. Note: follow the old 'alignment' for the true Route 66 atmosphere.

name: Shawnee Hills Wine Trail
notes: 16+ wineries in the rolling South of Illinois! Autumn: grape harvest + foliage = perfect combination. Some wineries also host festivals in September-October. Pomona, Alto Pass, Cobden - charming small communities. A good alternative to Napa if you are driving through Illinois anyway.

name: Superdawg Drive-In - Chicago
notes: Drive-in hotdog stand with stuffed animals on the roof since 1948! Maurice and Flaurie - hotdog couple look down on customers. Chicago-style hotdog: NEVER ketchup. Only mustard + vegetables. NW Chicago. Curb service the original way. American heritage at its most animalistic.

name: The Palmer House Hilton - Chicago
notes: Chicago's oldest hotel (1871) - rebuilt after the Great Chicago Fire! BIRTHPLACE of the chocolate brownie (1893)! Fabulous Loop lobby: frescoed ceilings, crystal chandeliers. Historic + luxury + central Loop location. Name: Palmer House. Visited before? Then a nostalgic return.

name: Volo Auto Museum
notes: 500+ vintage cars + movie vehicles + celebrity cars! Batmobile, Ghostbusters Ecto-1, Back to the Future DeLorean. Creepy doll collection as a bonus. Harvest Hosts location. Volo, 1 hour north of Chicago. Kids and parents alike will go wild.

name: World's Largest Catsup Bottle
notes: 170-foot-tall ketchup bottle as a roadside water tower! Built in 1949 as an advertisement for Brooks Catsup. Never demolished. Now protected as a historic landmark. Locals are proud of it. Collinsville, 15 min from St. Louis. Free photo stop. The Statue of Liberty for hot dog lovers.

name: Wrigley Rooftops B&B-stijl - Chicago
notes: Rooftop stands ABOVE the Cubs - unique Chicago sports experience! Houses next to Wrigley Field rent out rooftop seats. Sleep with a view of the field as a bonus. Somber or festive depending on the Cubs results. Phenomenal content for @roamingbonbons baseball episode.

name: Amish Country - Shipshewana/Middlebury
notes: Largest Amish community outside Ohio and Pennsylvania! Horse-and-wagons in traffic. No electricity. Shipshewana Market: Wednesday + Friday. Grand and authentic. Amish quilts, furniture, cakes: honest, top quality. NE Indiana. Time travel to 1850. No irony.

name: Bluespring Caverns - Bedford
notes: Longest navigable underground river in the US! Boat tour through the illuminated caves. Blind fish swim along. Bedford (Limestone Capital of the World). Families + geologist types: this is the place for you. Guided boat tours every hour. Open year-round.

name: Bob Ross Experience - Muncie
notes: ORIGINAL studio where The Joy of Painting was filmed! Recreated interior. Dozens of Bob Ross paintings. Interactive exhibition. Make your own 'happy trees'. Minnetrista Museum on the Ball family estate. Muncie, 1 hour from Indianapolis. Pilgrimage for a generation.

name: Cloud Country Balloon Rides - Indianapolis
notes: Sunrise balloon ride over the Indiana countryside! 1-hour flight. Fields, forests, misty morning air. Indianapolis + surroundings. Small groups. Champagne toast after landing. Weather dependent. Book well in advance.

name: Clubhouse 2050 - Indianapolis
notes: Members-only lifestyle club for swingers, BDSM, and exhibitionists! Private rooms available on-premise. Couples and singles welcome. Find us via Kasidie ​​+ sign up. Indianapolis. Broad crowd: from curious to experienced.

name: Columbus Indiana - Architectuur Stad
notes: Small city with 70+ buildings by WORLD-FAMOUS architects! I.M. Pei, Eero Saarinen, Richard Meere in one small town. 6th wealthiest concentration of architecture in the US. Architecture tour of the city center = a must. Why here? Cummins Engine paid the best architects. Period.

name: Conner Prairie Living History Museum
notes: Interactive historical park where you STEP into the story! 1836 Indiana. Actors stay completely in character. Balloons, animals, forge, prairie life. Fishers, just north of Indianapolis. Best living history museum in the Midwest. Really.

name: DeBrand Fine Chocolates Tour - Fort Wayne
address: 560 E Dupont Rd, Fort Wayne, IN 46825
notes: CHOCOLATE FACTORY TOUR + tasting in Indiana! DeBrand: award-winning fine chocolates. Made in Fort Wayne. Factory tour through glass walls to see how it is made. Serge: this is Belgian-level quality, but Hoosier. Fort Wayne. Tours multiple times a day. MANDATORY.

name: Fair Oaks Farms - Fair Oaks
notes: Largest working farm as a TOURIST ATTRACTION! 36,000 cows. Cheese production. Calf birth camera. Adventure Dairy, Pig Adventure, Crop Adventure. Fair Oaks, NW Indiana along I-65. Children: overwhelmed. Adults: too. Unique concept.

name: Fern Hills Club - Bloomington
notes: Indiana's most famous AANR naturist resort! 83 acres of hardwood forest in the hills of S-Indiana. 52-foot round pool. Volleyball, petanque, shuffleboard. Couples and families welcome. Call first. Blooming-ton area. Spring through October. 100% AANR.

name: Flick Statue - Hammond
address: South Shore Welcome Center, Hammond, IN 46320
notes: Bronze statue of the tongue-frozen Flick! From A Christmas Story - the triple-dog-dare tongue-frozen pole scene. The film is set in North Indiana. This is Flick's hometown. South Shore Welcome Center. FREE. Christmas season: extra fitting. No licking the pole.

name: Grabill Country Sales - Grabill
notes: Bakery + department store FULL of stuffed animals! Amish area of ​​Indiana. Totally unexpected taxidermy. Cheerful atmosphere despite the hundreds of dead stares. Grabill, NE Indiana Amish country. FREE to visit as a shop. Also buy Amish pie.

name: Grave in the Road - Franklin
notes: A GRAVE in the middle of the road - cars drive around it! Nancy Barnett buried on a hill in 1831. The family defended the grave with a rifle when they wanted to build a road. The state built two lanes AROUND it. FREE. Franklin, 30 min from Indianapolis. Short stop.

name: Hall of Heroes Superhero Museum - Elkhart
notes: FIRST superhero museum in the world - in a barn in Indiana! Originally founded by one fan. Now thousands of items. Original Batman cowl, rare comics, superhero merchandise. Elkhart, Northern Indiana. Small but absolutely unique. Comic book fans: this is Mecca. Don't miss it.

name: Holiday World Resort Cabins - Santa Claus
address: 452 E Christmas Blvd, Santa Claus, IN 47579
notes: Sleep IN Santa Claus's amusement park resort! Holiday World = one of the best theme parks in the USA. Splashin' Safari water park included. Christmas theme all year round. Honestly, that is. Summer only. Early booking required.

name: Indiana Dunes National Park
address: 1100 N Mineral Springs Rd, Porter, IN 46304
notes: NATIONAL PARK on Lake Michigan - no one knows it exists! Sand dunes up to 60 meters high right by the lake. Mount Baldy: living dune that swallowed a child (and survived). America the Beautiful pass valid! 90 min from Chicago. Best addition to a visit to Chicago.

name: Indiana Medical History Museum - Indy
notes: Psychiatric hospital frozen in time (1896-1994)! Original laboratories, autopsy theater, medical instruments. Left completely intact. Slightly creepy. Indianapolis. Limited opening hours - check in advance. For medical history nerds: Mecca. For others: genuinely fascinating.

name: Indiana Statehouse Architecture + Soldiers Monument
notes: Impressive City Hall with a free tour! Soldiers & Sailors Monument: 86 meters high with an observation platform. Top: free elevator ride up. Indianapolis panorama. FREE. Monument Circle = heart of Indianapolis. Great American monumental tradition at its best.

name: Indianapolis Motor Speedway + Aviation
notes: Indy 500 home – holiest track in the USA! IMS Museum with historic race cars. Hall of Fame. Track tours: driving on real asphalt! Indy 500 in May = a whole different world. Museum year-round. Track tours on request.

name: Iozzo's Garden of Italy - Indianapolis
notes: Italian restaurant with a heritage dating back to the 1900s! Fred Iozzo's granddaughter runs it now. Authentic recipes. Legendary meatballs. Homemade desserts. Won 'Best New Restaurant' + 'Best Italian' awards. S Meridian, Indianapolis. Reserve.

name: John's Famous Stew - Indianapolis
notes: The same stew on the menu for over 100 years! Indianapolis legend. Pork tenderloins, stews, peach cobbler that makes you cry. Kentucky Avenue. Cheap, authentic, local. The oldest restaurant in Indianapolis that hasn't changed at all. Lunch crowds are huge. Go early.

name: Kiwanis Indiana Balloon Fest - Bedford
notes: Big balloon festival in September with Pyromaniac skydivers! Spark-performing parachutists in the evening. Seriously. Dozens of hot air balloons. Night Glow + daytime launches. Bedford, South Indiana. September. Free parking. Beer and wine garden.

name: KokoMantis - Kokomo
notes: Giant Praying Mantis sculpture in the city center! Kokomo named it after its own name. Makes sense. Combine with Old Ben (the world's largest preserved bull)! Kokomo: more bizarre things than you expect. FREE photo stop. Kokomo Center. Quick to do.

name: Market Street Catacombs - Indianapolis
notes: REAL catacombs beneath the streets of Indianapolis! 20,000 m² tunnel network from the 1880s. Originally for cooling and storage. Limited tours available through Historic Indianapolis. FREE to know they exist. Book tours via website.

name: Milktooth - Indianapolis
notes: Award-winning breakfast restaurant with James Beard nominations! Creative brunch menu. Seasonal local produce. Fletcher Place neighborhood. Small space, big expectations. Weekend lines are epic. Weekday: better. Indianapolis' most renowned restaurant for breakfast.

name: New Harmony - Utopian Ghost Town
notes: Two utopian communes in the same location (1814 + 1825)! Rappites + Owenites built a dream – both failed. Roofless Church: open-air cathedral for all faiths. Labyrinth, historic buildings, silkworms. SW Indiana, 30 min from Evansville. Unknown but special.

name: Old Ben - World's Largest Steer - Kokomo
notes: Preserved bull of 1,100 kg in a city park! Old Ben lived 1902-1910. Weighed: more than any other bull. Now mounted behind glass in Highland Park. FREE. Park in the park and walk to the stable door. Kokomo: more bizarre than you thought. Always.

name: Pigeon River Fish Hatchery
notes: Indiana's largest warm-water fish farm! You can see the tanks full of trout. FREE. Mongo, NE Indiana. Small but unexpected. Combine with Amish Country drives. Quick stop. Kids love it.

name: Potato Creek State Park - North Liberty
notes: State park where finding real GOLD is possible! Gold panning in the creek is a legal activity here. Kayaking, cycling, hiking, camping. North Liberty, 20 min from South Bend. Children: gold fever. Adults: a bit too.

name: Reel One Indy - Indianapolis
notes: Indiana's oldest and only woman-owned lifestyle club (est. 1992)! 3 floors + 16,000 m² facility. Really big. Open Wednesday + Friday + Saturday. Couples and singles. On-premise. Longest-running club in the state. Call ahead.

name: Rotary Jail Museum - Crawfordsville
notes: ROTATING PRISON - the only one that still really rotates! Built in 1882. Cells rotate like a carousel. 32 tons of iron rotated via a single lever. Brilliant and dangerous. Prisoners lost fingers in the mechanism. Oops. Crawfordsville, 45 min from Indianapolis. Must see!

name: Santa Claus Brewing Company
address: 7200 E CR 1450 N, Santa Claus, IN 47579
notes: Brewery IN the city of Santa Claus - as unique as it sounds! Christmas-themed beer + good food all year round. Near Holiday World theme park. Want to taste Christmas in August? You can here. Unique location. Good beers. Weird but amazing.

name: Santa Claus, Indiana
notes: A CITY officially named Santa Claus! All year round. The post office stamps all mail with 'Santa Claus IN'. Santa's territory: Christmas atmosphere in August. The Holiday World theme park is here—one of the best in the US! Summer: Splashin' Safari water park. Perfect stopover.

name: Shapiro's Deli - Indianapolis
notes: Legendary Jewish deli in Indianapolis – since 1905! Corned beef, pastrami, matzo ball soup. Self-service cafeteria style. Portion sizes are inhuman. S Meridian St. Lunch favorite of locals. Best deli outside New York? Many say yes.

name: Sun Aura Resort - Lake Village
notes: 300-acre clothing-optional resort in Northern Indiana! Since the 1930s. RV + tent camping. Lake Village, close to the Illinois border. 21+ only. Couples and singles welcome. I-65 route - convenient stopover.

name: Sun King Brewing - Indianapolis
notes: Indianapolis' largest and most award-winning craft brewery! Sunlight Cream Ale + Wee Mac Scottish Ale are the classics. 3-building campus downtown Indianapolis. Great American Beer Festival medalists. Live music + food. Ideal post-IMS race stop.

name: Sun Shower Country Club
notes: 120+ acres naturist resort in North Indiana woods! Swimming pool, hiking trails, peaceful atmosphere. Roselawn, NW Indiana. Family-friendly. AANR affiliated. Easily accessible from the Chicago Corridor.

name: The Prewitt Restaurant & Lounge - Columbus
notes: Fine dining in a renovated 1920s cinema! Green eggs and ham on the breakfast menu. Seriously. Rooftop igloos in winter for private tables. Columbus: combine with an architecture tour. Creative American menu. Best diner in town.

name: Three Floyds Brewing - Munster
notes: Indiana's MOST FAMOUS craft brewery - top 20 nationally! Zombie Dust, Alpha King, Gumballhead, Dark Lord (legendary). Brewpub next to the brewery. Distillery as well. Munster, NW Indiana, near the Chicago border. Dark Lord Day = annual pilgrimage day for beer geeks.

name: Turkey Run State Park
notes: Spectacular sandstone canyons + hanging back hikes! Turkey Run State Park: Indiana's most beautiful state park. Suspension bridges over gorges. Scramble through gullies. Marshall, IN. Autumn: beautiful foliage. America the Beautiful pass NOT valid - state park.

name: Upland Brewing - Bloomington
notes: Indiana University's favorite craft brewery! Tart & Funk program: wild fermentations, sour beers. Bloomington campus town atmosphere. Groote taproom. Combine with a visit to Fern Hills naturist resort. Strawberry Wheat is their bestseller.

name: West Baden Springs Hotel
address: 8538 W Baden Ave, West Baden Springs, IN 47469
notes: Stay UNDER the largest church dome ever built! French Lick Resort complex. Casino. Spa. 5-star service. West Baden + French Lick = double resort day. SW Indiana, 2 hours from Indianapolis. Fairytale historic. One night minimum for the experience.

name: World's Largest Ball of Paint
address: 10696 N County Rd 200 W, Alexandria, IN 46001
notes: Started as a baseball in 1977. Now a 2,700kg MONSTER PAINTBALL! 27,000+ layers of paint. Almost spherical. Almost. YOU GET TO paint a layer - choose your own color! Private barn in Alexandria. Call/email for an appointment. FREE (donations welcome). Pure American obsession. REQUIRED.

name: Wyandotte Caves
address: 7315 S Wyandotte Cave Rd, Leavenworth, IN 47137
notes: Prehistoric caveman caves in South Indiana! Monument Mountain: largest underground mountain in the US. Amber-colored stalactite formations. Early prehistoric use. Leavenworth area. Harrison Crawford State Forest. Guided tours. Combines well with Bluespring Caverns.

name: Yats - Cajun/Creole - Columbus
notes: Cajun & Creole cuisine in the architectural capital of Indiana! Jambalaya, red beans, gumbo - New Orleans in Columbus IN. Affordable, authentic, locally loved. Columbus: also take an architecture tour while you're there. Simple concept, great flavors.

name: 7 Hills Brewing - Dubuque
notes: Dubuque's creative craft brewery with a view of the brewery! Open kitchen concept for beer. See the equipment while you drink. Brisket burgers + mac & cheese variations. Dubuque. Millwork District atmosphere. Combine with Brazen restaurant for a Dubuque day.

name: Albert the Bull - Audubon
notes: 30-ton concrete bull - the largest in the world! Built in 1964 as a symbol of Audubon County cattle ranching. FREE. Along US-71. Quick stop for an epic photo. Audubon, central Iowa. Everything in Iowa has a 'world's largest'. Combine with Squirrel Cage Jail for a bizarre Iowa day.

name: Amana Colonies
notes: 7 villages founded by a religious community (1855) - now a tourist destination! German immigrants. Wool, furniture, wine, beer - everything homemade. Ox Yoke Inn Restaurant: all-you-can-eat German dinner. Legendary. Amana, E-Iowa near I-80. The perfect time to relax on the Chicago-Des Moines route.

name: American Gothic House - Eldon
notes: THE house from Grant Wood's famous painting (1930)! You can stand in front of the house with a pitchfork - cost: free. Small visitor's room with a backdrop of the painting. Eldon, SE Iowa. The house is habitable and private - exterior only. For every art lover: a pilgrimage. For others: recognition.

name: Balloon Rides Iowa - Des Moines Area
notes: Sunrise balloon ride over the Iowa farmlands! Des Moines and surroundings. Champagne landing. Corn, soybeans, and wind turbines from above—truly beautiful. Spring and summer. Weather dependent. Book in advance. Small groups.

name: Big Grove Brewery - Iowa City/Des Moines
address: 1225 S Gilbert St, Iowa City, IA 52240
notes: Iowa's best farm-to-table craft brewery! Local ingredients for both beer and food. Award-winning. Iowa City: large patio + fire pits + play area for children. Des Moines + Cedar Rapids locations too. Thai green curry + IPA = unexpected but perfect combo.

name: Biggest Collection of Salt & Pepper Shakers - Traer
notes: 16,000+ sets of salt and pepper shakers! Started in 1948. Ruth Rasmussen started this as a hobby. Never stopped. Traer, central Iowa. Small farming town. FREE (small donation appreciated). For lovers of the absurd: this is the pinnacle.

name: Black Angel - Iowa City Cemetery
notes: Bronze angel that turned BLACK after decades - no one knows why! Ursula Feldvary's gravestone (1912). Once gold-colored, now raven black. Legend: kisses the dead on the spot. Pregnant women are not allowed to approach. Oakland Cemetery, Iowa City. FREE. For a bronze thing: oppressively present.

name: Brazen Open Kitchen - Dubuque
notes: Farm-to-table restaurant with an OPEN kitchen – you can see everything! Chef Kevin Scharpf: no freezer, everything fresh and local. Millwork District, Dubuque. Industrial-chic interior. Menu changes constantly with the season. Perhaps the best restaurant in Iowa. Make a reservation.

name: Breitbach's Country Dining - Balltown
notes: Iowa's OLDEST restaurant + bar - opened in 1852! Fat Germans built this on a hill overlooking Mississippi. All-you-can-eat Irish stew, Iowa catfish, bratwurst. Balltown: 75 inhabitants. View over Mississippi: dazzling. Miss Guy Fieri passed through here. Cash only. Go early.

name: Buddy Holly Crash Site - Clear Lake
address: Gull Ave & 315th St, Clear Lake, IA 50428
notes: Airfield from which the plane carrying Buddy Holly, Valens, and Bopper departed! February 3, 1959. Clear Lake is 10 minutes from Mason City. 'The Day The Music Died' - Don McLean's American Pie is about this. Memorial at the cornfield where it crashed. FREE. Combine with Surf Ballroom. Emotional but historic.

name: Captain Kirk Future Birthplace - Riverside
notes: Kirk was born HERE on March 22, 2228 – officially Star Trek canon! Riverside declared it themselves in 1985. Gene Roddenberry said OK. Bronze Kirk statue + USS Riverside model + Voyage Home Museum. In bloom: Trek Fest in June – Trekkies from everywhere. FREE monument. Museum: small entrance fee. Pure genius of a small town with 900 inhabitants.

name: Club G Lifestyle Club - Des Moines
notes: Des Moines' only private lifestyle club - 6,500 m²! Open every Saturday + some Fridays. Couples and singles. Members-only. Fully verified. Apply via website + wait for approval. Midwest lifestyle at its best. Far from conservative.

name: Confluence Brewing - Des Moines
address: 1235 Thomas Beck Rd, Des Moines, IA 50315
notes: Des Moines' most beloved local craft brewery! Des Moines IPA: their flagship. Bike-themed branding. Loyal to local ingredients + community events. Slipway tasting room on the Des Moines River. Cyclist-friendly: High Trestle Trail connection.

name: Decorah Eagles / Vesterheim Museum
notes: Vesterheim: the world's most comprehensive Norwegian-American museum! Decorah is the 'capital' of Norwegian-American heritage. Calfskin, rosemaling, Viking ships—all here. Decorah in NE Iowa: an almost Scandinavian landscape. Bald-legged eagles nest here in large numbers during the winter.

name: Elwood - World's Largest Concrete Gnome
address: Reiman Gardens, 1407 University Blvd, Ames, IA 50011
notes: Elwood: 15-foot-tall concrete gnome with a pointed hat! Beat all other concrete gnomes by meters. Ames, Iowa State University city. FREE. Ames City Centre. Combine with an Iowa State campus visit.

name: Fenelon Place Elevator - Dubuque
notes: SHORTEST AND STEEPEST funicular railway in the world! 65-foot-high, 296-foot-long incline - up in 35 seconds. Built in 1882 by a banker who wanted to get home faster. Dubuque. April–November. Panoramic view of Mississippi. Just $4 up and down. Uniquely American.

name: Field of Dreams Movie Site - Dyersville
notes: 'Is this Heaven? No, it's Iowa.' - Kevin Costner, 1989. Original farm + cornfield + baseball field from the movie. You CAN play on the field - gloves and balls available. Dyersville, NE Iowa. Seasonal. MLB played here in 2020! Sometimes unexpectedly dynamic. Honestly beautiful outside the hype.

name: Flying Mango - Des Moines
notes: Caribbean BBQ + live blues in Des Moines - completely unexpected! Smoked ribs, jerk chicken, mango salsa. Live blues music in the evening. The atmosphere is 100% not Iowa. Des Moines Beaverdale neighborhood. One of Iowa's most unique restaurants. Surprisingly excellent.

name: Grotto of the Redemption - West Bend
address: 300 N Broadway Ave, West Bend, IA 50597
notes: 'Eighth Wonder of the World' - 9 caves full of gemstones + fossils! Father Paul Dobberstein built this over 42 YEARS (1912-1954). Largest collection of minerals + rocks as religious art. West Bend, N-Iowa. Free walking outside. Small entrance fee for the museum. Absolutely overwhelming. Nothing comparable on Earth.

name: Hamburg Inn No. 2 - Iowa City
address: 214 N Linn St, Iowa City, IA 52245
notes: Presidential dinner with the legendary Pie Shake! Every 4 years: Iowa caucuses = every candidate eats here. Pie mixed into a milkshake. Scientifically sound. 1948. Nothing has changed. Nothing is required. Iowa City. Lunch without questions.

name: High Trestle Trail Bridge - Madrid
notes: Half-mile-long bike bridge 60 meters high - LIGHTS UP at night! Nighttime lighting makes it look like a tunnel in a mine shaft. Des Moines River Valley below. Spectacular at sunset. FREE. Madrid, 30 min from Des Moines. Bikes available via nearby rental. ICONIC Iowa.

name: Hotel Julien Dubuque
notes: Iowa's OLDEST hotel - opened in 1839! Al Capone stayed here. Mississippi River panorama. Historicly restored. Capone's Suite: stay where the gangster slept. Dubuque, E-Iowa. Riverfront location. Capone apparently had a preference for Iowa.

name: Iowa State Fair - Des Moines
address: E 30th St & E University Ave, Des Moines, IA 50317
notes: BUTTER SCULPTURE of a cow + other livestock - Iowa's holiest tradition! August. 11 days. 1 million visitors. Fried butter on a stick. Fried Oreos. Fried everything. Cattle, pig, and poultry shows. Everything Iowa. If the timing is right (Aug 2027): DO NOT SKIP. Americana at its best.

name: L.V. Campground - Coggon
notes: Iowa's only clothing-optional nudist camp - adults only! 5 acres, 25 hookups, 4 small cabins, 3 larger cabins. LGBTQ+ friendly. Various themed events. Coggon, Delaware County, 30 min from Cedar Rapids. Not an AANR, but acceptable for an Iowa stopover.

name: Loess Hills Scenic Byway
address: IA-12 langs de Missouri rivier, W-Iowa
notes: Unique loestopographic hills – only 2 places on Earth like this! Only in Iowa and China. Wind erosion created these undulating hills. West Iowa along IA-12. Spectacular prairie views. Spring: wildflowers. Autumn: golden yellow grass. FREE. Few tourists. Hidden gem of Iowa.

name: Maquoketa Caves State Park
notes: Iowa's most visited state park—and for good reason! 13 caves, including one large enough to DRIVE through. Beam rocks, stalactites, bat colonies. Maquoketa, E-Iowa. Self-guided. Autumn: bats leave the caves every evening. A spectacle.

name: Mississippi River Distilling - LeClair
notes: Small artisanal distillery along the Mississippi! Cow Boy Bourbon + River Baron Rye - local grains. LeClair: birthplace of Buffalo Bill Cody. Tours + tastings. Mississippi River view. Combine with Bald Eagle Bridge and Mississippi scenery.

name: National Balloon Classic - Indianola
notes: Annual national balloon festival in Iowa - late July/early Aug! Dozens of hot air balloons take off simultaneously. Night Glow spectacle + daytime launches. Indianola, 20 min from Des Moines. If timing is right: ride-sharing is possible! Book flights on-site.

name: Old Capitol Inn - Iowa City
notes: B&B opposite the historic Iowa State Capitol building! Victorian style, individual rooms, local breakfast. Iowa City center. Walkable to everything. Good base for Hamburg Inn breakfast + Black Angel evening. Book well in advance during football season (U of Iowa).

name: Ox Yoke Inn - Amana
notes: Legendary all-you-can-eat German buffet in the Amana Colonies! Bratwurst, sauerkraut, smoked pork - Grandma's recipe. Ox Yoke Inn has been around for decades. Tourists + locals. Amana. E-Iowa. Perfect stopover. Often fully booked on weekends - call ahead.

name: Pappajohn Sculpture Park - Des Moines
notes: Free open-air sculpture park with world-famous artists! Jaume Plensa, Richard Serra, Louise Bourgeois. 26 sculptures on 4.4 acres. FREE. In the heart of Des Moines. Surprisingly good for a cornfield state. Combine with a visit to the Des Moines Art Center.

name: Pottawattamie Squirrel Cage Jail - Council Bluffs
notes: THE ONLY three-dimensional rotating prison in the world! Rotates in a cylinder – prisoners stand still, cells rotate. Built in 1885. Can still be demonstrated as working. Council Bluffs, on the Nebraska border. Museum. 'Wheelbarrow' design = one guard for everything. Absurdly brilliant.

name: Snake Alley - Burlington
notes: Steepest and most winding street in the world - steeper than Lombard St SF! Built in 1894. 5 half + 2 quarter turns in 58 meters. 'Reptile'-like zigzags down the hill. FREE to view and walk. Burlington, Mississippi River. July: Crazy Criterium bicycle race up Snake Lane.

name: Starbucks Restaurant - Nevada, Iowa
notes: Has NOTHING to do with coffee - everything deep-fried + soft serve ice cream! Confusion guaranteed: Starbucks name, concept completely different. Burgers, fries, bizarre ice cream flavors: peach, watermelon, raspberry. Nevada IA, 30 min from Des Moines. Seasonal. Closes in winter - queue waiting for spring opening.

name: Surf Ballroom & Museum - Clear Lake
address: 460 N Shore Dr, Clear Lake, IA 50428
notes: Buddy Holly, Ritchie Valens, and The Big Bopper - LAST CONCERT Feb 3, 1959! That night they flew from Mason City. The plane crashed. 'The Day the Music Died' - Don McLean sang about it in American Pie. Surf Ballroom remains unchanged. Museum, stage, memorabilia. Clear Lake, N-Iowa. The place truly leaves you speechless.

name: Villisca Axe Murder House
notes: On June 10, 1912, 8 people, including 6 children, were murdered with an axe. Never solved. The house still stands exactly as it did then. Day tours + OVERNIGHT STAY IN THE MURDERERS' HOUSE available! 'Most haunted house in the US' - paranormal activity reported. Villisca, SW Iowa. Book for an overnight stay. Do you dare?

name: Zombie Burger + Drink Lab - Des Moines
address: 300 E Grand Ave, Des Moines, IA 50309
notes: Horror-themed burgers + zombie cocktails in Des Moines! Undead Elvis, Frankenfurter, 28 Days Later menu. Quicksand milkshakes. Dark interior. Totally wrong but so good. East Village Des Moines. Instagram-friendly. Unique. Tasty too.

name: Brandt's Meat Market - Lucas
notes: Homemade bologna from butcher Doug Brandt - right next to the Grassroots Art Center! Local meat, handmade sausage, fresh sausage. Small lunch stop in the most bizarre town in Kansas. Lucas, N-Kansas. Cash only probably. Perfect lunch after the Grassroots Art and Garden of Eden tour.

name: Castle Rock - Gove County
notes: Chalk-white rock peaks in the middle of the flat prairie - completely surreal! Smaller than Monument Rocks but just as spectacular. FREE. Unpaved road. Combine with Monument Rocks for a 1-day West Kansas chalk formation tour. Dense cluster of peaks: nature's own Stonehenge.

name: Central Standard Brewing - Wichita
notes: Award-winning European-style lagers and barrel-aged stouts! Old Town Wichita. Industrial-chic taproom. Czech Pilsner + Imperial Stout are the stars. Great American Beer Festival gold and silver medal winners. Best craft brewery atmosphere in Wichita.

name: Club G / Wichita Lifestyle (via Kasidie)
notes: Wichita lifestyle scene via Kasidie ​​and SDC platforms! No fixed local presence known - event-based. Find and sign up via Kasidie.com. Wichita has an active lifestyle community. Most discreet of the Midwest states.

name: Cozy Inn - Salina
notes: America's smallest hamburger restaurant - 12 seats max! Opened in 1922. Identical recipe ever since. Steam-cooked sliders: onion, pickle, meat. That's it. Salina, central Kansas. I-70 stop. Mandatory. Eat 6 pieces. Still unsure? Eat 8.

name: Doo-Dah Diner - Wichita
notes: Retro diner with gigantic portions of Southern comfort food! Chicken fried steak, biscuits & gravy, homemade pie. Breakfast all day. Local legend. Wichita center. Best for lunch. Go early - line is normal.

name: Dorothy's House and Land of Oz - Liberal
notes: Recreation of Dorothy's house + the Land of Oz! Built in 1999. Actress-led tours of the Oz world. Liberal is also home to 'Pancake Day' - annual pancake race vs. England! Liberal, SW Kansas. Middle of nowhere but completely dedicated. Wizard of Oz fans: definitely a pilgrimage.

name: Eisenhower Presidential Library - Abilene
notes: Presidential Library + Museum + Ike's Birth and Grave House!  Small farm town - great WWII heritage.  Abiline: home of Wild Bill Hickok and Dwight D. Eisenhower.  Combine with Tallgrass Prairie for central Kansas day.  Well done museum. Less known than other presidential libraries.

name: Free State Brewing - Lawrence
notes: Kansas' FIRST legal microbrewery after Prohibition (1989)! Lawrence, university town. Lively center. Ad Astra Ale + Copperhead Pale Ale are their classics. Massachusetts Street: Kansas' most beautiful high street. Good pub food + local beers. Relax here.

name: Garden of Eden - S.P. Dinsmoor
notes: Concrete garden park + mausoleum built by Civil War veteran (1905-1927)! 150+ figures: Adam, Eve, snake, Goddess of Liberty, socialist themes. Dinsmoor lies in his glass coffin in the mausoleum - you can see him! Next to Grassroots Art Center. Must-see combo. Lucas is the most bizarre city in Kansas. Period.

name: Geographical Center of 48 States - Lebanon
notes: EXACT geographical center of the 48 contiguous states! Small monument with a chapel. In the middle of a cornfield. FREE. Lebanon: 200 inhabitants. Center of EVERYTHING. Not even a gas station. But the center. Epic trivial.

name: Hot Air Balloon Rides - Wichita
notes: Sunrise balloon ride over the Kansas prairie and Flint Hills! Endless horizon, sunrise over rolling grasses. Various operators available via Visit Wichita. Spring and autumn: best weather conditions. Book in advance. Spectacular minimalist view.

name: Kansas Aviation Museum - Wichita
notes: Wichita = 'Air Capital of the World' - more aircraft built than anywhere else! Beechcraft, Cessna, Learjet: all born here. Vintage aircraft in historic terminal building. Wichita. Essential for aviation enthusiasts. Near Dwight D. Eisenhower National Airport.

name: Kansas Cosmosphere - Hutchinson
notes: Second largest space collection in the world after the Smithsonian! Apollo 13 command module. Liberty Bell 7 (James Glenn's capsule). Large Soviet space collection outside Russia. Hutchinson, central Kansas. A must for space nerds. Space museums bring their pieces here for restoration.

name: Kansas Underground Salt Museum - Hutchinson
notes: 600 feet underground – in an active salt mine! Elevator down. Centuries-old salt deposits form walls. Film and music tapes are stored here (perfect conditions). Hutchinson. Combine with Cosmosphere for an epic Kansas day. 14°C all year round. Bring a coat.

name: Keeper of the Plains - Wichita
notes: 44-foot-tall steel Native American sculpture at the confluence of 2 rivers! In the evening: a ring of fire around the base burns. Spectacular. Mid-America All-Indian Center next door. FREE. Wichita city center. Riverwalk.

name: Lucas - Grassroots Art Capital
notes: The whole city = outsider art Mecca! S.P. Dinsmoor's Garden of Eden: cement biblical scenes + homemade mausoleum. Bow Plaza: the most artistic public toilet in the world (really). Grassroots Art Center: pull-tab car, chewing gum cameos, limestone sculptures. Lucas, North Kansas. Allow half a day. Absolutely unique.

name: Monument Rocks - Gove County
notes: First National Natural Monument of the US (1968)! Chalky white rock formations 20m high in the middle of the prairie. Erosion created this 70+ million years ago: fossil seabed. FREE. Unpaved road - F-150 perfect. Gove County, W-Kansas. Sunset here = magical.

name: Old Cowtown Museum - Wichita
notes: Rebuilt Wild West cowtown from the 1870s! Costume demonstrations. Goldsmith, baker, sheriff. Wichita was the most lawless cowtown on the Chisholm Trail. 50+ historic buildings on 10 acres. Wichita. Family attraction. Well done.

name: Original Pizza Hut Museum - Wichita State University
address: Wichita State University Innovation Campus, Wichita, KS 67260
notes: The VERY FIRST Pizza Hut building! Little red hut. Dan Carney and Frank Carney opened here in 1958. Now on the campus of Wichita State University as a museum. FREE to view from the outside. Pizza Hut was born here. Say a prayer of thanks.

name: Post Rock Scenic Byway
address: US-24 tussen Lincoln en Luray, KS
notes: Scenic road through the post-rock limestone landscape! Pioneers cut fence posts out of the prairie soil here. Lucas is on this route—perfect combo. 90 miles from Lincoln to Luray. Spring: wildflowers. Autumn: golden grass. Little traffic.

name: Prairie Haven Nudist Park - Scranton
notes: AANR-affiliated naturist park 23 miles from Topeka! 30 acres with trees, swimming pool, covered jacuzzi. Family-friendly. Couples welcome. Scranton, Eastern Kansas. May through October. Call in advance for first visit.

name: Sandy Lane Club - Hutchinson
notes: AANR-affiliated naturist club at Hutchinson! Smaller and more primitive than Prairie Haven. Families and traditional couples. Hutchinson, central Kansas. Combine with Cosmosphere + Salt Museum day.

name: Sunflower Hotel - Dodge City
notes: Historic hotel in the most legendary cowtown in the US! Dodge City: Wyatt Earp, Doc Holiday, gunfights on Front Street. Front Street replica: historic shops, saloons. SW Kansas. Adjacent to Route 66. Authentic Western stop.

name: Tallgrass Prairie National Preserve
notes: Last great patchwork tallgrass prairie on Earth! Flint Hills. Sunrise over undulating grasses: emotionally beautiful. Bison herd on the property. Hiking trails 3-16 km. America the Beautiful pass valid. FREE. Strong City/Cottonwood Falls base. May: red Indian grass in bloom.

name: Wichita Brewing Company
notes: Kansas' most acclaimed craft brewery with award-winning wood-fired pizza! Buffalo Sweat Oatmeal Cream Stout + Shaven Yak brown ale (World Beer Cup 2024 Gold!). Pizzeria + taproom. Family-friendly. Wichita. Multiple locations. The best beer in a cornfield state.

name: World's Largest Ball of Twine - Cawker City
notes: Frank Stoeber started this in 1953. Now bigger than ever + allowed to add tourists! Annual Twine-a-Thon festival in August. Note: Iowa and Minnesota also claim 'world's largest' - Kansas is the real one! Cawker City, North Kansas. FREE. Garief: 4 streets, 1 cafe, 1 ball of rope.

name: World's Largest Hand-Dug Well - Greensburg
notes: 109 feet deep, 32 feet wide - hand-dug in 1887! Now a modern museum on top. Stairs down to the water's edge. Greensburg was 95% destroyed by a tornado in 2007 - rebuilt 100% sustainably. 'Greenest city in the US' after the tornado. Beautiful story of resilience. Small but memorable.

name: Apple Valley Hillbilly Garden - Marshall County
address: Calvert City area, Marshall County, KY 42029
notes: Folk art playground full of wooden sculptures, toys, and Elvis busts! Family gas station converted into an outsider art museum. 3,000+ toy objects in the museum. I-24, W-Kentucky. FREE to view from the outside. Inside: small entrance fee.

name: Bourbons Bistro - Louisville
notes: 130+ bourbons on the menu + farm-to-table cuisine! Louisville Frankfort Ave - the hippest street in town. High-quality American food. Good cocktails. The right way to get to know bourbon. Reserve.

name: Buffalo Trace Distillery - Frankfort
notes: Kentucky's OLDEST working distillery (1773)! FREE tour and tasting! (reservations recommended) Pappy Van Winkle, W.L. Weller, Eagle Rare produced here. Frankfort, state capital. The most complete distillery experience in Kentucky. Completely free!

name: Cumberland Falls - Moonbow
notes: The only place in the Western Hemisphere with a regular moonbow! Full moon + waterfalls + clear night = rainbow of moonlight. 68-foot waterfall - 'Niagara of the South'. Corbin, Southern Kentucky. Summer full moon night: come for this. Truly magical.

name: Dinosaur World - Cave City
address: 711 Mammoth Cave Rd, Cave City, KY 42127
notes: 150 life-sized dinosaur sculptures in the open air! I-65: impossible to miss. Kitsch but amazing. Fossils museum + sandpit for children. Cave City, next to Mammoth Cave. In August: witches' brew in the heat. Beautifully absurd.

name: Futuro House - Covington
notes: One of only 60 remaining Futuro Houses worldwide! 26-foot diameter fiberglass flying saucer (1968 design). Private residence, but can be admired from the outside. Covington, just across the bridge from Cincinnati. FREE photo stop. UFO architecture in Kentucky!

name: HedoFest / Louisville Lifestyle Events
notes: Louisville lifestyle scene via Kasidie ​​platform! HedoFest: annual couples event in Louisville. Private home parties and club events. Find and sign up via Kasidie.com. Louisville has an active lifestyle community.

name: Kentucky Aviation Museum - Lexington
notes: Kentucky aviation history + vintage planes! Blue Grass Airport, Lexington. Small but good. Combine with Horse Farm tours. Half-day activity.

name: Kentucky Bourbon Trail
notes: 60 distilleries - 95% of the world's bourbon made in Kentucky! Buffalo Trace (free!), Maker's Mark, Woodford Reserve. Bardstown = Bourbon Capital of the World. Kentucky Derby + Bourbon Trail = ultimate Kentucky weekend. Book tours in advance. Maker's Mark: dip your own bottle in red wax.

name: Kentucky Derby Hot Air Balloon - Louisville
notes: Hot air balloon ride over the blue Kentucky bluegrass regions! Wooden fences, horse farms, Bourbond distilleries. Louisville + Bardstown area. Spring + early summer. Champagne toast. Book in advance. Unique Kentucky perspective.

name: Kentucky Reptile Zoo - Slade
notes: One of the world's largest venomous snake collections! National Geographic + Animal Planet filmed here. Venomous snake shows. Contributing to antivenom research. Slade, Red River Gorge region. Not for the faint-hearted. Scientifically fascinating.

name: Louisville Slugger Museum
notes: 120-foot baseball bat leans against the museum! 68,000 pounds of steel. Factory made here in 1884. Working factory + museum. See real MLB bat production. Louisville downtown. Whiskey Row. Every MLB star ordered their bat here.

name: Maker's Mark Distillery - Loretto
notes: The only distillery with a signature red wax dip! You can dip your OWN bottle. Unique souvenir. National Historic Landmark. Beautiful estate. Loretto, Bourbon County. Tours several times a day. Book in advance.

name: Maker's Mark Distillery Star Hill Farm B&B
notes: Stay overnight *on* the Maker's Mark distillery grounds! Star Hill Farm: Victorian house on the estate. Private tour. Dip your own bottle. Loretto, West Kentucky bourbon country. One of Kentucky's most unique overnight stop options.

name: Mammoth Cave National Park
address: 1 Mammoth Cave Pkwy, Mammoth Cave, KY 42259
notes: Longest cave system in the world - 680+ kilometers explored! 1-6 hour tours available. Historic Wild Cave Tour. America the Beautiful pass valid! Cave City as base. I-65 corridor. Blind fish + dormice + ancient rocks.

name: Muth's Candies - Louisville
notes: Louisville's OLDEST candy store (1921) - original Modjeska recipe! Modjeska: caramel-dipped marshmallow. Iconic Kentucky. Handmade. Small shop. Great heritage. Louisville NuLu neighborhood. Bourbon balls too. Take home as a souvenir.

name: My Old Kentucky Home State Park
address: 501 E Stephen Foster Ave, Bardstown, KY 40004
notes: Federal Hill mansion - inspiration for Stephen Foster's 'My Old Kentucky Home'! Bardstown, Bourbon Capital of the world. Musical in the summer on the lawn. Combine with a bourbon trail for an authentic Kentucky day. Classic Southern Kentucky atmosphere.

name: Proof on Main - Louisville
notes: Fine dining at the 21c Museum Hotel – surrounded by modern art! Seasonal menu featuring Kentucky products. Innovative. Whiskey Row location. Art hotel restaurant concept: the best of both worlds. Reserve now. Unique for a special evening.

name: Rabbit Hash General Store - Rabbit Hash
address: 10021 Lower River Rd, Rabbit Hash, KY 41005
notes: Town of 6 inhabitants with a DOG as mayor! Already had several dog mayors. Democratically elected. 1831 General Store along the Ohio River. Still open! Rabbit Hash, N-Kentucky along the Ohio River. FREE to visit. Store with local crafts. Uniquely American.

name: Ramsey's Diner - Lexington
notes: Lexington's most beloved Southern diner! Country ham, biscuits, fried chicken, chess pie. Restaurant-level home cooking. Lexington town centre. Local legend. Breakfast + lunch. Wait outside: always a line.

name: Red River Gorge Geological Area
notes: Spectacular limestone arcades + 100+ natural bridges! Daniel Boone National Forest. FREE basic entry. World-class climbing wall. 100+ routes. Stanton, Eastern Kentucky. 1 hour from Lexington. Autumn: explosion of colors in the gorges.

name: The Brown Hotel - Louisville
notes: Historic grand hotel from 1923 - home of the Hot Brown! Georgia Revival architecture. Louisville's most iconic hotel. Downtown Louisville. Everything within walking distance. Kentucky Derby week: book well in advance. Stay WHERE the Hot Brown sandwich was born.

name: Thomas Merton's Hermitage - Gethsemani
notes: The cottage where famous monk and writer Thomas Merton lived! Abbey of Gethsemani: active Trappist monastery. Monastery shop: cheese and bourbon fruitcake (literally). Trappist, KY. Peace and silence guaranteed. FREE. Visits are welcome and you can even book retreats.

name: Vent Haven Museum - Fort Mitchell
address: 33 W Maple Ave, Fort Mitchell, KY 41011
notes: The only museum IN THE WORLD dedicated to ventriloquism + puppets! 900+ ventriloquist puppets stare at you. Utterly creepy. For Mitchell, Cincinnati border area. Tours by appointment. One of a kind. If the puppets talk at night? Run away.

name: Wigwam Village Motel - Cave City
address: 601 N Dixie Hwy, Cave City, KY 42127
notes: Sleep in a 20-foot-high concrete tipi! 15 concrete wigwams as hotel rooms. Retro Americana 1937. Mammoth Cave is 15 min away. Perfect themed overnight stay. Cave City, KY. I-65 corridor. Original Wigwam Village #2. Only 3 left in the US.

name: Woodford Reserve - Versailles
notes: Kentucky's most scenic distillery! National Historic Landmark. Stone buildings from the 1800s. Versailles (pronounced 'Ver-SALES' here), Central KY. Small batch bourbon. Premium quality. Tours are thorough and educational.

name: World's Tallest Three-Story Building - Morganfield
notes: Building that CLAIMS to be the tallest three-story building in the world! Including the groundwater level, the 4th layer is below ground. Morganfield, West Kentucky. FREE. Logical absurdity at its best. Photo and drive on. Quick stop.

name: Abandoned Six Flags - New Orleans
address: 12301 Lake Forest Blvd, New Orleans, LA 70128
notes: Six Flags New Orleans abandoned after Katrina (2005) - never reopened! 140 acres of post-apocalyptic amusement park in the wild. Not legally accessible - but visible from the outside. NO East. Urban exploring legend. FREE to view. Will eventually be demolished.

name: Abita Mystery House
notes: 'DARRELL' - half dog, half alligator! Plus thousands of bizarre objects. John Preble's outsider art collection in multiple buildings. Art cars, arcade machines, mosaics, antique scrap. Abita Springs, 30 min from New Orleans. A little gem outside the city. Completely unexpectedly absurdist.

name: Atchafalaya Basin Swamp
notes: Largest swamp landscape in North America - 1.4 million acres! Boat tours, kayak, airboat. Henderson, central Louisiana. Filming location for Robert Flaherty's 'Louisiana Story'. Autumn: spectacular bird migration.

name: Bayou Allure Clothing Optional B&B - Baton Rouge
notes: Clothing-optional bed & breakfast in Baton Rouge! 30 min from New Orleans. Private setting, adults only. Bayou view. Unique Louisiana naturist B&B experience.

name: Bayou Zipline Adventure - New Orleans
notes: Zipline OVER the Louisiana bayou - with alligators below! Adrenaline rush + wildlife guaranteed. New Orleans surroundings. Combined well with a swamp tour. Perfect content for @roamingbonbons.

name: Café Du Monde - New Orleans
notes: Open 24/7 SINCE 1862 - beignets + café au lait. Period. Decatur Street, French Market. Powdered sugar on everything around you. And on you. A must-stop. No choice. Do it. Night: the most wonderful time. Drunk people + beignets = New Orleans.

name: Central Grocery - Muffuletta
notes: INVENTOR of the Muffuletta sandwich (1906)! Round bread with Italian sausage, salami, olive relish. Decatur Street, French Quarter. Cash only. Normal line. Eat half: this is a sandwich for two people.

name: Colette New Orleans - Lifestyle Club
notes: New Orleans' most famous lifestyle club - one of the best in the US! $200/year or $30 per night membership. On-premise. Couples and select singles. Sign up via website + membership options. New Orleans is the most open city in America. Fitting.

name: Commander's Palace - New Orleans
notes: Garden District's most iconic fine dining restaurant! 25-cent martinis during weekend brunch (there is a limit - but...). James Beard Award winners learned here. Emeril Lagasse trained here. Victorian dining palace. Dress code. Book weeks in advance. Garden District.

name: Dooky Chase's Restaurant - New Orleans
notes: Leenda Chase's legend - 'Queen of Creole Cuisine' (1941)! The place where Thurgood Marshall and MLK discussed the strategy for civil rights. Best Creole gumbo in the world. Fried chicken legendary. Treme neighborhood, New Orleans. Reserve. Meeting place of the civil rights movement.

name: Galatoire's - New Orleans
notes: French Quarter institution since 1905 – unchanged! Overly buttery sauces. Sometimes a 2-hour wait in line. 'Old guard' New Orleans dining: loud, festive, decadent. Bourbon Street. Dress code after 5:00 PM. Friday lunch: the real test of who understands New Orleans.

name: Hotel Monteleone - New Orleans
notes: Home to the SPINNING Carousel Bar + literary legend! Tennessee Williams, William Faulkner, and Truman Capote slept here. Royal Street, French Quarter. 1886. Historic and stylish. Literary Trail designation. Every room has a story.

name: Indian Hills Nudist Park - Slidell
notes: AANR-affiliated naturist park 30 min from New Orleans! Swimming pool + hot tub. Adults only but family-friendly atmosphere. Slidell, N Louisiana. Since 1971. Couples welcome. Perfect naturist stop in the Deep South.

name: Laura Plantation - Vacherie
notes: Louisiana's most honestly told plantation tour! Explicit about slavery. Creole architecture. Br'er Rabbit stories trace back to tales that originated HERE. Vacherie, Great River Road. Book in advance. Small groups. Powerful.

name: Marie Laveau's Tomb - St. Louis Cemetery #1
notes: Grave of New Orleans' MOST FAMOUS Voodoo Queen (1881)! The only tourist tour cemetery in New Orleans (guide required). XXX scratched once again by pilgrims asking for a wish. French Quarter border. Film Interview with a Vampire photo location as well.

name: Muriel's Restaurant Séance Room
notes: Restaurant with a SECRET Séance room on the 2nd floor! Every evening, a table is reserved for the ghost of Pierre Antoine Lepardi Jourdan. Chartres Street, French Quarter. Food + supernatural atmosphere = unique Louisiana dinner. Reserve + ask for the séance room.

name: Museum of Death - New Orleans
notes: Paintings of serial killers, Dr. Kevorkian's Thanatron, autopsy videos! New Orleans branch of the infamous LA + SD museum. For strong stomachs. Utterly creepy and fascinating. French Quarter. 18+. Not for the faint of heart. We are going.

name: Natchitoches Christmas Festival
notes: Oldest inhabited city in Louisiana + EPIC Christmas Festival! This December: 300,000 lights along the river. The movie Steel Magnolias was filmed here! Natchitoches, NW Louisiana. If the timing is right (Dec 2027 route option): SPECTACULAR.

name: New Orleans Historic Voodoo Museum
notes: Real human skulls, voodoo dolls, Rougarou (man-alligator-head)! Founded by Charles Massicot Gandolfo. Authentic voodoo items. French Quarter. Small but truly oppressive. Marie Laveau voodoo queen heritage. New Orleans culture in its most uncomfortable form.

name: NOLA Brewing Company
notes: New Orleans' most acclaimed craft brewery! Mechanical Bull IPA + NOLA Brown are the star performers. Tchoupitoulas St, Garden District nearby. Tours on Saturdays. Large taproom. The best local beer in Louisiana.

name: Old New Orleans Rum Distillery
notes: Louisiana's first rum distillery in modern times! Sugarcane-based. Local raw materials. Frenchmen Street, Marigny. Tours + tastings. Small and authentic. Rum is Louisiana's true distilling tradition (Creole heritage).

name: Roosevelt Hotel (Waldorf Astoria) - New Orleans
notes: 1893 Grand Hotel - Huey Long's favorite hangout! Sazerac Bar: home of the original Sazerac cocktail. The lobby is an incredible architectural statement. Center New Orleans, Warehouse District. The Christmas decorations here are legendary.

name: Southern Seaplane - New Orleans
notes: Seaplane over the Mississippi Delta and bayous! Unique perspective on the river meanders + bayou patterns. Belle Chasse Airport, 20 min from New Orleans. Tours of 30-90 min. Make a reservation. Water landing experience.

name: St. Louis Cemetery #3
notes: Above-ground 'oven tombs' - Louisiana's iconic cemeteries! New Orleans builds tombs above ground due to water levels. Rows of white crypts. Completely surreal. Esplanade Avenue, Mid-City. 150+ years of burial history. Can be visited independently.

name: Statue of Ignatius J. Reilly - New Orleans
address: Canal Street bij Bourbon, New Orleans, LA 70130
notes: Bronze statue of A Confederacy of Dunces' main character! Toby's Corner, Canal Street. John Kennedy Toole's novel won the Pulitzer Posthumously. FREE photo stop. For literary pilgrims: hallowed ground.

name: Swamp Tour - Honey Island Swamp
notes: Purest Louisiana swamp experience – almost uninhabited! Alligators, turtles, herons, cypresses. Honey Island = legendary wilderness area. Slidell, 40 min from New Orleans. Spring + autumn: most wildlife active.

name: Acadia Air Tours - Bar Harbor
notes: Fly over Acadia National Park from the air! Vintage Cessna flights over the island coastline, Cadillac Mountain. Hancock County Airport, next to Bar Harbor. Summer only. Book early. Unique perspective on Maine's rocky coastline.

name: Acadia National Park
address: 20 McFarland Hill Dr, Bar Harbor, ME 04609
notes: Maine's most visited national park - spectacular coastline! Cadillac Mountain: first sunrise point in the US (Oct-March). America the Beautiful pass valid! Bar Harbor as a base. Summer: busy. Autumn: fantastic. Carriage roads free. Jordan Pond House: popover tradition.

name: Allagash Brewing Company - Portland
notes: Maine's most famous craft brewery - award-winning Belgian-style! Allagash White: the iconic white beer of New England. Tours + tastings. Portland. White beer made in Maine - more confusing than you think, but tastier. National distribution, but Portland = the source.

name: Baxter State Park - Mount Katahdin
notes: Endpoint of the Appalachian Trail + Maine's highest mountain (5,270 feet)! Percival Baxter: private purchase → donated to Maine. Highest difficulty level AT. Extreme hikers come here for the finish. Millinocket serves as the base. Summer only. America the Beautiful pass NOT valid - separate Maine state park.

name: Bigfoot Sightings Sign - Rangeley
notes: Official sign: 'Bigfoot Sightings in This Area'! FREE. Along the road near Rangeley. Locals claim with a straight face that sightings are normal. Combine with the Wilhelm Reich Museum for a bizarre Rangeley day. Maine humor at its driest.

name: Cadillac Mountain - First Sunrise USA
address: Cadillac Mountain Rd, Bar Harbor, ME 04609
notes: FIRST PLACE in the US where the sun rises (October to March)! 466m high = highest coastal mountain along the Atlantic coast north of Brazil. Reservations are MANDATORY for timed entry for sunrise via recreation.gov. Auto road or hike. Autumn view = incredible. America the Beautiful.

name: Desert of Maine - Freeport
notes: 40 acres of DESERT in Maine – created by overgrazing! Glacier sand from 12,000 years ago exposed by erosion. Tours + mineral collection. Freeport, 30 min from Portland. Half a strange natural phenomenon but completely fascinating.

name: Eartha - World's Largest Rotating Globe
notes: World's largest rotating globe - Guinness record 1999! 41.5 feet diameter. 2.5 tons. Rotates and tilts like the real Earth. DeLorme Mapping Company lobby. Free to view. Yarmouth, 20 min from Portland. If cartography inspires you: truly special.

name: Eventide Oyster Co. - Portland
notes: James Beard Award nominees! Best mussels + oyster bar in New England. Oyster bar + modern New England cuisine. Portland Old Port. Crowded. Just wait, it is worth it. Brown butter lobster roll = better than the traditional version.

name: Fore Street - Portland
notes: Portland's most acclaimed fine dining – wood-fire everything! James Beard Award-winning chef Sam Hayward. Old Port. Seasonal local produce. Book weeks in advance. Probably the best farm-to-table restaurant in New England.

name: International Cryptozoology Museum - Portland
notes: The only official museum dedicated to Bigfoot, Nessie, Yeti, etc.! Real 'evidence': hair, prints, casts. Portland. Lyle Rowland's 37-year collection. The world's ONLY cryptozoology museum. A nail in the scientific trunk. Wonderful.

name: Jordan Pond + Beehive Trail - Acadia
address: Jordan Pond Rd, Bar Harbor, ME 04609
notes: Jordan Pond: spectacular glacial lake with a perfect reflection of The Bubbles. Jordan Pond House famous for popovers and tea! Beehive Trail: intense short hike (3.5 km) with iron pins and ladders in the rock face – heart in your throat, but the reward is fantastic. Only for those without a fear of heights.

name: Kennebunkport Inn
notes: Charming historic inn in the heart of Kennebunkport! Walking distance to everything: harbor, restaurants, beaches. Classic Maine coastal atmosphere. Kennebunkport: also home to the Bush Sr. family. Summer: book well in advance.

name: Lenny the Chocolate Moose - Scarborough
notes: 1,700 pound life-sized CHOCOLATE MOOSE! Hand-carved from solid chocolate blocks. Len Libby Candies, Scarborough. FREE to admire. Buying candy is mandatory. The most Maenai attraction you can imagine.

name: LL Bean Flagship + Giant Boot - Freeport
notes: 16.5-foot brown boot + America's most famous outdoor store! Open 24/7/365 - no locks on the doors ever! Freeport is the outlet shopping town of Maine. FREE boot photo. Free entry to the store. The boot might be a size 400 L.L. Bean shoe or something.

name: Maine Lifestyle / Richmond Sauna meetups
notes: Maine's lifestyle scene is small but active via Kasidie ​​+ AFF! Richmond Corner Sauna sometimes serves as a neutral meeting place. Coordinate events via online platforms. Kasidie.com for Maine lifestyle couples. Small but discreet.

name: Maine Solar System Model - Presque Isle to Houlton
address: US-1, Presque Isle to Houlton, ME
notes: Scale solar system spread over 40 MILES of the road! High school students built this in 1999. Unique! Sun in Orono → Pluto in Houlton = correct scale distances. US-1 along the route. FREE and infinitely large. Literally.

name: Paul Bunyan Statue - Bangor
notes: 31-foot tall Paul Bunyan – probably the most handsome in the world! In Bass Park since 1959. Axe + lumberjack gear. Stephen King gave him a cameo in 'It' – come alive. Bangor is King's hometown – a perfect match. FREE. Quick stop. Impressive.

name: Pemaquid Point Lighthouse
notes: Most photographed lighthouse in New England – literally located at Maine State Quarter! Spectacular rock formations (folded granite, 500 million years old) right on the Atlantic Ocean. Fishermen's Museum next to the tower. Arrive early for the best light. $5 pp.

name: Portland Oyster Trail
notes: Portland = New England's food capital with oysters on every corner! Pachanga Portland, Duckfat, Eventide, Fore Street + 50+ others. Old Port: a drinkable walk past bars, oysters, and beer. Portland, ME. Food geeks come especially for this. And rightly so.

name: Red's Eats - Wiscasset
notes: 'World's Best Lobster Roll' claim - and you'll believe it after the first bite! 1.5 lb lobster on a hot dog bun. NO stuffing. Pure lobster. Wiscasset. The line sometimes stretches onto the bridge. Cash only. Summer only. Lobster hanging out on both sides. Eat outside.

name: Richmond Corner Sauna - Richmond
notes: Maine's best clothing-optional naturist B&B with Finnish saunas! Sunbathing area, indoor heated pool, hot tub. Open year-round – rare for Maine. Richmond, central Maine. Book now. Formerly swingers too – now purely naturist.

name: Shipyard Brewing Company - Portland
notes: Portland's most famous craft brewery - Export Ale classic! Brewery tours through historic cast-iron building. Portland downtown. Export Ale + Pumpkinhead Ale. Pumpkinhead in autumn = Maine beer tradition. Best stop after Eventide Oyster Co.

name: Stephen King's House - Bangor
notes: Stephen King's real house! Private residence - view from the outside. Spiderweb-iron fence with bats and spiders. Bangor. King still lives there (seasonal). FREE photo stop. Stan de Man: Bangor is the base of King's horror universe.

name: The Inn at Portland Headlight
notes: Historic B&B close to Portland Head Lighthouse! Visible from the coastal walk. Cape Elizabeth, 15 min from Portland. Authentic Maine stay. Sunrise over the ocean from your room.

name: Thunder Hole - Acadia
notes: SOOT-LOUD popping sea cave during stormy seas! Seawater + air trapped in the cave = cannon explosion. Ocean Drive, Acadia National Park. America the Beautiful Pass. Best time: 2 hours after low tide during moderate waves. Wait.

name: West Quoddy Head Lighthouse - Lubec
address: West Quoddy Head Rd, Lubec, ME 04652
notes: EASTERN point of the US + iconic candy-cane lighthouse! Built in 1808. Red and white striped. Unique design. Lubec, Downeast Maine. Far east of the continent. FREE outside the park. State park entry. Sunrise here = first sunlight in the continental US.

name: West Quoddy Head State Park
notes: EASTERN POINT of the USA! Candy Stripe Lighthouse (1808) with red and white stripes – an absolute eye-catcher. On a clear day, you can see Canada (New Brunswick) 5 km away. FIRST place in the US to see the sunrise (Oct-March). Walking path along spectacular tidal pools. $4 pp.

name: Wild Blueberry Land - Columbia Falls
notes: Dome building shaped like a giant blueberry + mini-golf + Willy Wonka vibe! Every hole: blueberry theme. Private farm behind it. Columbia Falls, Downeast Maine. Blueberries = Maine's sacred fruit. Delightfully kitschy and completely devoted.

name: Wilhelm Reich Museum - Rangeley
notes: Lab of controversial psychoanalyst + 'cloudbusters' inventor! Reich believed he could manipulate 'orgone energy'. The FDA burned his books. The FDA! Rangeley, NW Maine. Beautiful mountains. One of the most bizarre scientist-museums in America.

name: Addu Nature Park
notes: The park protects wetlands, mangroves and coastal habitats around Eydhigali Kilhi and Koattey. Gentle cycling, birdwatching and guided canoe outings make it suitable for a slower activity level, although reaching Addu requires a domestic flight.

name: Artificial Beach
notes: This man-made urban beach provides a swimming area and evening gathering place on Malé’s eastern waterfront. It is less idyllic than an outer island but convenient during a city stay and close to cafés and the airport ferry route.

name: Dhigurah Island
notes: Dhigurah is unusually long by Maldivian standards, with a forested path leading to an extended sandbank. The surrounding South Ari Atoll is famous for whale-shark excursions, which can be enjoyed with minimal physical effort from a guided boat.

name: Fulidhoo Island
notes: Tiny Fulidhoo combines a relaxed village, attractive beach and frequent sightings of rays near the harbor. The island is easily walkable and less hectic than Maafushi, though the longer speedboat transfer costs more.

name: Grand Friday Mosque
notes: The golden-domed mosque and Islamic Centre form one of Malé’s most recognizable landmarks. Visit outside prayer periods, wear modest clothing and combine it with Republic Square and the waterfront.

name: Gulhi Island
notes: Gulhi is a small local island with a pleasant bikini beach, calm lagoon and a quieter feel than Maafushi. It suits an easy-going beach day and can be combined with Maafushi using scheduled ferries or speedboats.

name: Guraidhoo Island
notes: Guraidhoo provides a more residential local-island atmosphere with access to nearby reefs and sandbanks. Accommodation and food are relatively affordable, while organized boat excursions should be booked through a guesthouse.

name: Hanifaru Bay
notes: This protected UNESCO biosphere site can host spectacular seasonal gatherings of manta rays, especially from roughly May through November. Entry is regulated, scuba diving is prohibited inside the bay and visits must use an authorized operator.

name: Hukuru Miskiy
notes: Built from carved coral stone in the seventeenth century, this is one of the Maldives’ most important historic buildings. Non-Muslim visitors should dress conservatively and may need permission to enter, while the exterior and old cemetery remain worthwhile.

name: Hulhumale Beach
notes: Hulhumalé offers a long, accessible beach without requiring an expensive resort transfer. Local-island dress rules apply outside designated tourist sections, and the promenade works well for an easy sunset walk or bike ride.

name: Hulhumale Central Park
notes: This modern public park has shaded paths, lawns, playgrounds and cafés amid Hulhumalé’s planned urban landscape. It is a low-effort stop that combines well with the beach and nearby mosque.

name: Isdhoo Old Mosque
notes: This historic coral-stone mosque is associated with important Maldivian copperplate records and early Islamic history. It lies well outside the standard resort circuit, making it most practical as part of a longer Laamu Atoll stay.

name: Ithaa Undersea Restaurant
address: Conrad Maldives Rangali Island, Alifu Dhaalu Atoll 20077
notes: Ithaa serves meals inside a glass-walled dining room about five meters beneath the lagoon. It is an exceptional but expensive experience, and outside guests must arrange resort access and transfers well in advance.

name: Kuruhinna Tharaagandu
notes: These archaeological remains preserve evidence of a Buddhist monastery dating from before the Maldives became Islamic. The site is modest and remote but rewards travelers interested in the country’s largely overlooked pre-Islamic history.

name: Maafushi Island
notes: Maafushi is the Maldives’ best-developed budget-tourism island, with guesthouses and competitively priced snorkeling, sandbank and dolphin trips. It is busier than smaller islands but makes an efficient and affordable base reached by public ferry or speedboat.

name: Maldives National Museum
notes: The compact national museum introduces Maldivian royal history, traditional crafts, coins, weapons and Buddhist-era artifacts. It is an easy indoor stop that pairs naturally with Sultan Park and the nearby historic mosques.

name: Maldives Whale Submarine
address: Laccadive Sea, departure from Malé, Malé 20000
notes: This tourist submarine descends below the surface without requiring guests to swim or dive. Marine sightings vary, but the unusual vessel suits travelers seeking an easy underwater experience near Malé.

name: Male Fish Market
notes: This working waterfront market offers an unfiltered look at the country’s tuna-based fishing economy. Go in the afternoon when catches arrive, expect wet floors and strong smells, and combine it with the produce market next door.

name: Mulee Aage
notes: This colorful early-twentieth-century building serves as the official presidential residence. The interior is generally closed, but the ornate exterior is an easy photo stop beside Hukuru Miskiy.

name: Rasdhoo Island
notes: Rasdhoo is the compact capital of its atoll and a good base for lagoon cruises, snorkeling and sandbank visits. The village has enough restaurants and services for comfort while remaining small enough to explore entirely on foot.

name: SEA Underwater Restaurant
address: Anantara Kihavah Maldives Villas, Kihavah Huravalhi, Baa Atoll 20215
notes: SEA surrounds diners with windows overlooking a living coral reef and passing marine life. It pairs particularly well with a Hanifaru Bay trip, although resort transfers and the meal make this a premium splurge rather than a mid-range staple.

name: Soneva Fushi Cinema Paradiso
address: Soneva Fushi, Kunfunadhoo Island, Baa Atoll 06170
notes: This open-air cinema screens films beneath the stars with wireless headphones to preserve the island’s quiet atmosphere. Access is primarily intended for resort guests, making it a memorable add-on rather than a standalone excursion.

name: Sultan Park
notes: Sultan Park is a landscaped green refuge in densely built Malé, created on part of the former royal palace grounds. It is best used as a quiet break between the National Museum, markets and mosques.

name: The Muraka
address: Conrad Maldives Rangali Island, Alifu Dhaalu Atoll 20077
notes: The Muraka is a two-level residence whose main bedroom sits beneath the Indian Ocean. An overnight stay is wildly beyond a mid-range budget, but architecture enthusiasts can ask whether limited tours or dining packages are available while visiting the resort.

name: Thulusdhoo Island
notes: Thulusdhoo is known for surfing, local guesthouses and a broad choice of water excursions. Non-surfers can enjoy the beach, lagoon and boat trips while watching experienced riders at the famous Cokes break.

name: Trans Maldivian Seaplane Flight
notes: A Twin Otter seaplane transfer provides extraordinary aerial views of reefs, lagoons and tiny islands. Flights normally operate as resort transfers rather than simple sightseeing tours, so choose a destination served by seaplane and verify baggage limits.

name: Ukulhas Island
notes: Ukulhas is a tidy local island recognized for environmental initiatives, a long tourist beach and accessible house-reef snorkeling. It offers a comfortable middle ground between basic village tourism and costly resort islands.

name: Utheemu Ganduvaru
notes: This preserved wooden palace was the childhood home of national hero Sultan Muhammad Thakurufaanu. Its carved interiors and guided stories provide rare insight into life beyond beaches, but reaching the far-northern island requires careful flight and boat planning.

name: Vaadhoo Bioluminescent Beach
notes: Glowing plankton can occasionally produce the celebrated “sea of stars” effect along Vaadhoo’s shoreline. The phenomenon is natural, unpredictable and never guaranteed, so treat it as a possible bonus rather than the sole reason for traveling there.

name: Villingili Island
notes: A short public ferry ride from Malé reaches a quieter residential island with beaches and vehicle-light streets. Walk or rent bicycles locally, observe conservative local customs and return before the last scheduled ferry.

name: Assiniboine Park Zoo - Winnipeg
address: 2595 Roblin Blvd, Winnipeg, MB R3R 2N7, Canada
notes: Canadian zoo with polar bears and Polish wolf! Journey to Churchill experience: polar bear exhibits. Winnipeg West Side. Combine well with the Human Rights Museum. Russian polar bears here + prairie animals.

name: Canadian Museum for Human Rights - Winnipeg
address: 85 Israel Asper Way, Winnipeg, MB R3C 0L5, Canada
notes: THE ONLY museum in the world entirely dedicated to human rights! Ranked as one of Canada's most beautiful buildings. Indigenous rights, Holocaust, LGBTQ+ stories. The Forks, Winnipeg. Beside the rivers. Architectural masterpiece. Opened in 2014.

name: Churchill - Beluga Whales Snorkelen
notes: 60,000+ beluga whales in the Churchill River in July-August! Snorkeling WITH the whales is possible – unique in the world. Kayak tours among the belugas. Summer (July-August): best season. Gentle + curious = close to you.

name: Churchill - Northern Lights Viewing
notes: Visible 300 days a year – directly under the aurora oval! Winter (Nov-Feb): longest nights, best intensity. Frontiers North Lodge + private guides. Dog sled tours during the day, aurora at night. One of the world's best Northern Lights destinations.

name: Churchill - Polar Bears
notes: Polar bear capital of the world - 1,000 km north of Winnipeg! October-November: bears wait on the ice of Hudson Bay. Tundra Buggy tours with Frontiers North Adventures. Only accessible by plane or train - no road! Time Magazine's Greatest Places 2023. Absolute bucket list.

name: Exchange District - Winnipeg
address: King St & McDermot Ave, Winnipeg, MB R3B, Canada
notes: Winnipeg's historic district with 150+ heritage buildings! Former grain trading capital of Canada. Now: restaurants, galleries, bars, theaters. Northern Lights casino nearby. Best neighborhood for exploring the city in Winnipeg.

name: Hecla Grindstone Provincial Park
notes: Icelandic heritage on an island in Lake Winnipeg! Hecla Island: Viking settlers in 1875. Goose sanctuary. Autumn: migratory bird spectacle. Riverton, 160 km N of Winnipeg. Ferry to the island. Campsite + lodge.

name: Helicopter Northern Lights Tour - Churchill
notes: Helicopter over the aurora borealis above the Canadian submarines! November-February. Churchill. Unique aerial perspective of the lights. Limited availability - ask Churchill operators. Ultimate Manitoba aerial experience.

name: International Peace Garden - Boissevain
address: 2702 Peace Garden Dr, Dunseith, ND/MB grens
notes: Cross-border garden park - half Canada, half USA! Gardens, monument, clock tower on the border. Boissevain, S-Manitoba. Atlas Obscura listing. Symbolic and calm. Free to wander around the gardens.

name: Lake Winnipeg - Grand Beach
notes: Canada's largest freshwater beach - 3 km of white sand! Lake Winnipeg: 5th largest freshwater lake in the world. Grand Beach, 90 km north of Winnipeg. Warm water (relatively speaking for Canada!). Busy in summer. When you forget you are in the prairies.

name: Lazy Bear Lodge - Churchill
address: 313 Kelsey Blvd, Churchill, MB R0B 0E0, Canada
notes: Hand-built stone + wood lodge in Churchill - the ultimate Polar Bear HQ! Built by local pioneer Wally Daudrich from boreal forest wood. Warm, rustic, epic. Meals included. Churchill is 1,000 km from Winnipeg. Fly there. Sometimes all-inclusive Polar Bear packages.

name: Lifestyle Manitoba / Kasidie Events
notes: Manitoba lifestyle scene via Kasidie ​​and SDC platforms! No fixed club address found - event-based. Winnipeg has an active online lifestyle community. Find and sign up via Kasidie.com. Private home events + occasional club nights.

name: Little Limestone Lake - Manitoba
notes: More that changes COLOR depending on temperature! Turquoise, blue, green, white - all due to calcium carbonate. Northern Manitoba. Fly or drive a long way. FREE but remote. Atlas Obscura favorite. Almost unknown outside Canada.

name: Narcisse Snake Dens - Narcisse
notes: Largest concentration of snakes in the WORLD - spring mating! Tens of thousands of redband snakes emerge from caves in May. Narcisse, N of Winnipeg. FREE. May + autumn (September-October). Snakes everywhere. EVERYWHERE. If you don't find that scary: perfect.

name: Nonsuch Brewing Co. + Restaurant - Winnipeg
address: 125 Pacific Ave, Winnipeg, MB R3B 0M3, Canada
notes: Manitoba-based craft brewery with a farm-to-table restaurant! Serves sharing plates with local ingredients alongside their beers. Exchange District, Winnipeg. Award-winning beers. Best brewery-restaurant combo in Manitoba.

name: Nonsuch Brewing Company - Winnipeg
address: 125 Pacific Ave, Winnipeg, MB R3B 0M3, Canada
notes: Manitoba's leading craft brewery - multiple awards!  Exchange District. Modern but authentic.  Mixed fermentation beers: saisons, sours, barrel-aged.  Restaurant next to the brewery.  The pride of Winnipeg beer scene.

name: One Great City Brewing - Winnipeg
address: 584 Wall St, Winnipeg, MB R3G 2T7, Canada
notes: Winnipeg Jets-themed brewery - local pride! NHL hockey + craft beer = Winnipeg at its best. Wall Street, Winnipeg West End. IPA + pale ale focus. Ideal for a hockey night.

name: Pilehenge - Rural Municipality of Rosser
address: RM of Rosser, MB R0H 0Z0, Canada
notes: Cluster of concrete SPIRINS in the middle of the Manitoba prairies! NW of Winnipeg. 'Cement Cemetery' old nickname. Often confused with a Stonehenge replica, but it is something else. FREE. Accessible off-road. Prairie art installation that no one explains.

name: Polar Bear Tundra Buggy Tour - Churchill
notes: Tundra Buggy drives past polar bears on their own territory! Not technical aviation, but the most spectacular Manitoba adventure. October-November. Frontiers North Adventures. 2-3 day programs available. Extremely safe. The only one in the world.

name: Riding Mountain National Park
notes: Manitoba's only national park - elk, bear, wolf, lynx! Wasagaming as a base: small resort town in the park. Climbing GroRiding Mountain (756m). America the Beautiful NOT valid - Parks Canada pass. Autumn: beautiful colors + elk rutting season.

name: Riding Mountain Scenic Drive - PTH 10
notes: Road from Winnipeg to Riding Mountain through rolling prairies! Colors from yellow-green (summer) to gold (autumn). Chance of spotting elk and canoes along the way. Take PTH 10 or PTH 5 heading north. Autumn: absolutely stunning colors in October.

name: Segovia Tapas Bar & Restaurant - Winnipeg
address: 484 Stradbrook Ave, Winnipeg, MB R3L 0J9, Canada
notes: Best Spanish tapas in Western Canada - authentic! Featured in Canada's 100 Best Restaurants. Osborne Village, Winnipeg. Sherry + sangria + txistorra. Reserve. Good wine list.

name: SMITH Restaurant at Inn at the Forks
address: 75 Forks Market Rd, Winnipeg, MB R3C 4L8, Canada
notes: Winnipeg's most award-winning farm-to-table restaurant! Local Manitoba products. Chef-driven menu. Rustic-urban interior by the rivers. Weekend brunch is a social event for locals. Reserve for dinner.

name: The Forks Market Food Hall - Winnipeg
address: 1 Forks Market Rd, Winnipeg, MB R3C 4L8, Canada
notes: 20+ local food stalls in a historic horse stable facility! Pickerel (whale) + perogies + bannock + Winnipeg specialties. The Common: 40+ craft beers + wines on tap. Winnipeg's best food market. Perfect for everyone: large groups, solo, family.

name: The Forks National Historic Site - Winnipeg
address: 1 Forks Market Rd, Winnipeg, MB R3C 4L8, Canada
notes: 6,000 years of history in one place – earliest human habitation in the region! Former horse stable facilities now used as a market and restaurants. Red and Assiniboine rivers meet here. FREE grounds. The Forks Market included. Winnipeg's social heart. Food, art, culture.

name: The Inn at the Forks - Winnipeg
address: 75 Forks Market Rd, Winnipeg, MB R3C 4L8, Canada
notes: Boutique hotel at THE FORKS location - everything within walking distance! Modern design. View of the river confluence. SMITH Restaurant in the hotel. Winnipeg city center. Best location in the city. Book well in advance in summer.

name: Winnipeg Art Gallery - Qaumajuq
address: 300 Memorial Blvd, Winnipeg, MB R3C 1V1, Canada
notes: Largest Inuit art collection IN THE WORLD! Qaumajuq (2021) expansion = architectural highlight. 13,000 Inuit works visible in a single vault wall. Winnipeg Center. The most powerful Indigenous arts collection in Canada.

name: Annapolis Historic District
notes: Colonial capital, the country's oldest state capital. Marine Academy campus: free to walk. Waterfront sailors' bars for lunch.

name: Antietam Battlefield National Cemetery
notes: Bloodiest day of the American Civil War: 23,000 dead in one day. National Parks Pass: FREE. The silence here is physically palpable. Impressive and austere at the same time.

name: Antrim 1844 Country Inn
notes: Antebellum plantation converted into a boutique inn. Restaurant in the old barn, wine cellar, orchard. Els: romantic getaway vibes. Serge: also agree.

name: Assateague Island Wild Ponies
notes: Wild ponies simply walk across the beach. FREE with a National Parks Pass. Legendary: feral for 500 years after a ship sank. Camping on the beach with ponies visiting your tent — surreal.

name: Bald Eagle spotting (Conowingo Dam)
notes: Hundreds of bald eagles gather here in November to catch fish. No admission fee — parking along the road. Birders and photographers from all over come for this.

name: Baltimore's 'The Block' nightlife area
notes: Baltimore's historic erotic entertainment district has existed for 150 years. Although it has shrunk, it is still a bizarre mix of bars, clubs, and gambling halls. Not for everyone, but definitely an Americana curiosity.

name: Blackwater National Wildlife Refuge
