notes: Bald eagles, ospreys, and Great Blue Herons present in massive numbers. Autumn: migratory birds in breathtaking numbers. Car drive-through circuit: perfect for the F-150.

name: Bowen's Inn (Solomons Island)
address: 14630 Solomons Island Rd S, Solomons, MD 20688
notes: Waterfront seafood bar on Solomon Islands. Oysters, crab soup, fish of the day. Local fisherman's table next to tourists = authentic.

name: Calvert Marine Museum
notes: Fossils 15-20 million years old. Picking up shark teeth from the cliffs on the beach = a free, bizarre activity. Imagine: seas where Maryland is now located.

name: Catoctin Mountain Orchard
notes: Cider with a view of the Catoctin Mountains. Camp David is located nearby (not open to visitors, but a fun fact). Taste hard cider in the shadow of presidential security.

name: Catoctin Mountain Park (Presidential Retreat area)
notes: National Parks Pass: free. Camp David is next to it but is not visible. Waterfalls, deer, and presidential mystique. Hiking trails through hemlock forests.

name: Chesapeake Bay Beach Club
notes: Resort directly on Chesapeake Bay: rooms with waterfront view. Perfect for a one-night stopover after Washington DC. Prices vary — much better off-season.

name: Chesapeake Bay Bridge
notes: 4.3 km bridge, one of the longest over the sea in the US. If you have a fear of heights: there is a shuttle service that drives your car. The view is spectacular. Sunset photo = a must.

name: Chesapeake Bay Maritime Museum
address: 213 N Talbot St, St. Michaels, MD 21663
notes: Maritime museum on the water in St. Michaels. Working lighthouse at the pier. Oyster boats, log canoes, and skipjacks: Chesapeake culture at its finest.

name: Chesapeake Naturist Beach (Sandy Point)
address: Sandy Point State Park, 1100 E College Pkwy, Annapolis, MD 21409
notes: Secluded naturist beach on the shore of Chesapeake Bay. Informal, not an official AANR park but tolerated. Come early for the best spot.

name: Civil War Medicine Museum
notes: Completely insane medical instruments from the war. Amputation saws, chloroform dispensers, surgical cases. Fascinating and gruesome at the same time. Typical Serge material.

name: Cunningham Falls State Park
notes: Largest waterfall in Maryland (78 feet): spectacular after rain. Pool at the falls: fast and refreshing. Combine with the Camp David area for a full day.

name: Edgar Allan Poe Museum (Baltimore)
notes: Poe's first house in Baltimore. The city's smallest museum. Original furniture and manuscripts. Lovers of dark literature: this is the place for you.

name: Enchanted Forest
address: 10300 Baltimore National Pike, Ellicott City, MD 21042
notes: Abandoned fairytale park partially rebuilt in a garden center. Original fiberglass princesses and castles scattered here and there. Absolutely surreal American kitsch at its best.

name: Faidley's Seafood (Lexington Market)
notes: Baltimore's most famous crab cake since 1886. No frills: just a bowl full of pure crab. Lexington Market included too — a bizarre folk market.

name: Flag Ponds Nature Park
notes: Beach where you find shark teeth in the cliffs — Miocene fossils. Clean little beach, no crowds of tourists. Els: a bucket list find when she finds a shark tooth.

name: Flying Dog Brewery - former Frederick location (closed)
notes: Hunter S. Thompson-inspired brewery with Ralph Steadman labels. Gonzo journalism meets craft beer. Tour on Saturday + taproom open daily.

name: Frederick's Carroll Creek Linear Park
address: Carroll Creek Linear Park, Frederick, MD 21701
notes: City park full of murals along a canal. Annual festival in October with lanterns on the water. Frederick's hidden gem — photogenic.

name: Geppi's Entertainment Museum (closed 2018)
notes: Four floors of nostalgia: comics, TV, toys, pop culture. From Superman to Transformers to Batman. Serge is going to hang out here for hours.

name: Graffiti Alley - Baltimore
notes: Graffiti Alley in Baltimore: one of the best legal spray-can tunnels in the US. More than 300 meters of chaos, color, and art. Free. Different every month. Photographer's paradise.

name: Great Falls of the Potomac
notes: Most dramatic waterfall on the East Coast — impressive. National Parks Pass: FREE. C&O Canal Towpath: perfect bike ride along the canal.

name: Harborview Marina Hotel
notes: Marina-side hotel in Baltimore's Locust Point neighborhood. Parking for the F-150 is no problem. Walk to Federal Hill = panoramic view of the city.

name: Havre de Grace Decoy Museum
address: 215 Giles St, Havre de Grace, MD 21078
notes: Thousands of wooden duck decoys as folk art. Sounds lame, but those things are truly artistic. Serge: I never knew duck hunting had such an aesthetic.

name: Heavy Seas Beer
notes: Pirate beer brewery with a nautical theme. Quayle's IPA and Loose Cannon are iconic. Taproom with a view of the brewery — tours available.

name: Herrington Harbour Marina Resort
notes: Marina resort on Chesapeake Bay with cottages and rooms. Boat rental and watersports on site. Perfect weekend stop for a rest stop on the route.

name: Hotel Indigo Baltimore Downtown
notes: Boutique hotel in a historic building in downtown Baltimore. Walking distance from Inner Harbor and museums. More budget-friendly than the big brands, more character.

name: Inn at Perry Cabin
notes: Historic luxury resort on the Eastern Shore. Above our budget but dream-worthy. 19th-century mansion converted into the ultimate retreat. Els: pin it for next time.

name: London Town and Gardens Ghost Ship
notes: 17th-century part of the city partly excavated, partly disappeared. William Brown House is the only remaining building. Ghosttown vibes with a colonial garden.

name: LP Steamers Crabs
notes: Authentic blue crabs, steamed with Old Bay, on brown paper. No cutlery, no fuss: hammer and fingers. THIS is Maryland food. Serge is going wild for this.

name: Maryland Racetrack / Pimlico (Preakness)
notes: Home of the Preakness Stakes, second leg of the Triple Crown. May 2027: check if timing matches route! Interesting to look around even outside of race season.

name: Miss Shirley's Cafe Baltimore
notes: Baltimore Brunch Institute. Crab Benedict = legendary. No line? Lucky. Line? Worth it. A must-eat for anyone visiting MD.

name: Museum of Eastern Shore Culture
notes: National museum of duck lure folk art. Sounds niche, but the sculptures are stunningly beautiful. Annual World Championship Carving Competition here.

name: National Cryptologic Museum (NSA)
address: 8290 Colony Seven Rd, Annapolis Junction, MD 20701
notes: NSA's secret language and code museum: FREE and totally bizarre. Enigma machines, Cold War spy gear, learn secret codes. Next to the real NSA campus — you are being watched while you watch.

name: National Electronics Museum
address: 1745 W Nursery Rd, Linthicum Heights, MD 21090
notes: Radar, radio, sonar — the entire history of electronic defense. Free and close to BWI airport. Geek heaven for Serge. Els: we can't seem to leave.

name: National Hard Crab Derby (Crisfield)
notes: Annual crab contest on Labor Day weekend — absurd and fantastic. Crabs are given 'painted' names by the governor. Crisfield: declaring himself 'Crab Capital of the World' — deserved?

name: National Museum of Dentistry
notes: Washington's teeth are here. REAL teeth of George Washington. Ultimately bizarre museum: the entire history of brushing teeth. Els: fascinating. Serge: a bit scary.

name: National Road Scenic Byway
notes: America's first federal highway (1811), now Historic US-40. Millstone markers, toll booths, historic inns. Alternative route through MD with historic stops.

name: Ocean City Boardwalk Bizarre Shops
notes: 6 km boardwalk full of fries, freak shows, and tattoo shops. Funnel cakes, buying hermit crabs as pets, photos with mermaids. Summer vibes but ultra kitsch — exactly what we are looking for.

name: Ocean City Inlet Jetty & Fishing Pier
address: S Boardwalk & 2nd St, Ocean City, MD 21842
notes: People have been fishing here for 150 years: from schoolboys to professional fishermen. Street performers, kites, sunset ritual. Free entertainment all year round.

name: Old Line Spirits Distillery
notes: Whisky and rum distillery in Baltimore with tour and tasting. Use military-grade rice from Maryland farmers. Craft spirits Baltimore style.

name: Patapsco Valley State Park
address: 8020 Baltimore National Pike, Ellicott City, MD 21043
notes: 32 km of bike paths and walking paths along the river. E-bikes are perfect here. Ellicott City historic downtown = bonus stop after the park.

name: Patuxent River Naval Air Museum
address: 22156 Three Notch Rd, Lexington Park, MD 20653
notes: FREE military aviation museum at the Navy test pilot base. Prototypes, test aircraft, and secret programs. Serge: eyes like saucers.

name: Patuxent River State Park (paddling)
notes: Kayak and canoe routes on the Patuxent River. Wilderness right next to DC suburbs — surreal contrast. Free admission, kayak rental separate.

name: Plummer's Island (entomologische vondsten)
address: C&O Canal towpath, near Cabin John, MD 20818
notes: Small island in Potomac where more than 10,000 insect species have been described. Accessible via the C&O Canal tow path — walking over rocks. Nerdy trip, but fascinating if you know what you are looking for.

name: Poe's Grave (Westminster Hall)
notes: Edgar Allan Poe is buried here, with his wife and uncle. Every year, a mysterious 'Poe Toaster' appears with roses and cognac. Free admission, bizarre tradition.

name: Port Discovery Children's Museum
notes: Maybe not immediately for you, but it features a floor full of bizarre interactive art. The 'Adventure Expeditions' exhibition is also fun for adults. A kids' museum that is actually pretty cool.

name: Sandy Point State Park
notes: Small beach in Chesapeake Bay with a view of Bay Bridge. Birdwatching, sailing, swimming. Annapolis is nearby: combine.

name: ScareHouse / Field of Screams (Halloween)
notes: Haunted attraction in October: outdoor horror route through the forest. If the timing is right (route is Oct-Nov), definitely do it. Els: maybe not. Serge: absolutely yes.

name: Shot Tower (Baltimore)
notes: 234-foot-high tower where molten lead was pumped up and fell down like hail. 1828, still fully intact. Free outdoor viewing. Inside during special events.

name: Star-Spangled Banner Flag House
notes: House where the original flag was made that inspired the 'Star Spangled Banner'. 1793, fully restored with period rooms. Original sewing tools on display.

name: Sugarloaf Mountain hike
notes: Private mountain, freely accessible by the Maddux family for 100 years. Short but steep hiking trail: 280m elevation gain. View over the Potomac valley. Perfect day trip from DC.

name: Swallow Falls State Park
notes: Maryland's most beautiful waterfall: Muddy Creek Falls, 53 feet. Old-growth hemlock forest, impressive. National Parks Pass does not work — small state park fee.

name: Swingers Club: The Velvet Nation
address: Baltimore area MD (private — verifieer via lifestyle forums)
notes: Lifestyle club in the Baltimore area. Verify via SDC.com or Kasidie ​​for current location and events. Private membership required for entry.

name: Taneytown Route 140 Roadside Kitsch
notes: Route 140 through Taneytown: roadside churches, dilapidated barns, and bizarre shop signs. Typical Maryland Americana countryside. Drive and take photos — free and bizarre.

name: Terrapin Adventures Ropes Course
notes: Ziplines and climbing walls in a historic cotton factory. Nature + adrenaline = Serge is instantly won over. Historic industrial decor = bonus.

name: The Visionary Art Museum (American)
notes: Outsider art by self-taught artists: totally insane and amazing. Gigantic whirligig 55 feet high outside. Els: squeeze your eyes shut or take it all in — both works.

name: The Walters Art Museum
notes: FREE museum with a collection of 55,000 works: Egyptian to modern. Not really their style, but a formidable collection for free. Good when it rains in Baltimore.

name: US Naval Academy Museum
notes: Free museum on the Naval Academy campus. Battle of Jutland models, admiral's uniforms, naval trophies. Annapolis is worth the visit in itself — this is the bonus.

name: Woodberry Kitchen
notes: Farm-to-table in an authentic 19th-century industrial building. Chefs using 100% local ingredients. Reservations recommended — popular with locals.

name: 🏨 Captain's House Inn - Chatham Cape Cod
notes: Charming B&B in historic Chatham style on Cape Cod – a captain's house from 1839! Perfect base for the Cape Cod National Park. English gardens, full breakfast included. Chatham is the quietest and most authentic Cape Cod town. Approx. $140/night. Much cozier than the chain hotels on the Cape.

name: 🏨 Hawthorne Hotel - Salem
notes: Salem's most famous hotel – built in 1925, right in the city center. Salem = THE witch city of America! October is a month-long celebration here (Halloween + Haunted Happenings festival). Hotel with a paranormal reputation. Close to all the Salem Witch Trial museums. Approx. $150 (October is more expensive – book well in advance).

name: Bash Bish Falls State Park
notes: Highest waterfall in Massachusetts - 18m double drop split by a massive granite block! So beautiful that artists have been coming here to paint for 200 years. Short walk (1.6 km). No swimming, but incredibly photogenic. FREE. In the Berkshires near the NY border.

name: Blue Hills Reservation - Great Blue Hill
notes: Spectacular view of the BOSTON SKYLINE from the forest - a surreal combination! Skyline Trail (blue) to Great Blue Hill (215m) = 360° panorama of city and forest. 15 min from downtown Boston. 125 km of hiking trails. Eliot Tower (1877) at the top. FREE - every day.

name: Boston Lifestyle Events (Kasidie)
notes: Boston lifestyle scene via Kasidie ​​+ private events! Boston has an active but discreet lifestyle community. Private hotel parties + home guests. Find them via Kasidie.com. Discreet style suits the New England mentality.

name: Cape Cod National Seashore
notes: 64 km of white sandy beach, spectacular dunes, and cranberry bogs protected as a national park! Province Lands = dune landscape reminiscent of the Sahara. Bike rental and bike paths through the park. America the Beautiful pass valid. Beach parking expensive in summer - come early or bike.

name: Glassflowers at Harvard
notes: 4,000 perfectly accurate glass flowers + plants! Leopold and Rudolf Blaschka's incredible work (1886-1936). Harvard Museum of Natural History. Cambridge. Glassblowers worked on this for 50 years. Amazing.

name: Harpoon Brewery - Boston
notes: Boston's largest craft brewery – since 1986! Harpoon IPA: New England classic. UFO Hefeweizen. Seaport District, Boston. Large taproom. Beer Hall with German-style tables. Beerfest in May + Oct. New England Beer Awards – always a medal winner.

name: Lake Chargoggagogg...
notes: Longest place name in the US - 45 letters! 'Chargoggagoggmanchauggagoggchaubunagungamaugg' A lake near Webster. Fishing and recreation. Webster, SW Massachusetts. FREE. Only for the photo at the sign.

name: Legal Sea Foods - Boston
notes: Boston's iconic seafood restaurant – for 70 years! Clam Chowder: New England's best. Lobster straight from the tank. Long Wharf, Boston Harbor. Tourists and locals alike. For a reason. New England Clam Chowder here = benchmark.

name: Liberty Hotel - Boston
notes: Former prison converted into a luxury hotel! Charles Street Jail (1851). Original cells as restaurant alcoves. Beacon Hill, Boston. Clink Restaurant: bar IN the old prison space. Most unique hotel conversion in New England.

name: Lizzie Borden House - Fall River
notes: The real house where Lizzie Borden (possibly) murdered her parents! 'Lizzie Borden took an axe, gave her father 40 whacks.' 1892 murder. Never convicted. House stands intact. Fall River, SE Massachusetts. Overnight stays in the murder house are also possible. Exciting!

name: Mapparium - Boston
notes: 30-foot diameter stained-glass globe - you are standing INSIDE the earth! Built in 1935. An exact map of the world at the time. Mary Baker Eddy Library, Boston. Unique acoustic effect: whisper on one side = you can hear it on the other. Mandatory. No one knows this exists.

name: Mount Greylock State Reservation
notes: Highest point in Massachusetts (1,064m) with a 145 km view over 5 states on a good day! The Appalachian Trail runs over the top. Bascom Lodge (CCC building 1937) at the summit for lunch. 45 miles of hiking trails. Autumn foliage in the Berkshires = spectacular. Road open May-Nov. FREE!

name: Museum of Bad Art - Boston
address: Dorchester Brewing Company, 1250 Massachusetts Ave, Boston, MA 02125
notes: Dedication to art that is so BAD it’s good! Originally, the collection hung in a cinema basement next to the toilet. Now: official museum. 700+ pieces of bad art. Somerville (Boston area) + other locations. FREE (or $5). Mission: 'art too bad to be ignored'.

name: Paper House - Rockport
notes: House made entirely of 100,000 newspapers - walls, furniture, everything! Elisa F. Stenman's hobby project as a summer house (1924-1942). Rockport, Cape Ann. April-October. Only $2. The news from 1930 literally holds your house upright.

name: Plymouth Rock
notes: Stone where the Pilgrim Fathers landed in 1620 - or something like that! 1620 inscription. Located in a neo-classical portico. Plymouth Harbor. FREE. Smaller than you expect. America's birth myth in a boulder. Symbolic.

name: Ponyhenge - Lincoln
notes: 30+ rocking horses in a meadow arranged like Stonehenge! Voluntarily placed by anonymous local artists. Growing. Lincoln, 20 min from Boston. FREE. Along the road. How. Why. Whose. No one knows. Perfect.

name: Salem Witch Board Museum
notes: The only museum IN THE WORLD dedicated to the history of the Ouija board! Salem, of course. 100+ boards throughout the centuries. History of the board + paranormal connections. Salem center. Perfect Salem day completion piece.

name: Salem Witch Museum
notes: Life-size dioramas of the witch trials of 1692! Live actors + presentation on the hysteria. Salem's most visited museum. Perfect Halloween city. Salem, 30 min from Boston. October: VERY busy but VERY worth it.

name: Sandy Terraces Associates - Barnstable
notes: AANR-affiliated naturist resort on Cape Cod! Barnstable / Marston Mills, Cape Cod. Family-oriented. Contact via AANR locator. Cape Cod + naturist combination = summer dream.

name: The Satanic Temple HQ - Salem
notes: Headquarters of The Satanic Temple - also an art gallery! World-famous religious organization (no actual worship of Satan). Art gallery + museum + gift shop. Baphomet sculpture! Salem. Perfect for the witch theme. Tours available. Provocative but serious.

name: The Witch House of Salem
notes: THE ONLY building in the world with a direct link to the Salem witch trials! Judge Jonathan Corwin's house. Interrogated defendants here. 1642 building preserved in perfect condition. Salem center. FREE outside - small entrance fee inside.

name: Union Oyster House - Boston
notes: Oldest continuously operating restaurant in the US (1826)! JFK had a regulars' table here on the upper floor. Boston Freedom Trail nearby. Oysters at the corner bar + seafood classics. Historic + delicious + authenticity guaranteed.

name: USS Constitution (Old Ironsides)
notes: Oldest active naval warship in the world (1797)! Still located at the Boston Navy Yard. FREE tour on board. Charlestown, Boston. Preserved and manned by the Navy. Annual sailing.

name: Walden Pond State Reservation
notes: The historic lake of Henry David Thoreau (Walden, 1854)! 2.4 km around the crystal-clear lake. Replica of Thoreau's cabin at the original location. 600,000 visitors every year - arrive early (parking limits). Swimming allowed! A sense of true peace and philosophy. $8 pp.

name: Ballonvaart boven Teotihuacán
address: San Martín de las Pirámides, Estado de México, Mexico
notes: Zonsopgang boven de piramides vanuit een luchtballon. GEEN coords — geocode-test.

name: Café de Tacuba
address: Tacuba 28, Centro Histórico, Ciudad de México
notes: Sinds 1912 — azulejos, enchiladas en mariachi. Betere churros dan de Brusselse wafel? Te testen.

name: Cenote Ik Kil
notes: Iconische open cenote, 26m diep zwemgat met lianen. Vroeg komen = geen bussen.

name: Chichén Itzá
notes: El Castillo + het beroemde slangenschaduw-effect bij equinox.

name: Hierve el Agua
notes: Versteende watervallen + infinity-poel op een klif. GEEN coords — geocode-test!

name: Hotel California
address: Calle Benito Juárez, Todos Santos, Baja California Sur
notes: Such a lovely place — niks met de Eagles te maken, maar de margarita’s zijn top. GEEN coords.

name: Isla de las Muñecas (Island of the Dolls)
notes: Honderden verminkte poppen in de bomen — creepiest boottocht van Noord-Amerika. Trajinera huren in Embarcadero Cuemanco. 🎎

name: La Rojeña — Jose Cuervo Distillery
address: Calle José Cuervo 33, Tequila, Jalisco, Mexico
notes: Oudste distilleerderij van Latijns-Amerika (1795), in het stadje Tequila zelf. GEEN coords — geocode-test.

name: Laguna de Bacalar
notes: Lagune van zeven kleuren blauw. Gratis, stil, en mooier dan de Malediven-brochures.

name: Las Pozas — Edward James Surrealist Garden
address: Camino Paseo Las Pozas, Xilitla, San Luis Potosí
notes: Surrealistische betonnen droomwereld in de jungle, gebouwd door een excentrieke Britse miljonair die bevriend was met Dalí en Magritte — ja, ónze Magritte. Trappen naar nergens, deuren naar de hemel, orchideeën overal. Reken minimum een halve dag, stevige schoenen, en neem de gids: de verhalen zijn de helft van de ervaring. Dit is exact het soort plek waarvoor Travellers 1969 bestaat.

name: Lucha Libre @ Arena México
notes: Gemaskerde worstelaars, vliegende lijven, bier in liters. Dinsdag/vrijdag avond.

name: Museo de las Momias
notes: Natuurlijk gemummificeerde lichamen — bizarre Belgische kelder-vibes maar dan écht.

name: Playa Zipolite
notes: Enige officiële naaktstrand van Mexico 🏖️😎 — relaxte hippie-vibe, wél straffe stroming: enkel zwemmen waar aangegeven.

name: Teotihuacán — Pirámide del Sol
address: San Juan Teotihuacán, Estado de México
notes: Grootste piramidestad van de Amerika’s. Combineren met ballonvaart bij zonsopgang.

name: Xcaret Park
address: Carretera Chetumal-Puerto Juárez km 282, Playa del Carmen
notes: Eco-themapark: ondergrondse rivieren, Maya-show. Duur maar volledig dagvullend.

name: 🏨 Black Star Farms - Suttons Bay
address: 10844 E Revold Rd, Suttons Bay, MI 49682
notes: Stay at a working winery & distillery on the Leelanau Peninsula (Sleeping Bear Dunes region)! Inn with 8 rooms surrounded by vineyards. Farmhouse wine, spirits, and cheese. Romantic, unique, perfect after Sleeping Bear Dunes. Approx. $150/night.

name: 🏨 Landmark Inn - Marquette
notes: Historic boutique hotel (1930) with Art Deco interior in Marquette, the capital of Michigan's Upper Peninsula. Amelia Earhart stayed here! View of Lake Superior. Gateway to Pictured Rocks (1 hour). Cathedral ceiling, ballroom, rooftop bar. Approx. $140/night.

name: Bell's Brewery - Kalamazoo
notes: Michigan's most famous craft brewery - Two Hearted Ale #1 beer USA! Eccentic Café + beer garden. Brewery tours available. Kalamazoo center. Oberon Wheat release in March = local holiday. Two Hearted Ale: most consistent award-winning beer in polls.

name: Bob-Lo Island Abandoned Park - Detroit River
address: Bois Blanc Island, Detroit River, MI
notes: Abandoned amusement park on an island in the Detroit River! Bob-Lo Island Amusement Park (1898-1993). Once popular. Private property. Views from the Detroit side of the river. Urban exploration legend. Melancholic and beautiful. A cruise past the Detroit River is the best option.

name: Buddy's Pizza - Detroit
notes: Inventor of Detroit-style pizza (1946) - thick rectangular crispy pizza! Cheese baked crispy all the way through and over the edges. Original location NE Detroit. Detroit-style pizza is trending everywhere now. This is where it all started. Reserve for weekend dinner.

name: Cherry Lane Resort - Adult Michigan
notes: Michigan's Adult Playground' - 21+ only! Clothing-optional pool + camping + events. Swinger-oriented. Chesterfield Township, NE Michigan. Friday night shenanigans are legendary. 21+ ONLY. Not family naturist.

name: Copper Harbor - Tip of the Keweenaw
notes: Northernmost point of Michigan's Keweenaw Peninsula! End of US-41 - 1,700 km from Miami starts here. Small village: coffee, ferry to Isle Royale. Upper Michigan wild seclusion. FREE to drive. 'Tip of the Tip'. Bucket list.

name: Frankenmuth - Beieren in Michigan
notes: Bavarian city in the middle of Michigan - Lederhosen, oompah, Christmas! Bronner's CHRISTmas Wonderland: the largest Christmas store in the world. Frankenmuth, Central Michigan. Time travel to Bavaria, but in the Midwest. Funny for Belgians: this is what Americans think Europe is.

name: Gilmore Car Museum - Hickory Corners
notes: Largest car museum outside the Smithsonian - 300+ historic cars! Original 1930s gas stations + dealer showrooms preserved. Hickory Corners, SW Michigan. Driving demonstrations. Car enthusiasts: this is Mecca. Seriously. Close to Kalamazoo. Easily spend half a day there.

name: Grand Hotel - Mackinac Island
notes: World's longest veranda (660m) + car-free island! Filming location for 'Somewhere in Time' (1980). Dress requirement: formally mandatory after 6:00 PM. Season: May-Oct. Accessible only by ferry. Book months in advance. Unforgettable.

name: Isle Royale National Park
notes: Remote island national park - minimum 2 days needed! Ferry from Copper Harbor or Houghton. Wolves + moose. Zero light pollution. Hiking only. America the Beautiful pass valid. Most underrated national park in the US. Absolutely.

name: Kitch-iti-kipi Mirror Lake - Palms Book SP
notes: Michigan's largest spring water – 60m wide, crystal clear up to 12m deep! Water is 6°C ALL year round. You float across on a self-propelled raft and look down: giant trout and spring clams bubbling up. Absolutely out of this world. Free in winter! Completely unique in the world.

name: Mackinac Bridge
notes: 5th longest suspension bridge in the world - 8 kilometers long! Connects the Lower and Upper Peninsula across the Strait of Mackinac. Mackinaw City to St. Ignace. Toll: $4. Driving over open grates = slightly frightening. Mackinac Island accessible via ferry on the other side.

name: Mackinac Island - Car Free!
notes: Island WITHOUT cars since 1898 - horse & carriage + bicycles only! Grand Hotel: longest veranda in the world (660m). Ferry from Mackinaw City or St. Ignace. 16 fudge shops on one island. There is literally a fudge law. Book the Grand Hotel well in advance.

name: Michigan's Adventure - Muskegon
notes: Michigan's largest amusement park + water park! Shivering Timbers: top 15 wooden roller coaster in the US. Muskegon. Summer only. Six Flags Spirit Card may be valid. Combo with Sleeping Bear Dunes for a perfect day out.

name: Motown Museum - Detroit
notes: Studio A where Berry Gordy created the Motown Sound! The microphone where Stevie Wonder, Diana Ross, and Marvin Gaye sang. Detroit W. Grand Blvd. Hitsville, USA. Emotionally and musically amazing. Tours every hour. Book now. A must for music lovers.

name: Pictured Rocks National Lakeshore
address: N8391 Sand Point Rd, Munising, MI 49862
notes: Spectacular colored sandstone cliffs (15-60m high!) along Lake Superior – red, orange, and brown due to minerals. 72 km long! Best viewed by BOAT (tours from Munising) or kayak. Miners Beach, Chapel Falls, and Grand Portal Point are top spots. FREE - America the Beautiful valid.

name: Porcupine Mountains Wilderness SP
notes: Michigan's largest wilderness area - 36,000 acres of old-growth forest (rare in the Midwest!). Lake of the Clouds = one of the most beautiful views in Michigan. 90+ km of hiking trails. Autumn = spectacular foliage color. Upper Peninsula hidden gem. $15 day pass.

name: Sleder's Family Tavern - Traverse City
notes: Michigan's OLDEST bar and restaurant (1882)! Original decor. Taxidermy on the walls. Authentic. Traverse City, NW Michigan. Burgers + local beer in a historic building. Nick Nolte sandwich on the menu. Real.

name: Sleeping Bear Dunes NL
notes: GMA's 'Most Beautiful Place in America' 2011 - and rightly so! 440-foot-high sand dunes RIGHT on Lake Michigan. Dune Climb: 150m up + sprint to the water = epic. Empire/Glen Arbor. America the Beautiful pass! Summer: perfect. Autumn: beautiful colors.

name: Sleeping Bear Dunes Pierce Stocking Drive
address: Pierce Stocking Scenic Drive, Empire, MI 49630
notes: 7-mile drive along the highest dunes with a view of Lake Michigan! Stop 9: a view that will bring you to your knees. 450 feet down. America the Beautiful pass valid. Empire, NW Michigan. Sunset here = absolute bucket list moment.

name: Tahquamenon Falls - Paradise
notes: Michigan's largest waterfall – coffee brown due to tannins in the water! Upper fall: 48 feet high, 200 feet wide. Paradise, Upper Peninsula Michigan. State park. Canoe rentals between the upper and lower falls. Autumn: golden yellow + brown water = surreal color combination.

name: Whispering Oaks - Oxford
notes: AANR-affiliated naturist resort on 200 wooded acres! 45 min from Detroit. Pool, hiking trails, RV campground. Family-friendly. May-September. Michigan's top-rated naturist resort.

name: Zingerman's Deli - Ann Arbor
notes: One of the world's best delis - Ann Arbor's pride! Sandwiches you can't close. 100+ cheeses. Ann Arbor downtown. U of Michigan campus. Food Network + Oprah + NYT wrote about it. The drive is outside, but it is absolutely worth it.

name: 🏨 Fitger's Inn - Duluth
notes: Authentic 1857 brewery conversion transformed into a boutique hotel with views of Lake Superior! Original industrial elements preserved – brick walls, beams. Close to Canal Park and Aerial Lift Bridge. On-site brewery and restaurant. Approx. $130/night. Perfect stop after North Shore Drive.

name: 🏨 Gunflint Lodge - Grand Marais
address: 143 S Gunflint Lake Rd, Grand Marais, MN 55604
notes: Remote wilderness lodge right on the Boundary Waters Canoe Area! Bungalows on Gunflint Lake, completely cut off from the world. Loon calls, aurora borealis opportunities, canoe trips. On-site restaurant. Deer + wolves in the garden. Approx. $150/night for a cabin. Book early.

name: Ax-Man Surplus Store - St. Paul
notes: John Waters Dollar General' - the most bizarre store in Minnesota! Aerospace parts, laboratory equipment, everything. Bizarre karaoke soundtrack always playing. St. Paul. Browse around for FREE. You buy something. You just didn't know it yet.

name: Big Ole Viking - Alexandria
notes: 28-foot Viking guards 'birthplace of America'! Kensington Runestone Museum: Norse runes in Minnesota (1362?). Alexandria, Central Minnesota. Historians are skeptical about the stone. Big Ole isn't. FREE outside. Museum: small entrance fee.

name: Boundary Waters Canoe Area
notes: 1 million acres of wilderness – accessible only by canoe! No roads, no motors, no electricity. Ely, NE Minnesota. Permit required (book early!). Loon cries at night. Milky Way without light pollution. Most remote spot in the Lower 48.

name: Glensheen Historic Estate - Duluth
notes: Victorian mansion + infamous double murder in 1977! Elizabeth Congdon + nurse murdered. 39-room mansion on Lake Superior. Duluth. Tours year-round. The murder mystery tour is the most popular. Naturally.

name: Gooseberry Falls State Park
notes: 5 spectacular waterfalls of the Gooseberry River right into Lake Superior! First stop on the legendary North Shore Drive. Easily accessible, 31 km of trails. Autumn = beautiful. The 5th waterfall = least visited and most romantic. Minnesota State Park sticker required ($7).

name: Indeed Brewing - Minneapolis
notes: NE Minneapolis neighborhood brewery with a great atmosphere! Day Tripper Pale Ale + Mexican Honey Imperial lager. Large patio. Food trucks. Community feel. NE Minneapolis Arts District. Best neighborhood brewery atmosphere in the Twin Cities.

name: Itasca State Park - Mississippi bron
address: 36750 Main Park Dr, Park Rapids, MN 56470
notes: HERE begins the Mississippi! You literally step over the source of North America's longest river on stepping stones – 2,552 km further on, it flows into New Orleans! Minnesota's oldest State Park (1891). Old-growth forests, 4,000-year-old Native American earthworks. $7.

name: Jay Cooke State Park - Swinging Bridge
notes: Spectacular suspension pedestrian bridge over the wild St. Louis River with its bizarre, jagged limestone rocks. Carlton Trail along the river = fantastic. Near Duluth (30 min). Autumn leaves + turbulent water = perfect photo opportunity. Minnesota's most dramatically shaped river.

name: Jolly Green Giant + Sprout - Blue Earth
notes: 55-foot GREEN GIANT along I-90 - Ho Ho Ho! Since 1979. Blue Earth = pea-producing county. Sprout now stands next to it too. Blue Earth, SW Minnesota. FREE. Pea Memorial Park. Meant completely seriously.

name: Kensington Runestone Museum
notes: Mysterious runestone: Vikings in Minnesota in 1362?! Found by a farmer in 1898. Inscription in runes. Historians say: forgery. But by whom? Alexandria, Central Minnesota. A good museum about a great mystery. Debate ongoing.

name: Kramarczuk's - Minneapolis
notes: Ukrainian deli + sausage master in NE Minneapolis since 1954! Kielbasa, pierogi, borscht. Everything handmade. NE Minneapolis, Ukrainian cultural heart. Cheap. Authentic. Phenomenal. Belgian sausage vs Ukrainian sausage: a debate to start while eating.

name: Largest Candy Store - Jordan
notes: Bright yellow building along the highway - 'Minnesota's Largest Candy Store'! Jordan, SW Minnesota. 45 min from Minneapolis. FREE to view. You will also buy candy. A monument to sugar consumption. Scarce competition for the title, but well-intentioned.

name: Lifestyle Minneapolis (Kasidie)
notes: Minneapolis lifestyle scene via Kasidie ​​platform! No fixed address found - event-based. Active online community. Search for Minnesota events via Kasidie.com. Private parties + hotel nights.

name: Mall of America - Bloomington
notes: Largest shopping mall in North America - own roller coaster INSIDE! Nicolet Park roller coaster + Sea Life aquarium + mini-golf. Bloomington, 20 min from Minneapolis. FREE entry. Attractions separate. A roller coaster in a shopping mall. Europe doesn't understand this.

name: Matt's Bar - Minneapolis
notes: Inventor of the JUCY LUCY – cheese fried IN the hamburger! Since 1954. Matt Bristol's creation. Cash only. Cedar Ave, Minneapolis. The cheese is melted liquid inside. Wait 3 min. Race with the '5-8 Club' to see who really invented it. Matt's was first.

name: Minnehaha Falls - Minneapolis
notes: 16m waterfall RIGHT IN THE MIDDLE OF Minneapolis - the only major city in the US with a waterfall within city limits! Famous from Longfellow's poem Song of Hiawatha. In winter, the drop freezes completely = just as spectacular. Bordering a regional park. FREE. Nice stop in the Twin Cities.

name: North Shore Scenic Drive - US-61
address: US-61, Duluth tot Grand Portage, MN
notes: 200 miles along Lake Superior's rugged coast! Split Rock, Gooseberry Falls, Tettegouche State Park. US-61 (Bob Dylan's birthplace + his famous album). FREE. Autumn: most colorful drive in Minnesota. Lake Superior looks like the ocean. Seriously.

name: Oakwood Club - Annandale
notes: AANR-affiliated naturist resort in Central Minnesota! Annandale, 1 hour from Minneapolis. Family-friendly. Contact via AANR locator. Minnesota summer = short but intense naturist season. May through September.

name: Paul Bunyan & Babe the Blue Ox - Bemidji
notes: Minnesota's iconic duo (1937) - lumberjack + blue ox! Bemidji claims to be the ORIGINAL Paul Bunyan location. Leech Lake shore. FREE. Iconic Midwest Americana. Bemidji: also the source of the Mississippi River.

name: SPAM Museum - Austin
notes: FREE museum dedicated to SPAM canned meat - brilliantly executed! Hormel Foods HQ. SPAM was born here in 1937. WWII: SPAM fed the Allies. Truly historic. Austin, S-Minnesota. I-90 corridor. FREE. Amazingly serious about a spam can.

name: Split Rock Lighthouse - Two Harbors
address: 3713 Split Rock Lighthouse Rd, Two Harbors, MN 55616
notes: Minnesota's most photographed landmark! 1910 lighthouse on dramatic cliffs above Lake Superior. Two Harbors, NE Minnesota. North Shore Scenic Drive nearby. Autumn: golden trees + blue lake = perfect postcard.

name: Surly Brewing - Minneapolis
notes: Minnesota's most awarded craft brewery! Doom + Furious IPA + Darkness Stout (annual release). Large brewery campus + restaurant + beer garden. SE Minneapolis. Surly changed Minnesota's beer regulations in 2011. Real politics.

name: Tettegouche State Park - Palisade Head
notes: Palisade Head and Shovel Point = most photographed spots on Lake Superior! Volcanic cliffs 60m directly above the lake. Baptism River Falls = largest waterfall entirely within Minnesota. 4 waterfalls in one park. Autumn + Lake Superior + red trees = surreal. Park sticker required.

name: The Saint Paul Hotel
notes: Classic grand hotel in the heart of Saint Paul (1910)! Rice Park view. F. Scott Fitzgerald's hometown. St. Paul city center. Everything within walking distance. Classic European hotel grandeur in America. Perfect for theater + dinner in the city center.

name: The Smack Shack - Minneapolis
notes: Minnesota's best lobster rolls + lobster mac & cheese! North Loop, Minneapolis. Formerly a food truck. Lobster in Minnesota: unexpected but phenomenal. Modern industrial interior. Reserve weekend dinners.

name: World's Largest Ball of Twine - Darwin
notes: 17,400-pound rope ball – Francis Johnson wound it for 29 YEARS! 12-foot diameter. Protected in its own gazebo. Darwin, Central Minnesota. 1.5 hours from Minneapolis. FREE. Weird Al Yankovic made a song about it. Small museum next door. Pure American bizarre obsession.

name: Abe's Bar-B-Q - Clarksdale
notes: Clarksdale BBQ legend RIGHT at the Crossroads intersection! Built in 1924. 'Come Back Sauce' - once you taste it, you'll always come back. US-61 & US-49 intersection, Clarksdale. Barbecue + Delta beer + blues atmosphere. Robert Johnson might have sat here eating on his Coca-Cola crate.

name: Close Encounters - Jackson (lifestyle)
notes: Mississippi's only regular lifestyle club! Off-premise club (no on-site play). Events-based. Jackson area. Find it via Kasidie.com. Mississippi's laws make on-premise clubs virtually impossible.

name: Delta Blues Museum - Clarksdale
notes: Blues BORN in the Mississippi Delta - this museum proves it! Muddy Waters' recorded shack is literally INSIDE the museum here. B.B. King's guitar. Robert Johnson's life story. Clarksdale, the heart of the Delta. A must for anyone who loves music.

name: Doe's Eat Place - Greenville
notes: Legendary steakhouse in a former greengrocery—for 80 years! Tamales + giant T-bone steaks. Greats came here. Greenville, Delta Mississippi. Cash only. No reservations. Wait in line. Presidents, governors, rock stars: all at Doe's.

name: Ground Zero Blues Club - Clarksdale
notes: Morgan Freeman's famous blues club in Clarksdale! Built in a former cotton warehouse. Live blues every weekend. Local musicians. Clarksdale town center. Freeman lives in Clarksdale. Sometimes he just walks in.

name: Lazy Magnolia Brewing - Kiln
notes: Mississippi's first microbrewery! Southern Pecan Ale = nationally known. Kiln, South Mississippi. Brett Favre's hometown, by the way. Award-winning Southern Pecan Brown Ale. Tours + tastings available. The fact that Kiln has a brewery is special in itself.

name: Longwood Octagon House - Natchez
notes: Largest octagonal Antebellum house in the US - NEVER finished! Construction stopped in 1861 when the Civil War broke out. Work never resumed. Upper floors rough. Downstairs completed, but the ladder is still there. Natchez. Quite a remarkable half-construction site. Unique concept.

name: Mammy's Cupboard - Natchez
notes: Restaurant UNDER the skirt of an 8-meter-tall mammy figure! Built in 1940. Local architect Annie Bost. Famous homemade pies + pastries. Natchez, US-61. Photo required BEFORE the dining experience. Order is important.

name: Margaret's Grocery - Vicksburg
notes: Theological park of stones built by a pastor for his wife! Reverend H.D. Dennis built this as a declaration of love for Margaret Rogers. Old school bus converted into a chapel. Colorful blocks. Vicksburg, US-61 North. FREE to view. Abandoned but epic. Pure Southern folk art.

name: Mississippi Petrified Forest
notes: 36-million-year-old petrified forest with a remarkable gemstone collection! Walking path through the fossils. Flora, central Mississippi. Privately managed. Small but special. Combine with Jackson for a day trip.

name: Natchez Trace Parkway
notes: Historic 716-mile trade route through 3 states! America the Beautiful pass valid. Natchez to Nashville. No trucks. No billboards. Beautiful secluded road past historic sites. Makes: one of the most beautiful drives in the South.

name: Robert Johnson Crossroads - Clarksdale
notes: THE crossroads where Robert Johnson sold his soul to the devil! Blues legend: Johnson achieved his guitar artistry through a satanic pact. 'Crossroads Blues' sung here. Eric Clapton covered it. Clarksdale, Mississippi Delta. FREE. Pure myth, but you feel something. Really.

name: Shack Up Inn - Clarksdale
notes: Sleep in REAL sharecropper shacks on a former plantation! Hopson Plantation. Shacks modernized with air conditioning + indoor plumbing. Blues memorabilia everywhere. Live music on the premises. Clarksdale, Mississippi Delta. One of the most unique hotel experiences in the US.

name: Turning Angel Statue - Natchez
address: Natchez City Cemetery, 2 Cemetery Rd, Natchez, MS 39120
notes: Grave statue looking at passing cars – say the locals! Memorial for victims of the Natchez Drug Co. explosion (1908). Natchez City Cemetery. FREE. Drivers say their heads turn along. It is an optical illusion. But still: slightly unsettling when you drive past it.

name: Windsor Ruins - Port Gibson
address: Windsor Ruins Rd, Port Gibson, MS 39150
notes: 23 cast-iron columns as the only remaining vestige of a grandiose plantation palace! Windsor Mansion burned down in 1890. Pillars stand like a ghostly monument. Port Gibson, Natchez Trace corridor. FREE. Incredibly photogenic. Film location. Surreal Greek temple vibe in the middle of a forest.

name: Witch's Grave - Yazoo City
address: Glenwood Cemetery, 601 Calhoun Ave, Yazoo City, MS 39194
notes: The 'witch' who cursed Yazoo City - her grave broke open during the Great Fire! Legend: Kate Fortune cursed the city. Her grave chain broke during the fire of 1904. Glenwood Cemetery, Yazoo City. FREE. Chain around the cemetery. A spooky story with eerie light.

name: 4 Hands Brewing - St. Louis
notes: St. Louis' best independent craft brewery! Citrus Circus IPA + Contact High Wheat. Laclede's Landing, St. Louis riverfront. Large taproom + frequent events. Anheuser-Busch is also here, but this is better.

name: Arabia Steamboat Museum - Kansas City
notes: 200 tons of pioneer goods excavated from an 1856 Mississippi shipwreck! Coffee, pots, shoes, medicine—all perfectly preserved in the river. Kansas City River Market. One of the most impressive excavation museums in America. The bottom of the Missouri River holds gold.

name: Arthur Bryant's BBQ - Kansas City
notes: Kansas City BBQ legend - Truman, Obama, and Clinton ate here! Brisket + burnt ends in a flat sandwich. Greasy fingers. No napkin helps. Brooklyn Ave, Kansas City. Since 1908. Authentic, old, tasty. KC BBQ is different from Memphis/Texas BBQ: here is the benchmark.

name: Boulevard Brewing - Kansas City
notes: Midwest's most awarded craft brewery - 'Midwest's Beer'! Tank 7 Farmhouse Ale + Unfiltered Wheat. Tours daily. Kansas City SW Boulevard. Tour Hotel: sometimes free with tour admission. Since 1989. Big and still locally proud.

name: Bridal Cave & Thunder Mountain Park
notes: Golf cart bar DEEP inside a cave on a mountain ridge! Bats included! Atlas Obscura lists this as truly unique - and it is true. Camdenton, Ozark Lake of the Ozarks region. If there is another drive-through golf cart bar in a bat cave, we don't know. For the most absurd drink of your life.

name: City Museum - St. Louis
notes: Not a museum – a SURREALISTIC play paradise for all ages! Giant climbing structures, cave system, rooftop Ferris wheel, secret rooms. Made from recycled industrial material. St. Louis city center. Absolutely one of the best things in the USA. Allow 4+ hours. REQUIRED!

name: First Sliced Bread City - Chillicothe
notes: Sliced ​​bread was sold for the FIRST time in Childlicothe - 1928! Otto Frederick Rohwedder's invention. Klingler Bakery. Childlicothe, N-Missouri. Hwy 36. 'The greatest thing since sliced ​​bread' - this is the best and the first. FREE. Plaque at the original bakery building.

name: Gateway Arch - St. Louis
notes: 630-foot-high stainless steel arch – truly impressive up close! Tram inside the arch to the top (America's strangest ride experience). Mississippi Riverfront. Underground museum. America the Beautiful pass valid! Much larger and more sweeping up close than in photos. Unique.

name: Leila's Hair Museum (closed 2025)
notes: 600+ hairpiece wreaths and jewelry made from human hair! Victorian America preserved loved ones' hair in jewelry. Leila Cohoon's 50-year collection. Independence, 20 min from Kansas City. 'Best hair museum' - the opposite of 'worst hair day'.

name: Mark Twain Boyhood Home - Hannibal
notes: Tom Sawyer and Huck Finn came to life here! Samuel Clemens' birthplace + museum. Hannibal, Mississippi River. Tom Sawyer Fence Whitewashing Contest every year in July. Hwy 36 'Way of American Genius' starts here.

name: Meramec Caverns - Stanton
notes: Jesse James hideout + Frank Lloyd Wright-style cave formations! Jesse James hid his gang and money here. Route 66 hidden gem. Self-guided boat tour. Stanton, Route 66 corridor. Combine with a Route 66 drive for a perfect Missouri day.

name: Museum of Osteopathic Medicine
notes: Medical wax museum with CREEPY surgical history! Skeleton of Andrew Taylor Still (founder of osteopathy). Patient records, instruments, human remains. Kirksville, N-Missouri. For medical curiosities enthusiasts: 10/10.

name: Ozark Caves & Mule Trading Post
notes: Branson, Missouri: kitsch entertainment capital of America! Country music shows, neon billboards, themed restaurants. Absolutely over the top, but completely visible. Branson, SW Missouri. The Las Vegas of country music.

name: Ozarks Folk Center... wait: Natural Pines Resort MO
notes: Adults-only clothing-optional + swingers resort in the Ozarks! Naturist and lifestyle activities. 21+. LGBT-friendly. Linn Creek, Lake of the Ozarks region. Open year-round. No pressure to participate in specific activities. The only open naturist/lifestyle resort in Missouri.

name: Pappy's Smokehouse - St. Louis
notes: Guy Fieri's Triple D favorite in St. Louis! Memphis-style ribs - smoked for 4-6 hours. ABSOLUTELY DELICIOUS. Olive Street, St. Louis. Line outside. Every day. No reservations. Closed when food runs out. Come early.

name: Route 66 Missouri - Joplin tot St. Louis
address: I-44/Route 66, Joplin tot St. Louis, MO
notes: Most beautiful stretch of Route 66 in the Midwest! Gay Parita Sinclair Station, Devil's Elbow, Meramec Caverns. Joplin to St. Louis via I-44. FREE road. Specifically follow old alignment for true 66 atmosphere. Most uninterrupted historic stretch of Route 66.

name: World's Largest Shuttlecocks - Kansas City
notes: Four 5.5-meter-high badminton shuttles scattered across the museum lawn! Claes Oldenburg + Coosje van Bruggen (1994). Deliberately absurdist. Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art, Kansas City. FREE exterior. Museum entrance separate. Art as a joke that you will appreciate later.

name: 🏨 Chico Hot Springs Resort
notes: Historic resort (1900) with open-air geothermal pools in the heart of Paradise Valley with views of the Absaroka Mountains! A magnet for movies and celebrities for decades. Great restaurant, quiet and romantic. 45 min from Yellowstone. Grizzly bear spotting in the area. Approx. $120/night.

name: 🏨 Murray Hotel - Livingston
notes: Legendary historic hotel from 1904 in the authentic cowboy town of Livingston! Sam Peckinpah lived here for years. Buffalo Bill and Calamity Jane once stayed here. Classic Western bar, great diner. Gateway to Yellowstone (55 min). Approx. $100-150/night. Real character, no plastic.

name: Avalanche Lake + Trail of the Cedars
address: Avalanche Creek Trailhead, Glacier NP, MT 59936
notes: Easiest major hike in Glacier! Trail of the Cedars (1.6 km) through 600-year-old cedar forests + Avalanche Lake (6 km extra) with waterfalls plunging directly into the lake. Chance of encountering both black and grizzly bears. Bear spray is mandatory. The park's most popular trail.

name: Bayern Brewing - Missoula
notes: America's only authentic Bavarian brewery! Munich recipes! Real Lager, Hefeweizen, and Amber – made straight from the traditional recipe. Missoula. Beer made just like in Bavaria. Els and Serge: this is the closest thing to Belgium you can find in Montana. Tours + tastings. Outdoor beer garden.

name: Beartooth Highway
address: US-212, Red Lodge naar Cooke City, MT
notes: Charles Kuralt's 'Most Beautiful Road in America'! 109 km over 3,333m passes. Snowfields in July! Red Lodge to Cooke City, Montana. FREE. But check weather conditions: closes during snowstorms. Summer only (May-Oct). Most spectacular Montana driving experience.

name: Big Sky Resort ⛷️ Ikon
address: 1 Lone Mountain Trail, Big Sky, MT 59716
notes: Ikon Pass: 7 DAYS. LARGEST ski area in the US (5,850 acres)! Lone Mountain summit (3,403m) = incredible views. Lots of terrain = never crowded. The summit is for experts, but the gondola zone is perfect for all levels. Big Sky town is an interesting stop in the summer too. If you are passing through Montana in the SUMMER: mountain hiking + summer gondola. A definite stop on the route through MT!

name: Evel Knievel birthplace - Butte
notes: Daredevil Evel Knievel BORN in Butte, Montana! Museum + his original motorcycle + memorabilia. Butte: fascinating mining town on a gift. Knievel attempted to break 277 bones. Achieved 433 fractures. FREE to see outside. Museum: small contribution.

name: Garden of 1000 Buddhas - Arlee
notes: 1,000 white Buddhas in a 'dharma wheel' pattern on the Montana prairie! Built by Ewam Buddhists. Living community. Arlee, Flathead Valley. Flathead Lake area. FREE. Peaceful and completely unexpected Montana stop. Surreal contrast: wild mountains + serene Buddhas.

name: Glacier National Park
notes: Crown of the Continent' - the most spectacular wilderness park in the USA! Going-to-the-Sun Road: 80 km mountain road (open June-Oct). Grizzly bears, mountain goats, glacial lakes. America the Beautiful pass valid! Vehicle timed entry tickets: Book MONTHS in advance in summer!

name: Glacier National Park Wild Clothing Optional - Avalanche Creek
address: Avalanche Creek Trail, Glacier NP, MT 59936
notes: Wild swimming holes in the heart of Glacier NP! Avalanche Creek: popular for cold mountain river swimming. Clothing-optional, common in remote spots. Parks Canada pass. Goldbug-style, but Montana mountain river. Cold. COLD.

name: Going-to-the-Sun Road
notes: Most beautiful mountain road in the US - 80 km through the heart of Glacier NP! Logan Pass: 2,026 m. Waterfalls, glacier views, wildlife. America the Beautiful pass included. June-October. Reserve vehicle permit MONTHS in advance. One of America's five most beautiful drives. No exaggeration.

name: Grinnell Glacier Trail - Glacier NP
notes: One of the most beautiful hikes in the US to an active glacier with a turquoise lake! Option: take the boat across Swiftcurrent + Josephine Lake (saves 5 km of hiking). Stromatolites (fossilized bacteria, 1.5 billion years old) at the lake. Chance of moose and grizzly bears. Book the boat early.

name: Hiawatha Mountain Bike Trail
address: East Portal (Taft Trailhead), Route 506, Taft, MT
notes: 15 miles of former Milwaukee Road railway line through 7 DARK tunnels (longest 2.7 km!) and 7 spectacular trestles along the Idaho/Montana border. Bring your headlamps! E-BIKES WELCOME and very handy for the shuttle back up. Open mid-June to mid-September. $14 pp + optional shuttle.

name: Hidden Lake Overlook - Logan Pass
address: Logan Pass Visitor Center, Glacier NP, MT 59936
notes: 4.8 km return from Logan Pass through alpine meadows to spectacular views of Hidden Lake. Mountain goats literally walk among the hikers! Early morning = no crowds. Same starting point as Highline Trail - plan both on one day. America the Beautiful is valid.

name: Highline Trail - Glacier NP
address: Logan Pass Visitor Center, Glacier NP, MT 59936
notes: MOST iconic hike in Glacier NP! 19 km along a spectacular mountain ridge high above Going-to-the-Sun Road. Sometimes literally chained along the rock face. Grizzly bears frequently visible. Start EARLY - Logan Pass parking lot fills up by 7 am in July/August. Shuttle back. America the Beautiful valid.

name: Kettlehouse Brewing - Missoula
notes: Missoula's favorite craft brewery! Cold Smoke Scotch Ale = Montana icon beer. Duo taprooms: Northside + Southside. Loyal to local customers. No franchise hassle. Since 1995. The soul of Missoula.

name: Lifestyle Billings (Kasidie)

address: 756 Battlefield Tour Rd, Crow Agency, MT 59022
notes: Custer's Last Stand - June 25, 1876! Native American perspective AND cavalry perspective well presented. Crow Agency, SE Montana. America the Beautiful pass valid! Controversial heritage honestly highlighted. Emotional terrain.

name: Lolo Hot Springs - Lolo
notes: Historic hot springs along the Lewis & Clark route! Indoor + outdoor pools. 38-40°C. Lolo, 45 min from Missoula. US-12. 'Back to Nature' clothing - optional overnight stays occasionally! Goldbug-style vibe. Rustic and authentic.

name: Mackenzie River Pizza - Missoula
notes: Montana-inspired gourmet pizza with wild mushrooms + bison! Misoula center. Local ingredients. Since 1989. Montana soul in a pizza. Good craft beers alongside the pizza. University town atmosphere + Bergers eat here.

name: Makoshika State Park
notes: Montana's LARGEST state park - badlands + dinosaur fossils! Triceratops and T-rex bones found here. Glendive, E-Montana. Hoodoos and erosion cliffs. Spring + fall: best. Summer: very hot. America the Beautiful pass NOT valid - state park.

name: Montana Club - Great Falls
notes: Montana's most famous steakhouse chain - homegrown ranch meat! Montana Prime beef straight from local ranches. Great Falls + multiple locations. Cowboy-style fine dining. Big-size meat. This is how Montana eats. Seriously.

name: Oasis 33 - Billings area
notes: Clothing-optional naturist park near the Montana-Wyoming border! Billings area. Primitive campground. Montana Naturist Organization closed in 2021 - this is an alternative. Private. Call ahead. Small but the only option in Montana.

name: Our Lady of the Rockies - Butte
notes: 27-meter-high Madonna figure on a ridge above Butte! Visible from everywhere in the valley. Illuminated at night. Gondola tour to the top from Butte. Butte. Up-gondola tour = best panorama above a mining town.

name: Pompey's Pillar National Monument
notes: The only remaining physical evidence of the Lewis & Clark Expedition! William Clark carved his name and date into the rock face: July 25, 1806. It is still there. Really. Pompleys Pillar, East Montana. Small entrance fee. Managed by the BLM. A point of contact with history from over 220 years ago. Highly recommended.

name: Boys Town - Omaha
notes: Famous youth residence for homeless boys - city status of its own! Own mayor: always an elected youth. Omaha area. Film Boys Town (1938): Spencer Tracy + Mickey Rooney. FREE visitor admission. Museum about Father Flanagan's legacy.

name: Carhenge - Alliance
notes: Stonehenge recreated from 39 GRAY CARS in Nebraska prairie! Jim Reinders built this in 1987 for his father's memorial. Alliance, NW Nebraska. Prairie wind, empty horizon, car-Stonehenge. FREE. All year round. Best at sunrise or sunset. America's most perfect absurdist monument.

name: Chimney Rock
notes: Landmark for Oregon Trail pioneers - the 'Great Post' of the prairie! 146 meters high. Pioneers called this their turning point. Bayard, W-Nebraska. Scotts Bluff Corridor. America the Beautiful pass valid! Just as you've always seen 'Die Prärie'. Now in real life.

name: Empyrean Brewing - Lincoln
notes: Lincoln's beloved craft brewery + Lazlo's restaurant concept! Apricot Ale + Burning Skye Scottish Ale are the most popular. Near Haymarket District, Lincoln. Since 1992. Nebraska veteran. Combine with a Haymarket walk for a Lincoln day.

name: Kool Aid Monument - Hastings
address: Kool Aid Park, 2nd & Minnesotan Ave, Hastings, NE 68901
notes: Kool Aid INVENTED in Hastings, Nebraska in 1927! Edwin Perkins' invention. Fountain + monument + museum. Hastings city center. FREE. Kool Aid Man statue awaits. Jim Jones used Kool Aid as a murder weapon. The drink has a dark image.

name: Le Bouillon - Omaha
notes: French brasserie in Omaha's historic Old Market district! Authentic bistro cuisine. Good wine list. Old Market, downtown Omaha. Best European dining in Nebraska. Make a reservation. Omaha's surprisingly good food scene.

name: Niobrara Scenic River
notes: Nebraska's most popular kayak river - 76-mile National Scenic River! Waterfalls, canyon, pools. Niobrara, N-Nebraska. America the Beautiful pass valid! July-August: busy. But always worth it.

name: Pioneer Village - Minden
notes: 26 buildings + 50,000+ artifacts about American daily life 1830-1970! One man's obsession: Harold Warp started this in 1953. Minden, South Nebraska. I-80 corridor. The most comprehensive Midwest daily life museum. Spend half a day. Overflowing with nostalgia.

name: Runza Drive-In - Lincoln
notes: Nebraska's iconic fast food: RUNZA sandwiches are legendary! Ground meat + cabbage-filled bun. Doesn't exist anywhere else. Lincoln + multiple Nebraska locations. Completely regional. Unforgivably tasty for such a simple concept. Els: this is the Nebraska version of a sausage roll.

name: Sandhills of Nebraska
notes: Largest sand dune system in the Western Hemisphere! 500 km² of stabilized grass dunes. Bison and prairie dogs. Valentine, N-Nebraska. Niobrara River Scenic Byway. FREE. Few visitors. Cycling, kayaking, camping in absolutely pristine prairie.

name: Scotts Bluff National Monument
notes: Impressive sandstone formations - a navigation point on the Oregon Trail! Highway uphill. Panorama over Platte River Valley. Slight, SW Nebraska. America the Beautiful pass valid! Beautiful sights at dawn. Less visited than you would expect.

name: Stuhr Museum of the Prairie Pioneer
notes: Living museum: Victorian village with 60+ original buildings! Costume actors in the village. Henry Fonda was born here. Grand Island, central Nebraska. May-Sept: best period for actors. Central Nebraska: no excuse not to stop on I-80.

name: Thunderhead Brewing - Kearney
notes: Nebraska's most authentic prairie craft brewery! Local grain + pure Nebraska flavors. Kearney, I-80 corridor stopover. I-80 makes it easy to stop. Cozy taproom after the long prairie drive.

name: Area 51 - Black Mailbox
notes: The iconic BLACK MAILBOX along the ET Highway! A local rancher had installed this specifically for 'alien mail'. Near Alamo, NV. Along NV-375. FREE. Photo stop. Most photographed mailbox in the world (possibly).

name: Bare Moon Ranch - Wells
notes: Nevada rural naturist ranch retreat! Wells, N-Nevada. Private ranch setting. Clothing optional. By-the-Year atmosphere. Contact via website. Nevada has few options, but this is an authentic ranch.

address: 4543 N Rancho Dr, Las Vegas, NV 89130
notes: Las Vegas' oldest craft brewery - anti-Strip! Red Hydrant Ale + Fat Dog Stout. NW Las Vegas. Local pub atmosphere. Not on the Strip, but that is an advantage. A good escape from the casino circus.

name: Clown Motel - Tonopah
notes: Scariest motel in America - 500+ CLOWNS in every room! Next to an old cemetery. Seriously. Tonopah, Central Nevada. Tonopah is also 'Star City'. Stay overnight or not? You decide. Theme suites available. Sleep tight.

address: NV-375, Crystal Springs tot Warm Springs, NV
notes: 'World's most photographed highway' - through Area 51 grounds! Rachel NV: 54 inhabitants. The 'Area 51' Alien Center along the road. Little A'Le'Inn café: 'earthlings welcome'. FREE ride. GPS coordinates of Area 51 gate for the photo. August 2019: 2 million people 'stormed Area 51'. This is that place.

name: Hoover Dam
notes: 726-foot-high concrete marvel - built Las Vegas and all of Southwest America! Built 1931–1936. Art Deco finish. Boulder City, Nevada. 45 min from Las Vegas. Tours inside the dam itself. Lake Mead: US first man-made reservoir (unfortunately shrinking).

name: In-N-Out Burger - Las Vegas
address: 4888 Dean Martin Dr, Las Vegas, NV 89103
notes: West Coast legend you can't eat in the East! Double-Double Animal Style: the cult order. Las Vegas (handy entry point for VEG to CA). Fresh, local ingredients. Never frozen meat. A ritual for every West Coast road tripper.

name: International Car Forest of Last Church
notes: 40+ cars planted nose-first in the desert ground - Cadillac Ranch Nevada! Goldfield, Central Nevada. Abandoned mining town. Free to visit. FREE. Combine with Tonopah for a central Nevada day. Nevada's darkest, avant-garde roadside art.

name: Las Vegas Strip Neon Museum
address: 770 Las Vegas Blvd N, Las Vegas, NV 89101
notes: Graveyard of iconic Vegas neon signs! Caesars Palace, Stardust, Sands - all buried here. North Las Vegas Blvd. Day + night tours (night is better). If Vegas makes you nostalgic: this is the place.

name: Lehman Caves - Great Basin NP
notes: Hidden national park with spectacular caves + bristlecone pines! Lehman Caves: stalactites + shields. Wheeler Peak: 3,982m. Bristlecone pines 3,000+ years old. America the Beautiful pass valid! Baker, E-Nevada. Least visited NP in the Lower 48.

name: Lotus of Siam - Las Vegas
address: 953 E Sahara Ave, Las Vegas, NV 89104
notes: Gault-Millau Nominee Thai: 'Best Thai Restaurant in North America'! James Beard Nominee Chef Saipin Chutima. E Sahara Ave, Las Vegas (not the Strip). Northern Thai cuisine: different from standard Thai. Book weeks in advance. Strip-avoiding locals know this.

name: Red Rock Canyon - Las Vegas
address: Scenic Loop Dr, Las Vegas, NV 89161
notes: Spectacular red cliffs 30 min from the Las Vegas Strip! 13-mile scenic loop. Hiking trails for all levels. BLM managed. $15 per vehicle. Go early (before 8 am) for parking. Perfect counterpoint to the neon frenzy of the Strip.

name: Reno Arch - Reno
notes: 'The Biggest Little City in the World' - neon arch lights up the night! 1926 slogan. Reno's signature neon arch. N Virginia St, downtown Reno. FREE. Best photo: night. Reno is not Las Vegas. Smaller, cheaper, more honest.

name: Sea Mountain Inn - Desert Hot Springs CA... nearby NV alternative: Las Vegas lifestyle
notes: Las Vegas is the swingers hotspot of the USA - dozens of clubs and events! H&M Club, Colette Las Vegas, various hotel takeovers. Las Vegas Strip + surroundings. Search via Kasidie: Las Vegas lifestyle events are numerous. What happens in Vegas... you already know.

notes: 7 towers of fluorescent boulders in the middle of the Mojave Desert! Ugo Rondinone's 2016 installation. Permanent. 10 miles south of the Las Vegas Strip on I-15. FREE. Sunrise = incredible light. The most Instagram-worthy stop in all of Nevada. Really.

name: Shoe Tree of Fallon
notes: Cottonwood tree COVERED with hundreds of passersby's shoes! US-50 'Loneliest Road in America'. People have been throwing shoes for years. Fallon, Nevada. FREE. Photo stop along the road. A tree that turns out to be a clothing store.

name: The Brewer's Cabinet - Reno
notes: Reno's most acclaimed craft brewery! Local and regional ingredients. Seasonal rotations. Downtown Reno. Grand taproom. Glass as antique furniture theme. Unique interior. Combo with Reno Arch for a downtown Reno evening.

name: Valley of Fire State Park
address: Valley of Fire Hwy, Overton, NV 89040
notes: Neon red Aztec rock formations – the most photographed spot in Nevada! Wave-like layered sandstone. Star Trek location. Overton, 90 min from Las Vegas. State park: $10 entrance fee. 'Fire Wave' trail: hike to an absolutely surreal landscape.

name: Algonquin Resort - St. Andrews
address: 184 Adolphus St, St. Andrews, NB E5B 1T9
notes: Castle hotel by the sea - 'the grande dame of New Brunswick'! 1889 Tudor-style resort. Golf. Spa. Sea view. St. Andrews-by-the-Sea, SW NB. One of the most beautiful hotels in Atlantic Canada. St. Andrews is NB's most charming coastal town anyway.

name: Cape Enrage - Rappelling + Zipline
address: 650 Cape Enrage Rd, Waterside, NB E4H 3N3
notes: Rappel down 45m steep cliffs above the Bay of Fundy! Zipline + climbing courses + 1838 lighthouse. Waterside, Fundy coast. May-October. Advance registration required. Adrenaline rush with the best tidal cliff views in North Brabant.

name: Chez Françoise - Shediac
notes: Best lobster restaurant in Shediac - the 'Lobster Capital'! Leibster from our own tongs. Homemade desserts. Shediac town centre. Summer: always full. Reserve. A whole lobster, butter, bread: it is enough.

name: Fundy National Park
address: 8 Alma Park Rd, Alma, NB E4H 1B4
notes: National park with the most extreme tides on Earth! Hiking trails along red sandstone cliffs. Sea kayaking. Alma as a base. Fresh rolls at Alma's bakeries are legendary. Parks Canada Pass. Autumn: maple colors + silence = perfect.

name: Fundy Trail Parkway
address: 1000 Main St, St Martins, NB E5R 1B2
notes: 41 km of pristine Fundy coastline - NOT accessible by regular car! Cycle or walk along 90m-high rocky cliffs. St. Martins, 45 min from Saint John. May-Oct. Electric bike rental available. Wildest and most pristine coastline of the Maritimes.

address: 131 Discovery Rd, Hopewell Cape, NB E4H 4Z5

Timing is everything. 38 km from Moncton. May-October. High tide kayak tour also possible – a completely different experience.

name: Kouchibouguac National Park
notes: Seal colony + sand dunes + caribou herd in one park! Kouchibouguac (pronounced: 'koo-she-boo-GWAK'). Northumberland Strait. Parks Canada Pass. Bike paths through swamp + beach = authentic New Brunswick.

name: Maritimes Swingers Club
notes: Maritimes-wide lifestyle club for NB + NS! Events based. Couples and singles. Sign up via website. Maritimes discreet but active lifestyle scene. Private events + hotel meetups.

notes: Tidal wave drives UP the Petitcodiac River - twice a day! The river flows in reverse as the Bay of Fundy tide enters. Bore Park, Moncton city centre. FREE. Schedule on website. Small, but the essence of Fundy tidal power is visible.

name: NB Naturist Club (NBNC) - South NB
notes: Non-landed naturist club for all of Atlantic Canada! Family-oriented. Events at members' homes and visited locations. South New Brunswick base. Contact via federation. No permanent site, but an active community.

name: Picaroons Brewing - Fredericton
notes: New Brunswick's most beloved craft brewery! Best Bitter + Maple Cream Ale are the classics. Fredericton city centre - everything within walking distance. Since 1994. Local pride. Combine with Fredericton's historic city centre.

name: Tide & Boar - Moncton

notes: 45 buildings + costume actors: Acadian life from 1770-1939! French culture that survived the English deportation. Caraquet, North North coast. Summer: living historical village in full operation. French-Canadian heritage at its most authentic.

notes: 15-meter-high steel axe as a monument to the forestry industry! Nackawic officially became the 'Forestry Capital of Canada' in 1991. Contains a time capsule that must never be opened. Nackawic, Saint John River. FREE. Impressive. Look up.

name: World's Largest Lobster - Shediac
notes: 90 tons of concrete lobster guards the 'Lobster Capital of the World'! Shediac: warm water beach + best lobster in the Maritimes. Photo + Fisherman's Paradise restaurant next door. Shediac, 30 min from Moncton. FREE photo. Then eat a real lobster. A must-do combination.

name: World's Longest Covered Bridge - Hartland

name: Arethusa Falls - Crawford Notch SP
notes: Highest waterfall in New Hampshire - 61m free fall! 4.8 km return through dense forest along Bemis Brook with several smaller waterfalls along the way. The Crawford Notch area is also beautiful for scenic drives. Combine with Mt Willard (panorama with hardly any climbing). Parking $5.

name: Artist's Bluff - Echo Lake
notes: NH's most photographed viewpoint! 1.6 km loop to a spectacular panorama over Echo Lake. Perfect autumn photo – boats on the lake, fiery pink forests all around. Short but steep climb. FREE! Combine with Bald Mountain (+800m) for a higher view. Near Flume Gorge.

name: Cathedral Ledge - North Conway
address: Echo Lake State Park, North Conway, NH 03860
notes: Spectacular 120m rock face - climb or drive to the top! North Conway, White Mountains. Echo Lake State Park. Swim in the lake at the foot. Visible year-round. State Park entrance. View of the Saco River Valley.

name: Clark's Trading Post - Lincoln

Four-legged chicken, 'man-eating clam', and a blackjack used in an 1897 bank robbery: the museums here are incredible.

name: Common Man - Windham
notes: NH's most beloved local restaurant group - authentic New England! Local ingredients + high-quality comfort food. Windham + multiple NH locations. Since 1971. The NH feeling on one plate. More than a restaurant: NH culture.

Option: historic Cog Railway (rack railway from 1869, still steam-powered). View over 6 states + Canada.

name: Mystery Hill (America's Stonehenge) - Salem
notes: Mysterious stone structures old enough to be pre-Columbian! Observatory, sacrificial table, druid-like enclosure. Salem, S-New Hampshire. Historians debate: Native American, settlers, or... Celts? FREE exterior. Entrance to the ground itself.

name: Santa's Village - Jefferson

name: Woodstock Inn + Brewery - Woodstock
notes: White Mountains micro-brewery + inn - local favorite! Piggy's Porter + Autumn Breeze are their stars. Woodstock, Kancamagus Highway start. Perfect stopover after the Kancamagus drive. NH's most-visited brewery-hotel combination.

notes: THE FIELD where the Hindenburg crashed on May 6, 1937! Naval Air Base. Freely accessible monument. Lakehurst, Central NJ. 'Oh, the humanity!' - spoken here by a journalist. FREE to visit. Small memorial plaque marks the exact spot.

notes: Second oldest naturist club in the US (1932) next to Rock Lodge! Hamburg, NW-NJ. Family-oriented. Mountains + pool. Contact via website for a trial visit. Both founded in the same year - historic NJ naturist community.

name: Stickwork Sculptures - Various NJ

notes: 42 acres with 270+ sculptures hidden in a botanical park! Life-size Impressionist paintings as 3D sculptures. Hamilton, Central NJ. One of the most beautiful open-air museums in the US. Saison: everything you see changes with the season.

name: White Manna Hamburgers - Hackensack
notes: NJ slider legend – mini-burgers on a grill next to the buns! Since 1939. 50 cm² kitchen. Classic. Hackensack, North NJ. Lunch only and often a queue. NJ is the slider state. This is where it all began.

name: Meow Wolf - House of Eternal Return - Santa Fe
notes: Immersive art 'narrative experience' - Alice in Wonderland for adults! House of secrets: refrigerator leads to another universe. Santa Fe. Run by an artist collective. The ORIGINAL Meow Wolf - since expanded to other cities. Allow 2-3 hours. Insanely creative.

name: PistachioLand - Organ
notes: 30-foot-tall pistachio nut sculpture guards a pistachio farm! Largest pistachio farm in the US. Tours available. Organ, near White Sands Missile Range. Shop: pistachio wine, ice cream, shelled nuts. A must-see stop on the way to White Sands.

name: Roswell UFO-Themed McDonald's
notes: McDonald's with a flying saucer roof – unique on Earth! Green alien design inside. UFO menu variations. Roswell, N Main Street. Yes, you are going to eat here. No, it tastes the same. Probably the most photographed fast food restaurant in the world.

name: Roswell Walking Dead Alien
notes: Life-sized alien sculptures everywhere in the streets of Roswell! Streetlights with alien heads. Shop windows full of extraterrestrial beings. Roswell town centre. FREE walking. The whole town is one big bizarre attraction.

name: Taos Pueblo
notes: Inhabited earth village for 1,000 years - UNESCO World Heritage Site! Tiwa-speaking people still live here without electricity. Taos Pueblo is open to visitors. Camera permit: extra. Most impressive living Native American site in the US.

name: Tent Rocks National Monument
notes: Pointed white 'tent-rock' hoodoos - completely surreal! Narrow slot canyon walk through the peaks. Cochiti, central NM. BLM managed. Spring + autumn: perfect. Summer: hot. FREE. Walking path: 2.5 miles back. A MUST be done.

name: The Mira Vista Resort - El Paso TX nabij NM grens
notes: Closest to NM AANR resort - just across the border in TX! El Paso TX, 15 min from NM. Family-friendly. Adults allowed. NM does not have its own AANR resort. Best option for naturist-minded visitors NM.

name: The Shed - Santa Fe
address: 113½ E Palace Ave, Santa Fe, NM 87501
notes: Santa Fe legend for New Mexican red chili cuisine! Green vs red chili: 'Christmas' is ordering both at the same time. Downtown Santa Fe. 1692 hacienda building. Drive every lunch. Reserve dinner. 'Red or green?' is New Mexico's state question. Answer: Christmas.

name: Tinkertown Museum - Sandia Park
address: 121 Sandia Crest Rd, Sandia Park, NM 87047
notes: Handmade universe behind walls of bottle-bottom glass! Ross Ward spent 40 years carving a 22-room miniature city + circus out of wood. Sandia Park, Sandia Mountains. April-November. Children and adults alike are equally amazed. Pure folk art.

name: Turquoise Trail - Albuquerque naar Santa Fe
address: NM-14, Tijeras to Santa Fe, NM
notes: 50 miles of mountain artist villages via the back route! Madrid: former coal mining town now full of art galleries. Cerrillos: turquoise mining town from the 1800s. NM-14 from Albuquerque to Santa Fe. FREE. Meanders through the Sandia Mountains. Lunch in Madrid is mandatory.

name: White Sands National Park
notes: 275,000 acres of snow-white gypsum dunes – nowhere else on Earth! Driving through them feels like driving on another planet. Alamogordo, Southwest. America the Beautiful Pass. Sunset: ultraviolet light + white dunes = almost painfully beautiful.

name: 🏨 Mohonk Mountain House
address: 1000 Mountain Rest Rd, New Paltz, NY 12561
notes: Victorian fairytale castle on a ridge above Hudson Valley – built in 1869! National Historic Landmark. 2,200-acre wilderness estate with private lake. 85 miles of hiking trails. Autumn here is world-famous. All-inclusive (3 meals/day). Above budget but ABSOLUTE bucket list. Approx. $350-500/night.

name: 🏨 The Sagamore Resort - Lake George
notes: Classic grand resort (1883) on its own island in Lake George - the Queen of American Lakes! Historic docks, private cruise ship, spa, multiple restaurants. Home of President Eisenhower. Adirondacks backdrop. Accessible via bridge. Approx. $200-300/night.

name: Brooklyn Brewery
notes: NYC's most famous craft brewery - Brooklyn Lager is a city symbol! Williamsburg. Tours + taproom. Since 1988. Nationally renowned. Combine with Peter Luger Steakhouse for the ultimate Brooklyn day. Brooklyn Lager in a beer glass in Williamsburg: perfect photo.

name: Catskill Mountains - Overlook Mountain
notes: Abandoned hotel ruins on a ridge + panorama over the Catskills! Overlook Mountain Trail: 2.4 mile ascent. Woodstock, Catskills. FREE hike. Woodstock + ruins + view = perfect day.

name: Coney Island Boardwalk
notes: Vintage amusement park + freak show + hot dogs + boardwalk - old-world kitsch! Cyclone (1927) wooden roller coaster. Nathan's Famous. Sideshow. Brooklyn, NYC. Subway accessible. Summer: busy but the atmosphere is unique. National Hot Dog Eating Contest on July 4: a religious experience.

name: Cooperstown - Baseball HOF
notes: National Baseball Hall of Fame - the holiest in American sports! Cooperstown, Otsego Lake. Induction Weekend every year in July. Finger Lakes region, Central NY. Self for non-baseball fans: Americana at its deepest.

name: Dia:Beacon - Hudson Valley
notes: Spectacular art museum in a former Nabisco factory on the Hudson! Slide: Beacon: minimalist and Land Art masters. Beacon, Hudson Valley. Accessible by train from NYC (Metro North). Weekend trip: train + museum + lunch in Beacon = perfect day.

name: Hedo NYC - New York
notes: New York's most famous lifestyle club event organizer! Hedo NYC organizes monthly events in private venues. Manhattan + surrounding area. Register via Kasidie.com + your own website. NYC has the most active lifestyle scene in North America.

name: High Line - Manhattan
address: Gansevoort St to 34th St, New York, NY 10001
notes: Abandoned train track transformed into a floating garden above Manhattan! 2.3 km green park at a height of 10m. Art + nature + city view. West Chelsea, Manhattan. FREE. Best way to explore West Chelsea and Hudson Yards. Sunset here over the Hudson = spectacular.

name: Intrepid Museum
address: Pier 86, W 46th St, New York, NY 10036
notes: WWII aircraft carrier + Concorde + submarine in the Hudson! SS Intrepid: aircraft carrier. Enterprise Space Shuttle. West Side Highway, Manhattan. Book tickets online. Unique for children + adults. Half-day minimum.

name: Juniper Woods - Middle Island
notes: AANR-affiliated naturist resort on Long Island! 40+ acres. Pool + hot tub. Family-friendly. Middle Island, Long Island. Since 1947. May-September. The easiest logistical naturist option from NYC.

name: Katz's Deli - New York
address: 205 E Houston St, New York, NY 10002
notes: Legendary deli from 1888 - 'When Harry Met Sally' scene here! 'I'll have what she's having.' Pastrami sandwich is a must. Lower East Side, Manhattan. Drive fast, it goes quickly. Keep the map handy! Most iconic deli on earth. Eating here is New York.

name: Lockport Locks - Erie Canal
notes: DOUBLE lock stairlift from 1825 - English engineering miracle! Lifts ships 12m up in steps via 5 locks. Lockport, W-NY, Erie Canal. Tours available. Cave of the Winds nearby. The canal that made New York City great.

name: Lucy-Desi Museum - Jamestown
notes: Museum for Lucille Ball and Desi Arnaz - 'I Love Lucy' homeland! Jamestown is Lucy's birthplace. Original costumes, scripts, and props from the show. Jamestown, West New York. Lucy Comedy Festival in August: comedians everywhere.

name: Niagara Falls - NY kant
notes: Maid of the Mist boat: straight for the waterfall - SOAKING WET! America's oldest state park (1885). NY side less commercial than Canada side. America the Beautiful pass + Maid of the Mist separately. Summer: spectacle. Winter: frozen cliffs = magical.

name: Peter Luger Steak House - Brooklyn
notes: New York's most talked-about steakhouse (1887) - cash only! Porterhouse for Two is the only choice that counts. Williamsburg, Brooklyn. Reserve 2-4 weeks in advance. The cash-only policy makes it even more exclusive than it already is.

name: Sagamore Hill - Oyster Bay
address: 20 Sagamore Hill Rd, Oyster Bay, NY 11771
