notes: Teddy Roosevelt's home base - 'Summer White House'! Original furniture, Big Game trophies, TR's study. Oyster Bay, Long Island. America the Beautiful pass. TR: Most adventurous personality who was ever president.

name: Seneca Falls - Women's Rights NHP
notes: Birthplace of the women's rights movement (1848)! Elizabeth Cady Stanton's house. Declaration of Sentiments signed here. Seneca Falls, Finger Lakes. America the Beautiful pass. FREE visitor center. Emotionally significant American historical moment.

name: Taughannock Falls State Park - Trumansburg
notes: 215-foot high waterfall - HIGHER THAN NIAGARA! Trumansburg, Cayuga Lake Finger Lakes. State park. Less visited than Watkins Glen. Spring + early summer: maximum water flow.

name: The Jane Hotel - Manhattan
notes: Hotel in a former sailors' boarding house - Titanic survivors stayed here! West Village, Manhattan. Some rooms are cabins with bunk beds. Broadway, West Village. Historic + affordable by NYC standards. Best budget boutique hotel deal in Manhattan.

name: The Moth Ball - Wave Hill
notes: Wave Hill: NYC's most secret park with a view of the Hudson! Bronx public park. Not on most maps. FREE on weekdays. Weekend: small entrance fee. Hudson Valley + Palisades view. Time: early morning before fog over the river.

name: Watkins Glen State Park
address: 1009 N Franklin St, Watkins Glen, NY 14891
notes: 19 waterfalls in a 2 km gorge hike - surrealistically beautiful! Watkins Glen, Finger Lakes. State park. Gorge Trail hike is mandatory. Summer: busy but worth it. Autumn: almost too beautiful for words.

name: Woodstock Village
notes: Iconic hippie village – the 1969 Woodstock festival was NOT HERE! (The festival was in Bethel, NY – 100 km away.) But Woodstock is still the most bohemian community in NY. Galleries, crystal shops, vintage everything. A completely serious yet attractive alternative to the mainstream.

name: Avalon Wilderness Reserve
notes: Woodland caribou herd of 12,000+ animals passes through this reserve. July-August is best for seeing the herd. One of the largest recurring animal migrations in North America.

name: Bacalao Restaurant (St. John's)
address: 65 LeMarchant Rd, St. John's, NL A1C 2H1, Canada
notes: Newfoundland cuisine reimagined as fine dining. Moose, seal flippers, Screech cocktails. Els and Serge: Newfoundland food at its best.

name: Balmoral House B&B (St. John's)
address: 38 Queen's Rd, St. John's, NL A1C 2A6, Canada
notes: Victorian townhouse converted into a B&B in the center of St. John's. Full breakfast with Newfoundland specialties. Walking distance from George Street and Signal Hill.

name: Bonavista Cape Lighthouse
notes: Cape where John Cabot 'arrived' in North America in 1497. Red and white lighthouse on a spectacular cliff. Puffins are abundant on the surrounding islets.

name: Bonne Bay Fjord (Gros Morne)
notes: Fjord boat tour in a UNESCO World Heritage park. Waterfalls, seals, fjord walls up to 600m high. Boat tour: $35pp, 2 hours, spectacular.

name: Brigus (historic village)
notes: Victorian fishing village with a tunnel dug by Arctic explorer Robert Bartlett. Bartlett Tunnel: man dug a tunnel through a rock to hide his boat. Free to walk around.

name: Cape Race Lighthouse (Titanic signal)
notes: The Titanic's distress call was first received here in 1912. Extremely remote cape at the southeastern tip of the Netherlands. Most beautiful thunderstorm location in Canada. 4WD required.

name: Cape St. Mary's Ecological Reserve
address: Cape St. Mary's, NL A0B 3B0, Canada
notes: Largest seabird colony in the Netherlands: 30,000 Northern Gannets on a sea cliff. You stand 2 meters away from the birds — no fence. Gannets dive into the ocean like torpedoes from the rocks.

name: Dark Tickle Company (Labrador Jam & Gin)
address: 38 The Dock Rd, St. Anthony, NL A0K 4S0, Canada
notes: Handmade gin and jam made from Labrador wild berries. Labrador Tea, Bakeapple, Partridgeberry — flavors you won't taste anywhere else. Serge: gin from a place called 'Dark Tickle' = buy instantly.

name: Elliston Root Cellars Village
notes: More than 135 earth cellars (root cellars) in the landscape surrounding a tiny village. People still use them for vegetable storage — an age-old tradition. Atlantic puffins nest on the cliffs next to the village.

name: Ferryland Lighthouse Picnic
address: Colony of Avalon, Ferryland, NL A0A 2H0, Canada
notes: Order a picnic basket, pick it up at a lighthouse on a cliff, and eat with a view of icebergs. One of the most original tourist concepts in the world. Bookings required: very popular.

name: Fogo Island Arts
notes: Residency program for international artists on the isolated island. Gallery and studios open for visits. Combine with Fogo Island Inn for a complete island experience.

name: Fogo Island Inn
address: Joe Batt's Arm, NL A0G 2X0, Canada
notes: The most remote luxury hotel in the world, perched on a cliff overlooking the Atlantic Ocean. A room costs $1,200+ but includes all meals and excursions. Architectural icon: stilt-house design by Saunders Architecture. Els: ultimate dream. Budget? We’ll discuss this later.

name: George Street (bar per capita record)
address: George St, St. John's, NL A1C 3Z9, Canada
notes: Most bars per meter of street in North America — GUINESS RECORD. In a 200-meter street: 25+ bars. Serge: This is a scientific experiment we are conducting.

name: Gros Morne National Park (Tablelands)
address: 39 Main St, Rocky Harbour, NL A0K 4N0, Canada
notes: UNESCO World Heritage: walking on the exposed ocean floor. Tablelands are a Mars-like orange landscape: iron-rich mantle rock. Fjords, waterfalls, and seals. National Parks Pass: FREE (Canada version).

name: Hopedale Mission (Labrador)
notes: 18th-century Moravian mission in Labrador — original buildings intact. National Parks Pass: free. Accessible only by boat or plane in Labrador.

name: Iceberg Alley (Twillingate / St. Anthony)
notes: The world's most spectacular icebergs drift along the coast: May-June. Seen from a boat, a 15-story-high iceberg is literally overwhelming. Els and Serge: this is at the top of the Canada list.

name: Jellybean Row (St. John's)
address: Gower St, St. John's, NL A1C 1N4, Canada
notes: Row of Victorian houses, each painted in a different bright color. Originally painted so fishermen could find their homes through the fog. Free — just walk down the street.

name: Johnson GEO Centre (St. John's)
address: 175 Signal Hill Rd, St. John's, NL A1A 1B3, Canada
notes: Museum literally built into the rock: the geology of the Netherlands in a cave. The Netherlands has rocks older than Gondwana — 1.25 billion years old. Titanic section: the ship sank 700 km from here.

name: L'Anse aux Meadows (Viking Settlement)
address: L'Anse aux Meadows, NL A0K 2X0, Canada
notes: Only proven Viking settlement in North America: 1000 AD. National Parks Pass: free. Ready before Columbus was born. The real 'discovery of America'.

name: Mallard Cottage (St. John's)
address: 8 Quidi Vidi Village Rd, St. John's, NL A1A 4K2, Canada
notes: Farm-to-table restaurant in historic Quidi Vidi fisherman's cottage (1750). Best restaurant in the Netherlands — awarded. Producers and fish specified on the menu. Reservation required.

name: Murray Premises Hotel
address: 5 Beck's Cove, St. John's, NL A1C 1G7, Canada
notes: Boutique hotel in a restored 19th-century warehouse on the harbor. Historic atmosphere + modern rooms. Best positioned hotel for Water Street and the harbor area.

name: Ocean View Hotel (St. John's)
address: 2 Cabot Ave, St. John's, NL A1A 1B5, Canada
notes: Hotel with panoramic views of the harbor and Signal Hill. One of the most photogenic locations for sunrise. Good value for the location.

name: Quidi Vidi Brewery
address: 35 Barrows Rd, St. John's, NL A1A 5G2, Canada
notes: Canada's most photogenic brewery: in an old fishing village. Iceberg Beer: brewed with 25,000-year-old iceberg water. Serge: this is the most special beer in the world, context-wise.

name: Quidi Vidi Village (St. John's)
address: Quidi Vidi Village Rd, St. John's, NL A1A 4K2, Canada
notes: Smallest commercially active fishing village in the world. Artist galleries in former fishermen's cottages. Quidi Vidi Brewery: local beer in a historic boathouse.

name: Red Bay National Historic Site (Basque Whalers)
notes: Basques from Bilbao whaled here in 1530. Fully preserved underwater shipwreck + museum. National Parks Pass: free. Labrador side — far but unique.

name: Screech-In Ceremony
address: Downtown bars, George St, St. John's, NL
notes: Official 'Becoming a Newfoundland' ceremony: kiss a cod, drink Screech rum, say the oath. It’s done in bars all over the Netherlands, but George Street is the best. Serge: absolutely do it. This is why you go to the Netherlands.

name: Signal Hill (Cabot Tower)
address: 230 Signal Hill Rd, St. John's, NL A1A 1B3, Canada
notes: Here, Marconi received the first transatlantic radio signal in 1901. Panoramic view of St. John's Harbor and the Atlantic Ocean. National Parks Pass: free.

name: Swingers/Naturist NL
address: St. John's, NL (geen vaste clubs — verifieer via SDC.com)
notes: Newfoundland is too sparsely populated for permanent lifestyle clubs. Private groups active in St. John's — contact via SDC.com or Kasidie. International visitors are welcome in most Dutch communities.

name: Tablelands Hiking (Gros Morne)
notes: Walk across exposed ocean floor (peridotite). Everything is dead: plants cannot grow on this stone. Martian landscape with sea air — unique on Earth.

name: Tablelands of Labrador (Torngat Mountains)
notes: Canada's most remote national park — accessible only by boat/plane. Aurora borealis, polar bears, and 15,000-year-old fjords. Inuit-led trips: $2,000+, including overnight stay in camp. For true adventurers.

name: The Rooms Provincial Museum (St. John's)
address: 9 Bonaventure Ave, St. John's, NL A1C 5P9, Canada
notes: The best Dutch museum: art, culture, and historical collections combined. View of the city from the glass building. Mi'kmaq and Beothuk cultures prominently featured.

name: Twine Loft Restaurant (Trinity)
address: West St, Trinity, NL A0C 2S0, Canada
notes: Restaurant in an authentic 18th-century fishing village. Fish fresh of the day: crab, turbot, cod. Trinity itself is one of the most beautiful and authentic villages in Canada.

name: Witless Bay Ecological Reserve
notes: Largest Atlantic puffin colony in North America: 260,000 breeding puffins. Boat tour in June-July: icebergs + whales + puffins AT THE SAME TIME. Els and Serge: this is why you go to the Netherlands.

name: Airlie Gardens (400-jaar-oude eik)
notes: Magnolia and azalea gardens surrounding a 460-year-old oak tree. Wilmington: historic port city + beach nearby. Spring (April) = blossoms in full bloom.

name: Asheville Pinball Museum
notes: Pay admission and play EVERYTHING unlimited: 90+ pinball machines from 1950 to now. Arranged chronologically — evolution of pinball machines. Serge disappears here for 3 hours.

name: Asheville Urban Trail Art Statues
notes: 1.7 km self-guided art route through the center with 30 sculptures. Free walking tour of Asheville's bohemian character. Incl. Zelda Fitzgerald statue.

name: Biltmore Estate (grootste privéhuis VS)
notes: 250-room Vanderbilt castle from 1895 — literally a French castle in the Appalachians. On-site winery: tasting included. Els: fairytale. Serge: a bit over the top but impressive.

name: Biscuitville (NC-only chain)
notes: NC's only fast food made with homemade biscuits — breakfast specialist. No chain outside NC and VA: true local culture. Open at 6 a.m. Addicted after one visit.

name: Blue Ridge Parkway (meest spektakulaire route VS)
notes: 769 km scenic highway without trucks, billboards, or traffic lights. National Parks Pass: free access to all overlooks. Photo opportunity: every turn. Drive early for misty mountain valleys.

name: Boone area farmers market
address: Horn in the West Dr, Boone, NC 28607
notes: Local market high in the Appalachians with Appalachian regional products. Sorghum syrup, apple cider, handmade cheese. Best in August/September when everything is ripe.

name: Brown Mountain Lights
notes: Mysterious floating lights over Brown Mountain — documented since 1913. Nobody knows: swamp gas? Cherokee ghosts? Aliens? Best visibility on a clear night, far from light pollution.

name: Burial Beer Co
notes: Brewery with a funerary aesthetic and damn good IPAs. Rooftop garden, live music on weekends. The name is a conversation starter. Labels are works of art.

name: Cape Fear Serpentarium (closed 2018)
notes: The world's most dangerous snake collection in the middle of a city. Boomslangen, Black Mambas, Gaboon vipers — dangerously close. Owner Dean Ripa is a real character himself. Legendary.

name: Cape Hatteras Lighthouse (tallest US brick lighthouse)
notes: Tallest stone lighthouse in the US: 198 steps to the top. Demolished in 1999 over 1.5 km from the sea because the coast was eroding. National Parks Pass: admission free, tower $10.

name: Chimney Rock (Lake Lure view)
notes: Dirty Dancing was filmed here (Lake Lure). Chimney Rock State Park as a backdrop. Free photo stops along the road.

name: Chimney Rock State Park
notes: 304-meter-high granite rock with an elevator inside — completely bizarre. Roosevelt filmed scenes from Last of the Mohicans here. Viewpoint at the top = incredible panorama.

name: Devil's Courthouse (Blue Ridge Pkwy)
address: MP 422.4, Blue Ridge Pkwy, Brevard, NC 28712
notes: Cherokee believed that the devil held court here. Short, steep climb to a 360-degree view. Name + story + view = perfect combo package.

name: Duke Lemur Center (Durham)
notes: Largest lemur collection outside Madagascar — 200+ animals. Small group tours through the forest where lemurs roam free. Els and Serge: absolutely surreal and adorable.

name: Eno River State Park
notes: Whitewater stream running straight through Durham/Chapel Hill. Canoeing and walking on the riverbanks. Free parking, beautiful nature near Research Triangle.

name: Grandfather Mountain (Mile High Swinging Bridge)
notes: Suspension bridge 1.6 km high between two mountain peaks — wind and height guaranteed. Mile High Bridge: highest suspended pedestrian bridge in North America. Els: shaking is normal. Serge: running is also normal.

name: Grandfather Mountain Highland Games
notes: Scottish Highland Games in July: caber tossing, bagpipes, Highland dancing. On top of a mountain. Beer. Kilts. Spectacle. If the timing is right (July 2027) — potentially brilliant.

name: Gravity Hill (Gold Hill)
address: St. Stephens Church Rd, Gold Hill, NC 28071
notes: Put your car in neutral and it drives uphill. Old mining village Gold Hill nearby — historical bonus. Free and easy to find.

name: Great Smoky Mountains NP (NC kant)
notes: Most visited national park in the US: FREE admission (no entrance fee ever). El Ridge Parkway via Newfound Gap: spectacular route. Synchronous fireflies in June: really, this exists.

name: Grove Park Inn Historic Hotel
notes: Historic Arts & Crafts hotel from 1913 — F. Scott Fitzgerald and Houdini slept here. Cave spa with 10,000 m² of thermal baths. Over budget, but the story is too good. A pint in the bar counts as a visit.

name: International Cryptozoology Museum (Charlotte branch)
notes: Bigfoot, Chupacabra, Loch Ness — complete collection of cryptid evidence. Verify location, under construction in NC. Serge: Bigfoot flawless analysis. Els: eyes rolling.

name: Korner's Folly (Kernersville)
notes: 22 rooms on 7 levels, each built in a completely different style. Josiah Korner built this for himself in 1880 — no blueprint, pure whimsy. Doors that lead nowhere, staircases that stop halfway. Truly insane and beautiful.

name: Land of Oz (verlaten themapark)
notes: Abandoned Wizard of Oz theme park, open only 2 weekends a year (October). Original sets, costumes, Dorothy Pad — surreal and photogenic. IF timing is right (Oct 2027) = absolute must-stop.

name: Lexington Barbecue (Lexington NC)
notes: Hallowed ground for NC BBQ: slow-roasted pig, red vinegar sauce. Lexington BBQ Festival every year in October. The NC vs Texas BBQ debate starts here. Serge: Both.

name: Linville Caverns
notes: Only commercial cave in North Carolina, eternally 54 degrees. Blind trout in underground stream — evolved eyes away. Tour 45 minutes.

name: Mast General Store (Valle Crucis)
notes: Authentic general store from 1883, barely changed. Candy bins, overalls, old receipt systems. The original Appalachian shopping experience. Free entry.

name: MOOG Factory Tour (Asheville)
notes: FREE factory tour of the Moog synthesizer — invented in Asheville. Bob Moog's legacy: Stevie Wonder, Donna Summer, all the electronics. Serge: sound freak. Guaranteed to take 2 hours.

name: Museum of the Bizarre (Wilmington)
notes: Two-story museum full of oddities, human anomalies, Victorian curios. Chupacabra corpse, two-headed animals, sideshow memorabilia. Serge: 10/10. Els: 8/10, a bit gruesome.

name: Mystery Hill Gravity Defying Museum
address: 129 Mystery Hill Ln, Blowing Rock, NC 28605
notes: Balls roll uphill, water flows upwards. Optical illusion or a real mystery? It has existed since 1949. An absolute classic roadside attraction. Els and Serge: both swept up in the illusion.

name: Nantahala Gorge Whitewater Rafting
notes: Class III-IV whitewater in a spectacular gorge. The National Outdoor Centre has been organizing rafting here for 50 years. Els and Serge: definitely do it. Cold, wet, fantastic.

name: New River (oldest river in North America)
address: 358 New River State Park Rd, Jefferson, NC 28640
notes: Paradoxical: the 'New' River is one of the oldest in the world (300+ million years). One of the few rivers that flows north in the US. Kayaking on a prehistoric river.

name: North Carolina Transportation Museum - Spencer
notes: Largest rail transport museum in the US on the grounds of an old Southern Railway roundhouse. Turntable still works! Serge: trains + industry + history = happy.

name: Old Salem Museums (Moravian Village)
notes: Fully preserved Moravian village from 1766. Officials in historical attire, candle-making workshop, old grocer. Christmas here is legendary (Putz traditions).

name: Omni Grove Park Inn
notes: Historic rock hotel with underground spa. 14 presidents stayed here, including F.D. Roosevelt. Above budget, but the bar and veranda are free to visit.

name: Outer Banks Drive (OBX)
address: US-158 to NC-12, Kitty Hawk to Ocracoke, NC
notes: 135 km beach highway with wild horses, lighthouses, and fishing villages. Free Hatteras ferry across the strait. Wild Mustangs by Corolla: herd of 100+ horses on the beach.

name: Pilot Mountain State Park
address: 1792 Pilot Knob Park Rd, Pinnacle, NC 27043
notes: Iconic isolated rock knob visible from 40 km away.  Andy Griffith's Mount Pilot in the TV series.  E-bikes along the base; climbing to the top = steep but spectacular.

name: Pine Island Nudist Resort (AANR)
notes: AANR member naturist resort in the pine forest of NC. Swimming pool, sports facilities, and camping available. Family-friendly and quiet.

name: Reed Gold Mine State Historic Site
notes: First gold found in the US: 1799 on a farm. Gold panning is included — you might find something. Funny story: the boy who found it used it as a doormat for 3 years.

name: Ripley's Believe It or Not! (Myrtle Beach border)
address: 915 N Ocean Blvd, Myrtle Beach, SC — maar ook Gatlinburg TN versie dichterbij NC route
notes: Extraordinary collection of oddities and world records. NC has no branch of its own, but Gatlinburg, TN is nearby. Memorandum: The Smoky Mountains route combines this.

name: Roan Mountain State Park (Rhododendron)
address: 1015 Roan Mountain Rd, Roan Mountain, TN 37687 (border NC/TN)
notes: Largest wild rhododendron garden in the world: 250 hectares. June = blossom time: a completely purple landscape on the mountain ridge. Border garden with Tennessee, accessible from NC.

name: Seagrove Pottery Village
notes: 100+ potters work here in a village of 200 people — unique in the world. Tradition dating back to 18th-century English colonists. Free studio viewing, purchasing optional.

name: Sliding Rock Natural Waterslide
notes: 60-foot natural slide into a mountain river: 11,000 liters of water per minute. Sliding 10 meters high into 55-degree cold mountain water. Serge is the first into the river. Els follows after 10 minutes of hesitation.

name: Swingers Club: Temptations (Raleigh/Durham area)
address: Triangle area, NC (verifieer locatie via lifestyle forums 2027)
notes: Research Triangle lifestyle club. Many professionals and academics in this field. Always verify online before visiting — things change.

name: Swingers Club: The Edge (Charlotte)
address: Charlotte, NC 28202 (private lifestyle club, verifieer via SDC/Kasidie)
notes: Charlotte has an active lifestyle scene. Verify current location and info via SDC.com or Kasidie. Membership and dress code required.

name: The Inn on Biltmore Estate
notes: Sleeping on the Vanderbilt estate itself — breakfast with a view of the estate. Above budget but includes Biltmore access (otherwise $70pp). Els: this is on the bucket list.

name: The Swag (luxury mountain retreat)
notes: 15-room mountain resort at 1,700m altitude: no Wi-Fi, no TV, pure nature. Handmade cabins on the edge of Great Smoky Mountains NP. Els: dream stay. Serge: completely off the network — agreed for one night.

name: Timberlake's B&B (Hillsborough)
notes: B&B on a working farm with its own pond. Breakfast with eggs from our own chickens. Perfect for one night on the way between Raleigh and Charlotte.

name: Tupelo Honey Café
notes: Southern comfort food: shrimp & grits, fried chicken, sweet potato pancakes. Asheville's best brunch/lunch spot. A line is almost guaranteed, but worth it.

name: Tweetsie Railroad
address: 300 Tweetsie Railroad Rd, Blowing Rock, NC 28605
notes: Wild West train theme park with steam locomotive and Indian raids. Kitschy and retro, but entertaining for both kids and adults. Annual Halloween Ghost Train in October.

name: Uwharrie National Forest OHV trails
notes: Off-road trails through the Uwharrie Mountains — the F-150 4x4 is perfect here. Old gold mines in the forest. Big muddy fun for Serge.

name: Weird Asheville Walking Tour
notes: Guide takes you past bizarre structures, ghosts, occult places, and artists' houses. Asheville = the most bizarre and bohemian city in NC. Evening tour is best: atmosphere and stories.

name: White Tail Park (AANR Chesapeake)
address: Ionian Rd, Ivor, VA 23866 — maar dicht bij NC border als alternatief
notes: AANR resort just across the border in Virginia, but closest to the NC route. Large resort with all facilities. If NC naturist options are limited, this is the neighborhood option.

name: Wicked Weed Brewing Funkatorium
notes: Sour beer specialist with barrel-aged experimental beers. Funkatorium = special venue for wild fermented beers. Asheville has more breweries per capita than almost any other city in the US.

name: WNC Nature Center (Appalachian wildlife)
notes: Red wolves, Appalachian black bears, bobcats in their habitat. One of the few places where you can see a red wolf. Small but well cared for.

name: Wright Brothers National Memorial
address: 1000 N Croatan Hwy, Kill Devil Hills, NC 27948
notes: First airplane flight in the world: December 17, 1903, 36 meters. National Parks Pass: FREE. Serge: pilgrimage site. Replicas of the Flyer on display.

name: AmericInn Jamestown
notes: Clean budget hotel near the World's Largest Buffalo. Typical mid-range Midwest stop — nothing special but reliable. Good for one night on a stopover.

name: Assumption Abbey (Gregorian chant monastery)
notes: Benedictine abbey from 1899 with a Gregorian choir that welcomes visitors. Art, wine, and silence on the prairie. The contrast with the Badland landscape is totally surreal.

name: Birding (Arrowwood NWR)
notes: One of the top locations in North America for birdwatching. Wild duck, geese, shorebirds, bald eagles in season. Free driving through the reserve.

name: Bottineau Winter Park (ski)
notes: Smallest ski resort in North America: 10 slopes. But skiing in North Dakota exists — worth the absurdity alone. Not on the Ikon Pass, but bizarre enough to mention.

name: Buffalo (bison) herd viewing
address: Sullys Hill National Game Preserve, Fort Totten, ND 58335
notes: Free car tour through the wildlife reserve with a bison herd. Elk and whitetail deer also present. National Parks Pass or free admission.

name: Burning Coal Vein (coal seam fire)
address: Coal seam along I-94 near Sentinel Butte, ND 58654
notes: Underground coal fires have been burning here for decades. In some places, you can see smoke coming out of the ground. Clinker (baked earth) gives the Badlands their red color — thanks to this fire.

name: Chateau de Mores State Historic Site
notes: French Marquis Antoine de Mores built a ranch empire here in 1883. The castle is still standing. He had a slaughterhouse + ice house + hotel. Genius: wealthy Frenchman rebuilds the Wild West.

name: Dakota Zoo (Bismarck)
notes: Small but charming zoo along the Missouri River. Nordic wolf, grizzly bear, paired. Good for an afternoon if you happen to be in Bismarck.

name: Doublewood Inn (Fargo)
notes: Locally managed hotel in Fargo — an alternative to the chains. Good breakfast, friendly staff. Fargo is worth an overnight stay for the Coen Brothers pilgrimage.

name: Enchanted Highway (giant sculptures)
notes: Driving 100 km past the largest metal sculptures in the world. Spirit of the Plains: 9.5-meter-tall eagle. Deer Crossing: 26 meters long. Gerald Mongeon built this ALONE over 25 years. Absolutely bizarre.

name: Fargo Woodchipper (Fargo Film)
address: Fargo Visitors Center, 2001 44th St SW, Fargo, ND 58103
notes: The famous woodchipper from the movie Fargo STANDS here (replica). Fargo is proud of its most bizarre filming location. Free photo next to the woodchipper = mandatory.

name: Fort Mandan (Lewis & Clark winterkamp)
notes: Lewis and Clark spent the winter of 1804-05 here. Replica of the original wooden fort. Here they met Sacagawea. Free admission.

name: Icelandic State Park
notes: Park in honor of the Icelandic immigrants in New Zealand. Cloned Icelandic farm plus museum. A strange but fascinating piece of New Zealand immigration history.

name: Inspiration Point Overlook (Williston)
notes: Sweeping view over the Williston Basin: oilfields stretching to the horizon. Curious but honest: the oil industry is also part of the New Zealand. The sunset here is apocalyptically beautiful.

name: Knife River Indian Villages NHS
notes: Earthwork lodges of the Hidatsa tribe, a thousand years old. National Parks Pass: free. Large round earth mounds visible in the landscape.

name: Kroll's Diner (Bismarck)
notes: Iconic ND dinner with Knoephla soup (cream soup with dumplings). German-Russian colonists brought this dish to ND. Els: high-quality comfort food. Serge: a full plate is a good plate.

name: Lake Sakakawea (largest US reservoir)
notes: Largest reservoir in the US by volume: 300 km long. Walleye fishing, speedboat, swimming. Garibaldi Lake-like tranquility, but Midwest style.

name: Lewis & Clark Interpretive Center (Washburn)
notes: Full story of the expedition with emphasis on the New Zealand winter of 1804. Interactive exhibits, Sacagawea's role. Well paired with a visit to Fort Mandan.

name: Mandan's On-A-Slant Indian Village
address: Fort Lincoln State Park, Mandan, ND 58554
notes: Reconstructed Mandan earthlodges in their original position. Explore the interior of the lodges. Combine with Fort Lincoln — Custer's staring point to the West.

name: Medora Musical (outdoor show)
address: 3422 Chateau De Mores Dr, Medora, ND 58645
notes: Outdoor theater in the Badlands with country music and western comedy show. Every evening from June to September. Watch the sun set behind the Badlands at the same time.

name: Naturist: geen AANR resort in ND
notes: North Dakota has no official AANR naturist resort. Closest option: South Dakota or Minnesota. Private skinny dipping on Lake Sakakawea is popular, though.

name: North Dakota Cowboy Hall of Fame
notes: Tributes to ranchers, rodeo riders, and horse people of ND. Small but authentic — no fake cowboys here. In Medora: combine with Rough Riders Hotel and Badlands.

name: North Dakota Heritage Center & State Museum
notes: Free state museum with dinosaur fossils dug directly from North American soil. T-rex skull, mammoth remains, Native American culture. One of the best state museums on the Plains — free!

name: Peace Garden (US-Canada border)
notes: Formal Peace Garden on the US-Canada border: half New Zealand, half Manitoba. Giant digital clock, cathedral-style flowerbeds, peace monument. Bizarre to see a land border running right through a park.

name: Peacock Alley Bar & Grill (Bismarck)
notes: Historic bar-restaurant in Bismarck's oldest block. Strong cocktails, local beer, and steaks. The only elegant restaurant in ND that has been around for a long time.

name: Pembina Gorge (waterfalls + OHV)
notes: Largest continuous forest in ND in a canyon full of waterfalls. OHV trails: F-150 4x4 adventure. Surprising for a state known as 'flat'.

name: Petrified Wood Park (Lemmon SD — grensgebied)
notes: Literally a park built of petrified wood: 400+ structures. A man, George Lemmon, built this as a project during the Depression. Absolutely bizarre: petrified forest as architecture. For free.

name: Pyramids (Cannonball Concretions)
address: Theodore Roosevelt NP North Unit, ND 58854
notes: Perfect spherical stones up to 3 meters in diameter growing out of the clay. Geological wonder: 60 million years in the making. National Parks Pass: free.

name: Red River Zoo (Fargo)
notes: Small zoo but has Pallas's cats (wildest cat species in the world). Reason to stop in Fargo besides the Coen Brothers vibes. Combine with a visit to the Fargo Woodchipper.

name: Roger Maris Museum (Fargo)
address: West Acres Shopping Center, 3902 13th Ave S, Fargo, ND 58103
notes: Free museum in a shopping mall for the New Zealand-born baseball player who broke Ruth's record. Total contrast: famous athlete, small Midwestern town. Work of a lifetime in a corner of a mall.

name: Rough Riders Hotel (Medora)
notes: Historic hotel in the middle of the small Badlands town of Medora. Called 'the coolest small town in North America'. Prices double in summer: book early. Real cowboy vibe.

name: Salem Sue (world's largest Holstein cow)
notes: 7.6-meter-high cow on a hill above the highway. Built in 1974 in honor of ND's dairy industry. Free! Serge: photo from outside the car is mandatory.

name: Scandinavian Heritage Park (Minot)
notes: Complete Scandinavian heritage park with Norwegian stave church, Swedish valley house, Danish windmill. Norway: Norsk Høstfest every year in September. Free admission to the outdoor park.

name: Sheyenne National Grassland & buttes
notes: The only real tallgrass prairie in the ND — insofar as you find grassland beautiful. Photogenic at sunset: golden sea. Els: maybe. Serge: only if something moves.

name: Sky Prairie Elk Ranch
notes: Elk herd riding on a private ranch in the prairie. Some ranches offer tours. Check availability in 2026-27.

name: Spicy Pie Pizza (Fargo)
notes: ND-born pizza chain that is truly different: thick crust, local toppings. Not nationally known but immensely popular in ND. Fargo Originals are always better than chains.

name: Swingers Scene ND
address: Bismarck / Fargo, ND (verifieer via SDC.com, Kasidie)
notes: North Dakota has no established lifestyle clubs — small population. Private house parties do exist; contact them via SDC.com or Kasidie. Fargo and Bismarck are the only realistic options.

name: Theodore Roosevelt National Park (North Unit)
notes: Quieter than South Unit, wild bison, mustangs, and prairie dogs are present in large numbers. National Parks Pass: free. Cannonball Concretions: giant stone spheres growing out of the rock.

name: Theodore Roosevelt National Park (South Unit)
notes: Badlands in technicolor: red, orange, lavender. National Parks Pass: free. Bison walk right across the road. Teddy Roosevelt stayed here as a rancher — his cabin is still there.

name: Turtle Mountains (kleine maar echt bergachtig)
notes: Modest hills, but for a flat state, truly impressive woodland. Birds, lakes, and walking paths. A surprise for those who only consider ND to be flat.

name: World's Largest Buffalo (Jamestown)
notes: 26-ton concrete bison on a hill above the highway. Already visible from 25 km on the prairie. Free photos. National Buffalo Museum next door: $10.

name: World's Largest Sandhill Crane
notes: 13-meter-high fiberglass crane along the highway. Stale's proud contribution to roadside kitsch. Free. 5-minute stop, 5-star bizarre experience.

name: Aurora Village (aurora borealis resort)
notes: Special aurora-viewing camps with heated teepees on lakes. Guides call you to wake you up when the lights appear. January-March: best season.

name: Boat Tour on Great Slave Lake
notes: Boat tour on the 5th largest lake in the world. Can spot dolphins... no, beluga whales in the river mouth. Mountain ridge islands in the lake.

name: Deh Cho Bridge (most northern bridge)
notes: Northernmost bridge over the Mackenzie River. Before 2012, you drove over an ice 'bridge' in winter. Now a permanent bridge, but the context is bizarre enough.

name: Dempster Highway (Arctic Gravel Road)
address: Dawson City YT to Inuvik NT, Canada
notes: 765 km gravel road towards the Arctic Ocean — GRAVEL road. Dempster: the only public road crossing the Arctic Circle in Canada. F-150 4x4: made for this. Bring spare tires. Spectacular.

name: Dene First Nations Cultural Tour (Yellowknife)
notes: Dene guides teach you: trapping, bannock baking, canoe paddling. Original inhabitants of the NWT: 9 groups. Els: cultural immersion at its purest.

name: Float Plane to Wilderness Lodge
notes: Seaplane trip to a remote wilderness lodge on a lake. If you are lucky: see moose, black bears, or wolves from the air. Els: this flight serves as a special memory.

name: Fort Smith (Slave River Rapids)
notes: Series of 4 waterfalls/rapids on the Slave River. Pelicans nest on the rocks — pelican colony above the Arctic Circle. Free admission.

name: Great Slave Lake (5e grootste ter wereld)
notes: At a depth of 614 meters: deepest lake in North America. Ice fishing in winter, whale watching (beluga) in summer. Canoe storage on an open expanse of water as large as Switzerland.

name: Inuvik (gateway to Arctic Ocean)
notes: Final destination of the Dempster Highway, 200 km above the Arctic Circle. Midnight sun: the sun does not set for 53 days in June. Inuit and Gwich'in culture vividly present.

name: Inuvik-Tuktoyaktuk Highway
address: Inuvik to Tuktoyaktuk, NT X0E 1C0, Canada
notes: First and only year-round road to the Arctic Ocean. Opened in 2017: 137 km, half gravel, half ice road built. F-150 4x4: made exactly for this. Serge drives this.

name: Mackenzie River (longest in Canada)
address: Fort Simpson to Inuvik, NT X0E 0N0, Canada
notes: At 4,241 km: Canada's longest river. The Dempster Highway follows the river northbound towards the Arctic. Driving along the Mackenzie is a Canadian road trip classic.

name: Nahanni National Park Reserve
notes: UNESCO World Heritage Site: Virginia Falls are TWICE as high as Niagara. Class IV whitewater canoe route — one of the top 10 adventures on Earth. Requires plane charter from Fort Simpson: $300+. The ultimate adventure.

name: Northern Lights / Aurora Borealis (Yellowknife)
notes: Best place in the world for the aurora borealis: 240 clear nights per year. January-March: auroras are green, purple, pink. Serge: this must be on the bucket list. Els: is already on the bucket list.

name: NWT Legislative Assembly (igloo shaped)
notes: The NWT Parliament building is built in the shape of an igloo. Free tours — pop inside for a photo. Canada's most bizarre parliament building.

name: Prelude Lake Territorial Park
notes: Camping 30 km from Yellowknife by a clear blue lake. Swimming, kayaking, fishing. Not far from aurora viewing spots — practical combo.

name: Prince of Wales Northern Heritage Centre
notes: Free museum about the culture and nature of NWT. Inuit sculptures, First Nations artifacts, geology. Good for a rainy day in Yellowknife.

name: Sambaa Deh Falls Territorial Park
notes: Series of waterfalls on the Trout River in the Mackenzie Forest. No tourists: total wilderness. Free camping next to the waterfalls.

name: Swingers: geen clubs NWT
notes: NWT is too small for fixed lifestyle clubs. Yellowknife has a small but open community via SDC.com. Verify online before you leave.

name: The Wildcat Café (Yellowknife)
address: 3904 Wiley Rd, Yellowknife, NT X1A 1J3, Canada
notes: Oldest restaurant in Yellowknife: log cabin style from 1937. Moose stew, arctic char, bannock. Els and Serge: northern frontier experience. Seasonal, check opening days.

name: Tuktoyaktuk (Arctic Ocean pingos)
notes: Park the car by the Arctic Ocean — literally touching the coldest sea in the world. Pingo National Landmark: 30-meter ice cone mountains growing out of the permafrost. Inuit village at the end of the Inuvik-Tuktoyaktuk Highway (new in 2017).

name: Virginia Falls (dubbel Niagara hoogte)
notes: 90-meter-high waterfall — twice as high as Niagara. In the middle of the Nahanni wilderness, accessible only by canoe or plane. National Parks Pass + plane charter required.

name: Wood Buffalo National Park (bisons)
notes: Largest national park in the world: 44,807 km². Largest free-living bison herd in the world: 5,000+ animals. National Parks Pass: free. Whooping Crane nesting area.

name: Yellowknife Old Town (Weledeh)
address: Old Town, Yellowknife, NT X1A 1J7, Canada
notes: Old mining village on rocks by Great Slave Lake. Huts on stilts over the water, huskboats, and Dene First Nations culture. Walk through it: free, surreal combination of poverty and adventure.

name: Alexander Keith's Brewery (Halifax)
address: 1496 Lower Water St, Halifax, NS B3J 1R9, Canada
notes: Oldest brewery in North America still in operation (1820). Costume tour with 'historical' guides in 19th-century attire. Best tour of Halifax: theater + beer.

name: Annapolis Royal Historic Gardens
address: 441 St George St, Annapolis Royal, NS B0S 1A0, Canada
notes: Thematic gardens through 400 years of Acadian/Nova Scotian history. Victorian Garden, Kitchen Garden, Acadian garden. Boring? A bit. But a great photo opportunity.

name: Baddeck (Bell's estate)
address: 559 Chebucto St, Baddeck, NS B0E 1B0, Canada
notes: Alexander Graham Bell lived and died here on Cape Breton Island. National Parks Museum: free. His airplane and kite experiments on the lake are a bizarre part.

name: Balancing Rock (Long Island NS)
notes: 8-meter-high basalt rock balancing on a point in the sea. Short 2.5 km walk through the forest to the end of a cliff. Free, surreal, beautiful. Serge: top 10 of Canada.

name: Bluenose II (Schooner)
address: Lower Water St, Lunenburg, NS B0J 2C0, Canada
notes: Replica of the legendary racing schooner on the Canadian dollar coin. Sea voyages from Lunenburg. Bluenose won every race between 1921 and 1938. Never lost.

name: Cabot Trail (Cape Breton Highlands)
address: Baddeck to Cheticamp, NS B0E 1B0, Canada
notes: Consistent top 3 of the most beautiful road trips in the world: 300 km. Autumn: colors in the Highlands are incredible. Els and Serge: this is the route that will stay with you forever.

name: Cape Breton Highlands National Park
address: 36082 Cabot Trail, Ingonish Beach, NS B0C 1L0, Canada
notes: Spectacular mountain coastlines, wetlands, and wildlife. National Parks Pass: FREE. Moose are present in massive numbers here — more beautiful than in any zoo.

name: Cape Breton Miners' Museum
address: 42 Birkley St, Glace Bay, NS B1A 5X9, Canada
notes: Underground coal mine tour: old miner guides you through an active mine. Age: some guides worked in the mine themselves. Els: intense experience. Serge: underground claustrophobic but done it.

name: Citadel Hill National Historic Site
address: Citadel Hill, Halifax, NS B3J 1H9, Canada
notes: Star fort on a hill above Halifax: active from 1749 to 1906. National Parks Pass: free. Daily cannon shot at 12:00 — watch your ears.

name: Dark Sky Preserve Kejimkujik
address: 3005 Main Pkwy, Maitland Bridge, NS B0T 1B0, Canada
notes: Official Dark Sky Preserve: no light pollution, Milky Way perfectly visible. National Parks Pass + small camping fee. Mi'kmaq petroglyphs on the rocks in the park — 400 years old.

name: Five Fishermen Restaurant (Halifax)
address: 1740 Argyle St, Halifax, NS B3J 2C6, Canada
notes: Seafood restaurant in a historic building that served as a morgue for Titanic victims. Best master lobster and crab in Halifax. Reservations recommended. Dark and atmospheric.

name: Glooscap Heritage Centre (Mi'kmaq)
address: 65 Treaty Trail, Millbrook, NS B0N 1V0, Canada
notes: Mi'kmaq Cultural Centre with the legend of the giant Glooscap. Indigenous art, stories, and traditional society. According to legend, Glooscap created the Bay of Fundy tides.

name: Halifax Explosion Memorial (1917)
address: Fort Needham Memorial Park, Halifax, NS B3K 2C9, Canada
notes: Largest non-nuclear explosion in human history: 1917. French ship loaded with explosives struck Belgian ship and exploded. Belgian connection! 2,000 dead, 9,000 wounded.

name: Hall's Harbour Lobster Pound
address: 1157 Hall's Harbour Rd, Hall's Harbour, NS B0P 1K0, Canada
notes: Fresh lobster straight from the Hummer boat in a small harbor on the Bay of Fundy. You sit on a dock, choose your lobster, and they cook it live. Els: this is the most beautiful restaurant concept ever.

name: Halliburton House Inn (Halifax)
address: 5184 Morris St, Halifax, NS B3J 1B3, Canada
notes: Three Victorian townhouses merged into a boutique hotel. Finest hotel in Halifax city center. The basement restaurant is one of the best in the city.

name: Hopewell Rocks (Bay of Fundy)
address: 131 Discovery Rd, Hopewell Cape, NB E4H 3L5, Canada
notes: Sometimes counted as NB but from the NS route: flowerpot rock formations 15 meters high. At low tide you walk on the seabed; at high tide you kayak in between. One of Canada's most bizarre and photogenic places.

name: Inverary Resort (Baddeck)
address: 368 Shore Rd, Baddeck, NS B0E 1B0, Canada
notes: Resort on Bras d'Or Lake on Cape Breton Island. Charm, waterfront, good starting point for the Cabot Trail. Autumn here is spectacular.

name: Joggins Fossil Cliffs (UNESCO)
address: 100 Main St, Joggins, NS B0L 1A0, Canada
notes: UNESCO World Heritage: 300-million-year-old Coal Age fossils. At low tide, you walk along cliffs full of petrified trees. Darwin visited Joggins — said it is the dirtiest fossil site in the world.

name: Lunenburg (UNESCO Historic District)
notes: UNESCO World Heritage Site: Most intact European colonial fishing town in North America. Brightly colored wooden facades, fishing boats, authentic 18th-century streets. Free to wander around.

name: Marconi Trail (Glace Bay)
notes: Location from where Marconi sent his first transatlantic wireless transmission in 1902. National Parks Pass: free. The other side of the story (Signal Hill NL received it).

name: Milford House (South Milford)
address: 5 Milford House Rd, South Milford, NS B0T 1E0, Canada
notes: Cottage resort from 1870 with 30 wooden cottages in the forest. No Wi-Fi, no TV: pure nature. Kayaking, canoeing, fishing — all included.

name: Murphy's on the Water (Halifax)
address: 1751 Lower Water St, Halifax, NS B3J 1S5, Canada
notes: Terrace restaurant on the Halifax waterfront. Lobster rolls, fish & chips, clam chowder. Most popular tourist spot — but authentic enough.

name: Naturist: Tatamagouche Naturist Club
notes: Small naturist club in North NS. Non-commercial: contact AANR for access. Private estate with basic facilities.

name: Peggy's Cove Lighthouse
address: Peggy's Point Rd, Peggy's Cove, NS B3Z 3S1, Canada
notes: Canada's most photographed lighthouse on spectacular granite rock formations. No fence between you and the ocean — people have already been washed away. Sunset: photogenic level 1000.

name: Salty Rose Vintage Pub (Halifax)
notes: Local maritime pub atmosphere: dark wood, sea-themed wall decor, local beer. Fish soups, lobster rolls, chowder. Halifax has the best pub culture in Atlantic Canada.

name: Swingers Nova Scotia (Halifax)
address: Halifax, NS B3J 0C1 (private lifestyle club — verifieer SDC.com)
notes: Halifax has a small but active lifestyle community. Verify via SDC.com or Kasidie ​​for current clubs and events. Private members-only access.

name: The Harbourview Inn (Lunenburg)
address: Knickle's Rd, Lunenburg, NS B0J 2C0, Canada
notes: B&B with panoramic harbor view over Lunenburg. Perfectly located for the UNESCO historic walk. Breakfast with a view is the best part.

name: The Ovens (coastal caves)
address: 325 Ovens Rd, Feltzen South, NS B0J 2C0, Canada
notes: Walking path along sea caves and scour holes in the cliff coast. During stormy weather, columns of water shoot 20 meters into the air through the caves. Gold panning on the beach (small gold basket available): bizarre.

name: The Wooden Monkey (Halifax)
address: 1707 Grafton St, Halifax, NS B3J 2C5, Canada
notes: 100% local menus, seasonal, organic — but hip and tasty. Not one of those 'healthy-and-boring' restaurants. Good for vegetarian Els and meat-eating Serge.

name: Tidal Bore (Bay of Fundy, Truro)
address: Tidal Bore Rd, Truro, NS B2N 6T8, Canada
notes: Largest tidal range in the world: up to 16 meters in a single 6-hour cycle. At low tide, you walk on the seabed; 6 hours later, there is 16 meters of water. Watch for free at Tidal Bore Park.

name: Trans Canada Trail coastal section
notes: E-bikes perfect along the coastal sections of the Trans Canada Trail. Cape Breton section: coastal strait with sea view. Free to ride with your own bike.

name: Aurora Borealis boven Iqaluit
notes: Above the Arctic Circle: the auroras here are green, purple, and white at the same time. January-March: best season, temperature -35°C but it is worth it. Iqaluit = northernmost capital of a Canadian province.

name: Auyuittuq National Park (Fjords & Glaciers)
notes: Arctic fjords, glaciers, and 2,000m high cliffs — no one is here. Auyuittuq = 'the land that never melts' in Inuktitut. National Parks Pass + plane charter required. Absolute wilderness.

name: Canadian High Arctic Research Station
notes: New scientific station in the Arctic Ocean coastal zone. Visitor center open in summer. Arctic research: climate change, permafrost, Arctic dynamics.

name: Ellesmere Island Ice Shelf
notes: Icebergs that are 3,000 years old are now melting due to climate change. Some were once as large as Belgium — now pieces breaking off. One of the most frightening and fascinating places in the world.

name: Inuit Art Gallery (Dorset Fine Arts)
notes: World's most famous Inuit artist collective: active for 70 years. Prints and sculptures hanging in MoMA are made here. Visit Kinngait Studios: artists in their studio.

name: Iqaluit (Frobisher Bay bezoek)
notes: Capital of Nunavut: 8,000 inhabitants, no road network outside the city. Everything by plane or snowmobile. Inuit culture, country food market (seal, walrus, caribou).

name: Katannilik Territorial Park (hiking)
notes: Spectacular valley with waterfalls on West Baffin Island. Traditionally an Inuit hunting and fishing area. Free to hike, but accessible only by boat from Kimmirut.

name: Keewatin Inuit Heritage Site
notes: Baker Lake: geographical center of Canada and home to the Caribou Inuit. Traditional stone cairns (Inuksuit) throughout the landscape. Large herds of Caribou pass by in August.

name: Midnight Sun (24h zonlicht)
notes: June-July: the sun does NOT set 24 hours a day. Walking at midnight in daylight = completely surreal. Els: completely disrupted sleep pattern for a week — worth it.

name: Narwhal sighting (Baffin Island)
notes: Narwhals in June-July in the straits of Baffin Island. Groups of 100+ narwhals possible in Milne Inlet. Boat tour organized by Inuit guides.

name: Polar Bear Safari (Hudson Bay)
notes: Polar bear safari along Hudson Bay in October: best season for polar bears. Bears walk towards the frozen sea ice. Rankin Inlet is the logistical starting point.

name: Quttinirpaaq NP (northernmost park on earth)
notes: Northernmost national park in the world: 83° N latitude. Polar bears, musk oxen, Arctic wolves, and permanent glacier ice. Expeditions: $5,000+ per person, flight from Resolute Bay. For the true adventurer with a deep budget.

name: Resolute Bay (research station)
notes: Northernmost permanent settlement on the planet (next to Longyearbyen NE). NASA and ESA use this as a Mars simulation site. Serge: Mars on Earth. Summer temperature: -5°C.

name: Sirmilik National Park (Bylot Island seabirds)
notes: More than 70,000 thick-billed murres nest on Bylot Island. Narwhals in the fjord in June-July. National Parks Pass + charter flight from Pond Inlet.

name: Swingers/Naturist Nunavut
address: Iqaluit, NU (geen clubs — verifieer via SDC.com)
notes: Nunavut is too sparsely populated for lifestyle clubs. Iqaluit has an international community (UN staff, NGOs). Private contact via SDC.com or Kasidie ​​when you are actually there.

name: 21c Museum Hotel Cincinnati
notes: Boutique hotel and art museum at the same time: 24/7 free museum for guests and the public. Contemporary art everywhere: in the lobby, hallways, and rooms. Els: you have to stay here if you visit Cincinnati.

name: Bob Evans Farm (original farm)
notes: The original Bob Evans farm from 1946 — before the restaurant chain existed. Museum, pigsty, historic buildings. Unknown fact: Bob Evans started as a truck-stop sausage stand.

name: Brandywine Falls (Cuyahoga Valley)
notes: Ohio's most beautiful waterfall: 67 feet high. National Parks Pass: free. Short hiking trail from the parking lot.

name: Cedar Point (Roller Coaster Capital)
address: One Cedar Point Dr, Sandusky, OH 44870
notes: Most epic roller coaster park in the world: 17 coasters incl. Top Thrill 2 (420 feet). Your route DEFINITELY goes past Sandusky — this is mandatory. Els: maybe not all 17. Serge: definitely all 17.

name: Cedar Point Shores Waterpark
address: One Cedar Point Dr, Sandusky, OH 44870
notes: Water park next to Cedar Point, separate ticket or combo. Perfect after a day of coasters. Combine for a 2-day Sandusky adventure.

name: Clifton Mill (smallest Christmas in world)
notes: Water-powered mill with Christmas decorations of 3.5 million lights. In November-January: an over-the-top Christmas experience. Not in your season (July-August), but the mill is worth visiting year-round.

name: Columbus Zoo and Aquarium
notes: One of the best zoos in America (Jack Hanna's Creation). Not typically your thing, but overwhelmingly good. If you do Columbus and it rains: top option.

name: Cuyahoga Valley National Park
notes: National park between Cleveland and Akron — unique for an urban setting. National Parks Pass: free. Historic Ohio & Erie Canal Towpath: perfect for e-bikes.

name: Dawes Arboretum (weird tree art)
notes: Enormous arboretum with trees planted in the shape of letters spelling 'DAWES ARBORETUM' — visible from the air. Free admission. Next to the Longaberger basket building: doubleslag in Newark.

name: Flint Ridge State Memorial (ancient flint quarry)
notes: Prehistoric flint quarry used by Native Americans for 10,000 years. Flint from here found all along the Mississippi. Walking over the old quarry pits.

name: Football-shaped building (First Federal Savings)
notes: Bank building built in the shape of an American football. Reportedly the only football building in the world. Free photo from the street. Perfect roadside stop.

name: Glacier Ridge Metro Park (drumlins)
notes: Drumlins: elongated hills formed by ice sheets 12,000 years ago. Walking trails through wetlands and tallgrass prairie. Free. Geologically fascinating if you know what you are looking at.

name: Gravity Hill (Richfield OH)
notes: Give your car free rein in neutral and it pulls uphill. Optical illusion or real mystery — debate ongoing. Free, 5 minutes, classic roadside moment.

name: Great Lakes Brewing Company (Cleveland)
notes: Pioneer of craft beer in Ohio: open since 1988. Christmas Ale is so popular that people line up for it. Brewpub in the historic Ohio City neighborhood of Cleveland.

name: Great Lakes Science Center
notes: NASA Glenn Research Center artifacts + Great Lakes ecology. Next to Rock Hall: do both in one day. Suitable for all ages, but also impressive for adults.

name: Haunted Ohio: Loveland Castle
notes: Medieval castle built by one man: Harry Andrews, solo, for 50 years. Started in 1929 with stones from the Little Miami River. He founded a knightly order of Flemish inspiration there. Belgian connection!!

name: Hocking Hills State Park (gorges + caves)
notes: Old Man's Cave, Cedar Falls, Ash Cave — all free. Hemlock canyons, sandstone caves, and waterfalls. Ohio's most spectacular nature. E-bikes along the gorge trails.

name: Jackie O's Brewery (Athens)
notes: Ohio's Best Craft Brewery: winner of multiple national awards. Ohio University City: vibrant cultural scene. Specialties include sour beers and farmhouse ales.

name: Jolly's Drive-In (Springfield)
notes: Authentic 1950s drive-in with carhops on roller skates. Hot dogs, milkshakes, burgers — the original American feeling. Els and Serge: time machine to 1957.

name: Kalahari Resorts (Sandusky)
notes: Large African-themed indoor water park resort. Perfect place to stay if you visit Cedar Point — a 10-minute drive. Indoor water park, so great even when it rains.

name: Lake Erie Islands (Put-in-Bay)
notes: Island in Lake Erie accessible by ferry: golf carts are the mode of transport. Perry's Victory Monument: 96 meters high on a 5 km² island. Summer party island: party and bizarre island vibe.

name: Lake Hope State Park
notes: Lake and forest in the Wayne National Forest. One of Ohio's most remote state parks. Good for camping, kayaking, and nature reset.

name: Marblehead Lighthouse (oldest on Great Lakes)
notes: Oldest lighthouse in the Great Lakes: 1821, still active. Brief but photogenic view of Sandusky Bay. Perfect stopover after Cedar Point.

name: Melt Bar and Grilled - former Lakewood location (closed 2025)
notes: Gourmet grilled cheese sandwiches as big as your head. Local craft beer on tap. Hard to choose: the menu is a 6-page book.

name: Motorcycle Hall of Fame Museum
notes: National motorcycle heritage collection: from Harley-Davidson 1903 to modern MotoGP. Serge: hours of fun. Close to Columbus, easily combined.

name: Mütter-achtige collectie: Dittrick Medical History Center
notes: Free medical history museum: 19th-century surgical instruments, pathological models. Part of Case Western Reserve University. Serge: medically obscure. Els: more than 10 minutes here is enough.

name: National Museum of the U.S. Air Force - Dayton
notes: FREE and gigantic: the largest military aviation museum in the world. 4 hangars, SR-71 Blackbird, Kennedy's Air Force One. Serge: he disappears here all day. Els: brings a book and is also captivated.

name: National Road/Zane Grey Museum
notes: Museum about America's first federal highway (National Road = US-40). Zane Grey: cowboy romance writer who was born here. Small but good: toll numbers, horse-drawn wagons, Western literature.

name: Naturist: Paradise Gardens Naturist Park (AANR)
notes: AANR member naturist park in Amish Country, Ohio. Gegen, pool, volleyball. Amish neighbors don't know what hit them. (Just kidding. They do.)

name: Naturist: Whispering Pines (AANR)
notes: AANR naturist park in Ashtabula County, NE Ohio. Swimming pool, pond, sports facilities. Close to Cleveland and Lake Erie: a good combination.

name: Olentangy Indian Mounds
notes: Hopewell culture earthworks from 100 BC, excellently preserved. Inside, two large earth mound structures run. Easily combined with a visit to Columbus.

name: Piqua Historical Area (General Harrison fort)
notes: Fort reconstruction + historic farm + Miami Erie Canal section. Canoe trips on the canal. Unknown historical gems of Ohio.

name: Pro Football Hall of Fame (Canton)
address: 2121 George Halas Dr NW, Canton, OH 44708
notes: The mecca of American football. Serge: If you like football, this is it. Els: Wait outside with a book. Canton has this thing in the middle of a boring city — but the museum itself is impressive.

name: Rhinegeist Brewery (Cincinnati)
notes: Rooftop bar at a historic brewery in Cincinnati's Over-the-Rhine neighborhood. One of the largest taprooms in the US: a 30,000 m² former beer warehouse. Serge: you won't want to leave here.

name: Rock and Roll Hall of Fame (Cleveland)
notes: I.M. Pei-designed pyramid right on Lake Erie. From Chuck Berry to Nirvana to Beyoncé: the complete history of rock. Serge: 4 hours minimum. Els: also more captivated than expected.

name: Scenic Ohio: Hocking Hills Scenic Byway
address: Logan to Chillicothe, OH via OH-664 / OH-56
notes: Ohio's most beautiful route: sandstone canyons, waterfalls, wooded roads. E-bikes perfect on the smaller trails. Spring and fall are the best seasons.

name: Serpent Mound State Memorial
notes: Largest snake pottery in the world: 411 meters long, made by the Adena people. From the air (drone): full snake spiral visible. Magnetic anomaly measured on site — completely bizarre.

name: Skyline Chili (Cincinnati-style chili)
notes: Cincinnati chili is literally different: on spaghetti, with cinnamon and chocolate inside. 'Way 2' = chili on spaghetti. 'Way 5' = everything on top. Els: this is weird. Serge: this is deliciously weird.

name: Swensons Drive-In (Akron)
notes: Iconic drive-in restaurant from 1934 — carhops bring your food to the car. Galley Boy burger: double with two sauces, famous in Ohio. Perfect for the F-150: window down, tray on the door.

name: Swingers Club: The Champagne Club (Columbus)
notes: Columbus has an active lifestyle scene. Verify current location and events via SDC.com. Ohio is known as a liberal state for lifestyle.

name: Swingers Club: Utopia (Cincinnati)
notes: The Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky border region has multiple lifestyle clubs. Kentucky border = sometimes different rules, check both cities. Verify via Kasidie ​​for current info.

name: The Drury Inn & Suites (Sandusky — Cedar Point nabij)
notes: Budget-friendly hotel 10 min from Cedar Point with a pool. Breakfast included. Perfect 2-night base for a visit to Cedar Point.

name: The Mansion on Forsythe - Zanesville
notes: Victorian mansion B&B in the historic center of Zanesville. Close to the Y-Bridge (the only triple-spanned bridge in the world). Els: charm and comfort at a high level.

name: The Worthington Inn (Columbus suburb)
notes: Historic B&B in picturesque Worthington village near Columbus. Original 1831 inn, renovated with character. An alternative to the Columbus chains.

name: Thurman Café (Columbus)
notes: Famous burger made with 1.5 pounds of meat: The Thurmanator. Open since 1942, family business. If you finish it: free photo on the wall.

name: Tommy's Restaurant (Cleveland Heights)
notes: Cleveland Institute: hippie vibe, huge menu, open for 50 years. Vegans and meat eaters alike: both are well represented. Els: paradise. Serge: also satisfied, because the milkshakes are legendary.

name: Waffle House Museum - Avondale Estates, Georgia
address: 2719 E College Ave, Avondale Estates, GA 30002
notes: Not a real museum — but the Waffle House culture IS bizarre. FEMA uses Waffle House as a disaster indicator ('Waffle House Index'). Els: this is a chain. Serge: but an iconic and bizarre chain.

name: World's Largest Basket (Longaberger HQ)
notes: Former headquarters built as a GIANT BASKET: 7 floors. Longaberger made hand-woven baskets and built their HQ in the shape of them. Now owned by a different owner, but the building is still standing — free photo.

name: Wright Brothers Bicycle Shop (Dayton)
notes: Exactly the workshop where the Wright Brothers designed the airplane. National Parks Pass: free. Minimalist museum, but the story is everything.

name: Y-Bridge (Zanesville — uniek in wereld)
notes: The only bridge in the world with three directions: a Y-shape spanning two rivers at the same time. Old joke: 'How do I get off the bridge?' 'Just drive straight ahead.' Driving over it for free, unique and bizarre. Serge: I want to drive this.

name: Admiral Twin Drive-In (Tulsa)
notes: Classic drive-in cinema, originally from 1951, rebuilt after a fire. Watching a movie from the F-150: the ideal combo. Open every weekend in the summer.

name: Alabaster Caverns State Park
notes: Only commercial alabaster cave in the world: 1.2 km, alabaster walls sparkle. Various colors of selenite and alabaster — unique mineral palette. The cave has existed for 200 million years.

name: Ambassador Hotel (Oklahoma City)
address: 1200 N Walker Ave, Oklahoma City, OK 73103
notes: Historic 1920s hotel, fully renovated, in the arts district. Good restaurant in the hotel. Walking distance from Oklahoma City Museum of Art.

name: American Banjo Museum
address: 9 E Sheridan Ave, Oklahoma City, OK 73104
notes: 300+ historical banjos from 1830 to the present. The banjo as an Appalachian instrument told through music and history. Els: surprisingly interesting. Serge: who knew this existed?

name: Anthem Brewing (Oklahoma City)
notes: Oklahoma City's hippest craft brewery with events and food trucks. Hazy IPAs and sours as specialties. SW OKC neighborhood: developing rapidly.

name: Black Mesa (highest point OK)
notes: Highest point in Oklahoma: 1,516 m, along the New Mexico border. From here, you can see 4 states at once. The mesa landscape is totally different from the rest of OK.

name: Blue Whale of Catoosa
notes: Giant blue concrete whale in a pond along Route 66. Built in 1972 by Hugh Davis as a birthday gift for his wife. For decades, it was a swimming spot. Now: a free photo stop. A must.

name: Cain's Ballroom (Tulsa)
notes: Legendary dancehall from 1924: Bob Wills' Western Swing headquarters. Live music every night — country, rock, folk. One of the best live music venues in the Midwest.

name: Campbell Hotel (Tulsa)
notes: Historic Art Deco motel on Route 66, fully restored. Each room has a different theme: from cowboy to Native American. The perfect Route 66 overnight stay in style.

name: Cattlemen's Steakhouse (Oklahoma City)
address: 1309 S Agnew Ave, Oklahoma City, OK 73108
notes: Steakhouse in the historic Stockyards District, open since 1910. Oklahoma USDA beef of the highest quality. Serge: This is the best steak in the Midwest. Els: Also good.

name: Chickasaw Cultural Center
notes: Modern museum complex about Chickasaw Nation culture and history. Full-fledged recreation of a historic Chickasaw village outside. One of the best Native American cultural centers in the US.

name: Discoveryland USA outdoor Oklahoma! musical (closed after 2011)
address: 1164 S Elwood Ave, Sand Springs, OK 74063
notes: Outdoor theater featuring the legendary Oklahoma! musical every summer weekend. Tulsa neighborhood: Discoveryland runs from June to August. If the timing is right: a very special piece of Americana.

name: Elgin Giant (Elgin)
notes: Smallest roadside eatery with the Giant Burger: half a kilo. Elgin = just about the smallest village in OK. Serge: this is Elgin's only trump card and they are using it well.

name: Elmer's Bottle Tree Ranch (Route 66)
address: 24266 National Trails Hwy, Oro Grande, CA 92368
notes: NB: This is along Route 66 in CA — but the concept tree sculpture tradition also has Tulsa versions. Oklahoma has its own Route 66 art installations. Verify local versions in 2027 for Route.

name: Gilcrease Museum (Western art)
address: 1400 N Gilcrease Museum Rd, Tulsa, OK 74127
notes: Largest collection of Western art and Native American artifacts in the world. Frederic Remington and Charlie Russell originals. Tulsa: hidden art mecca of the Midwest.

name: Gloss Mountain State Park (selenite peaks)
notes: Mountain peaks covered with selenite crystals — they literally glisten in the sun. 'Gloss' = Spanish word for shiny. Free, spectacular, and totally unknown outside Oklahoma.

name: Hamburger Inn (Ardmore)
notes: Tiny diner open since 1942 — family recipe onion burger. Oklahoma's signature dish: grilled onion as filling. Simple, local, authentic.

name: Little Sahara State Park (sand dunes)
notes: 450 hectares of sand dunes in flat Oklahoma — totally surreal. ATVs and sand rails can be rented. Serge: F-150 4x4 on the dunes = happy.

name: Marshall Brewing (Tulsa)
notes: Tulsa's first craft brewery: open since 2008. Big Truck Pale Ale: named after Oklahoma trucking culture. Taproom in an industrial building in the Tulsa Arts District.

name: Museum of Osteology (skulls)
address: 10301 S Sunnylane Rd, Oklahoma City, OK 73160
notes: Museum full of skulls and skeletons of animals from all over the world. The only one of its kind in the world. Serge: 10/10. Els: also secretly fascinated.

name: National Cowboy & Western Heritage Museum
notes: Largest Western art and culture museum in the world. Real cowboys, Rodeo Hall of Fame, Native American collections. Serge: this is his world. 5 hours minimum.

name: National Weather Center (tornado research)
address: 120 David L. Boren Blvd, Norman, OK 73072
notes: Free tour of the National Tornado Research Center. Oklahoma: 'Tornado Alley' of the US — this is the epicenter. Serge: tornado hunting with experts. Els: interested, but not in a tornado.

name: Natural Falls State Park
notes: Illinois Waterfall: 77 feet high in a deep canyon. The hiking trail down to the fall is spectacular. Free, relatively unknown — ideal stop.

name: Naturist: geen AANR resort in OK
notes: Oklahoma has no official AANR naturist resort. Nearest options are in Texas (multiple) or Arkansas. Skinny dipping at Lake Tenkiller is popular with locals.

name: Nic's Grill (Oklahoma City)
address: 1201 N Pennsylvania Ave, Oklahoma City, OK 73107
notes: Tiny diner with the best burger in Oklahoma: counter packed with people, grill smoking. Nic's onion burger: invented during the Depression as a cheap filler. Els: this is authentic America in a bun.

name: Oklahoma City National Memorial
address: 620 N Harvey Ave, Oklahoma City, OK 73102
notes: Memorial Museum for the 168 victims of the 1995 bombing. Outdoor area free, museum $15. Awesome and impressive monument.

name: Oklahoma History Center
address: 800 Nazih Zuhdi Dr, Oklahoma City, OK 73105
notes: Landing place for Oklahoma history: Dust Bowl, Trail of Tears, Land Run 1889. Grand architecture, excellent collections. Free parking, low entrance fee.

name: Oral Roberts University (bizarre campus)
notes: Futuristic campus of televangelist Oral Roberts: golden glass towers, 30-meter Pray Hands sculpture. The Pray Hands sculpture is one of the most bizarre religious objects in the US. Walk around the campus for free.

name: Philbrook Museum (Tulsa villa)
notes: Italian villa of oil baroness Waite Phillips converted into an art museum. Gardens are free and spectacular. International art collection in a totally unexpected building.

name: Pops Route 66 (soda pop museum + diner)
notes: Restaurant with 700+ types of soda bottles and an 18-meter neon bottle along Route 66. The Route 66 iconic architecture + bizarre soda selection. Els: overload of sugar. Serge: taste what is tasteable.

name: Robbers Cave State Park
notes: Jesse James and Belle Starr hid in these caves. Bandit hideout in a rocky state park. Walking trails through the cave systems.

name: Round Barn (Arcadia)
notes: Circular barn from 1898 on Route 66 — unique construction technique. Built into the hillside for extra stability. Free exterior, small donation for interior visit.

name: Route 66 Kitsch through Oklahoma
notes: Oklahoma has the longest continuous section of the original Route 66: 400 km. Neon motels, vintage diners, resting classic cars — the real 'Mother Road' feeling. Many free stops: just drive and stop.

name: Sequoyah's Cabin (Cherokee script inventor)
notes: Sequoyah invented the Cherokee alphabet — ALONE, never before done by anyone who knew neither reading nor writing. His original log cabin is still standing. One of the most remarkable stories of North America.

name: Swingers: Encounters OKC
notes: Oklahoma City has a small but active lifestyle scene. Verify your current location via SDC.com or Kasidie. Oklahoma is conservative, so verify before you leave.

name: Talimena Scenic Drive (Ouachita Mountains)
notes: 54 km mountain road through the Ouachita Mountains: Oklahoma's only real mountain scenery. Autumn = spectacular colors. Els and Serge: this is mandatory if you drive via OK.

name: Tenkiller State Park (lake + cliffs)
notes: Oklahoma's clearest lake in green hills — almost mountainous. Swimming, diving, kayaking. Hidden gem of eastern Oklahoma.

name: The Cave House (Route 66)
notes: House built in and around a rock: literally growing in a cave. Private residence, but clearly visible from the street. Drive by for free to take a photo.

name: The Mayo (Tulsa)
notes: Art Deco hotel from 1925 in the historic center of Tulsa. Elvis, Bob Hope, and John F. Kennedy were once hosted here. Best location in Tulsa for the Arts District walking tour.

name: Totem Pole Park (Ed Galloway)
notes: 90-foot-tall totem pole — the largest in the world — built by one man. Ed Galloway worked on it for 11 years, never got paid a day. Folk art on an epic scale. Free.

name: Turner Falls Park (waterfall swimming)
notes: Oklahoma's most beautiful waterfall: 77 feet, with a pool at the base. Medieval castle as a backdrop (built by a local eccentric). Busy but spectacular every summer.

name: Wichita Mountains Wildlife Refuge
notes: Free-roaming bison, longhorn, and elk in granite mountains. Granite peaks in flat Oklahoma — a total surprise. Free admission, majestic landscape.

name: Woolaroc Ranch (Frank Phillips)
notes: Frank Phillips' (Phillips 66) oil baron's villa converted into a wildlife reserve and museum. Buffaloes, longhorns, and elk roam freely on the estate. Western art + oil wealth + animals = fascinating.

name: 1000 Islands (boat cruise)
address: 1 Front St, Gananoque, ON K7G 2H6, Canada
notes: 1,864 islets in the St. Lawrence River. Boat tour: small castles, opulent villas, secret islets. 1000 Islands dressing was INVENTED here. Really.

name: Agawa Canyon Train Tour
address: 129 Bay St, Sault Ste. Marie, ON P6A 1W7, Canada
notes: Day trip by train in a canyon only accessible by rail. Autumn (Sept-Oct): colors are incredible. Serge: train + canyon + no road = perfect inaccessible place.

name: Algonquin Provincial Park (canoe routes)
address: Highway 60 Corridor, Whitney, ON K0J 2M0, Canada
notes: Iconic Canadian national park: 7,600 km² of forest and lakes. Moose, otters, beavers — present everywhere. E-bikes on the Highland Backpacking Trail.

name: Art Gallery of Ontario (AGO)
address: 317 Dundas St W, Toronto, ON M5T 1G4, Canada
notes: Frank Gehry-renovated art museum with a Canadian and international collection. Largest Rubens collection in North America. Wednesday evening after 6 pm: free.

name: Bala Cranberry Festival
notes: Annual cranberry harvest festival in Muskoka: late October. Harvesting floating cranberry fields: walking through a red sea. If timing matches the route (autumn 2027).

name: Bare Oaks Family Naturist Park (AANR)
address: 20237 Kennedy Rd, East Gwillimbury, ON L9N 0P9, Canada
notes: Largest AANR member naturist park in Canada, 30 min from Toronto. Swimming pool, sports, sauna, naturist campsite. Known as super friendly and family-oriented.

name: Big Nickel (Sudbury)
address: 122 Big Nickel Rd, Sudbury, ON P3C 5T7, Canada
notes: Largest coin in the world: 9-meter-high nickel coin outside the museum. Sudbury is the nickel production capital of the world. Free photo from the street.

name: Blue Mountain Resort ⛷️ Ikon
address: 190 Gord Canning Dr, The Blue Mountains, ON L9Y 0V9
notes: Ikon Pass: UNLIMITED. Best option in Ontario if you already have Ikon. Not high (220m vertical) but well-maintained. 2 hours from Toronto. Lively village with restaurants and shops. If you are driving towards Toronto in the winter: perfect day stop. Not an adventurous ski area, but good for a freshen-up day. Els: flat and predictable terrain. Serge: short visit, more for the atmosphere.

name: Blue Mountain Ski Resort (non-ski season)
address: 190 Jozo Weider Blvd, The Blue Mountains, ON L9Y 3Z2, Canada
notes: Georgian Bay water park, gondola, mountain biking in the summer season. Not for skiing, but the resort is also fun in the summer. E-bikes on the mountain bike trails: perfect.

name: Boldt Castle (Hart Island, 1000 Islands)
address: Heart Island, Alexandria Bay, NY — vanuit Gananoque ON
notes: American millionaire built a castle for his wife — she died before the opening. He abandoned construction immediately and never continued it. Ruined castle on an island full of romantic drama.

name: Canada Aviation and Space Museum (Ottawa)
address: 11 Aviation Pkwy, Ottawa, ON K1K 4R3, Canada
notes: National Aviation and Aerospace Collection: 130 aircraft. First Avro Arrow — the most secretive Canadian aircraft of the Cold War. Serge: the Arrow is a national trauma and a must-see.

name: Carousel Bakery (Toronto)
address: St. Lawrence Market, 93 Front St E, Toronto, ON M5E 1C3, Canada
notes: The legendary Peameal Bacon Sandwich — Toronto's icon. Pork rolled in cornmeal, grilled to order. Saturday market: line up but wait 10 minutes.

name: CN Tower (EdgeWalk)
address: 290 Bremner Blvd, Toronto, ON M5V 3L9, Canada
notes: At 356 meters, hanging on the outside of the tower — without a railing, ropes attached to your body. EdgeWalk: walking around the tower on a narrow tube. Serge: booked immediately. Els: watching from below.

name: Distillery District (Toronto)
address: 55 Mill St, Toronto, ON M5A 3C4, Canada
notes: Largest preserved Victorian industrial complex in North America, now an arts district. Restaurants, galleries, and theaters in historic distillery buildings. Free walking. Breweries and distilleries on site.

name: Flowerpot Island (Fathom Five NP)
notes: Stacked rock formations ('flowerpots') on an island in Lake Huron. Boat trip from Tobermory + walk across the island. Crystal-clear water above 19th-century shipwrecks.

name: George Restaurant (Toronto)
address: 111 Queen St E, Toronto, ON M5C 1S2, Canada
notes: Modern Canadian fine dining in Toronto's arts district. Menu changes every week with local seasonal produce. Reservations required. Best dinner in Toronto for a special occasion.

name: High Park (Toronto)
address: 1873 Bloor St W, Toronto, ON M6R 2Z3, Canada
notes: 161-hectare city park with a zoo, ponds, and oak forest. April-May: Japanese cherry blossoms (free). Free admission at all times.

name: Hilton Niagara Falls/Fallsview Hotel & Suites
address: 6361 Fallsview Blvd, Niagara Falls, ON L2G 3V9, Canada
notes: Fallsview Hotel: direct view of the waterfalls from the room. Slightly above budget, but that waterfall view is unique. The illuminated waterfalls are most beautiful in the evening.

name: Horseshoe Falls Illumination
notes: Free light show: the waterfalls are illuminated in the colors of the rainbow every evening. Best spots: Queen Victoria Park or Rainbow Bridge. Free, spectacular, lasts from sunset until midnight.

name: Hotel X Toronto
address: 111 Princes Blvd, Toronto, ON M6K 3C3, Canada
notes: Trendy hotel next to Exhibition Place and Lake Ontario. Rooftop pool and bar: spectacular view of the lake. A bit above budget, but the location and view are worth it.

name: Inn on the Twenty (Jordan Village)
address: 3836 Main St, Jordan Station, ON L0R 1S0, Canada
notes: Boutique inn in the Niagara Escarpment wine region. Perfect for wine tastings at Cave Spring Winery nearby. Els: this is the ideal 1-night Niagara after-the-falls stop.

name: Inniskillin Winery (icewine)
notes: Pioneer of Canadian ice wine: Vidal Icewine is world-famous. Wine tasting with a view over the Niagara Escarpment. Els: ice wine = the Belgian chocolate equivalent of Canada.

name: Journey Behind the Falls
address: 6650 Niagara Pkwy, Niagara Falls, ON L2E 6T2, Canada
notes: Tunnel behind the waterfall: deafening and wet. Stands 1 meter away from 57,000 liters of water per second. Surreal experience — you stand BEHIND the drop.

name: Kakabeka Falls (Niagara of the North)
address: Trans-Canada Hwy, Kakabeka Falls, ON P0T 1W0, Canada
notes: 47-meter waterfall in a 1.5 billion-year-old canyon. Legendary: Ojibwe princess leading the enemy over the falls. F-150 parking right next to the fall.

name: Kensington Market (Toronto)
address: Kensington Market, Toronto, ON M5T 2L4, Canada
notes: Bohemian neighborhood full of vintage shops, international street food, artists, and musicians. Every summer Pedestrian Sunday: cars prohibited, festivals. Totally different Toronto from the downtown towers.

name: Kingston (historic limestone city)
notes: Original capital of Canada (1841-1844). Limestone forts, Military College, penitentiary on an island. Day trip between Toronto and Montreal.

name: Manitoulin Island (werelds grootste zoetwatereiland)
notes: Largest freshwater island in the world: 2,766 km². Witnesnek lake-and-water-in-an-island-in-a-lake-in-an-island (real). Ojibwe sacred island: respectful visiting culture.

name: Muskoka Cottage Country (Lakes district)
notes: Thousands of lakes with summer cottages: Canadian summer at its purest. Kayaking, swimming, sunset bonfires. Els: this is Canada as it should be.

name: Niagara City Cruises
address: 5920 Niagara Pkwy, Niagara Falls, ON L2G 3K9, Canada
notes: Boat right under the waterfall — the original 'Maid of the Mist' but Canadian. Poncho included. You will get soaking wet. You might as well put it on. Els: this is the only really wet water adventure I do voluntarily.

name: Niagara Falls (Canadian kant)
address: Niagara Pkwy, Niagara Falls, ON L2G 3K6, Canada
notes: The Canadian side is superior to the US side: wide panorama, closer to the drop. Table Rock: you are literally standing 1 meter from the edge. Mist that soaks you = free shower. Free view outside.

name: Niagara-on-the-Lake (historisch stadje)
notes: Canada's most preserved Victorian city at the mouth of Niagara. Shaw Festival Theatre, local wine route. Walking distance to everything: clean, beautiful, somewhat busy.

name: Ottawa Parliament Hill
address: Wellington St, Ottawa, ON K1A 0A9, Canada
notes: Free tours of the Canadian Parliament building. Summer: Changing of the Guard every morning at 10:00 AM. Perfect background for a @travellers1969 post.

name: Ponderosa Nature Nudist Resort (AANR)
notes: AANR naturist resort near Guelph (Ontario). Swimming pool, sports grounds, friendly community. Easily combined with the Toronto or Niagara Trail.

name: Rideau Canal (UNESCO)
address: Rideau Canal, Ottawa to Kingston, ON
notes: UNESCO World Heritage Site: 202 km of canal built 1826–1832 for military purposes. Never used for war — now the world's longest winter ice rink. Cycling or kayaking along the canal: classic Canadian.

name: Royal Ontario Museum (ROM)
address: 100 Queens Park, Toronto, ON M5S 2C6, Canada
notes: Spectacular Daniel Libeskind architecture: crystal prisms protrude from an old building. Dinosaurs, Egyptian mummies, Canadian Indigenous art. Toronto's best museum.

name: Science North (Sudbury)
address: 100 Ramsey Lake Rd, Sudbury, ON P3E 5S9, Canada
