notes: Science museum IN a quarry next to a crater lake. Sudbury Basin = site of an asteroid impact 1.85 billion years ago. Space, geology, nickel industry — all in one place.

name: Sleeping Giant Provincial Park
notes: Cliff resembling a lying giant on Lake Superior. Hiking trail to the summit: panorama over the world's largest freshwater lake. Near Thunder Bay.

name: St. Lawrence Market (Toronto)
address: 93 Front St E, Toronto, ON M5E 1C3, Canada
notes: Peameal Bacon Sandwich: Toronto's signature food for 150 years. Bruges' Waffle: Belgian waffle in Toronto — see how many things they do wrong. Farmers market every Saturday on the surrounding streets.

name: Swingers: Club Taboo (Toronto)
address: Toronto, ON M6H 1T6 (verifieer adres via SDC.com 2027)
notes: Toronto has a large and open lifestyle scene. Club Taboo is one of the most well-known Canadian lifestyle clubs. Verify address and calendar via SDC.com or Kasidie.

name: Swingers: Le Château (Ottawa)
notes: Ottawa also has a lifestyle scene despite the government setting. Verify current info — Canadian clubs are generally open and well-organized. Membership registration recommended.

name: The Ace (Ottawa)
address: 8 Clarence St, Ottawa, ON K1N 5P3, Canada
notes: Artisanal pizza and craft cocktails at the Byward Market. Ottawa's most beloved local restaurant in the bohemian neighborhood. Walking from Parliament Hill.

name: The Burroughes Building (Toronto)
address: 639 Queen St W, Toronto, ON M6J 1E5, Canada
notes: Boutique apart-hotel in a historic department store building in Queen West. Long-term stays possible, kitchen in room. Queen Street West: best neighborhood in Toronto.

name: Toronto Islands Park
address: Toronto Islands, Toronto, ON M5J 2C6, Canada
notes: Small islands accessible by ferry (15 min) with panoramic views of the skyline. Nudist beach (Hanlan's Point): official nudist beach close to the city center. Els: she already did it in Antwerp — just a beach.

name: Wawa Goose (giant Canada Goose)
address: Trans-Canada Hwy at Hwy 17, Wawa, ON P0S 1K0, Canada
notes: Giant goose, 8 meters tall, at the entrance to the city of Wawa. Wawa = Ojibwe for 'wild goose'. Classic roadside kitsch for the photo. Free.

name: Wilno Tavern (oldest Canadian tavern)
notes: Canada's oldest Polish community in Renfrew County. Tavern with authentic Polish-Canadian food: pierogi, sauerkraut, bigos. Small village, big culture.

name: Astoria (oldest US settlement west of Rockies)
notes: Oldest permanent American settlement west of the Rockies (1811). The Goonies movie was shot here: a complete fan pilgrimage route. Astoria Column: 600 steps, panorama over the Columbia River.

name: Bonneville Dam (fish ladder)
address: 70543 NE Herman Loop, Cascade Locks, OR 97014
notes: Free visitor center at a huge dam on the Columbia River. Fish ladder: see salmon swimming uphill through the dam. Serge: engineering geek heaven.

name: Cathedral Park (St. Johns Bridge)
address: N Edison St & N Pittsburgh Ave, Portland, OR 97203
notes: Gothic-style bridge piers from 1931 create a cathedral effect under the bridge. Best underpass photography in the US. Free, spectacular at night.

name: Collins Lake Resort - Government Camp
address: 88149 E Creek Ridge Rd, Government Camp, OR 97028
notes: Portland has an open lifestyle scene. Verify address and events via SDC.com before 2027. Dress code: elegant.

name: Columbia River Gorge Scenic Byway
address: Historic Columbia River Hwy, Troutdale to The Dalles, OR
notes: Historic highway past 14 waterfalls in one route. Multnomah Falls: 189 meters, free access (reserve parking). National Forest Pass of America the Beautiful: free.

name: Crater Lake Lodge
address: 565 Rim Village Dr, Crater Lake, OR 97604
notes: Historic lodge on the edge of Crater Lake: view of the deepest lake. Fully booked in the summer: book early. The evening light on the lake from your room is unforgettable.

name: Crater Lake National Park
notes: Deepest lake in the US: 592 meters. Color is a surreal royal blue. National Parks Pass: free. Wizard Island is a volcanic island in the middle of another volcanic lake.

name: Crater Rock Museum
notes: Rock, mineral, and fossil collection of 100,000 specimens. Meteorites, opals, thunder eggs (OR state rock). Oregon is famous for thunder eggs — buy one yourself.

name: Deschutes Brewery (Portland pub)
notes: Oregon's most famous brewery: Black Butte Porter is iconic. Pub in the Pearl District — good food alongside the beers. Serge: Black Butte Porter = perfect Oregon experience.

name: Heceta Head Lighthouse B&B
notes: Sleep in the 1894 lighthouse keeper's cottage, stunning view of the Pacific Ocean. Breakfast prepared by the hostess included. Haunted reputation: the ghost of 'Rue' is still present. Magical and over budget, but special.

name: International UFO Museum (McMinnville)
notes: Annual UFO festival in May — but the museum is open year-round. McMinnville UFO photos from 1950 are the 'most convincing' in the world. Els: 'interesting'. Serge: 'I don't believe in it, but look at this'.

name: Jake's Famous Crawfish (Portland)
notes: Portland's oldest restaurant: open since 1892. Seafood as a specialty — Dungeness crab, crawfish, Pacific halibut. Els and Serge: classic, tasty, authentic.

name: John Day Fossil Beds National Monument
notes: 45 million years of fossil geology: colorful layers visible in the canyon walls. National Parks Pass: free. Combine with Painted Hills (also in this monument) for a full day.

name: Lardo (Portland)
notes: Best sandwiches in Portland: Dirty Fries with pork scraps are famous. Portland sandwich culture: more serious than in Belgium. Serge: this is a religious experience with bread.

name: Lava Beds and Lava River Cave (Bend area)
notes: 2 km long lava tunnel: Newberry Volcanic National Monument. Bring your own light source (mandatory) — total darkness inside. Free with America the Beautiful Pass.

name: McMenamins Edgefield (Troutdale)
notes: Former impoverished county farm from 1910 converted into a hotel, brewery, winery, and golf course. Murals everywhere, ghost reports, fantastic grounds. One of the most unique hotels in North America.

name: McMenamins Kennedy School Hotel (Portland)
notes: Hotel in a former elementary school: sleep in the classrooms, drink in the gym. Cinema, restaurants, soaking pools — all in the building. Els: this is the most original hotel in the US.

name: Mt. Bachelor ⛷️ Ikon
notes: Ikon Pass: 7 DAYS. Close to Bend (great craft beer town!). Volcanic mountain with unique open terrain and fantastic views. Summit = 360° panorama of Cascade volcanoes. Season sometimes until May. If you are passing through Oregon in the spring: combine a skiing day trip with the Bend brewery scene! Beginners: West Village is easy. Serge: Lift to the summit for epic runs.

name: Newberry National Volcanic Monument
notes: Active volcanic area: obsidian fields, lava lakes, but shield volcano. Obsidian flow: shiny black volcanic glass as far as the eye can see. National Forest fee of America the Beautiful: free.

name: Oaks Park (Portland's old amusement park)
address: 7805 SE Oaks Park Way, Portland, OR 97202
notes: Oldest active amusement park on the West Coast (1905). Roller skating rink + retro roller coasters. Portland old-school entertainment.

name: Opal Creek Ancient Forest
notes: Ancient hemlock and cedar forest along a turquoise river. 8 km hike to a swimming hole in crystal-clear mountain water. One of the most beautiful swimming spots in Oregon — free.

name: Oregon Caves National Monument
notes: Marble caves formed by rainwater over millions of years. National Parks Pass + small tour fee. Guided tour mandatory: interesting guide stories about the history of discovery.

name: Oregon Coast Scenic Route (US-101)
address: US-101 from Astoria to Brookings, OR
notes: 600 km coastal road: rocky cliffs, beachy beaches, port towns. Every beach in Oregon is PUBLIC LAND — free for everyone. Els and Serge: best day of the road trip. Especially when the sun is shining.

name: Oregon Dunes National Recreation Area
notes: Largest walking dunes in North America: 65 km long, up to 150 meters high. ATV riding on the dunes: available for rent on site. F-150 4x4 + sand dunes = Serge happy.

name: Oregon Shakespeare Festival (Ashland)
notes: World-famous Shakespeare festival from March to November. Performed in an open-air Elizabethan theater. If the timing is right: a literary experience.

name: Oregon Vortex (Gold Hill)
address: 4303 Sardine Creek Left Fork Rd, Gold Hill, OR 97525
notes: Balls roll uphill, people hunch against gravity. Native Americans avoided this area — too many unseen forces. Oregon's best-known mystery spot. Truly bizarre.

name: Painted Hills (John Day Fossil Beds)
notes: Striped hills in red, gold, black, and green — total Martian atmosphere. National Parks Pass: free. Dawn or sunset: colors change dramatically.

name: Pfriem Family Brewers (Hood River)
address: 707 Portway Ave Suite 101, Hood River, OR 97031
notes: Award-winning brewery with a view of the Columbia Gorge and Mt. Hood. Belgian-inspired beers — the name sounds Belgian, the beer tastes Belgian. Els: this is a brewery for us.

name: Portland Saturday Market
notes: Largest outdoor craft market in the US: every Saturday and Sunday. Handmade art, local food, live music — the real Portland vibe. Free to walk around. Buying food is mandatory.

name: Rogue Ales - former Newport location (closed 2025)
notes: Brewery on the Pacific coast with its own hop farm and distillery. Beard-yeast experimental beers: Chatoe Rogue is unique. Newport Aquarium right next to the brewery.

name: Salt & Straw Ice Cream (Portland)
notes: Artisanal ice cream with bizarre flavors: Blue Cheese & Pear, Bone Marrow. A new themed menu every month. Els: experimental ice cream! Serge: bone marrow ice cream? Yes.

name: Sea Lion Caves (world's largest sea cave)
notes: World's largest sea cave: elevator down, hundreds of sea lions in winter. Elevator goes 60 meters down into the rock. Autumn/winter: sea lions INSIDE the cave. Summer: outside on the rocks.

name: Serenity Mountain Retreat - Estacada
notes: AANR naturist resort 30 km from Portland — unusual name 'Boring, OR'. Lake, pool, camping. Oregon's best AANR option near a major city.

name: Smith Rock State Park (rock climbing mekka)
address: 9241 NE Crooked River Dr, Terrebonne, OR 97760
notes: Oregon's most photogenic climbing rock: 245-meter tuff rock formations above Crooked River. Walking trail along the base: spectacular without climbing. E-bikes on the bike path along the river.

name: Squaw Mountain Ranch (Mollala — AANR)
notes: AANR naturist ranch in the Cascade foothills. Swimming pool, campground, naturist hikes. Oregon has a long naturist tradition.

name: The Freakybuttrue Peculiarium (Portland)
notes: Bigfoot exhibits, strange curiosities, Chupacabra stuffing. Ice cream bar in a curiosities museum: unexpected combo. Portland at its most absurdist. Free to look inside, pay for food.

name: Thor's Well (Cape Perpetua)
address: Cape Perpetua Scenic Area, Yachats, OR 97498
notes: Basalt pit in the ocean that swallows and spits out water at the right moment. During storms and high tides: completely spectacular. National Forest fee: $5. Free with America the Beautiful Pass.

name: Thor's Well + Devil's Churn + Spouting Horn combo
notes: Three spectacular ocean phenomena along the OR coast. Spouting Horn: a hole in the rock that fountains when waves blow. America the Beautiful Pass: all included.

name: Tillamook Cheese Factory
notes: Free cheese viewing at Oregon's largest dairy cooperative. Ice cream with custom cheese flavors: cheddar ice cream exists. Serge: compare with Belgian fromage. Conclusion to follow.

name: Tillamook Cheese Factory Ice Cream
notes: Free tasting of all cheeses + ice cream in an amazing assortment. Not a restaurant but a food stop: ideal for the route along the coast. Els: Try 4 flavors before you choose.

name: Timberline Lodge (The Shining exterior)
address: 27500 E Timberline Rd, Government Camp, OR 97028
notes: Kubrick's The Shining was filmed outside here (exterior). Art Deco National Register building on Mt. Hood with year-round skiing. Over budget but iconic. Bar drinks count.

name: Tu Tu' Tun Lodge (Gold Beach)
address: 96550 North Bank Rogue, Gold Beach, OR 97444
notes: Luxury lodge on the Rogue River, accessible by jet boat. Current favorite of the Upper class: no Wi-Fi, no TV. Els and Serge: nature retreat level 100.

name: TUSK (Portland)
notes: Modern Mediterranean restaurant on Portland's east side. Vegetarian-heavy but with meat options: perfect for Els and Serge. Small plates concept — good for experimenting.

name: Voodoo Doughnut (Portland)
notes: 24/7 open donut shop famous for voodoo-doll donuts and obscene toppings. Cities with waiting lists. Voodoo-doll style donut with korspelon. Els: this is baking with attitude. Serge: buy at least 3.

name: Allegheny Portage Railroad NHS
notes: First railroad across the Appalachians: 1834 technology to hoist trains up the mountain. National Parks Pass: free. Engineering wonder of its time — incline planes and stationary engines.

name: Amish Country (Lancaster County)
notes: Largest Amish community in the world: horse-drawn wagon on the highway, no electricity, no photos. Farm markets, quilts, fresh deli meats — everything handmade. Bizarre time capsule in the middle of modern America.

name: Andy Warhol Museum (Pittsburgh)
notes: Largest museum in the world dedicated to a single artist. Andrew Warhola was born in Pittsburgh as the child of Slovak immigrants. Els: you can spend hours here. Serge: also surprised by the depth.

name: Boyertown Museum of Historic Vehicles
notes: Unique collection of vehicles made in Pennsylvania: wagons, buggies, early cars. Farm wagons alongside steam carriages. Serge: transport through the ages. Small but fascinating.

name: Brauhaus Schmitz (Philadelphia)
notes: Authentic German beer and sausage house in the heart of Philadelphia. 30 German beers on tap, Schweinshaxe, Käsespätzle. Serge: compare with Belgian beer. Conclusion: different but good.

name: Bushkill Falls (Niagara of Pennsylvania)
notes: 8 waterfalls in a ravine in the Poconos. Short hiking trails alongside each waterfall. Most beautiful during wet periods (spring after snow).

name: Centralia (underground coal fire ghost town)
notes: Town of 1,000 inhabitants abandoned because an underground coal fire has been burning for 60 years. Smoke rises from cracks in the roads. Danger present, but walking is allowed. Inspiration for Silent Hill. Free — but do not stand in dangerous spots.

name: Drake Well Museum (first oil well)
notes: World's first commercial oil well: 1859, Edwin Drake. Working replica of the original drilling rig. The petroleum industry started here — the world was never the same again.

name: Eastern State Penitentiary
notes: Al Capone was incarcerated here. Prison designed as a penitential monastery in 1829. Dilapidated cells, creepy corridors, decaying prison chapel. The Halloween Haunted House here is legendary (October).

name: Ephrata Cloister (18e eeuwse sekte)
notes: 18th-century religious commune: celibate monks and nuns in separate buildings. Germanic sectarian monastery in the middle of Pennsylvania Dutch country. Original buildings completely intact — surreal place.

name: Fallingwater (Frank Lloyd Wright)
address: 1491 Mill Run Rd, Mill Run, PA 15464
notes: Most famous private residence in the world: built over a waterfall in 1935. Frank Lloyd Wright's masterpiece — every architecture student knows this building. Reservation required, tour limited.

name: Federal Pretzel Bakery (Philadelphia)
notes: Real Philly soft pretzels, hand-rolled. Selling out by 6 am until they're gone. The Philadelphia pretzel is different from the rest: thinner, rolled, with mustard.

name: Flight 93 National Memorial
notes: Memorial monument for the heroes of Flight 93 on 9/11. National Parks Pass: free. Quiet, impressive place in the Pennsylvanian countryside.

name: Geno's Steaks (cheesesteak rival)
notes: Pat's eternal rival: 50 meters away, also 24/7. Neon-lit outdoor counter: eat while standing. Do both — Pat's vs Geno's debate is a mandatory part of Philadelphia.

name: Gettysburg Battlefield
notes: Most decisive battle of the Civil War: 51,000 dead in 3 days (1863). National Parks Pass: free. Car tour 40 km long. In the evening: ghost walks are legendary.

name: Gravity Hill (New Paris)
address: Gravity Hill Rd, New Paris, PA 15554
notes: Car in neutral: driving uphill. One of the most famous in the US. Free, easily accessible. Film yourself and post it — @travellers1969 content guarantee.

name: Hawk Mountain Sanctuary (raptor migration)
notes: Most visited raptor migration site in the world: September-November. Thousands of hawks, eagles, and storks every day in autumn. Els: photography paradise.

name: Hersheypark + Chocolate World
notes: Theme park built by Milton Hershey for his factory workers. Gateway: Chocolate World free — chocolate factory tour + tasting. Streets are named Chocolate Ave and Cocoa Ave. Belgian chocolate manufacturer Serge: how daring.

name: Hotel Hershey
notes: Grand hotel built by Milton Hershey in 1933: Mediterranean-style resort. Chocolate Spa — body scrub with cacao: yes, really. Over budget, but the chocolate connection makes it unique.

name: Inclines of Pittsburgh (Duquesne + Monongahela)
notes: Funiculars going up Mt. Washington: panorama of Pittsburgh 'Golden Triangle'. Pittsburgh's most spectacular view: three rivers together. Round trip $5 — photogenic every hour.

name: Inn at Bowman's Hill (New Hope)
notes: Romantic boutique inn in the Delaware River Valley. New Hope is a bohemian artist town: galleries, restaurants, antiques. Els: this is the perfect resting place between NYC and Philadelphia.

name: Jim Thorpe (Little Switzerland of America)
notes: Victorian mining village in a Pocono Gorge: literally looks like a European mountain town. Jim Thorpe (the Olympic athlete) is buried there — at the request of his widow, as he had never been there. Cycling and hiking in the surrounding mountains.

name: Kecksburg UFO Incident site
notes: In 1965, something mysterious crashed in the Kecksburg forest. An army convoy took it away. The municipality placed a replica acorn-shaped object at the fire station. Free — just drive and take a picture of that acorn.

name: Knoebels Amusement Resort (free admission)
notes: FREE parking and free admission — you only pay per ride. Family business, for 100 years. Phoenix wooden roller coaster: top 10 in the world. Els: this is an amusement park like it used to be.

name: Laurel Caverns (largest cave PA)
notes: Pennsylvania's largest cave: a labyrinth of 6.5 km of tunnels. Go-kart slide through the cave — yes, really. Serge: a cave with a go-kart track is the perfect combination.

name: Mütter Museum (medical oddities)
notes: Most famous medical oddities museum in the world: skulls, deformed skeletons, Einstein's brain. Conjoined twin organs, a woman who turned into soap after death. Els: gruesome AND fascinating. Serge: 10/10 without a doubt.

name: Naturist: Penn Sylvan Health Society (AANR)
address: Dauphin County area, PA (verifieer via AANR 2027)
notes: AANR member nudist club in central Pennsylvania. Contact via the AANR website for current info. Smaller and more private than White Thorn.

name: Naturist: White Thorn Lodge (AANR)
notes: AANR naturist resort in western Pennsylvania near Pittsburgh. Swimming pool, sports fields, campground, lodge. One of the larger naturist resorts in Pennsylvania.

name: Ohiopyle State Park
notes: Ohiopyle State Park: whitewater rafting on Youghiogheny River, class III-IV.  Laurel Highlands: most beautiful nature in Pennsylvania.  Free entrance to the park, rafting tours separately.

name: Pat's King of Steaks (cheesesteak original)
notes: Original cheesesteak inventor: Pat Olivieri, 1930. Open 24/7, stand outside, no chairs — just the sandwich. Order correctly: 'Whiz wit' = cheese sauce with onions. No debate.

name: Pennsylvanian Dutch Hex Signs (barn tour)
notes: Colorful geometric symbols on Amish barns — protection against witches. Driving through Lancaster County: every barn has a different pattern. Free roadside art experience.

name: Philadelphia Magic Gardens (Isaiah Zagar)
notes: Mosaic fantasy wonderland: courtyard and tunnels covered with millions of shards. Isaiah Zagar worked on it for 14 years. Els: this is the most beautiful special place in Philadelphia.

name: Pine Creek Gorge (PA Grand Canyon)
notes: 800-foot deep canyon: 'Pennsylvania Grand Canyon'. E-bikes on the Pine Creek Rail Trail (27 km along the canyon). Free admission.

name: Presque Isle State Park (Lake Erie beach)
notes: Peninsula in Lake Erie: beachy, birdwatching, swimming. Erie Bluffs State Park nearby: spectacular Lake Erie cliffs. Free state park.

name: Priory Hotel (Pittsburgh)
notes: Former Benedictine monastery converted into a boutique hotel. Gothic vaults, monastery courtyard, history everywhere. North Side Pittsburgh: walking distance from the Andy Warhol Museum.

name: Reading Terminal Market
notes: Largest indoor market in the US in a historic train station. Amish bakers, seafood, Philly cheesesteaks, everything under one roof. Els: this is markets as they should be.

name: Ricketts Glen State Park (21 waterfalls)
notes: 21 waterfalls on a single hiking trail: 11 km, most spectacular nature in PA. Old-growth hemlock forest — some trees 500 years old. Free state park.

name: Roadside America miniature village (closed 2020)
notes: 300m² indoor miniature city built by one man over 60 years. Night show with auroras and a sunset every 30 min. One of the best roadside attractions in the US. Definitely do it.

name: Scenic Byway: Route 6 (northern PA)
address: US-6 from Meadville to Milford, PA
notes: Most beautiful driving route in northern Pennsylvania: forest, lakes, small towns. PA Wilds region: one of the largest uninhabited areas in the East. E-bikes along the quiet back roads.

name: Strasburg Railroad (oldest in US)
notes: Oldest still-operating steam train in the US (1832). Runs through Amish farmland — horse-drawn wagons cross the tracks. Combine with the Pennsylvania Railroad Museum next to the station.

name: Swingers: Club Risque (Philadelphia)
notes: Philadelphia has an active lifestyle scene. Verify current location and events via SDC.com or Kasidie. Dress code required.

name: Swingers: Pittsburgh lifestyle scene
notes: Pittsburgh hosts private lifestyle events via Kasidie. No fixed clubs, but an active community. Verify before visiting via online platforms.

name: The Inn at Jim Thorpe
notes: Victorian hotel in the mountain town of Jim Thorpe. Views of the Lehigh Gorge from some rooms. Perfect base for hiking and cycling in the Poconos.

name: The Mercer Museum + Fonthill Castle
notes: Henry Mercer built three concrete castles with his own hands in 1916. Mercer Museum: tools from before industrialization — 50,000 objects hanging from the ceiling. Fonthill: his home — 44 rooms, no two alike, concrete with tiles.

name: Victory Brewing Company (Downingtown)
notes: One of the best craft breweries in Pennsylvania: HopDevil, Golden Monkey. Restaurant and taproom in picturesque Downingtown. Day of Gettysburg + Victory Brewery = perfect Pennsylvania day.

name: Weyerbacher Brewing (Easton)
notes: Experimental brewery making Belgian-style ales in Pennsylvania. Tours and tastings on weekends. Els: Belgian beer in Pennsylvania — surreal but tasty.

name: World's Largest Shoe House (Hellam)
notes: House built in the shape of a shoe: 6 rooms, 2 bathrooms, shoe-shaped garage. Built in 1948 by shoe salesman Mahlon Haines. Free exterior viewing. Privately occupied but visible from the road.

name: Yuengling Brewery (oldest US brewery)
notes: Oldest brewery in the US: open since 1829 in the same buildings. Free tour of the historic brewery and free beer afterwards. Serge: this is historic beer drinking.

name: Zahav (Israeli fine dining Philadelphia)
notes: James Beard Award: Best Chef and Best Restaurant for multiple years. Modern Israeli: hummus, salatim, whole-roasted lamb. Reserve weeks in advance. Absolutely worth it.

name: Anne of Green Gables Heritage Place
address: 8619 Cavendish Rd, Cavendish, PE C0A 1N0, Canada
notes: The house that inspired L.M. Montgomery for Anne of Green Gables (1908). National Parks Pass: free. Els: read the book aloud. Serge: I can't promise that.

name: Basin Head Fisheries Museum (singing sands)
notes: Beach with sand that 'sings' or 'squeaks' when you walk over it. Acoustic phenomenon caused by the silica grain size. Els: do we have to hear this? Serge: this is a special beach.

name: Cavendish Boardwalk & Amusement Parks
notes: Kitsch and colorful Cavendish with minigolf, go-karts, and entertainment. A totally different atmosphere from the quiet rest of PEI. Kiddie-kitsch Canadian style along the boardwalk.

name: Charlottetown (birthplace of Canada)
notes: Canada's 'birthplace': Confederation in 1867 was discussed here. Province House: free to walk around. Small but charming center with Victorian architecture.

name: Confederation Bridge (longest in world over ice)
address: Trans-Canada Hwy, Borden-Carleton, PE C0B 1X0, Canada
notes: 12.9 km long across the Northumberland Strait — longest bridge over a freezing sea in the world. Toll paid upon leaving PEI (free entry). Serge: F-150 on Canada's longest bridge = perfect photo.

name: East Point Lighthouse (PEI's eastern tip)
notes: Easternmost point of PEI: lighthouse on a cliff above churning water. Seals and seabirds from the rocks. Red and white lighthouse with 'walking tour' guided tour.

name: Green Gables Shore Scenic Drive
address: Rte 6, North Rustico to Cavendish, PE
notes: Coastal route along red cliffs, green farmlands, and blue sea. The color palette is unique in North America. E-bikes perfect on the quiet coastal road.

name: Lucy Maud Montgomery Birthplace
address: 6461 New London Rd, New London, PE C0B 1M0, Canada
notes: The birthplace of the author of Anne of Green Gables. Original Victorian farmhouse with personal belongings. A must for fans of the book; others: skip.

name: New Glasgow Lobster Suppers
address: 604 Rte 258, New Glasgow, PE C0A 1N0, Canada
notes: PEI's legendary lobster supper tradition: whole lobster + soup + mussels + dessert. All-inclusive dining concept in a village hall — for 60 years. Els and Serge: this is the reason to go to PEI (along with the oysters).

name: North Cape Wind Energy Interpretive Centre
address: 21817 Rte 12, North Cape, PE C0B 2B0, Canada
notes: Wind farm at the northernmost point of PEI. Land and sea meet: at low tide, you can walk on a sandbank connecting both beaches. Literally feel the Atlantic wind power.

name: PEI Brewing Company (Charlottetown)
address: 54 Queen St, Charlottetown, PE C1A 4A7, Canada
notes: PEI's largest craft brewery in the heart of Charlottetown. Sir John A Amber: named after Canada's first PM, born here. Tours and tastings available.

name: PEI Potato Museum
address: 1 Dewar Ln, O'Leary, PE C0B 1V0, Canada
notes: Museum dedicated to the potato — the product that defines PEI. Largest potato in the world (replica): 4 meters tall. Els: this is the most PEI thing in the world. Serge: a museum for French fries!

name: PEI Shellfish Festival (Charlottetown)
notes: October: oyster tasting, lobster crack competitions, mussels as far as the eye can see. PEI produces 40% of all Canadian oysters. Els and Serge: this is the culinary reason to go to PEI.

name: Red Sand Beaches (PEI National Park)
address: 2 Palmers Ln, Charlottetown, PE C1A 5V6, Canada
notes: Iron-rich red sand makes PEI's beaches uniquely reddish-brown-pink. National Parks Pass: almost free. Cavendish Beach: longest and most beautiful.

name: Rossignol Estate Winery
address: 11147 Shore Rd, Little Sands, PE C0A 1W0, Canada
notes: PEI's best winery on the Northumberland Shore. Fruit wines and mead made from local fruit. Els: wine tasting with a sea view. Check.

name: Swingers/Naturist PEI
notes: PEI is too small and conservative for lifestyle clubs. Private contacts possible via SDC.com. Island community: everyone knows everyone — discretion is key.

name: The Dunes Studio Gallery (Brackley Beach)
address: 3622 Brackley Point Rd, Brackley Beach, PE C1E 2T2, Canada
notes: Gallery featuring ceramics, sculpture, and paintings by PEI artists. Garden filled with large ceramic sculptures. Free to look around, purchase optional.

name: The Great George Hotel (Charlottetown)
address: 58 Great George St, Charlottetown, PE C1A 4K3, Canada
notes: Boutique hotel in historic Confederation-era buildings in the city center. Multiple buildings connected by a courtyard. Walking distance to everything in Charlottestown.

name: The Inn at St. Peters (shore resort)
address: 1 Resort Ln, St. Peters Bay, PE C0A 2A0, Canada
notes: Coastal resort on St. Peters Bay: rustic cottages with waterfront views. Restaurant with fresh PEI oysters and lobster. Perfect starting point for the Points East Coastal Drive.

name: Victoria-by-the-Sea (tiny arts village)
notes: Canada's smallest active theater village: 100 inhabitants, own playhouse. Chocolate shop, art galleries, and summer theater. Victoria Theatre: small-scale but charming.

name: Au Pied de Cochon (Martin Picard)
address: 536 Rue Duluth E, Montreal, QC H2L 1A9, Canada
notes: Canada's most extravagant restaurant: foie gras on everything, poutine with foie gras, duck-in-a-can. Martin Picard = the Heston Blumenthal of Quebec. Reservation weeks in advance. Serge: this is the only restaurant on the entire list that I absolutely want.

name: Auberge du Vieux-Port (Montreal)
address: 97 Rue de la Commune E, Montreal, QC H2Y 1J1, Canada
notes: Waterfront hotel with a view of the St. Lawrence River and Old Montreal. Converted historic warehouse, balcony overlooking the harbor. Perfect for an evening stroll through Old Montreal.

name: Auberge Saint-Antoine (Quebec City)
address: 8 Rue Saint-Antoine, Quebec City, QC G1K 4C9, Canada
notes: Boutique hotel in the heart of Old Quebec built around archaeological finds. Artifacts from the 18th century visible in the hallways and rooms. Els: this is the best hotel in Quebec City.

name: Biodiversarium (insectenrestaurant)
notes: Restaurant that serves insect snacks: cricket brownies, mealworm tacos. Montreal has several eateries that use insects as an ingredient. Serge: we are going to do this. Els: we are going to discuss this.

name: Biodôme de Montréal
address: 4777 Ave Pierre-De Coubertin, Montreal, QC H1V 1B3, Canada
notes: Four ecosystems under one roof: tropical rainforest, Laurentian forest, Gulf of St. Lawrence, Sub-Arctic. Penguins, lynxes, and tropical birds — all free-roaming. Els: this is a small but spectacular concept.

name: Cabane à sucre (sugar shack season)
address: 2350 Rang de la Montagne, Saint-Benoît-de-Mirabel, QC J7N 2R9, Canada
notes: Maple syrup harvest in March-April: eating straight from the tree, taffy on snow. Traditional Québécois feast: soupe aux pois, tourtière, maple pie. Els and Serge: this is a unique seasonal experience. Timing checked!

name: Château Frontenac (iconic hotel)
address: 1 Rue des Carrieres, Quebec City, QC G1R 4P5, Canada
notes: Most photographed hotel in the world: castle on top of a cliff. Over budget, but the bar and terrace are for everyone. Els: one cocktail on the terrace is mandatory — photo for @travellers1969.

name: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve (F1 track)
address: Île Notre-Dame, Montreal, QC H3E 1A2, Canada
notes: Formula 1 circuit on an island in the St. Lawrence — free riding/cycling outside of race weekends. Serge: riding an F1 circuit on an e-bike. Montreal Grand Prix: June — check timing with route!

name: Cirque du Soleil (headquarters Montréal)
notes: Cirque du Soleil was born in Montreal and has its world headquarters here. If a show is playing during your visit: definitely go. Check the show calendar for July 2027.

name: Grosse Île (Irish quarantine island)
notes: Island where Irish famine refugees were quarantined (1847). 5,000 Irish died here and are buried in mass graves. National Parks Pass + boat from Berthier-sur-Mer.

name: Habitat 67 (Moshe Safdie architecture)
address: 2600 Ave Pierre-Dupuy, Montreal, QC H3C 3R6, Canada
notes: 354 prefabricated concrete cube houses stacked like Lego: residential building from the 1967 Expo. Looks like a disaster but works perfectly as a residential complex. View exterior for free. Privately occupied.

name: Hotel Gault (Montreal)
address: 449 Rue Sainte-Hélène, Montreal, QC H2Y 2K9, Canada
notes: Minimalist design hotel in an 1871 cast-iron warehouse in Old Montreal. Large loft-style rooms with concrete walls. Els: design-minded stay in the most beautiful part of Montreal.

name: Ice Hotel (Hôtel de Glace)
address: 1860 Boul Valcartier, Saint-Gabriel-de-Valcartier, QC G0A 4S0, Canada
notes: Complete ice hotel: walls, bed, glass — everything ice and snow. Rebuilt every year with a different theme, every room unique. January-March: off your route BUT too spectacular not to mention.

name: Jean-Talon Market (Montreal)
address: 7070 Ave Henri-Julien, Montreal, QC H2S 3S3, Canada
notes: Canada's largest and oldest market: Quebec cheese, maple syrup, foie gras, local vegetables. Quebec culinary culture summarized in one place. Els and Serge: at least 2 hours here minimum.

name: Laurentian Mountains Scenic Drive
notes: Autumn (Sept-Oct): this route is completely gold, orange, and red. Villages like Saint-Sauveur and Sainte-Adèle along the route. One of the most beautiful autumn routes in Canada.

name: Mont Tremblant ⛷️ Ikon
address: 1000 Chemin des Voyageurs, Mont-Tremblant, QC J8E 1T1
notes: Ikon Pass: Unlimited (check current pass for the 27-28 season). MOST picturesque ski resort in Eastern Canada! Pedestrian-only village has an old-European Québécois character - feels like a mini-Mont Blanc. 96 trails on 2 mountain sides. Els: South Side is softer and better for beginners. 2 hours from Montreal. Après-ski scene is cozy and completely French - bienvenue! Serge: North Side for more of a challenge.

name: Montmorency Falls (hoger dan Niagara)
address: 2490 Av. Royale, Quebec City, QC G1C 1S1, Canada
notes: 83 meters high — higher than Niagara but narrower. Suspension bridge at the top of the drop: view of the St. Lawrence and Quebec City. Winter: a 30-meter icicle forms at the base.

name: Montreal Underground City (RÉSO)
address: Place Ville-Marie, Montreal, QC H3B 2B5, Canada
notes: 33 km underground network of shops, restaurants, and metro — no coat needed in winter. Largest underground complex in the world. Els: shopping without the cold. Serge: getting lost here is a sport.

name: Mount Royal Park (Olmsted)
address: 1260 Remembrance Rd, Montreal, QC H3H 1A2, Canada
notes: Frederick Law Olmsted (Central Park NYC) designed this park.  View of Montreal from the Kondiaronk Belvedere.  E-bikes on the trails: free and spectacular.

name: Musée de l'Amérique Francophone (Quebec City)
address: 2 Côte de la Fabrique, Quebec City, QC G1R 3V6, Canada
notes: Canada's oldest museum (1806): French-Canadian cultural history. Natural history collection and religious artworks from the New France period. Pairs well with the Old Quebec walking tour.

name: Naturist: Domaine de la Louisiane (AANR)
address: 565 Rang de la Louisiane, Saint-Cuthbert, QC J0K 2C0, Canada
notes: AANR naturist resort in the Lanaudière region north of Montreal. Swimming pool, sports, camping. French-Canadian naturist atmosphere: warm and social.

name: Naturist: Domaine Soleil Levant
address: 1800 Rang Saint-Jacques, Saint-Jean-de-Matha, QC J0K 2S0, Canada
notes: Naturist domain in the Laurentian Highlands. Lakeside setting with various facilities. Close to Mont-Tremblant: easy to combine.

name: Notre-Dame Basilica Montreal (lightshow)
address: 110 Rue Notre-Dame O, Montreal, QC H2Y 1T2, Canada
notes: Most impressive church in North America: blue-gold interior with a 10,000-pipe organ. AZIMUT light show in the evening: spectacular multimedia event. Celine Dion got married here. That aside.

name: Observation Tower du Lac Mégantic (dark sky)
notes: Dark sky reserve in the Eastern Townships. Milky Way visible to the naked eye outside the city. Tragic region (2013 train disaster) but also beautiful nature.

name: Old Quebec City (UNESCO Walled City)
address: Old Quebec, Quebec City, QC G1R 4P3, Canada
notes: Only walled city in North America north of Mexico. Chateau Frontenac dominates the skyline: Canada's largest photogenic building. Free walking, streets full of terraces and galleries.

name: Parc de la Chute-Montmorency
address: 2490 Av Royale, Boischatel, QC G0A 1H0, Canada
notes: Cable car up or stairs down along the waterfall. In winter: ice climbing on the frozen waterfall. Zip line over the waterfall available in summer.

name: Parc Omega (wildlife drive-through)
notes: Car safari through Canadian wildlife: wolves, bears, moose, and deer come to the windows. Bringing carrots and baby carrots for the animals. Els: This is the best idea for the F-150. Window down, moose eats from hand.

name: Plains of Abraham (Battlefields Park)
address: 835 Ave Wilfrid-Laurier, Quebec City, QC G1S 3C2, Canada
notes: Where the battle was fought that made Canada French or English (1759). Both generals (Wolfe AND Montcalm) died in the battle. Free park visit — museum separate.

name: Plateau-Mont-Royal (neighbourhood walk)
notes: Bohemian neighborhood with colorful wooden staircases (outdoor stairs) as an architectural feature. Street art, terraces, Marché Jean-Talon. Montreal's nicest neighborhood to just walk around.

name: Pointe-à-Callière Museum (buried city)
address: 350 Place Royale, Montreal, QC H2Y 3Y5, Canada
notes: Museum built above the archaeological remains of the first Montreal (1642). You literally walk through layers of history. Serge: underground city and museum = perfect.

name: Poutine (La Banquise, Montreal)
address: 994 Rue Rachel E, Montreal, QC H2J 2J2, Canada
notes: 24/7 poutine restaurant with 30 variations: from classic to foie gras. Invented in Quebec in the 1950s — fries + cheese and grains + brown sauce. Els: these are Belgian fries with a Quebec twist. Judge after tasting.

name: Route des Vins (Eastern Townships)
notes: Wine Route through the Eastern Townships: more than 20 wineries. Rolling hills, French charm, direct wine sales. Els: this is the best day in Quebec for me.

name: Saguenay Fjord National Park
notes: 300-meter-deep fjord with vertical cliffs: spectacular kayaking. Statue of Notre-Dame du Saguenay on a 180m high cliff. National Parks Pass (Quebec version) available.

name: Schwartz's Deli (Montreal smoked meat)
address: 3895 Blvd Saint-Laurent, Montreal, QC H2W 1X9, Canada
notes: Legendary Montreal smoked meat deli: open since 1928. The line is always on the street — every day. Smoked meat sandwich: it is not pastrami, it is not corned beef, it is Montreal.

name: St-Viateur Bagel Shop (Montreal)
address: 263 Rue Saint-Viateur O, Montreal, QC H2V 1Y1, Canada
notes: 24/7 open wood-fired bagel bakery in the Mile End neighborhood. Montreal bagel vs New York bagel: this is the better one. Fresh from the oven, sesame or poppy, with lox and schmear.

name: Swingers: Club 281 (Montréal)
address: 281 Rue Sainte-Catherine E, Montreal, QC H2X 1L8, Canada
notes: Iconic LGBTQ+ inclusive strip and lifestyle bar in Montreal. Montreal has the most open and diverse nightlife scene in Canada. Verify current formula via website or SDC.com.

name: Swingers: Taboo Nantes (Montréal lifestyle)
notes: Montreal has several lifestyle clubs — open and well-organized. French-speaking culture = more open and less taboo than Anglophone Canada. Verify address and calendar via Kasidie.

name: Tadoussac (whale watching)
notes: Best whale watching location in Canada: Belugas year-round, Blue whales in summer. Saguenay Fjord flows into the St. Lawrence here. Boat tour: June-September is the best season.

name: Tremblant (ski resort + village)
address: 3005 Chemin de la Chapelle, Mont-Tremblant, QC J8E 1E1, Canada
notes: Most visited ski resort in eastern Canada — but summer is beautiful too. Pedestrian village with colorful Québécois architecture. Hiking trails and e-bike trails in the Laurentian Mountains.

name: Val-Jalbert Ghost Town (Quebec)
address: 95 Rue Saint-Georges, Chambord, QC G0W 1G0, Canada
notes: Completely abandoned pulp mill town from 1926: factory buildings, houses, school — everything intact. Gondola over the 72-meter Ouiatchouan waterfall. One of Canada's best-preserved ghost towns.

name: Village Québécois d'Antan (living history)
address: 1425 Montplaisir Blvd, Drummondville, QC J2C 7H5, Canada
notes: Open-air museum with 70 historic buildings and actors in 19th-century attire. Brewery, blacksmith, pharmacist — everything working. Drummondville: eccentric folk festival on Saturday evening.

name: Benefit Street (Mile of History)
notes: The most densely built street with 18th- and 19th-century architecture in the US. Colonial, Federal, and Victorian homes on one street. Free walking. H.P. Lovecraft, Edgar Allan Poe, and Roger Williams all connected.

name: Big Blue Bug (Nibbles Woodaway)
address: 2235 S County Trail, East Greenwich, RI 02818
notes: Giant blue termite (9 meters long) on ​​the roof of a pest control company. A landmark along I-95 for 40 years. Free photo from the car. Serge: already visible from the highway.

name: Block Island (day trip or overnight)
notes: Island 20 km off the coast, accessible by ferry. Mohegan Bluffs: 60-meter cliff above the ocean. Five of the twelve best beaches in the US are located here — no cars on the island.

name: Charlestown Breachway (barrier beach)
notes: Long barrier beach between lagoon and ocean. Fishing, surfcasting, and camping directly on the beach. Campsite on top of the beach itself: rare in the US.

name: Conanicut Island (Jamestown)
notes: Island in the middle of Narragansett Bay accessible via bridge. Fort Wetherill State Park: granite rock cliffs for diving and kayaking. Quiet alternative to busy Newport.

name: Fort Adams State Park
notes: Largest coastal fort in the US: construction began in 1824 and took 33 years. Boat tour from the harbor offers the best view. National Parks Pass: free access to the park area.

name: H.P. Lovecraft walking tour (Providence)
notes: H.P. Lovecraft was born in Providence — the city that inspired his eerie universe. Self-guided or guided tour of places from his life and stories. Fans of cosmic horror: this is a pilgrimage.

name: Haven Brothers Diner (mobile diner)
notes: Diner on a trailer that parks next to City Hall every night at 5 am. In exactly the same spot for over 130 years — but it is a trailer. Burgers, hot dogs, milkshakes. Open until 3 am.

name: Hemenway's (Providence seafood)
address: One Providence Washington Plaza, Providence, RI 02903
notes: Providence's best seafood restaurant: clam chowder, lobster, swordfish. Waterfront location overlooking the bay. Reservations recommended for the weekend.

name: Hotel Viking (Newport)
notes: Historic 1926 hotel at the beginning of the Bellevue Avenue mansion strip. Walking distance from all Newport mansions and Cliff Walk. Over budget, but the location is unbeatable.

name: International Tennis Hall of Fame
notes: In the Newport Casino (1880) — the first tennis club in the US. Interactive exhibition on the history of tennis. Not for everyone, but the building is beautiful even without an interest in tennis.

name: Museum of Natural History (Roger Williams Park)
notes: Free museum in beautiful Roger Williams Park. Natural history of Rhode Island + planetarium. Good for a rainy day in Providence.

name: Narragansett Bay whale watching
notes: Whale watching tours from Galilee/Point Judith to the open Atlantic Ocean. Humpbacks, finbacks, and straight whales in the summer. Els: whales are always worth it.

name: Naturist: geen AANR resort RI
address: Dichtstbijzijnde: Cape Cod MA of Connecticut
notes: Rhode Island has no official AANR naturist resort. Closest options: Sandy Terraces (CT) or Cape Cod (MA). An informal nude beach exists on Block Island.

name: Newport Cliff Walk (3 mile ocean path)
notes: 5 km path along ocean cliffs with views of the Vanderbilt mansions. Free, spectacular, photogenic at every point. Els: this is the most beautiful walk on the East Coast.

name: Newport Folk Festival
address: Fort Adams State Park, Newport, RI 02840
notes: Legendary music festival: Bob Dylan plugged in his electric guitar here in 1965. July weekend: folk, roots, americana. Check the 2027 lineup — it can always be spectacular.

name: Newport Mansions Night Tours (ghost tours)
notes: Ghost tours along the dark sides of Newport's rich history. Stories of death, shady deals, and ghosts in the Gilded Age villas. Els: maybe. Serge: definitely.

name: Olneyville New York System (wieners)
notes: Rhode Island-style hot dogs: small sausages with special 'hot wiener' sauce, celery salt, and mustard. Providence Institute for over 80 years. Serge: this is Americana at its most enigmatic.

name: Pastiche Fine Desserts (Providence)
notes: European-style patisserie in Federal Hill (Providence's Italian neighborhood). Tarts, eclairs, croissants — everything perfectly handmade. Els: this is the level we consider normal in Belgium.

name: Providence Arcade (oldest US indoor mall)
notes: Oldest covered shopping arcade in the US: built in 1828. Now converted into micro-apartments upstairs, shops and eateries downstairs. Greek temple facade in downtown Providence.

name: RISD Museum (Rhode Island School of Design)
notes: Art museum of the world's most famous design school. Collection of 100,000 works: from Japanese ceramics to modern paintings. Els: unexpectedly impressive for a university museum.

name: Slater Mill (Industrial Revolution birthplace)
notes: First successful textile factory in the US: 1793, start of the Industrial Revolution in America. Working machines, historical guides. Samuel Slater smuggled the factory blueprints from England into his head.

name: Swingers: Rhode Island lifestyle scene
notes: Providence has a small but active lifestyle community. No fixed clubs — private events via SDC.com or Kasidie. Boston (1-hour drive) has more options.

name: The Athenaeum (Providence library)
notes: One of the oldest library buildings in the US (1836). Edgar Allan Poe read aloud from his work here and flirted with a local woman. Free admission — the historic atmosphere is palpable.

name: The Breakers (Vanderbilt mansion)
notes: 70-room 'summer cottage' by Cornelius Vanderbilt II, built in 1895. Renaissance palace by the ocean: gold, marble, frescoes everywhere. Els: incredibly overdone. Serge: how dare they call it a cottage.

name: The Breakers + The Elms + Marble House combo
notes: Mansion combo ticket: 3 Gilded Age villas in one day. Each villa competes with the previous one in excess. Serge: this is capitalism as art. Els: guilty pleasure.

name: The Dean Hotel (Providence)
notes: Hippest hotel in Providence: rock 'n roll aesthetic, Boombox bar, tattoo parlor in the lobby. Neighborhood full of restaurants and bars. Els: this is cool without being over the top.

name: The Francis (Newport B&B)
notes: B&B in a Victorian townhouse 5 min from the mansions. Full breakfast included, friendly owners. Best value for money in Newport.

name: Touro Synagogue (oldest in US)
notes: Oldest synagogue in the US (1763): George Washington wrote his famous letter on religious freedom there. National Historic Site + National Parks Pass. Small but historically incredibly important.

name: WaterFire Providence (fire art event)
notes: 100 fire basins on three rivers illuminate the night: free outdoor art installation. Summer and autumn on irregular evenings. Accompanied by ambient music and gondolas. Check the schedule for 2027!

name: Waterman Grille (Providence)
notes: Steak and seafood restaurant on the banks of the Providence River. Live jazz every night. Elegant yet affordable for the quality.

name: Batoche National Historic Site
notes: Battlefield of the Northwest Rebellion of 1885: Louis Riel's Métis were defeated here. National Parks Pass: free. Bulletin holes in the church are still visible.

name: Big Muddy Badlands (outlaw territory)
address: Big Muddy Valley, SK S0H 2B0, Canada
notes: Vast badlands where Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid hid. Nestor the outlaw's cave is still present. This valley has no road — 4x4 required. F-150: perfect.

name: Cannington Manor (eccentric British colony)
address: Cannington Manor Provincial Heritage Park, Manor, SK S0C 1R0, Canada
notes: British aristocrats attempted to establish an English landlord colony on the prairie here in 1882. Cricket, afternoon tea, foxhunting — on the Saskatchewan plains. The colony disappeared after 20 years, but the buildings still stand. Free.

name: Crooked Bush (leaning aspen grove)
notes: Grove of white poplars that ALL grow crooked and twisted — a genetic mutation. Nobody knows why. Scientists investigated it without a conclusion. Free, in the middle of a field. Serge: this is Silent Hill, but with trees.

name: Cypress Hills Massacre Site (1873)
notes: Site where 20 Assiniboine were killed by American wolf catchers — the incident led to the establishment of the RCMP. National Parks Pass: free. Historic watershed moment for Canada.

name: Delta Hotels Regina
address: 1919 Saskatchewan Dr, Regina, SK S4P 4H2, Canada
notes: Solid central hotel in Regina — nothing special but reliable. Walking distance from RCMP Heritage Centre and Wascana Park. Parking for F-150 is not a problem.

name: Diefenbaker Canada Centre (Prime Minister)
address: 101 Diefenbaker Pl, Saskatoon, SK S7N 5B8, Canada
notes: Museum about Canada's 13th Prime Minister John Diefenbaker, born in SK. Free admission. Bunker-style building on the University of Saskatchewan campus.

name: Elk Ridge Resort (Prince Albert NP area)
notes: Lakeside lodge next to Prince Albert National Park. Kayaking, hiking, and wildlife viewing included. Els: This is the perfect nature retreat.

name: Grasslands National Park (prairie dogs)
notes: Last pristine mixed-grass prairie in North America. National Parks Pass: free. Prairie dog towns, black-footed ferrets (nearly extinct), and bison. Dark sky preserve: Milky Way here is incredible.

name: Hearth Restaurant (Regina)
address: 1876 Hamilton St, Regina, SK S4P 2C1, Canada
notes: Wood-fired everything in a cozy Regina restaurant. Saskatchewan grains, bison, wild-caught fish. Best dinner in Regina after the RCMP museum visit.

name: Inglis Grain Elevators NHS
address: Inglis, MB — border SK (net over de grens)
notes: Five wooden grain elevators in perfect condition: the icon of the prairie. National Parks Pass: free. The most Saskatchewan thing in the world: grain, prairie, wooden tower.

name: Last Mountain Lake Bird Observatory
address: Last Mountain Lake, SK S0G 2H0, Canada
notes: Oldest protected wildlife area in North America (1887). Millions of geese and cranes stop here on migration — Sept/October. Free bird watching.

name: Mac the Moose (world record moose statue)
address: On the Trans-Canada Hwy, Moose Jaw, SK S6H 4P4, Canada
notes: 9.8-meter-high moose sculpture along the Trans-Canada Highway. Largest moose sculpture in the world (disputed by Stor-Elvdal in Norway). Free. Photo required. Serge: bigger is better.

name: Moose Jaw (weird name + weird city)
notes: City with one of the weirdest names in Canada — no one knows the exact origin. Tunnels + Mac the Moose (biggest moose statue in the world) + Wakamow Valley. Serge: a city named Moose Jaw MUST be on the list.

name: Naturist: geen AANR resort SK
notes: Saskatchewan has no official AANR naturist resort. Closest options are in Alberta or Manitoba. Private skinny dipping at Last Mountain Lake is popular.

name: Northern Lights viewing (Prince Albert NP)
notes: Dark Sky Preserve: Good aurora chances already in September-October. National Parks Pass: free. Combine with camping in the park.

name: Odd Couple Restaurant (Saskatoon)
address: 118 2nd Ave N, Saskatoon, SK S7K 2B7, Canada
notes: Asian-Canadian fusion in downtown Saskatoon. Saskatoon berry cheesecake: the province's must-try dessert. Els: the Saskatoon berry is like a blueberry, but better.

name: Potash Mine Tour (Mosaic)
notes: Saskatchewan produces 30% of the world's potassium salt: underground mine visit. Indoor mine shaft at a depth of 1 km — as big as a city. Serge: industrial underground adventure.

name: Radisson Saskatoon
address: 405 20th St E, Saskatoon, SK S7K 6X6, Canada
notes: Best located hotel in Saskatoon: on the Saskatchewan River. Breakfast included with some rates. Good base for day trips to Wanuskewin and around the city.

name: Ravine Ecological Reserve (Regina)
address: Wascana Centre, Regina, SK S4P 3V7, Canada
notes: Wascana Lake in the middle of Regina: one of the largest city parks in North America. Pelicans, white swans, and coyotes in the park. Free, beautiful for a morning walk.

name: RCMP Heritage Centre (Mounties birthplace)
address: Dewdney Ave W, Regina, SK S4P 3J7, Canada
notes: The Royal Canadian Mounted Police — the iconic red-clad Mounties — were born here in 1873. Museum + daily Sunset Retreat ceremony in summer. Serge: the red jacket + horse combo = absolutely photogenic.

name: Reesor Lake (cypress hills)
address: Cypress Hills Interprovincial Park, SK S0C 2B0, Canada
notes: Cypress Hills: highest point between the Rockies and Labrador. During the last Ice Age, this was a refuge island above the ice. Elk and mule deer everywhere.

name: Saskatchewan Science Centre (Regina)
address: 2903 Powerhouse Dr, Regina, SK S4N 0A1, Canada
notes: Interactive science museum for all ages. IMAX theater attached to the building. Good for a rainy day in Regina.

name: Saskatoon Berry picking
notes: Saskatoon berries are only found in Saskatchewan and Alberta: violet, sweet, unique. U-pick farms everywhere in July-August. Els: berries taken from the F-150 fridge.

name: Swingers: geen clubs SK
notes: Saskatchewan is sparsely populated and conservative: no established lifestyle clubs. Private groups in Saskatoon and Regina via SDC.com. Verify before visiting via online platforms.

name: Tunnels of Moose Jaw
address: 18 Main St N, Moose Jaw, SK S6H 3J8, Canada
notes: Underground tunnels with guided tours about Chinese immigrants and Al Capone. Al Capone is said to have gone into hiding here in the 1920s — the evidence is wafer-thin, but the story is gold. Els: perfectly bizarre underground experience.

name: Wakamow Valley (Moose Jaw)
address: 1 River Dr W, Moose Jaw, SK S6H 6L4, Canada
notes: River Valley City Park in Moose Jaw. Good for an e-bike ride along the Moose Jaw River. Free.

name: Wanuskewin Heritage Park
notes: 6,000 years of First Nations history at one site: tipi rings, bison jumps, medicine wheel. Nominee for UNESCO World Heritage. Cultural performances and heirloom kitchen restaurant.

name: Waskesiu Lake (Prince Albert NP)
address: 2 Waskesiu Dr, Waskesiu Lake, SK S0J 2Y0, Canada
notes: National park with the largest caribou herd in Saskatchewan. National Parks Pass: free. Grey Owl's cabin accessible by canoe: famous English man who lived as an Ojibwe.

name: Weczeria Food & Wine (Saskatoon)
address: 608 10th St E, Saskatoon, SK S7H 0G9, Canada
notes: Best restaurant in Saskatchewan: local prairie ingredients as fine dining. Bison, saskatoon berries, caragana honey. Els: this is prairie cuisine as it should be.

name: Angel Oak Tree (500+ jaar)
address: 3688 Angel Oak Rd, Johns Island, SC 29455
notes: Living oak at least 500 years old: branches span 17 meters horizontally. Free. Truly surrealistically large. Els and Serge: this is a tree the size of a cathedral.

name: Beaufort Historic District
notes: Antebellum city that was too beautiful to burn: General Union occupied and spared. Big Chill, Forrest Gump, and Prince of Tides were filmed here. Free walking tour.

name: Biltmore-inspired Broome House (Abandoned)
notes: Abandoned country house in the middle of the woods: nature is swallowing it up. Private property, but keep away from the road. Ghost vibes in the Deep South.

name: BMW Zentrum Museum (Spartanburg)
notes: Free BMW factory tour + museum at the only BMW factory outside Germany. SC manufactures all BMW X models. Serge: This is a religious experience for car people.

name: Boone Hall Plantation
address: 1235 Long Point Rd, Mount Pleasant, SC 29466
notes: Avenue of Oaks: 300m avenue of 250-year-old living oaks — one of the most beautiful photo trails in the US. North & South TV series filmed here. Elants awareness of slavery history is fully present.

name: Brookgreen Gardens (largest sculpture garden)
notes: Largest sculpture garden in North America on a former rice plantation estate. Live alligators in the garden. Els: sculpture + nature + alligators = perfect.

name: Caesars Head State Park
notes: Spectacular rock lookout post 3,000 feet high in the Blue Ridge. Raptor migration in October: thousands of hawks. Els: standing here is incredible.

name: Carolina Lowcountry Scenic Byway
notes: Coastal route along salt marshes, Riverine oyster farming, and Gullah Geechee cultural landscapes. Photogenic at every turn. E-bikes on the cycle routes around the sea islands.

name: Charleston Historic District
notes: Most beautiful historic city in the South: pastel-colored Antebellum houses, cobblestone streets. Free walking tour of Rainbow Row. Els: this is Europe in America.

name: Congaree National Park
notes: Largest untouched bottomland hardwood forest in the US. National Parks Pass: free. Bioluminescent fireflies in sync in June: a truly unique spectacle.

name: Cypress Gardens
address: 3030 Cypress Gardens Rd, Moncks Corner, SC 29461
notes: Cypress swamp with boats: trees with hanging moss over black water. Alligators, herons, water lilies. Free flatboat ride included.

name: Edisto Island Serpentarium
notes: Private snake collection of an eccentric herpetologist on an island. Live king cobras, rattlesnakes, and gators in a garden setting. Small but intense experience.

name: FIG Restaurant (Charleston)
notes: Farm-inspired gastronomy — best local cuisine in the region. Charleston's most awarded restaurant. Reservations required.

name: Folly Beach (Charleston's surf beach)
notes: Surfer beach 30 min from Charleston: bohemian, laid-back. Best sunrise photography in the region. Free beach.

name: Hunting Island State Park (lighthouse + beach)
address: 2555 Sea Island Pkwy, St. Helena Island, SC 29920
notes: The only lighthouse accessible to the public and wild beaches with palmetto trees. Beach with driftwood and free-roaming loggerhead turtles. Forrest Gump beach scenes: filmed here.

name: Husk Restaurant (Charleston)
notes: Best restaurant in Charleston: anything south of the Mason-Dixon line. Sean Brock's masterpiece: heirloom varietals, smoke, Southern technique. Reserve weeks in advance. Serge: this is the top 5 of the trip.

name: International African American Museum (Charleston)
notes: New museum (2023) on the site of the largest slave market area in the US. Groundbreaking story of the African diaspora in America. Els: this is mandatory in Charleston.

name: Lewis Barbecue (Charleston)
notes: Texas BBQ pit master who moved to Charleston: giant brisket, ribs. 1,000 pounds of meat a day on a wood fire. Serge: Texas BBQ in South Carolina. Debate is open.

name: Litchfield Beach & Golf Resort
notes: Coastal resort with golf courses, swimming pools, and beach views. Pawleys Island: quiet alternative to busy Myrtle Beach.

name: Magnolia Plantation & Gardens
notes: Oldest plantation in the Deep South open to the public: 1676. Azalea festival in April: millions of flowers at once. Boat trip through the swamp.

name: Middleton Place (oldest landscape garden)
notes: Oldest formal gardens in North America (1741): geometric terracing along a river. Breath swans, alligators, and Barbados longhorn cattle. Els: garden architecture nerd heaven.

name: Myrtle Beach Boardwalk
address: 1200 N Ocean Blvd, Myrtle Beach, SC 29577
notes: Typical boardwalk: mini-golf, tattoo shops, fried Oreos, Skywheel. 60 golf courses in the region — Serge's playground. Kitsch overdrive but amusing.

name: Naturist: Sun Air Nudist Resort (AANR)
address: Myrtle Beach area, SC (verifieer via AANR 2027)
notes: AANR member naturist resort in the Myrtle Beach region. Verify current info via the AANR website. SC has a warm lifestyle community.

name: Old Sheldon Church Ruins
address: Old Sheldon Church Rd, Yemassee, SC 29945
notes: Gothic ruins of a 1753 church, burned twice (Revolution + Civil War). Oaks with hanging moss grow through the walls. Free, photogenic, hauntingly perfect.

name: Peachoid Water Tower (Gaffney)
notes: Water tower built like a gigantic peach — including the slit. Gaffney = peach production capital. Famous from House of Cards. Free photo from the car.

name: Ravenel Bridge (Charleston)
notes: Highest cable-stayed bridge in the US: 182-meter towers above the Cooper River. Walking and cycling path on the bridge: 8 km return with panoramic views. E-bikes across the bridge to Mount Pleasant.

name: SC Festival of Flowers (Greenwood)
notes: SC's largest flower festival in July. Fireworks, live music, local commerce. Combine with nearby Blue Ridge Country.

name: SkyWheel Myrtle Beach
address: 1110 N Ocean Blvd, Myrtle Beach, SC 29577
notes: 187-foot-high Ferris wheel directly on the beach. Night: illuminated gondolas over the Atlantic Ocean. Good for 20 minutes of entertainment.

name: South of the Border (roadside complex)
notes: Pedro the Mexican welcomes you with 97 billboards along I-95. Gigantic kitsch complex: motel, restaurants, arcade, souvenirs — everything Mexican-themed. The irony is complete: right in the middle of South Carolina. Free to walk around.

name: Swamp Fox Brewing (Florence)
notes: Craft brewery named after the Revolutionary hero. Local ingredients such as pecan and magnolia.

name: Swingers: Club Privata (Columbia SC)
notes: Columbia has an active lifestyle scene. Verify via SDC.com or Kasidie. SC is conservative, but Columbia (university city) has more openness.

name: Table Rock State Park
notes: Two striking mountain peaks in the Blue Ridge foothills: Table Rock and Pinnacle. Hike to the top: panorama over Piedmont. E-bikes on the lower trails.

name: The Restoration (Charleston)
notes: Modern boutique in a renovated historic building. Rooftop terraces with views of the city. Walking distance to everything in Charleston.

name: The Spectator Hotel (Charleston)
notes: Boutique hotel in the heart of Charleston with Art Deco 1930s style. Each room is decorated differently with vintage maps. Els: this is the best hotel in Charleston.

name: The Swamp Fox (Francis Marion NF)
notes: National forest named after the revolutionary guerrilla Francis Marion. Walking trails through swamps with alligators. Free admission.

name: Two Notch Road ghost town (Columbia area)
notes: Abandoned 19th-century trading post along a historic route. Dilapidated buildings in the forest. Free exploration.

name: Waterfall tour (Oconee County)
notes: 12+ waterfalls accessible in the Blue Ridge foothills of Oconee County. Issaqueena Falls, Yellow Branch Falls — most free. E-bike on the backroads of the Upstate.

name: Westbrook Brewing Company
notes: South Carolina's most awarded brewery. Mexican Cake Imperial Stout: legendary. Serge: this beer is on the list.

name: York W. Bailey Museum (Gullah culture)
address: 16 Penn Center Circle W, St. Helena Island, SC 29920
notes: Gullah-Geechee culture: descendants of West African slaves preserved a unique language and culture. Penn School was the first school for freed slaves after the Civil War. Els: this is a story that needs to be told.

name: 1880 Town (Murdo)
notes: Fully recreated Western town with 31 buildings and 1880s heritage. Old wagons, blacksmith, one-room schoolhouse. Kitsch but charming.

name: Badlands National Park
notes: Eroded pinnacles and buttes in pink-orange-gray: sci-fi landscape. National Parks Pass: FREE. Bison walk across the road. Prairie dogs everywhere. Stars at night = breathtaking.

name: Big Thunder Gold Mine tour
notes: Real Black Hills gold mine: 200-foot descent into an active mine. Gold panning afterwards. Combine with a Mount Rushmore day.

name: Black Hills Wild Horse Sanctuary
address: 12163 Cheyenne River Rd, Hot Springs, SD 57747
notes: 500 wild mustangs live freely on 11,000 hectares. Car tour to find and observe the herd. Els: free horses in a wild landscape.

name: Cedar Pass Lodge (Badlands)
notes: Only lodge within Badlands NP: sleep literally in the park. Sunrise over the spire formations from your room. Book early — small accommodation.

name: Corn Palace (Mitchell)
notes: Building completely covered in murals of corn cobs in 9 colors. Redecorated every year: never the same. Els and Serge: this is the most South Dakota thing in the world.

name: Crazy Horse Memorial (in progress)
address: 12151 Avenue of the Chiefs, Crazy Horse, SD 57730
notes: World's largest sculpture under construction: Lakota war hero Crazy Horse. Construction for 75 years, not yet finished — the process IS the monument. Indigenous cultural center and Crazy Horse's outstretched arm are already pointing.

name: Custer State Park (wildlife loop)
notes: 1,300 free-roaming bison in a 726 km² park. Wildlife Loop Road: car safari with burros knocking on windows. National Parks Pass doesn't work but worth every penny.

name: Deadwood Historic District
notes: Gold Rush city where Wild Bill Hickok was murdered during poker in 1876. Front Street still intact with saloons, casinos, and historic hotels. Free to walk around — gambling is legal here.

name: Deadwood lodging options
notes: Historic hotels in the gold rush town: Bullock Hotel (built by the sheriff in 1895). Gambling at the hotel — Deadwood is a legal casino town. Els: sleeping in a 19th-century saloon. Yes.

name: Dinosaur Park (Rapid City)
notes: Free! 7 life-size concrete dinosaurs on a hill above Rapid City. Built in 1936 as a Depression-era work project. Anal-retentive accurate for 1936.

name: Falls Park (Sioux Falls)
address: 300 N Phillips Ave, Sioux Falls, SD 57104
notes: Waterfall park in the middle of the city: pink quartzite stone. Free visit with observation tower. Sioux Falls is a surprise — better city than expected.

name: Jewel Cave National Monument
notes: Third longest cave in the world: 340 km map. National Parks Pass: free. Caves covered with calcite jewels that reflect light.

name: Mammoth Site (Hot Springs)
address: 1800 Hwy 18 Truck Bypass, Hot Springs, SD 57747
notes: Active excavation site of 60 mammoths: you watch as paleontologists dig. One of the largest in situ mammoth excavations in the world. Els and Serge: pulling mammoths OUT of the ground right before your eyes.

name: Minuteman Missile NHS
notes: Original Cold War nuclear missile silo — intact and open to visitors. National Parks Pass: FREE. Serge: You are standing next to a nuclear missile. That isn't possible everywhere.

name: Minuteman Missile Visitor Center
notes: Documentation on the US Cold War nuclear strategy. National Parks Pass: FREE. Combine with an outdoor silo visit.

name: Mount Moriah Cemetery (Deadwood)
notes: Wild Bill Hickok and Calamity Jane buried next to each other. They were not in a relationship, but fans placed them together. Funny post-mortem love story.

name: Mount Rushmore National Memorial
notes: Four presidential faces carved in granite: Washington, Jefferson, Roosevelt, Lincoln. National Parks Pass: FREE (parking $10). The sunset lighting ceremony is the best moment.

name: Naturist: geen AANR resort SD
notes: South Dakota has no official AANR naturist resort. Private skinny dipping at Pactola Lake or Sylvan Lake in Custer SP. Nearest AANR: Timber Trails Iowa.

name: Needles Highway (iron + granite)
notes: 16 km of roads through narrow granite spire tunnels and pinhead-like formations. Driving through the eyes of needles: spectacular. Custer State Park fee applies.

name: Pactola Lake (Black Hills)
notes: Clear mountain lake in the middle of the Black Hills. Kayaking, swimming, fishing. Gloomiest name, most beautiful lake in SD.

name: Prairie Homestead (original sod house)
notes: The only original surviving prairie sod house in the US. Built in 1909, remained habitable until 1961. Every aspect of the prairie pioneer life can be felt here.

name: Presidents on the Street (Rapid City)
notes: Life-size bronze statues of all 43 presidents in the center. A different president in every corner. Free. Selfie with your favorite president.

name: Sioux Falls Sculpture Walk
notes: Annually changing outdoor sculptures in the center. Free to walk around. Best use of Sioux Falls for a morning.

name: Spearfish Canyon Scenic Byway
notes: 22 km of roads through a 300-meter-deep limestone canyon with waterfalls. Spearfish Falls and Roughlock Falls along the route. Free, spectacular.

name: Sturgis Motorcycle Rally
notes: World's largest motorcycle rally: 500,000+ riders in August. August 2027: check timing with route! Even without a motorcycle: Sturgis during the rally is a spectacle.

name: Swingers: SD lifestyle scene
address: Rapid City / Sioux Falls, SD (verifieer SDC.com)
notes: SD is too sparsely populated for permanent lifestyle clubs. Private events in Sioux Falls via SDC.com. Sturgis week: anything is possible in August.

name: Tatanka: Story of the Bison
notes: Kevin Costner (Dances with Wolves) built this museum. Dance with Wolves: the Lakota perspective on Western expansion. The museum and sculpture garden.

name: Wall Drug (original roadside attraction)
notes: Drugstore grown into a 76,000 m² mini-city with 5-cent coffee. Billboards start 800 km before the entrance. Serge: this is the progenitor of all roadside attractions.

name: Wind Cave National Park
notes: One of the longest caves in the world + bison prairie above. National Parks Pass: FREE. Boxwork: rare calcite honeycomb formations found nowhere else as good.

name: Bankers Alley Hotel Nashville, Tapestry Collection by Hilton
notes: Art museum + hotel: contemporary art in every hallway and room. Downtown Nashville, walking distance to everything. Els: this is the right type of hotel.

name: Beale Street (Memphis blues)
notes: Birthplace of the blues: live music coming from every door, 24/7. The smell of barbecue hangs in the air permanently. Big mistake: planning only one evening here.

name: Bristol Motor Speedway
notes: NASCAR circuit in a canyon of steel: steepest oval grandstand in the world. When there is a race (April and August): spectacular. Tours available outside of race weekends as well.

name: Central BBQ (Memphis)
notes: Memphis-style BBQ: dry rub ribs, smoked sausages, baked beans. Difference from Texas and KC: no sauce on the ribs. Serge: comparing every BBQ style is a scientific project.

name: Coker Museum of Transportation (Chattanooga)
address: 411 W M.L. King Blvd, Chattanooga, TN 37402
notes: 150 vintage cars and motorcycles in a former bus station. From 1902 steam cars to 1970s muscle cars. Serge: this is a day of entertainment on wheels.

name: Crash Pad (Chattanooga)
notes: Outdoor-sports inspired boutique hotel for climbers and adventurers. In the best outdoor adventure city of the South. Crashpad because climbing and crashing are connected.

name: Cumberland Gap NHP
notes: Passage used by Daniel Boone to 'discover' Kentucky in 1775. National Parks Pass: free. Three-state point: TN, KY, VA from a single viewpoint.

name: Dollywood
address: 2700 Dollywood Parks Blvd, Pigeon Forge, TN 37863
notes: Dolly Parton's own theme park in the Smoky Mountains: not kitsch, but authentic Appalachian. Miner roller coaster 'Lightning Rod': fastest wooden launch coaster in the world. Els: Dolly = icon. Serge: the roller coasters are really good.

name: Graceland (Elvis)
notes: Elvis' house: Jungle Room, gravestones in the garden, cars, airplane. Kitsch at its very best: polyester, almost orange decorations. Els and Serge: this is mandatory. Banana bread at the snack bar too.

name: Great Smoky Mountains NP (TN kant)
notes: Most visited NP in the US: always free, no admission fee. Mist over the mountains = magical. Elk + black bears in massive numbers. Clingmans Dome: highest point in the Appalachians.

name: Hattie B's Hot Chicken (Nashville)
notes: A more famous name than Prince's, but almost as good. Rij is always on the street. Els: I'm doing the mild version. Serge: I'm doing the medium.

name: Hot Springs (Warm Springs NC border)
notes: Traditional hot springs on the French Broad river. Soaking tubs over the river: romantic and relaxing. Els: soaking here after the Great Smokies hike.

name: Jack Daniel's Distillery (Lynchburg)
notes: Free tour of the oldest distillery in the US (1866). Irony: Lynchburg is a DRY county — you are not allowed to buy there. Limited tasting available for adults.

name: Lookout Mountain Incline Railway
address: 827 E Brow Rd, Lookout Mountain, TN 37350
notes: Steepest passenger railway in the world: 72.7% gradient. Combine with Rock City and Ruby Falls for a full Lookout Mountain day.

name: Lorraine Motel / National Civil Rights Museum
notes: Martin Luther King Jr. was assassinated here on April 4, 1968. The motel is intact, the bullet impact still visible. Impressive, a must-visit.

name: Mammoth Cave (KY border)
address: 1 Mammoth Cave Pkwy, Mammoth Cave, KY 42259
notes: Longest cave in the world: 676 km map. National Parks Pass: free park admission + discounted cave tour. Technically Kentucky, just a day trip from Nashville.

name: Museum of Appalachia
notes: Largest collection of Appalachian folk artifacts: musical instruments, quilts, handmade tools. Live demonstrations of traditional crafts. Els: this is Appalachian culture at its deepest.

name: Nashville honky-tonk strip
notes: Lower Broadway: row after row of honky-tonk bars, live country music from morning till night. Free music in every bar if you buy a drink. Serge: 3 hours here is a must.

name: Natural Bridge (Red River Gorge area)
address: Natural Bridge State Resort Park, Slade, KY 40376
notes: Larger natural arch than Rainbow Bridge: sandstone arch 80 feet wide. Technically Kentucky, but Red River Gorge is a day trip from Eastern TN. SkyLift Park bridge: $30, spectacular.

name: Parthenon (Nashville)
notes: Complete reproduction of the Athenian Parthenon, including a 12-meter-high statue of Athena. Built in 1897 for a state fair and never demolished. Nashville's most bizarre building. Free park, small museum ticket.

name: Prince's Hot Chicken (Nashville)
notes: Original Nashville Hot Chicken: cayenne-speckled chicken on white bread with pickles. Since 1945. Scale 'Medium': already extremely hot. Serge: medium is the maximum for Belgians.

name: Rendezvous (Memphis ribs)
notes: Memphis ribs institute in an alley under a hotel. Has been there since 1948, never changed. Els and Serge: alley entrance, stairs down, best ribs in the world.

name: Rock City (Lookout Mountain)
notes: Spectacular rock formations on the mountaintop with signs on barns saying 'See Rock City' all over the South. Claim: 7 states visible from the top. Fairy Tale Caverns: kitsch at its finest.

name: Rock Haven Lodge - Murfreesboro
notes: AANR naturist resort in Tennessee. Verify location and details via the AANR website. Tennessee has hot summers — naturism makes sense here.

name: Ruby Falls (Lookout Mountain)
notes: 145-meter underground waterfall — deepest commercially accessible cave in the world. Elevator down, laser show on the drop. Els: this is cave entertainment at its finest.

name: Ryman Auditorium (Mother Church of Country)
notes: Original home of the Grand Ole Opry (1943-1974). The acoustics are so good that artists love performing there. Backstage tour available.

name: Swingers: Club XTC (Nashville)
notes: Nashville has an active lifestyle scene. Verify address and opening hours via SDC.com or Kasidie. Bachelorette city = open attitude.

name: Tennessee Walking Horse National Celebration - Shelbyville
notes: Tennessee Walking Horse National Championship in August. The horse with the most extreme gait — controversy in the animal welfare world. If the timing is right: fascinating and controversial.

name: Tennessee Whiskey Trail
notes: Driving route past 30+ bourbon and whiskey distilleries.  George Dickel, Corsair, Nelson's Green Brier.  Serge: a route that is DEFINITELY on the agenda.

name: The Hermitage Hotel (Nashville)
notes: Grand hotel from 1910, best address in Nashville. Ten-year renovation complete: Art Deco grandeur. Above budget, but the bar (The Oak Bar) is free to visit.

name: The Loveless Cafe (Nashville)
notes: Nashville Institute since 1951: biscuits, country ham, homemade preserves. Presidents and country stars have eaten here. Els: the biscuits are pure magic.

name: Alamo Heights Ice Cream Fiesta
notes: Local ice cream culture: paletas (Mexican popsicles) everywhere. Lucha Dora Paletas: bizarre flavors like chile mango. Els: this is the snack of South Texas.

name: Austin Bat Colony (Congress Bridge)
notes: 1.5 million Mexican free-tailed bats leave the bridge every evening at sunset. Largest urban bat colony in the world. Free viewing from the bridge path or a boat on the river.

name: Barton Creek Greenbelt (Austin)
notes: 12 km of hiking and climbing trails through a canyon in the middle of Austin. Swimming holes after periods of rain. Free admission.

name: Barton Springs Pool (Austin)
notes: Constant 20°C spring water pool in Zilker Park. Austin's cherished public swimming spot. El: this is a privilege of Austin residents that we are also allowed to use.

name: Big Bend National Park
address: 1 Panther Junction, Big Bend NP, TX 79834
notes: Biggest dark sky in the lower 48 states: Milky Way is spectacular. National Parks Pass: FREE. Rio Grande canyons, Chisos Mountains, desert — all in one park.

name: Buffalo Bayou Park (Houston)
notes: 160 hectares of city park along the canal: sculpted gardens, art installations. Free admission. Houston has better nature than you expect.

name: Cadillac Ranch (Amarillo)
notes: 10 Cadillacs half-buried in the Texan plains, completely covered in graffiti. Bring your own spray can and contribute. Free, 24/7. Serge: this has been there for 50 years and it is growing.

name: Dallas Arboretum (spring festival)
notes: Spectacular tulips and spring flowers in April. Dallas Blooms: the largest flower festival in the South. Beautiful for Els.

name: El Real Tex-Mex - former Houston restaurant (closed 2019)
notes: Tex-Mex in the historic Tower Theater building. Crispy beef tacos, enchiladas verdes, margaritas. Els: this is the real Tex-Mex, not the Chipotle version.

name: Enchanted Rock State Natural Area
notes: Gigantic pink granite dome: 130 meters high, 3 km wide. Native Americans believed that the spirits of the dead lived inside it at night. Sunset from the top = photographic.

name: Float the Frio River (Garner SP)
notes: Gently floating on an inflatable ring through a crystal-clear river. Garner State Park on the Frio: a popular Texas summer vacation spot. Els and Serge: relaxed and beautiful.

name: Flower Field of Ennis (Bluebonnets)
notes: Texas state flower, Bluebonnet: blooms late March / April. Ennis is the official Bluebonnet Capital: fields full of blue. Free to look at along the roads.

name: Franklin Barbecue (Austin)
notes: #1 BBQ in the world according to many rankers. The line starts at 6 am, before opening time at 11 am. If it runs out: too bad. Serge: this is the only reason to stand in line for 5 hours.
