name: George Ranch Historical Park (Houston)
notes: Texas ranch life from 1830-1930 in one park. Live cowboys, cattle driving, cowboy kitchen. Time capsule of the Texas ranching tradition.

name: Guadalupe Mountains NP
notes: Highest point in Texas: Guadalupe Peak (2,667m). National Parks Pass: FREE. 265-million-year-old fossil reef.

name: Hamilton Pool Preserve
address: 24300 Hamilton Pool Rd, Dripping Springs, TX 78620
notes: Hidden grotto with a waterfall that drops 15 meters into an emerald green pool. Reservations required due to popularity. Els: This is the most beautiful swimming hole in Texas.

name: Hotel Emma (San Antonio)
address: 136 E Grayson St, San Antonio, TX 78215
notes: Former brewery converted into a luxury hotel in the Pearl District. Brewhouse cellars as a lobby, vintage brewing equipment as decoration. Els: this is the most beautiful hotel concept of the trip.

name: Hotel Van Zandt (Austin)
notes: Music-inspired design hotel in the Rainey Street district. Live music in the hotel every evening. Rainey Street: Austin's best bar/restaurant strip.

name: Jester King Brewery (Austin)
notes: Farmhouse brewery on 50 hectares in the Hill Country. Wild fermentation with local microorganisms: every batch unique. Els: this is the Belgian lambic equivalent of Texas.

name: La Barbecue (Austin)
address: 2027 E Cesar Chavez St, Austin, TX 78702
notes: Competition for Franklin: female-run BBQ pit, just as good. Shorter line than Franklin. Els: brisket so tender you don't need a knife.

name: Luckenbach Texas (legendary honky-tonk)
notes: Village of 3 inhabitants but the most famous honky-tonk in Texas. Waylon Jennings wrote a song about it. Live country every night, $5 beer.

name: Marfa (artscene + mystery lights)
notes: Art village in the middle of the desert: Donald Judd's minimalist art permanently installed in an abandoned army base. Marfa Lights: mysterious floating lights at night — free viewing at the Viewing Area. Els: this is the most bizarre and beautiful village in Texas.

name: Naturist: Hippie Hollow (Austin)
notes: Texas' only legal public nude beach on Lake Travis. County park: paid admission, 18+ only. Els and Serge: this is legal nudity at a lake in Texas — unique.

name: Padre Island National Seashore
notes: Longest barrier island in the world: 113 km of pristine beach. National Parks Pass: FREE. Sea turtles lay eggs here.

name: Palo Duro Canyon (Texas Grand Canyon)
notes: Second largest canyon in the US: 30 km wide, 300 meters deep. Texas Prairie is BORING? Not here. E-bikes on the canyon floor trails.

name: Perot Museum of Nature and Science
notes: Modern architecture + dinosaurs + space + sports. 12-meter-long T-rex skull. Els and Serge: this is a day activity.

name: San Antonio River Walk
address: 849 E Commerce St, San Antonio, TX 78205
notes: 4 km canal path below street level: restaurants, hotels, galleries along the water. Gondola ride on the water. Night: illuminated and romantic.

name: San Jacinto Monument (taller than Eiffel)
address: 3523 Independence Pkwy S, La Porte, TX 77571
notes: 177-meter-high monument — taller than the Eiffel Tower — for the battle that gave Texas independence. Sits on top of a museum. Elevator to the star at the top.

name: SeaWorld San Antonio
notes: SeaWorld + Aquatica water park next to San Antonio. Your SeaWorld Fun Card works here AFTER registration in Florida. Check the card terms and conditions for San Antonio.

name: Shiner Beer Factory tour
notes: Free tour of the Spoetzl Brewery, founded in 1909 by Czech immigrants. Shinner Bock: Texas' most famous local beer. Small town, big brewery.

name: Six Flags Fiesta Texas (San Antonio)
notes: Six Flags Park — your Prestige Pass is valid here! The Roar Coaster and Superman are the highlights. Free with the pass you already have.

name: Sixth Street (Austin live music)
notes: Live Music Capital of the World: 250+ venues, free music on the streets. Every night of the week: country, blues, rock, jazz. Serge: this surpasses Nashville for the pure music experience.

name: South by Southwest (SXSW)
notes: March: film, music, tech — the largest event convergence in the world. Free showcases all over the city outside the festival. If the timing is right (March 2027): the holy grail of festivals.

name: South Congress Avenue (Austin)
notes: Austin's hippest street: vintage shops, food trucks, murals, neon lights. I Love You So Much mural: an Instagram must. Free to walk around.

name: Space Center Houston
notes: NASA's official visitor center: Mission Control original, Saturn V rocket, ISS training mockup. Saturn V: 111 meters long — you walk underneath it. Serge: this is his personal Mecca.

name: Stubb's BBQ (Austin)
notes: BBQ restaurant and open-air concert venue. C.B. Stubblefield was a legend in Texas music. Serge: food + live music.

name: Swingers: Le Trapeze (Dallas)
notes: Dallas has an active lifestyle scene. Verify current location via SDC.com or Kasidie. Texas-style: large and well-organized.

name: Swingers: Utopia Lifestyle Resort (Cypress TX)
notes: One of the largest lifestyle resorts in the US, outside Houston. Pool, jacuzzi, spacious indoor/outdoor facilities. Verify with SDC.com for 2027 events.

name: Terlingua Ghost Town
notes: Abandoned mercury mining town near Big Bend: bars, artists, and eccentricities. Not entirely abandoned: 200 people still live there, partly in ruins. Chile Cook-Off in November: legendary.

name: Texas State Cemetery (Austin)
notes: Cemetery for Texas Heroes: Sam Houston, Stephen Austin, Ann Richards. Free, day admission. Beautiful resting place in the heart of Austin.

name: The Alamo
notes: Where 189 Texans fought and died against 1,800 Mexicans in 1836. Free admission — donations welcome. Els: the story is gripping. Serge: 'Remember the Alamo' feels different when you stand there.

name: Alpine Distilling - Park City
notes: #1 Distillery in Utah 2024 (Salt Lake Magazine)! Award-winning gin, whiskey, and liqueurs. Local ingredients. Artisanal and innovative. Park City + SLC locations. Tours + tastings available. Taking a bottle back to Malta?

name: Alta Ski Area ⛷️ Ikon (skiërs only)
notes: Ikon Pass: 7 DAYS. NO snowboards! LEGENDARY world's best powder snow. Sunnyside lift: surprisingly good long beginner run for such a rugged mountain. BUT: jump beginner → intermediate is aggressive. 1 day for the authentic Utah powder experience. Serge: if there is fresh powder, make this a PRIORITY DAY. Combine with Snowbird (next door, not on Ikon).

name: Antica Forma - Moab
notes: Authentic Neapolitan pizza in the heart of canyon country! Wood-fired oven, Italian flour, local ingredients. Modern interior, casual atmosphere. Moab has a surprisingly good dining landscape. Best pizza 200 miles around.

name: Arches National Park
notes: More than 2,000 natural arches – the most in the world! Delicate Arch = Utah's icon. Fiery Furnace labyrinth. America the Beautiful pass valid! Spring + autumn: pleasant. Summer: 40°C+ in the canyon. Timed entry system – book AHEAD during the season!

name: Baker Hot Springs - Delta
address: Baker Hot Springs Rd, Delta, UT 84624
notes: FREE wild hot springs in the Utah desert! 3 primitive cement pools in the middle of nowhere. Clothing optional (BLM grounds). Goldbug style! Delta, 2 hours from SLC. Off-road final kilometers. 4WD recommended. No facilities. Pure nature.

name: Bonneville Salt Flats
notes: 30,000 hectares of white salt - NOTHING else. Pure surrealism. Speed ​​wheel records broken here. Cars drive 600+ km/h! The ground looks like snow but is rock-hard salt. FREE. Best visited: morning or evening (heat!) July-August: Speed ​​Week. Epic otherwise.

name: Bonneville Speedway / Salt Flats Racing
address: Bonneville Salt Flats International Speedway, Wendover, UT
notes: Legendary cars that broke land speed records! Thrust SSC, Blue Flame, Spirit of America - face to face. Wendover: half Utah, half Nevada - casinos on the other side. Small museum but authentic. Combine with the Salt Flats drive for a complete Bonneville day.

name: Bridal Veil Falls - Provo Canyon
notes: 607-foot double waterfall - SPECTACULAR in the spring! Used to be a tramcar going up (destroyed in an avalanche in 1996). Now hiked via a short path. FREE parking. Provo Canyon = most beautiful mountain drive near SLC. Spring: maximum water volume. Summer: busier but still beautiful.

name: Bryce Canyon National Park
notes: Orange and red hoodoos as far as the eye can see! Sunrise at Inspiration Point = a religious experience. America the Beautiful pass valid! Highest point: 2,700m - cooler than other parks. Autumn: snow hoodoos. Summer: very crowded but unforgettable.

name: Burr Trail Road
notes: Legendary 4WD drive through the Escalante wilderness! Switchbacks in Circle Cliffs = cinematic and slightly terrifying. From Boulder to Capitol Reef 66 miles. F-150 recommended - dry season OK with 2WD. Grand Staircase-Escalante National Monument, FREE.

name: Canyonlands Ballooning - Moab
notes: SUNRISE balloon over Arches + Canyonlands! Since 2008. Family business. 60+ minutes. Arches sandstone floats past. La Sal Mountains horizon. Max 16 passengers. Champagne landing. Spring and autumn are the best times. Book weeks in advance!

name: Canyonlands National Park
notes: Utah's largest national park - four totally different districts! Island in the Sky: a breathtaking mesa view. Needles: red needle rocks, backpacking, 4WD. America the Beautiful pass valid! Less visited than Arches but just as spectacular.

name: Capitol Reef National Park
notes: Utah's least known Big-5 park - WRONGLY! Waterpocket Fold: geological wonder, 100 miles long. Gifford Farmhouse: selling fresh apple pie in a national park! America the Beautiful pass valid! Least crowded of the Mighty Five. Torrey as home base.

name: Carl's Critter Garden - Hanksville
notes: Garden FULL of dinosaur sculptures made from old machine parts! Carl's outsider art at its purest: recycled metal monsters. Hanksville is the end of the world anyway. FREE to view. Small but fantastically bizarre. Combined with Goblin Valley: perfect weird day in central Utah.

name: Dead Horse Point State Park
address: Dead Horse Point Rd, Moab, UT 84532
notes: MOST PHOTOGRAPHED spot in Utah (so they say)! Colorado River makes a 300° turn 1,800 feet UNDER your feet. Filming location of Thelma & Louise (the end!) Near Canyonlands Island in the Sky. $20 state park, ATB pass NOT valid. Always worth it!

name: Deer Valley Resort ⛷️ Ikon (skiërs only)
address: 2250 Deer Valley Dr S, Park City, UT 84060
notes: Ikon Pass: 7 DAYS. NO snowboards - skiers only! Highest-rated adult ski instruction in the US. Impeccably groomed slopes = beginner paradise. ELS PRIORITY! Book premium lessons here. Accommodation and dining: SO EXPENSIVE - stay in Park City and drive up. 2002 Olympic slopestyle venue. One of the BEST experiences for Els of the entire trip!

name: Dinosaur National Monument - Utah kant
notes: 1,500+ dinosaur BONES IN THE ROCK WALL - literally! Quarry Exhibit Hall: glass wall displays real fossils in situ. Colorado + Utah border splits the park. America the Beautiful pass valid! Jensen side has the dinosaurs. Vernal for hotels.

name: Fisher Brewing - Salt Lake City
address: 320 W 800 S, Salt Lake City, UT 84101
notes: SLC's most acclaimed craft brewery - employee-owned! 100+ unique beers brewed per year. Granary District: SLC's hippest neighborhood. Large taproom + terrace. Best IPAs: Salt Flats + Kicker. Visitor favorite.

name: Flying J Truck Museum - Tooele
notes: Collection of vintage trucks + bizarre mechanical artifacts! Personal museum of a truck enthusiast. Tooele: 40 min from SLC towards Nevada. Small, unexpected, free. The Utah desert is full of these kinds of private obsession museums.

name: Fresh Starts Club - Salt Lake City
address: 2131 S W Temple, Salt Lake City, UT 84115
notes: Utah's most famous lifestyle club! Est. 1995. Couples, women, and select single men. On-premise. Vetting required by phone. Salt Lake City – a spicy contrast to the LDS capital! Contact via Kasidie ​​or directly. Call in advance.

name: Gilgal Sculpture Garden
address: 749 E 500 S, Salt Lake City, UT 84102
notes: Mormon bishop built his own apocalyptic sculpture park! Joseph Smith as the Sphinx. Himself in brick pants ('Mr. Brick Pants'). Carved entirely by hand between 1945 and 1963. Now a FREE city park. Completely bizarre and unique. Small but ABSOLUTELY worth it. Combine with SLC day.

name: Gilgal Wish Tree - Provo
notes: Tree COVERED with coins, cans, and bottles full of wishes! Uttah's version of a wishing well – but a tree. Local tradition that no one really knows how it started. FREE. Provo center. Quick photo stop. Add your own wish! Belgian francs if you have one.

name: Goblin Valley State Park
address: Temple Mountain Rd, Green River, UT 84525
notes: THOUSANDS of rock formations that look like aliens! Hoodoos, goblins, mushroom boulders - surreal moonscape. Walk freely AMONG the rock monsters. No paths! Just go. Filming location of Galaxy Quest (1999). Star Trek fans: pilgrimage! America the Beautiful pass NOT valid - state park.

name: Great Salt Lake - Antelope Island
notes: Great Salt Lake: 8x saltier than the ocean - you DON'T SINK! Antelope Island: 600 bison on an open island in the lake. Pink color due to halophilic algae (swimming = ticklish). Bizarre extreme salt experience. Shower IMMEDIATELY afterward. State park. Best spring/fall - summer = mosquitoes AND stench!

name: Hell's Backbone Grill - Boulder
notes: FARM-TO-TABLE in the heart of nowhere! Almost everything on the menu is home-grown or local. Vegetarian-friendly. Buddhist owners. Boulder: 200 inhabitants. Restaurant: nationally renowned. Book weeks in advance. Best food on Utah 12.

name: High West Distillery - Wanship
notes: Utah's FIRST legal distillery after Prohibition (1870-2000)! Americana Whiskey + Double Rye are nationally renowned. Tour + tasting. Historic ranch location. Park City: 15 min. Perfect après-ski stop. Best whiskey in the Rockies. Seriously.

name: High West Saloon - Park City
notes: America's only ski-in, ski-out DISTILLERY! House-made whiskey with après-ski food. Park City's coolest spot. Historic building. Whiskey flights + roast meats = Utah enjoyment. Reserves for dinner. Bar: first come first served.

name: Hole N' The Rock - Moab
notes: 5,000 m² home CARVED OUT of a sandstone rock! Albert Christensen built this for 12 years with his bare hands. Zoo, gallery, and Navajo pottery next door. Along US-191 just outside Moab. Roadside classic! Guided tours of the rock chambers. DO NOT miss.

name: Kingston Canyon - Polygamy Town
notes: Active FLDS polygamy community in a remote canyon! Kingston Clan: 100+ women, dozens of children per man. Can be seen from the outside - do not enter. In the middle of nowhere, 3 hours from SLC. Most bizarre: ordinary Walmart pickup trucks + women in pioneer dresses.

name: Lucin Ghost Town
notes: Former train station, now abandoned micro-community. One DIY kite flyer living in a hangar – that’s all! Alas Obscura calls it 'a proto-micronation of artists'. Near Sun Tunnels – perfect combo. FREE, abandoned, end-of-the-world atmosphere.

name: Metaphor: The Tree of Utah
address: I-80 milepost 26, Bonneville Salt Flats, UT
notes: 87-foot-tall PSYCHEDELIC tree in the middle of the salt flats! Swedish artist Karl Momen built this in 1986. Concrete trunks covered with colorful ceramic spheres. Along I-80 towards Nevada. FREE. Completely surreal. Best contrast: tiny tree on ENDLESS white expanse.

name: Moab Brewery
notes: THE ONLY full-service microbrewery in Moab! Dead Horse Amber Ale = local legend. Large patio. Popular after visiting the national park. Utah beer rules = 5% ABV max on tap - bring your own pitchers! Hikers, cyclists, climbers: everyone here.

name: Moab Brewery - Moab
notes: Only microbrewery in Moab! Post-hike MANDATORY. Dead Horse Amber Ale, a local legend. Utah beer rules: 5% max. Take pitchers outside. Big place, good food, no pretension. Moab Adventure Center is next door.

name: Moab Skydiving
notes: Tandem skydive over the Red Canyon canyons of Moab! 10,000 feet altitude. 60 seconds free fall. Arches and Canyonlands panorama from the air. Small plane, personal approach. Via Sorrel River Ranch and local operators.

name: Mystic Hot Springs - Monroe
notes: GOLDBUG STYLE, but paid and with vintage bathtubs! Antique clawfoot bathtubs IN the geothermal water. Clothing optional after dark. Hippie vibe, live music. Monroe, 3 hours from SLC. Camping on site. Perfect stopover on the way to Bryce Canyon. Unique concept!

name: Newspaper Rock State Historic Monument
notes: 2,000 years of petroglyphs on ONE rock – the most in the US! Fremont, Navajo, Anasazi, and Anglo – they all signed here. FREE. Right by the road. Short 5-minute stop. Road to Canyonlands Needles District. Best photographed: cloudy day (no harsh shadows).

name: Nine Mile Canyon Petroglyphs
address: Nine Mile Canyon Rd, Price, UT 84501
notes: 'World's Longest Art Gallery' - 40+ miles full of petroglyphs! Fremont Indians scratched here thousands of years ago. Bison, hunters, snake rituals - all in the rocks. Unpaved road but normally accessible by car. FREE. Little visited. Combine with Price as a base.

name: Painted Pony - St. George
address: 2 W St. George Blvd, St. George, UT 84770
notes: Fine dining with Southwestern flair in St. George! Rattlesnake chili + local organic ingredients. Upscale but not pretentious. St. George: gateway to Zion of the West. Good dinner for the Zion day trip.

name: Paria Canyon / Vermilion Cliffs
notes: WILD mountain goats on fuchsia/orange cliffs! Condor viewing: 40+ California Condors on the heat lift. Wave permit lottery from here (Arizona side). Kanab as a base. FREE cliff viewing from the outside. Near Page AZ and Antelope Canyon. Beautiful cluster.

name: Ray's Tavern - Green River
notes: Legendary 'river rat mecca' of Utah! Chargrilled burgers + local beer. No frills. Ratters, motorcyclists, and travelers meet. Green River: perfect stopover Moab ↔ Price. Has been open for decades. Local culture at its purest.

name: Red Iguana - Salt Lake City
address: 736 W North Temple, Salt Lake City, UT 84116
notes: SLC's best MOLE sauces - 7 varieties available at once! Legendary Mexican restaurant, always a line outside. Family-run. Local favorite for decades. North Temple, 10 min from the center. Bes: lunch service avoids wait times.

name: Republic of Zaqistan
notes: MICRONATION on BLM land in the Utah desert! Artist Zaq Landsberg bought the plot in 2005 for $610. Own passport, flag, constitution, and border guard (a robot). Near Wendover. GPS coordinates on the website. FREE to visit if you can find it. Absurd performance art.

name: Scenic Biplane Rides - Moab
notes: Biplane above the canyon landscape! Open cockpit, wind in your hair, canyon below you. Canyonlands Airport as departure point. Small, intimate, unforgettable perspective. Bookable via Moab Adventure Center.

name: Snowbasin Resort ⛷️ Ikon
notes: Ikon Pass: 7 DAYS. First Utah stop. Littlecat base area = fantastic protected beginner zones for Els. Luxury day lodges = perfect break. NO slopeside hotels - drive up from Ogden every morning. 2002 Olympic Games location. Spectacular mountain scenery. Less crowded than Park City resorts!

name: Solitude Mountain Resort ⛷️ Ikon
address: 12000 Big Cottonwood Canyon Rd, Solitude, UT 84121
notes: Ikon Pass: UNLIMITED. Perfect relaxed practice day! The Link lift = quiet, slow, and gentle - perfect for Els. 1-2 day stop recommended. Big Cottonwood Canyon traffic can be extremely bad on powder days. Quieter alternative vs. busy Park City. Free bus from Salt Lake City available. Less touristy than neighbors.

name: Sorrel River Ranch - Moab
notes: RIVERFRONT ranch resort on the Colorado River! 4,000-acre ranch. Horseback riding, river floating. Luxurious suites with canyon views. High-end, but the LOCATION is unparalleled. 17 miles from Moab. Silence, space, starry skies.

name: Summum Pyramid - Salt Lake City
address: 707 Genesee Ave, Salt Lake City, UT 84104
notes: Small pyramid as the HQ of an obscure religion that makes mummies! Summum: a mix of ancient Egyptian and modern philosophy. They embalm animals *and* people. Preserved for eternity. Tours available by appointment. FREE to view from the outside. SLC's craziest landmark. No one knows it exists.

name: Sun Tunnels - Lucin
notes: 4 concrete tunnels aligned with the SUMMER SUNNESTIL and WINTER NIGHT! Nancy Holt (1976) created this land art masterpiece. Holes in the tunnels form constellations in daylight. In the middle of the West Desert - 45 min from Wendover. FREE. Solstice periods are MAGICAL. Far away, hugely worth the effort.

name: The Burrito Lady - Torrey
notes: Iconic little taco truck at Capitol Reef! Handmade burritos + fresh salsas. Torrey's most talked-about eatery. Simple but perfect. Drives by the station or find the location on social media. Cash only. Go early because it sells out.

name: This Is The Place Heritage Park
address: 2601 E Sunnyside Ave, Salt Lake City, UT 84108
notes: Brigham Young stood here and said 'This is the place!' (1847). Living historical village with Pioneer period buildings. Costumest actors. Crafts, trains, animals. The 'This is the place' monument is free. The park pays. SLC day out. Children love it.

name: Thistle Ghost Town
notes: Ghost town swallowed by a GIGANTIC mudslide! In 1983, a landslide blocked the canyon. The town drowned. The ruins are still visible along US-6. FREE to see from the car. Short walk possible. Spanish Fork Canyon. Quick stop towards Price.

name: Topaz Mountain - Gemstone Digging
address: Topaz Cove Rd, Juab County, UT 84624
notes: Dig your own topazes out of the desert soil! BLM soil: completely FREE and legal. 1 kilo per day. Juab County desert - 90 min from SLC. Best time: autumn and spring (summer is dangerous). Bring: hammer, chisel, gloves. Pure treasure hunting!

name: Torrey Schoolhouse B&B
notes: Historic school building converted into a B&B! 1914 schoolhouse. Capitol Reef 10 min away. Cozy rooms, local breakfast, garden seating. Torrey: perfect base for Capitol Reef visitors. Booking in advance is essential during the season.

name: Under Canvas Bryce Canyon
notes: GLAMPING in luxury tents with a view of the stars! Comfortable tents with real beds + bathroom. Utah 12 Corridor. Bryce 15 min away. One of the most popular glamping resorts in the US. Sunset + Milky Way here = unforgettable.

name: UP House (Pixar-inspired) - Herriman
address: 13703 S Herriman Rose Blvd, Herriman, UT 84096
notes: Exact REPLICA of the UP house from the Pixar movie! Owner built to exact film specifications. Outside AND inside. Private residence - view outside only please. Herriman, 30 min from SLC. FREE photo stop. Instagram GOLD. Not affiliated with Disney.

name: Utah 12 Scenic Byway
address: SH-12 tussen Panguitch en Torrey, UT
notes: MOST BEAUTIFUL drive in the US - voted so multiple times! 124 miles through Grand Staircase, Bryce, Escalante, Capitol Reef. Hogback Ridge: road runs over a narrow mountain ridge with NO guardrails. Boulder, Escalante, Torrey as stopping points. Autumn: golden-yellow poplars + red rock = explosion.

name: Wasatch Naturists (Club - geen resort)
notes: Utah's only active naturist club! Monthly skinny dip pool parties + outings. 18+ only. No permanent site - events-based. Trips to hot springs, Baker HS, outdoors. Contact Wasatch Naturists via website for events calendar.

name: Wendover Will Neon Sign
address: 1985 W Wendover Blvd, West Wendover, NV 89883
notes: 63-foot-tall neon man with cowboy hat - iconic sign! The 'Blade Runner' neon of the desert. Technically Nevada but right next to the Utah border. FREE. Wendover Nevada casino side. Night: most impressively lit.

name: Zion National Park
notes: Angels Landing: terrifying chain hike HIGH above the canyon. The Narrows: wade through the Virgin River - WET SHOES! America the Beautiful pass valid! Free shuttle from Springdale - car must be left behind. Spring/Autumn: perfect. Summer: 38°C in the canyon = sauna.

name: Ben & Jerry's Ice Cream Factory
notes: Graveyard of Flavors: buried flavors that no longer exist. Factory tour: how Phish Food is made. Els: this is a pilgrimage. Free tasting after the tour.

name: Burlington Church Street Marketplace
notes: Pedestrian shopping street in the heart of Burlington. Farmers market, buskers, local shops. Waterfront directly behind: Lake Champlain sunset.

name: Cold Hollow Cider Mill
notes: Freshly pressed apple cider before your eyes. Cider donuts baked while you watch. Els: cider donuts = reason to go to Vermont.

name: Covered Bridge Tour (Mad River Valley)
notes: 15+ covered wooden bridges in the Mad River Valley. Autumn: red bridge + orange leaves = perfect photo. Free ride past all bridges.

name: Green Mountain National Forest - Long Trail
notes: America's OLDEST long-distance hiking trail (1910)! 483 km from Massachusetts to Canada, straight through the Green Mountains. Route 100 (Vermont's most beautiful road) runs parallel—perfect fall route. Countless day hike starting points. FREE. The Appalachian Trail also crosses here.

name: Hill Farmstead Brewery
notes: Best brewery in the world (RateBeer #1 for multiple years): in the middle of a field. Location: driving through the mountains is worth it. Serge: pilgrimage to the best brewery in the world.

name: Lake Champlain (Champy monster)
notes: Our own Loch Ness monster: Champ, first sighted in 1609 by Samuel de Champlain. Boat trips on the lake: search for Champ included (mentally). Burlington: Vermont's nicest city on the lake.

name: Lawson's Finest Liquids
notes: Superpunch Imperial IPA: one of the most sought-after beers from New England. New taproom open in Waitsfield. Serge: two top breweries in Vermont = route like this.

name: Maple Syrup sugarbush tour
notes: March-April: tapping and boiling maple sap in traditional sugarhouses. VT produces 50% of all American maple syrup. Els: this is the Belgian chocolate equivalent of the US.

name: MASS MoCA (North Adams, MA — Vermont border)
address: 1040 Mass MoCA Way, North Adams, MA 01247
notes: Largest art museum in North America: factory complex of 27 buildings. Permanent James Turrell and Sol LeWitt installations. Els: this is the top 5 art spot of the trip.

name: Montpelier (smallest US capital)
notes: Smallest state capital in the US: 8,000 inhabitants. Golden Dome State House free to visit. Walk from one end to the other in 15 minutes.

name: Moss Glen Falls - Stowe
address: Moss Glen Falls Rd, Stowe, VT 05672
notes: Vermont's most beautiful waterfall in a gorge full of moss and ferns – a 37m drop in a surreal setting. Short walk (800m). Autumn is also fantastic – golden leaves surround the water. FREE. Easy to combine with Mt Mansfield or Smugglers Notch. Very little visited.

name: Mount Mansfield - Stowe
notes: Highest point in Vermont (1,339m)! Take the gondola or toll road up, or hike. Views of 5 states plus Canada on a clear day. In autumn: the Green Mountains are ablaze with yellow, orange, and red. The Stowe area is *the* Vermont destination for autumn. Gondola approx. $30pp.

name: Naturist: geen AANR resort VT
notes: Vermont has no official AANR naturist resort. Private skinny dipping at the many lakes is common. Nearest AANR: Sandy Terraces CT or Solair RI.

name: Pitcher Inn (Warren)
notes: Luxury boutique inn in Mad River Valley: every room has a Vermont theme. Best restaurant in the region. Above budget, but the experience is unique.

name: Quechee Gorge (Vermont's Grand Canyon)
notes: 18-meter-deep crack in the landscape: shortest walk to a spectacular view. Free parking, free bridge over it. Combine with Woodstock Village.

name: Robert Frost's Farm (Ripton)
notes: Robert Frost wrote his best poems here in the summers. Public walking path past his house and forest. Free — literary pilgrimage in the most beautiful VT landscape.

name: Rock of Ages Quarry (Barre)
notes: Deepest active granite quarry in the world: 150 meters deep. From a viewing platform, you look down at men carving out stones. Serge: the scale is unimaginable.

name: Shelburne Museum (37 buildings)
notes: 37 historic buildings towed from all over New England to one location. A carousel, a steamboat, a lighthouse, a circus tent — all original. Els: this is a museum that is a village.

name: Smugglers' Notch State Park
notes: Dramatic mountain canyon filled with gigantic boulders – 19th-century smugglers used this path for forbidden whiskey to Canada! Bizarre rock formations with names like The King and The Singing Bird. Second highest point in Vermont. Road open only in summer. $5 day pass.

name: St. Johnsbury Athenaeum
notes: Victorian library with an original 1871 art gallery — never modernized. Albert Bierstadt's 'Domes of the Yosemite' painting dominates the space. Free, surreal time capsule.

name: Stowe (ski + fall foliage)
notes: Most beautiful village in Vermont: Stowe Pinnacle walk, village church, beautiful main street. Autumn (Sept-Oct): richest colors of New England. Ikon Pass: Mount Mansfield ski area also in winter.

name: Stowe Cider
notes: Craft cidery in Stowe: Vermont apples, wild fermentation. Els: cider is the Belgian beer of Vermont.

name: Swingers: VT lifestyle scene
notes: Vermont is too small for permanent lifestyle clubs. Private events in Burlington via SDC.com. Boston (3h) has many more options.

name: The Inn at Shelburne Farms
notes: Victorian country house on a 400-hectare working organic farm. Farm-made cheese breakfast every morning. Els: This is the most Vermont thing in the world.

name: Trapp Family Lodge (Stowe)
notes: Hotel built by the Sound of Music family after their flight from Austria. Austrian lodge style in the green Vermont hills. Serge: von Trapp family + beer + mountains = agreed.

name: Vermont Country Store (Weston)
notes: General store as it existed in 1897: flame retardants, old-fashioned candy, flannel underwear. Nostalgia as a product. Free to browse, buying optional.

name: Vermont Teddy Bear Factory (Shelburne)
notes: Factory tour: how the famous teddy bears are made. You can design your own bear. Funnier than expected.

name: Woodstock Village
notes: The most English village in America: covered bridges, church, commons, everything perfect. National Geographic called it the 'most beautiful village in America' in 1938 — still true. Free to walk around.

name: Abingdon (Virginia Highlands)
notes: Victorian town with the oldest theater west of the Alleghenies. Virginia Creeper Trail: Virginia's best rail-to-trail bike route. E-bikes perfect: 56 km trail.

name: Appalachian Trail (Harpers Ferry start)
notes: Harpers Ferry is the midpoint of the AT: 3,500 km trail. Historic town where John Brown made his raid in 1859. Day trips on the AT in Virginia are spectacular.

name: Arlington National Cemetery
notes: JFK, Robert Kennedy, astronauts, and plane crash victims are buried here. Free admission, Changing of the Guard every half hour. Impressive and quiet.

name: Blue Ridge Parkway (VA sectie)
notes: Virginia's section of the Blue Ridge Pkwy: 217 km from the NC border to Shenandoah NP. National Parks Pass: FREE. Autumn here = absolutely spectacular.

name: Breaks Interstate Park (Grand Canyon of the South)
notes: Largest canyon east of the Mississippi: Russell Fork River. Virginia and Kentucky share the park. Class IV-V whitewater rafting in October: spectacular.

name: Charlottesville wine tour (Monticello Wine Trail)
notes: 30+ Wineries on the Monticello Wine Trail: Thomas Jefferson started here with Italian grapes.  Autumn: grape harvest plus foliage.  Els: this is Virginia at its best.

name: Chincoteague National Wildlife Refuge
notes: Wild ponies on Assateague Island — the same as near Maryland but on the Virginia side. National Parks Pass: admission. Pony swim every July: horses swim across the channel.

name: Colonial Williamsburg
notes: Fully reconstructed 18th-century colonial city: 500 actors in period attire, authentic working crafts. Largest historical open-air museum in the US. Els: this is time travel at a high level.

name: Hotel Roanoke
notes: Tudor Revival hotel from 1882 with Tiffany stained-glass windows. Perfect for the Blue Ridge Parkway section. Good value historic hotel.

name: Inn at Little Washington
notes: Patrick O'Connell's legendary 5-star restaurant-inn: Michelin 3-star. Way above budget, but the culinary pilgrimage is worth it for one night. Els: if luxury goes on the road trip for once: this.

name: Jamestown Settlement
notes: First permanent English settlement of the US (1607). Replica of Susan Constant (the ship). Combine with Colonial Williamsburg.

name: Luray Caverns
notes: Virginia's most beautiful caves: colossal formations and a stalactite organ that plays real music. Stalacpipe Organ: the largest musical instrument in the world. Serge: music from stalactites — this exists and it sounds good.

name: Maymont (Richmond)
notes: Victorian mansion on 40 hectares + Italian and Japanese gardens + zoo. Everything free — donations welcome. Els: this is a hidden gem of Richmond.

name: Monticello (Thomas Jefferson)
notes: Thomas Jefferson's masterpiece: architecture as a self-portrait. Jefferson designed every detail himself over 40 years. National Parks Pass: not applicable — private.

name: Mount Vernon (George Washington)
address: 3200 Mount Vernon Memorial Hwy, Mount Vernon, VA 22121
notes: Washington's plantation along the Potomac: his house, workshops, slave cabins. Story of slavery told honestly — not glossed over. Reconstructed farm shows real 18th-century farming.

name: Natural Bridge State Park
notes: Gigantic natural calcite bridge: 20 meters wide, 60 meters high. George Washington engraved his initials in it as a young man. National Parks (State) fee.

name: Natural Tunnel State Park
notes: Railway tunnel through a mountain: 800 meters long, 60 meters high — formed entirely by nature. William Jennings Bryan called it 'the Eighth Wonder of the World'. Chairlift down to the tunnel. Trains still occasionally run through it.

name: Naturist: White Tail Resort (AANR)
notes: One of the largest AANR member naturist resorts in the US. Swimming pool, campground, lodge. Virginia's premier naturist destination.

name: Peaks of Otter (Blue Ridge Pkwy)
notes: Lodge directly on the Blue Ridge Parkway: sunrise over the Appalachians from the room. Award-winning summer program with rangers. Perfect stop on the Parkway route.

name: Richmond Murals Tour
notes: Richmond has one of the best street art scenes on the East Coast. Arts District: Boulevard and surrounding streets. Free self-guided tour.

name: Shenandoah National Park (Skyline Drive)
notes: 170 km scenic highway along the Blue Ridge crest: apple blossoms in May, colors in October.  National Parks Pass: FREE.  E-bikes on overlook trails along the route.

name: Skyline Caverns (Front Royal)
address: 10344 Stonewall Jackson Hwy, Front Royal, VA 22630
notes: The only caves in the world with anthodites: white calcite spikes that grow in every direction. Never found outside this cave. Front Royal: perfect Skyline Drive starting point.

name: Swingers: The Velvet Nation (Northern VA)
notes: Northern Virginia / DC metro has an active lifestyle scene. Verify via SDC.com or Kasidie ​​for current information. DC environment = international community = open attitudes.

name: Tangier Island (vanishing island)
notes: Island in the Chesapeake Bay that is slowly sinking: rising sea level. Residents speak the Elizabethan English dialect unchanged. Ferry from Onancock or Crisfield MD. Do it fast.

name: The Homestead Creamery (Wirtz)
notes: Family farm with its own ice cream and cheese. Virginia milk transformed into wonderful products. Els: this is the Belgian farm shop, but Virginia style.

name: The Omni Homestead Resort (Hot Springs VA)
address: 7696 Sam Snead Hwy, Hot Springs, VA 24445
notes: Resort in operation since 1766: oldest resort in America. Natural thermal springs, golf, spa. Els: historic resort + hot springs + mountains.

name: Virginia Beach Boardwalk
notes: 8 km boardwalk along the Atlantic beach. Neptune's statue, surfers, military planes over the beach. Largest resort town on the East Coast.

name: Virginia Museum of Fine Arts (Richmond)
address: 200 N Arthur Ashe Blvd, Richmond, VA 23220
notes: Free museum with impressive Art Nouveau, Fabergé, and Himalayan collections. Best free museum in Virginia.

name: Virginia's Explore Park
address: Off Blue Ridge Pkwy MP 115, Roanoke, VA 24012
notes: Adventure park with ziplines and mountain biking on the Blue Ridge. The Blue Ridge Parkway runs straight through the park. E-bikes on the trails.

name: Boeing Factory Tour (Everett)
notes: Largest building in the world by volume: Boeing 747/787 assembly. You watch from a walkway while planes are being built. Serge: This is better than any aviation museum.

name: Canlis Restaurant (Seattle)
notes: Legendary restaurant since 1950 overlooking Lake Union: three generations of family. Tasting menu: modern Pacific Northwest cuisine. Reservations 2 months in advance. Serge: this is the fancy night in Seattle.

name: Chihuly Garden and Glass (Seattle)
notes: Dale Chihuly's glassblowing masterpiece: gardens full of gigantic colored glass sculptures. Inside + outside: spectacular day and night. Els: this is the top 5 of the entire trip.

name: Columbia River Gorge (WA kant)
notes: North Bank of the Columbia Gorge: less crowded than the Oregon side but just as beautiful. Kiteboarding paradise at Hood River. Walking trails along the river.

name: Deception Pass State Park
notes: Spectacular bridge over a strait: strong currents pull the sea through the rocks. Washington's largest visited state park. E-bikes on the 38 km of walking trails.

name: Diablo Lake (turquoise alpine lake)
notes: Electric turquoise-blue glacial lake formed by glacial flour minerals. North Cascades Highway runs past it: free view. National Parks Pass: free.

name: Dry Falls (world's largest waterfall once)
address: 10 Dry Falls Park Rd, Coulee City, WA 99115
notes: Dried-up waterfall 5 times the width of Niagara: 15,000 years ago, this was the largest waterfall ever. Now a dry cliff of 120 meters: astounding. Geological wonder. Washington Scablands.

name: Fremont Brewing (Seattle)
notes: Seattle's best brewery in the alternative Fremont neighborhood. Summer Ale: #1 in WA for several years. Outdoor terrace with a view of the Aurora Bridge.

name: Ginkgo Petrified Forest SP
notes: 15-million-year-old petrified forest: stone ginkgo tree trunks. Pictures above the Columbia Gorge: Native American rock art. Free admission. I-90 corridor.

name: Grand Coulee Dam
notes: Largest concrete structure in the US: 168 meters high, 1,592 meters wide. Summer laser light show in the evening on Dam Square: free. Serge: this is engineering on a cosmic scale.

name: Hoh Rainforest (Olympic NP)
notes: Moss-heavy rainforest: every tree, stone, and floor covered with thick green moss. National Parks Pass: FREE. Hall of Mosses: most photogenic forest in the US.

name: Hurricane Ridge (Olympic NP)
address: Hurricane Ridge Rd, Port Angeles, WA 98362
notes: Subalpine meadows at 1,600m above the Strait of Juan de Fuca. National Parks Pass: FREE. Marmots, black deer, snowfields in August.

name: Inn at the Market (Seattle)
notes: Hotel directly above Pike Place Market with a view of Puget Sound. Walk directly from the hotel to the fish market. Els: best location in Seattle.

name: Leavenworth (Bavarian theme village)
notes: A small Washington village that has transformed itself into a Bavarian village, complete with Oktoberfest, lederhosen, and glockenspiel. Total kitsch, but hilariously well executed. Els: this is Belgian kitsch tolerance tested.

name: Mount Rainier National Park
notes: 14,411-foot active volcano with eternal snow: most prominent mountain of the lower 48. National Parks Pass: FREE. Wildflower meadows in August: thousands of colors around the mountain.

name: Mount St. Helens National Volcanic Monument
address: 3029 Spirit Lake Hwy, Castle Rock, WA 98611
notes: Active volcano that erupted in 1980: partially reforested but a large cleared zone is still visible. National Forest Pass of America the Beautiful. Rangers tell the story of the eruption.

name: Mt. Baker (winter drive)
notes: Most snowfall ever recorded in a single season: 29 meters in 1998-99. The Mt. Baker Highway (SR-542) is free to drive towards the mountain. Ikon Pass: Mt. Baker ski area.

name: Naturist: Club Paradise (WA)
notes: Washington has multiple AANR naturist clubs. Verify current options via the AANR website. Pacific Northwest has a strong naturist tradition.

name: North Cascades National Park
notes: Alpine mountain landscape with 300+ glaciers: wildest wilderness of the lower 48. National Parks Pass: FREE. North Cascades Highway (SR-20): one of the most beautiful mountain roads in the US.

name: Old Rainier Brewery Building - Seattle
notes: Iconic neon R logo on hilltop is a Seattle landmark. Rainier beer is the working-man's beer of PNW. Not the best brewery, but the heritage value is high.

name: Olympic National Park (Hoh Rainforest)
address: 3002 Mount Angeles Rd, Port Angeles, WA 98362
notes: Three totally different ecosystems: rainforest, mountain coast, alpine. National Parks Pass: FREE. Hoh Rainforest: densest forest in the US, moss on everything.

name: Palouse Falls State Park
notes: Washington's state waterfall: 57 meters high in a dry basalt canyon — a total contrast. Spring: melting snow maximizes the drop. Free parking + small fee.

name: Paseo Caribbean (Seattle)
notes: Caribbean roast sandwich: Seattle's most acclaimed sandwich. Always a line, but always fast. Serge: this is the best sandwich of the trip.

name: Pike Place Market (Seattle)
notes: Fish toss, first Starbucks ever, daisy-chain flower stall. Free to walk around, pay for food. Els: the flower market is the best part.

name: San Juan Islands
address: Friday Harbor, San Juan Island, WA 98250
notes: Seeing orcas from the rocky coast: June-September. Anacortes ferry: 1-hour journey. Els and Serge: orcas swim 5 meters from the coast.

name: Sleeping Lady Mountain Resort (Leavenworth)
notes: Eco-resort in the Icicle Canyon near Leavenworth. Art, nature, and yoga in the middle of the Cascades. Els: this is the perfect counterpoint to the kitsch Bavarian village.

name: Space Needle (Seattle)
notes: 1962 World's Fair Tower: 184 meters tall, rotating restaurant. Urban glass floor on the observation deck. Seattle's icon — photogenic even from the ground.

name: Swingers: Club Sapphire (Seattle)
notes: Seattle has an open lifestyle scene. Verify current location and events via SDC.com. PNW culture: open and non-judgmental.

name: Taylor Shellfish Farms (Shelton)
notes: Straight from the oyster farm to your plate: 20+ varieties of oysters on site. Bayshore walk along the oyster beds. Els: Belgian mussels versus Washington oysters — comparing is mandatory.

name: Tom Douglas restaurants (Seattle)
notes: Seattle's most famous chef: Dahlia Lounge, Serious Pie, Lola. Pacific Northwest ingredients: salmon, Dungeness crab, Walla Walla onions. Choose your favorite from the portfolio.

name: 🏨 Blackwater Falls Lodge - Davis
notes: Rustic state park lodge RIGHT next to Blackwater Falls - the most beautiful waterfall in West Virginia (red falls due to tannic acid in the water)! Treehouses and cabins available. Canaan Valley 10 min away. Autumn here is an underrated jewel of the East Coast. Approx. $100-130/night.

name: Blackwater Falls State Park
notes: Waterfall with black tannin water over boulders: yellow and orange moss. Autumn: leaves + black water = photogenic. Lodge on the rim of the canyon.

name: Brooks Bird Club (songbird migration)
notes: WV is one of the best states for bird migration in the East. Warblers, tanagers, grosbeaks — hundreds of species. Els: birding paradise without the hype.

name: Cass Scenic Railroad (steam train)
notes: Historic steam train climbs an 800-meter elevation difference in 11 km. Old logging village of Cass completely preserved. Serge: steam train through the Allegheny mountains.

name: Country Road Scenic Drive (US-219)
notes: Most beautiful backroads of WV: hollers, old barns, Allegheny crestline. Autumn: abandoned farms + colors. E-bikes on the side roads.

name: Dolly Sods Wilderness
notes: High-lying swamp plateau in the Alleghenies: looks more like Canada than West Virginia. Bears, elk, and migratory birds are present in abundance. Free wilderness — 4x4 vehicle required for some trailheads.

name: Gauley River Whitewater (September)
notes: Gauley Season in September: dam release makes this Class V+. The hardest controlled whitewater in the world. Els and Serge: if you dare — this is the extreme level.

name: Greenbrier Bunker Tour
address: 101 Main St W, White Sulphur Springs, WV 24986
notes: Secret nuclear war bunker for 1,000 congressmen built beneath the resort. Keep secret until 1992 — journalist discovered it. Serge: Visiting a Cold War bunker while the rich golf above you.

name: Greenbrier Resort (historic grand hotel)
address: 101 Main St W, White Sulphur Springs, WV 24986
notes: Legendary grand resort since 1778: presidents, royal guests, a secret bunker. Secret bunker built in 1958 for Congress in the event of a nuclear attack — now open to visitors. Over budget, but the bunker tour is unique.

name: Harpers Ferry National Historical Park
notes: Three rivers meet in a spectacular small town. John Brown's Raid of 1859: catalyst of the Civil War. National Parks Pass: FREE.

name: Hatfield-McCoy Trails (off-road)
notes: 800 km of ATV trails through the coalfields: named after the famous blood feud. F-150 4x4s are allowed on some sections. Serge: this is the common thread running through WV culture.

name: Lost World Caverns
notes: Wild Cave tour through unexplored cave passages: crawling, climbing, splashing. War Club stalagmite: 30 tons, 5 meters high. Serge: wild cave = real cave experience.

name: Mothman Museum (Point Pleasant)
notes: Mothman: winged creature sighted before the Silver Bridge disaster of 1967. 46 deaths in that bridge collapse. Museum + life-size Mothman sculpture outside: free photo.

name: Naturist: geen AANR resort WV
notes: West Virginia has no official AANR naturist resort. Closest: White Tail Resort VA or other VA clubs. Private swimming in the rivers is popular.

name: New River Gorge Bridge
notes: Largest steel arch bridge in the world: 267 meters above the river. Pedestrians are allowed to walk on the catwalk at the UNDERSIDE of the bridge every day. Serge: this is the coolest bridge in the US.

name: New River Gorge National Park
notes: Deepest and oldest river canyon in the Appalachians. National Parks Pass: FREE. Bridge Day in October: BASE jumping and rappelling from the bridge — open to pedestrians one day a year.

name: Rafting New River (Adventures on the Gorge)
notes: New River Gorge whitewater: Class III-V depending on water level. Best whitewater east of the Rockies. Els and Serge: we are going to get wet here.

name: Seneca Rocks
notes: Dramatic quartzite pinnacles rising 300 meters above the valley. One of the most photogenic spots in the East. Climb or just look: both are spectacular.

name: Smoke Hole Caverns
notes: Cave with the longest stalactite strip in the US. Used by Native Americans as a smoking room. Tour 45 min.

name: Snowshoe Mountain (ski)
notes: Best ski area in the US Middle East: 1,500 down foot drop. Not on Ikon Pass but a winter route option. Good alternative if Colorado is full.

name: Swingers: WV lifestyle scene
notes: WV is small and conservative: no fixed clubs. Private events in Charleston via SDC.com. Pittsburgh, PA (2 hours) has more options.

name: 🏨 Canoe Bay - Chetek
notes: Absolutely secret wilderness resort – Frank Lloyd Wright-inspired architecture right on a private lake in the Wisconsin woods! Only 4 private cottages. No TV, no telephone – just nature. Voted one of the most romantic lodges in America. For an ultimately special night.

name: 🏨 The American Club - Kohler
notes: The only 5-star resort in Wisconsin located in a former immigrant hostel of sanitary giant Kohler! Bizarre backstory: the luxury hotel stands on the factory complex. Four golf courses surrounding it. Museum on Kohler sanitary innovation included. Forbes 4-star. Unique in the world. Approx. $200/night.

name: Apostle Islands National Lakeshore
notes: 22 islands in Lake Superior: sea caves, lighthouses, turtle beach. National Parks Pass: FREE. Winter: ice caves accessible across the frozen lake — awesome.

name: Cave of the Mounds
address: 2975 Cave of the Mounds Rd, Blue Mounds, WI 53517
notes: Smaller cave but exceptional formations: pink, orange, and white calcite. Discovered in 1940 during a quarry explosion. Can be easily combined with a House on the Rock day.

name: Cheeseburger in Caseville (Lake Huron)
address: Caseville, MI — maar WI heeft ook varianten
notes: NB: WI has its own crazy cheese culture. Kaasenburg in Plymouth, WI: cheese festival and cheese museum. WI = America's Dairyland: honor the concept.

name: Circus World Museum (Baraboo)
notes: Original winter quarters of Ringling Brothers Circus: 50 historic circus wagons. Summer: live circus performances in the tent. Els: this is nostalgia for a vanished world.

name: Devils Lake State Park
notes: Quartzite cliffs surrounding an Ice Age lake. Best climbing rock in Wisconsin. Largest visited state park in WI.

name: Effigy Mounds National Monument (Iowa border)
notes: Earthworks in the shape of animals (bear, bird, deer): Hopewell culture. National Parks Pass: FREE. Technically Iowa but border region WI/IA culture.

name: Frank Lloyd Wright Trail (WI)
notes: Driving route past 7 Frank Lloyd Wright works in WI: Taliesin, Seth Peterson Cottage, SC Johnson Administration Building. SC Johnson Racine: free tour of the administration building. Serge: architecture road trip.

name: Green Bay Packers stadium tour (Lambeau Field)
notes: Lambeau Field: temple of American football. Hall of Fame and stadium tour available. Serge: the only community-owned NFL franchise — socialist football.

name: Horicon Marsh (bird migration)
notes: Largest freshwater cattail marsh in the US: 200,000 geese in autumn. Boat trips and kayaking available. Free self-drive tours along the marsh.

name: House on the Rock (Spring Green)
notes: Alex Jordan built this on a rock and filled it with the most bizarre collections: Carousel with 269 horses (never ridden), world's largest hanging sea monster. Neil Gaiman used this as the setting in American Gods. 5/5 most bizarre place in Wisconsin.

name: International Crane Foundation (Baraboo)
address: E11376 Shady Lane Rd, Baraboo, WI 53913
notes: All 15 crane species in the world in one park. Conservation workshop open to visitors. Baraboo: circus + cranes = strange but perfect WI.

name: Kettle Moraine State Forest (geology)
address: N1765 County Rd G, Campbellsport, WI 53010
notes: Drumlins, kettles, and moraines: perfect geology of the Ice Age. Nordic trail and mountain bike routes. E-bikes on the 50 km trails.

name: Kohler Design Center
notes: FREE museum of the Kohler sanitary firm: 100 years of bathrooms and ceramic art. Stunning bathrooms in all aesthetic styles. Combine with the Kohler Art Center for a bizarre day in the bourgeoisie.

name: Mars Cheese Castle (Kenosha)
notes: Gigantic cheese shop with 200+ types of Wisconsin cheese, beer tasting, Belgian chocolate. On I-94: perfect stopover. Serge: Belgian chocolate in Wisconsin. We approve.

name: Milwaukee Art Museum (Calatrava)
address: 700 N Art Museum Dr, Milwaukee, WI 53202
notes: Santiago Calatrava's wings museum: folds open and closed like a bird every day. WI's most photogenic building. Els: architecture as performance.

name: Milwaukee Public Market
notes: Covered market in the historic Third Ward. WI cheese, local sausage, freshly baked bread. Free to wander around, eating is the activity.

name: Naturist: Sun Ray Hills (AANR)
notes: AANR naturist resort in East Wisconsin. Swimming pool, sports, and camping. Verify via the AANR website for current details.

name: New Glarus (Little Switzerland)
notes: Swiss immigrant village: chalet architecture, Schweizer Stube, yodeling festivals. New Glarus Brewing: Spotted Cow is the most requested WI beer. Serge: compare the Swiss with the Belgians. Subtle difference.

name: New Glarus Brewing Company
notes: Spotted Cow: WI's most beloved beer, only available in-state. Free brewery tour. Els: surprisingly good Belgian-inspired beers here.

name: Norske Nook (Osseo)
notes: Legendary Norwegian bakery-restaurant: best pie in America (recognized by James Beard). Gooseberry pie, pecan, sour cream raisin. Els: this type of bakery exists in Belgium too, but it is different from this.

name: Old World Wisconsin (Eagle)
notes: 59 historic buildings of Wisconsin immigrants: German, Polish, Norwegian, Finnish. Actresses in clothing from 1860-1915. Els: multicultural immigrant history as an experience.

name: Pabst Mansion (Milwaukee)
notes: Mansion of beer baroness Frederick Pabst (Pabst Blue Ribbon): 37 rooms, completely intact. Victorian opulence. Milwaukee = beer culture, this is the architectural embodiment.

name: Peninsula State Park (Door County)
notes: Wisconsin's most beautiful state park: 8 km coastline, lighthouses, bike paths. Through County = Wisconsin's wine and cherry region. E-bikes perfect on the 32 km bike route.

name: Real Chili (Milwaukee)
notes: Milwaukee-style chili: unique recipe with Cheddar and secret spices. Open for 50 years — unchanged. Serge: anyone who makes chili in Wisconsin — respect.

name: Rocky Arbor State Park (ancient forest)
notes: Small but intimate park with ancient forest in a Cambrian sandstone canyon. Good campground near Wisconsin Dells. Combine with a day at the Circus Museum in Baraboo.

name: Smoky's Club Supper Club (Madison)
notes: Wisconsin Supper Club: unique genre — full of chicken, prime rib, relish tray, brandy old fashioned. Doesn't exist anywhere outside of WI. Serge: this is the most Wisconsin experience in the world.

name: Sprecher Brewing (Milwaukee)
notes: Milwaukee's best craft brewery with root beer and craft beer. Root beer made with Milwaukee honey and vanilla. Tour + tasting included.

name: Swingers: TPC (Milwaukee lifestyle)
notes: Milwaukee has an active lifestyle scene. Verify via SDC.com or Kasidie. Midwest lifestyle: friendly and welcoming.

name: Taliesin (Frank Lloyd Wright)
address: 5481 County Road C, Spring Green, WI 53588
notes: Frank Lloyd Wright's own home and school: he built it three times (burned down twice). Combine with House on the Rock — 30 min apart. Frank Lloyd Wright Route: WI has more of his works than any other state.

name: Wisconsin Dells (water park capital)
notes: Water park capital of the world: 20+ indoor and outdoor parks. Kitsch tourist resort, but the water entertainment is seriously good. Els: a day here is allowed.

name: Atlantic City WY (ghost town)
notes: Gold Rush ghost town with remaining residents: abandoned gold mines, original saloon. Authentic ghost town atmosphere. Free to explore.

name: Ayres Natural Bridge
notes: Free!, least known natural bridge in the US — 100 years ago it was more famous than Rainbow Bridge. La Prele Creek flows through it. Private park: FREE camping available.

name: Cheyenne Frontier Days
notes: Largest outdoor rodeo in the world: 10 days in July. Bull riding, barrel racing, parade. July 2027: check timing with route. Could be perfect.

name: Devil's Tower National Monument
notes: Gigantic basalt column of 386 meters rising from the prairie: Close Encounters of the Third Kind. Native Americans consider it sacred. National Parks Pass: FREE. Route to Mount Rushmore.

name: Flaming Gorge National Recreation Area
notes: Deep red canyon filled with emerald-green reservoir: boating, fishing, whitewater. Red Canyon Visitor Center: view like visiting Mars. America the Beautiful Pass: free.

name: Fossil Butte National Monument
notes: 50-million-year-old fossil fish perfectly preserved in green slate. National Parks Pass: FREE. Fossil fish excavation workshop available.

name: Grand Encampment Museum
notes: Copper mine ghost town from 1897: completely intact with 14 historic buildings. Transcontinental tramway system to transport copper over the mountain. Hidden gem of Wyoming.

name: Grand Teton National Park
notes: Most photogenic mountain range in the US: sharp granite peaks directly above the Snake River plain. National Parks Pass: FREE. Moose in abundance in the valley. Sunrise: phenomenal.

name: Hulett (Devils Tower gateway)
notes: Tiny cowboy village of 400 people near Devils Tower. Pub where real cowboys drink. Serge: this is the authentic West.

name: Jackson Hole (ski + town)
notes: Most intimidating ski resort in the US: Corbet's Couloir and Hobacks. Ikon Pass: Jackson Hole Mountain Resort. Jacksontown: cowboy bars and millionaires side by side.

name: Jackson Hole Aerial Tram
notes: Gondola to the top of Rendezvous Mountain: 3,185m. Summer: hiking and mountain biking on the alpine plateau. View over the entire Grand Teton National Park.

name: Jackson Hole Aerial Tram and Gondola Rides
address: 3275 West Village Dr, Teton Village, WY 83025, USA

name: Jackson Hole Mountain Resort ⛷️ Ikon
notes: Ikon Pass: 7 DAYS. ICONIC resort - an absolute must-see! Solitude Station beginner zone is modern + comfortable for Els. BUT: jump beginner → intermediate is VERY steep and intimidating. Town Jackson = wildlife (bison along the road!), Grand Teton views, great après-ski. Serge: advanced bowls are world-class. Els: stay in the Solitude Station zone!

name: Midway Geyser Basin Trl, Wyoming 82190
address: Midway Geyser Basin Trl, Wyoming 82190, USA

name: Moran Junction (Tetons + Yellowstone)
notes: Crossroads where the two most spectacular national parks in the US meet. Serpentine road along the mountain flanks. Each speaks the road over at dawn.

name: National Elk Refuge (Jackson)
notes: 7,500+ moose overwinter here: one of the largest elk concentrations in the world. Sleigh ride through the herd in December-April. Els: this is the most beautiful wildlife experience in Wyoming.

name: Naturist: geen AANR resort WY
notes: Wyoming has no official AANR naturist resort. Thermopolis Hot Springs is informal, clothing-optional at night. Nearest AANR: Colorado or Idaho.

name: Old Faithful (Yellowstone — buiten route maar nabij)
notes: NB: Yellowstone has already been visited by you — skip! Old Faithful Geyser erupts every 90 minutes: as predictable as a train. National Parks Pass: FREE. But already done!

name: Old Faithful Visitor and Education Center
address: View Avenue, Yellowstone National Park, WY 82190, USA

name: Pinedale (Green River Lakes)
notes: Spectacular alpine lakes with Squaretop Mountain as a backdrop. Green River source area: one of the most beautiful places in Wyoming. E-bikes on the path along the lake.

name: Saratoga Hot Springs Resort
notes: Outdoor hot springs pool on the North Platte River: in the middle of the wilderness. 105°F (40°C) water. Els and Serge: soaking while moose walk by.

name: Signal Mountain (Grand Teton NP)
notes: Spectacular viewpoint on Signal Mountain: 360 degrees over the Jackson Hole valley and Tetons. National Parks Pass: FREE. Early morning: reflection of the Tetons in Jackson Lake.

name: Snowy Range (Medicine Bow NF)
notes: Route 130 through the Snowy Range: alpine lakes at an elevation of 3,000m in the middle of Wyoming. Little visited: true wilderness. America the Beautiful Pass: free.

name: String Lake (Grand Teton NP)
notes: Crystal-clear glacial swimming lake at the foot of the Tetons. National Parks Pass: FREE. Els: This is the most beautiful swimming hole in Wyoming.

name: Swingers: WY lifestyle scene
notes: Wyoming is too sparsely populated for permanent clubs. Jackson Hole has an international community. Verify via SDC.com or Kasidie ​​for private events.

name: Ten Sleep Canyon
notes: Rock climbing mecca through a red sandstone canyon. Ten Sleep Creek: fly fishing in clear water. Driving through the canyon is spectacular in itself.

name: Thermopolis (world's largest mineral hot spring)
notes: Largest mineral hot springs in the world by volume. State Bath House: free soaking in the hot springs water! Wyoming permits FREE access by law.

name: Vedauwoo (granite climbing & formation)
notes: Chaos of enormous granite blocks: looks as if a giant threw them down. I-80 corridor: easy to stop. America the Beautiful Pass or small fee.

name: Wyoming Capitol Building tour
notes: Free tour of the recently restored State Capitol. Cheyenne is also known for its Frontier Days rodeo. July: Frontier Days is the largest outdoor rodeo in the world.

name: Wyoming Dinosaur Center (Thermopolis)
notes: Active dinosaur excavation site: watch or help dig. Fully articulated T-rex in the museum. Combine with hot springs for a full Thermopolis day.

name: Carcross (desert + historic village)
notes: Smallest desert in the world (3 km²) — sand dune in the middle of the forest. Carcross: railway crossing from the Gold Rush, historic center preserved. Free to explore.

name: Dawson City (Gold Rush capital)
notes: Klondike Gold Rush town from 1896: 30,000 gold prospectors influx in two years. The buildings are leaning due to permafrost movement. Diamond Tooth Gertie's: only legal casino on YT, cancan shows.

name: Dempster Highway (Yukon sectie)
address: Dawson City to YT/NWT border, YT Y0B 1G0
notes: Canada's most famous gravel road: 740 km towards the Arctic Circle. F-150 4x4: ideal for this. Bring two spare tires. Wildlife: caribou, grizzlies, Dall sheep.

name: Klondike Highway scenic drive
address: Skagway AK to Dawson City YT
notes: Spectacular historic gold route from Skagway, Alaska to Dawson City. Driving through the upper White Pass: glaciers, sand tunnels. F-150 4x4: born for this.

name: Kluane Lake (largest lake in Yukon)
address: Kluane Lake, Burwash Landing, YT Y0B 1V0, Canada
notes: Turquoise Glacial Lake: 65 km long, surrounded by the Kluane Ranges. Al Capone Hot Springs nearby (warm, unbuttered springs). The Alaska Highway runs along the lake.

name: Kluane National Park (largest icefields outside polar)
notes: Largest non-polar ice fields in the world: 22,000 km² of ice. National Parks Pass: FREE (Canada version). UNESCO World Heritage Site with Mount Logan — Canada's highest mountain.

name: Midnight Sun (June solstice)
notes: Around the summer solstice: the sun no longer sets. Golfing or picnicking at 2 a.m. in daylight. Els and Serge: biological clock is broken after a week.

name: Miles Canyon (Whitehorse)
address: Miles Canyon Rd, Whitehorse, YT Y1A 6B6, Canada
notes: Spectacular basalt canyon through which the Yukon River flows. Walking path along the canyon rim. Free admission.

name: Northern Lights / Aurora Borealis (Whitehorse)
notes: September-April: the aurora borealis over Yukon is spectacular. Whitehorse has B&Bs that call you to wake you up when the lights are active. Els and Serge: this is the ultimate bucket list.

name: Sourtoe Cocktail (Dawson City)
address: 2nd Ave, Dawson City, YT Y0B 1G0, Canada
notes: A real amputated human toe in your drink — tradition since 1973. Ten rules: 'The toe must touch the lips.' Els: no. Serge: yes. Debate closed.

name: SS Klondike National Historic Site
notes: Original sternwheeler steamboat restored and placed on the bank. National Parks Pass: FREE. Guided tour of the ship: the life of the river steamboat era.

name: Tombstone Territorial Park
address: Dempster Hwy KM 72, YT Y0B 1H0, Canada
notes: Dramatic black granite peaks and tundra: resembles Mordor. Best reached via Dempster Highway KM 72. Free camping and hiking.

name: Whitehorse Log Skyscraper
notes: Six-story building constructed entirely of logs (1947). Large considering that this is timber construction. Free photo from the street.

name: Yukon Wildlife Preserve
address: Mile 5 Alaska Hwy, Whitehorse, YT Y1A 5X7, Canada
notes: Car safari through the park with all the Yukon animals: wood bison, caribou, musk ox, grizzly, lynx. The only place in the world where you are guaranteed to see them. Driving around in the F-150: window-level animals.
